faq.a: One standard grilled piece of otak-otak in banana leaf is 80 calories. That's for a 50g piece, which is typical hawker size. The steamed version is 65 calories and the fried version hits 110 calories.

faq.q: Is otak-otak good for weight loss?
faq.a: It's one of the better hawker snacks for dieting, honestly. Eighty calories per piece with 8g protein and it's mostly fish. The main thing to watch is how many pieces you eat and whether they're grilled or fried. Three grilled pieces is 240 calories and 24g protein, which is a proper snack.

faq.q: What makes otak-otak so high in fat?
faq.a: It's not that high really, 4g fat per piece. The fat comes mostly from coconut milk, which is used as a binder in the fish paste. Compared to most fried snacks at the same stall, otak-otak is actually on the leaner side because the banana leaf wrapping keeps it from soaking up extra oil during grilling.

foods.name: Keropok Lekor
foods.metaDescription: Keropok lekor has about 270 calories per bag (8-10 pieces). The frying oil is the sneaky part. Losong version cuts it to 195. Here's the full breakdown.
foods.summary: Terengganu's famous fish sausage, boiled then deep-fried until chewy, served in a bag with chilli sauce on the side.
foods.answer: A standard bag of keropok lekor (about 8 to 10 pieces, 120g) comes in at 270 calories. That might not sound scary, but nearly a third of those calories are pure oil soaked up during deep frying. The fish paste itself is quite lean at around 55 calories for 55g, but the sago flour base adds 135 calories of carbs, and the frying oil piles on another 80. So yes, it's a snack, not a meal replacement, and the numbers add up faster than you think if you grab two bags.
realTalk: 270 calories per bag sounds manageable until you realise you're probably eating two bags while watching people fish at the jetty. The fish paste from ikan parang or tenggiri is honestly decent protein, 13g per bag, but the sago flour base is pure carbs and the frying adds 80 calories of oil on top. To be upfront, the numbers here are a solid estimate, not a lab reading. Hard data on keropok lekor is thin and different aunties fry theirs differently, so treat 270 as a reasonable ballpark, not gospel. If you're watching calories, one bag is fine. Two bags liao you're at 540 calories for a snack.

What actually swings the maths hard is which version you pick. Losong, the boiled or steamed version without frying, comes in at around 195 calories per serving because there's zero oil absorption. That's 75 calories less for the same amount of food, same fish, same sago base. The thin crispy sliced version (keropok lekor nipis) goes the other direction, hitting about 380 calories because the surface area is huge and it soaks up oil like a sponge. And if you're dipping in that sweet chilli sauce, add another 30 to 50 calories easy depending on how generous you are. Practical tip: ask for losong if the stall has it, eat one bag with a proper meal instead of as a standalone snack, and skip the second bag.
lighter: Order losong (boiled version) instead of fried and you cut about 75 calories per bag automatically.
One bag as a side, not a standalone snack. Pair it with a proper meal so you're not reaching for a second bag because you're still hungry.
Go easy on the chilli dipping sauce, which can add 30 to 50 calories depending on how much you pour.
Avoid the thin crispy sliced version (keropok lekor nipis), it hits 380 calories per serving because of much higher oil absorption.
If you're buying from a stall, freshly fried pieces that aren't sitting in oil are lower in absorbed fat than ones left sitting in the fryer basket.

faq.q: How many calories in Keropok Lekor?
faq.a: A standard bag of fried keropok lekor (about 8 to 10 pieces, 120g) has around 270 calories. The losong (boiled) version is lower at about 195 calories, while the thin crispy sliced version is higher at around 380 calories.

faq.q: Is keropok lekor high in calories for a snack?
faq.a: It's moderate but not low. At 270 calories per bag it's in the same range as a small meal, and it's easy to eat two bags without thinking. The fish itself is lean and gives you 13g of protein, but the sago flour and frying oil push the calorie count up.

faq.q: Is losong healthier than fried keropok lekor?
faq.a: Yes, noticeably so. Losong skips the deep frying entirely so there's no oil absorption. It comes in at around 195 calories per serving versus 270 for the fried version. Same fish, same sago base, just 75 fewer calories and much less fat.

foods.name: Nestum Chicken
foods.metaDescription: Nestum Chicken packs around 700 calories per plate. Find out where those calories come from and how to enjoy it without blowing your whole day.
foods.summary: Crispy deep-fried chicken tossed in buttery Nestum cereal, sweet and dangerously easy to overeat.
foods.answer: One plate of Nestum Chicken (2-3 bone-in pieces, roughly 220g) comes in at around 700 calories. That is not a typo. The cereal coating sounds innocent but it is deep-fried chicken tossed in butter and Nestum, so the calories add up fast. The chicken itself accounts for about 235 calories, and then you have 135 calories from the Nestum cereal plus another 150 calories from the butter used for tossing. Order this at a kopitiam and you are looking at a solid 700-calorie lauk before you even touch your rice.
realTalk: Nestum Chicken is one of those dishes that tricks you. It looks like a moderate-sized chicken dish, not a bowl of laksa or a plate of nasi lemak with everything on top. But at 700 calories for 2-3 pieces, it is punching way above its weight. The culprit is not the chicken itself. It is the combination of deep frying plus a proper butter toss with the Nestum cereal. About 150 of those calories come from the butter alone, and another 135 from the Nestum cereal coating. That sweet, fragrant crunch you love? That is where a huge chunk of the damage comes from. To be fair, these are ballpark estimates since hard nutritional data for this dish is basically nonexistent, so treat the 700 figure as a solid educated guess rather than a lab-verified number.

What actually changes the maths here is prep method and portion. A baked or air-fried version drops this to around 430 calories because you skip most of the frying oil and cut the butter way down. If you are ordering at a zi char place that goes heavy on the buttery Nestum sauce, you could easily hit 850 calories for a larger portion. Pair this lauk with a full plate of white rice and you are probably sitting at 1,000+ calories for one meal. If you want to make it work for weight loss, share the plate between two people or limit yourself to one piece and load up on plain veg on the side. The protein is decent at 35g, so the chicken part of this is genuinely useful. It is just the cereal-butter party around it that you need to manage lah.
lighter: Order one piece, not two or three. One bone-in piece is roughly 230-250 calories. That alone makes a big difference.
Ask for less butter when ordering at a restaurant. Some places will accommodate, especially at zi char stalls.
Eat it with plain steamed rice instead of fried rice. You are already at 700 calories on the lauk alone.
Skip the extra gravy or sauce at the bottom of the plate. That pooled butter-Nestum mixture is where a lot of extra fat hides.
Make it at home with an air fryer and half the butter. A homemade version can come in near 430 calories and still tastes solid.

faq.q: How many calories in Nestum Chicken?
faq.a: A standard plate of Nestum Chicken with 2-3 bone-in pieces (about 220g total) comes to roughly 700 calories. The main calorie drivers are the butter used for tossing (150 calories) and the Nestum cereal coating (135 calories), not just the chicken itself.

faq.q: Is Nestum Chicken healthy or is it just junk food?
faq.a: It is somewhere in between. The chicken gives you a decent 35g of protein per serving, which is actually pretty good. But the deep frying plus butter-Nestum toss means the fat is at 38g for one plate. It is fine to eat occasionally, but it is not a low-calorie dish you want to have every day if you are watching your weight.

faq.q: Can I make Nestum Chicken lower calorie at home?
faq.a: Yes, and it makes a big difference. Using an air fryer instead of deep frying and cutting the butter down to 10-15g can bring the whole plate to around 430 calories. You lose a bit of the richness but the Nestum crunch is still there. Worth trying if you want to eat this more regularly without the calorie hit.

foods.name: Tempoyak
foods.metaDescription: Tempoyak has about 40 calories per 2 tbsp. It's one of the more calorie-friendly Malaysian condiments, but portion size and how it's cooked really matters.
foods.summary: Fermented durian sambal eaten as a condiment with rice, pungent and flavourful in tiny amounts.
foods.answer: Tempoyak comes in at about 40 calories per 2 tablespoons (30g), which is honestly quite low for something that tastes this intense. The calories come almost entirely from the fermented durian flesh itself, around 35 calories worth, with a tiny bit from chili if it's made sambal-style. For a condiment eaten alongside rice, 40 calories is barely anything. The catch is most people don't stop at 2 tbsp.
realTalk: Forty calories per 2 tablespoons sounds almost too good for something made from durian, right? The numbers here are honestly a ballpark estimate because hard data on fermented durian is basically nonexistent in any nutrition database worth citing, so take these figures with some salt, literally. What we do know is that fermentation doesn't magically add fat or sugar, so plain tempoyak stays close to durian's natural calorie profile. Carbs are the dominant macro in durian, not fat or protein, which is why the macros here lean carb-heavy at roughly 4g carbs per 2 tbsp. The issue is never the tempoyak itself. It's what surrounds it. You have tempoyak as one of four lauk on your nasi campur plate, you're staring at 600 calories total before you've even sat down properly, bro.

The maths changes completely the moment tempoyak gets cooked into something. Sambal tempoyak at 45 calories per portion is still fine as condiments go. But ikan patin masak tempoyak or masak lemak with santan? Now you're eating a proper bowl of coconut milk curry, and that 30g of tempoyak has absorbed fat from the gravy and brought fifty other ingredients along for the ride. Keep it as a side condiment and the calorie cost is minimal. Order it as the cooking base in a curry and it depends entirely on how much santan went in and how big your portion is.
lighter: Keep it at 2 tablespoons alongside your rice. It's strong enough that a little goes a long way, you genuinely don't need more.

Go for plain sambal tempoyak as a condiment rather than ordering dishes where it's been cooked into a coconut milk curry. That masak lemak version can triple the calories for the same apparent portion.
Pair it with plain steamed rice and a lean protein like grilled ikan kembung instead of using it to zhng up an already oily plate.
If you're making it at home, skip the extra oil some recipes call for. Traditional tempoyak is just fermented durian plus salt, no oil needed.
Use it as a flavour hit on the side rather than mixing it through your whole plate of rice. You get all the taste for a fraction of the calories.

variants.note: Just fermented durian flesh with salt, no added chili or oil

variants.name: Sambal tempoyak (with chili, shallots, belacan)
variants.note: Mixed with pounded chili and aromatics as a sambal condiment

variants.note: Estimating 2 tbsp equivalent portion when cooked into curry with santan; absorbs fat from coconut milk

faq.q: How many calories in Tempoyak?
faq.a: A standard 2 tablespoon portion (about 30g) of tempoyak has around 40 calories. Plain tempoyak is closer to 35 calories, sambal tempoyak sits around 45, and if it's been cooked into a lemak curry with coconut milk, budget around 80 calories for the same sized portion.

faq.q: Is tempoyak fattening?
faq.a: Not really, if you use it like a condiment and keep portions small. 2 tbsp is only 40 calories. Where it gets you is when tempoyak gets cooked into masak lemak or gulai with santan, and then you're eating a full bowl of that curry, not just 30g. The tempoyak itself isn't the problem.

faq.q: Can I eat tempoyak when I'm on a calorie deficit?
faq.a: Yes, a small spoonful with rice is totally fine. The pungency means you don't need much to feel satisfied. Just be careful with the masak lemak version, where coconut milk pushes the calories up significantly. Stick to sambal tempoyak as a condiment and it won't hurt your numbers.

foods.name: Sayur Lemak
foods.metaDescription: Sayur Lemak has around 190 calories per hawker serving. Most of that comes from santan, not the veg. Here's what changes the count.
foods.summary: Vegetables cooked in coconut milk gravy, where the santan does most of the calorie heavy lifting.
foods.answer: A standard hawker serving of Sayur Lemak (about 180g) comes in at roughly 190 calories. Most of that is from the santan, not the vegetables. The coconut milk alone accounts for about 125 of those calories, which is the trade-off you make every time you scoop up that rich, yellowish gravy. As a veg side dish, 190 calories is moderate, though it can swing quite a bit depending on how heavy-handed the cook is with the coconut milk.
realTalk: Sayur Lemak is one of those dishes that tricks you into thinking you're eating healthy because, hey, it's vegetables. And technically you are. But that pale yellow gravy is basically coconut milk, and coconut milk gets around 85% of its calories from fat. Out of 190 calories in a normal hawker scoop, roughly 125 come from the santan alone. The vegetables themselves, whether pumpkin, pucuk manis, or cabbage, contribute maybe 45 calories total. So you're not eating a low-calorie dish. You're eating a moderate-calorie dish that happens to have some vegetables in it. Fair to flag here: these numbers are a genuine ballpark estimate because detailed lab data for sayur lemak specifically is thin. MOH figures and food tracker baselines vary quite a bit depending on the variant, so treat 190 as a reasonable middle ground, not gospel.

What actually moves the number is the santan ratio. A labu masak lemak can be as low as 120 calories for the same 180g serving, mainly because pumpkin itself is low-calorie so even with a standard santan gravy the overall dish comes in lighter. A rich sayur lemak campur with extra santan can push past 240 calories. The vegetable choice matters less than you'd think. It's the gravy that decides. Practically speaking, if you're eating this at a nasi campur stall, ask for less gravy and more solid veg, and you can probably shave 40 to 60 calories off that serving. If you cook at home, using reduced-fat santan or diluting with water drops the fat content significantly. As a side dish at lunch with plain rice and a piece of grilled chicken, 190 calories is absolutely fine. The problem is when you take two scoops and pour all that gravy over your rice lah.
lighter: Ask the stall for less gravy and more solid vegetable pieces, which can cut 40 to 60 calories per serving.
At home, use reduced-fat coconut milk or dilute full-fat santan with water at a 1 to 1 ratio to roughly halve the fat from the gravy.

Pick the labu (pumpkin) version when available, it typically runs around 120 calories per serving because pumpkin itself is low-calorie so even with a standard santan gravy the overall dish comes in lighter.
Pair it with plain steamed rice rather than nasi lemak or nasi goreng, no point stacking coconut dishes on top of each other.
Treat it as a side, not a main. One scoop alongside a lean protein like grilled chicken or tofu keeps your total meal reasonable.

variants.note: MOH data: ~50 kcal per 60g senduk; pumpkin is low-calorie so even with standard santan the dish comes in lighter

variants.note: MOH data: ~135 kcal per 70g; cabbage holds less gravy than leafy greens

variants.note: Richer coconut gravy, more santan; Snapcalorie baseline ~250 kcal/200g

faq.q: How many calories in Sayur Lemak?
faq.a: A typical hawker serving of Sayur Lemak (180g) has around 190 calories. The range is roughly 120 to 240 calories depending on how rich the santan gravy is and which vegetable is used.

faq.q: Is Sayur Lemak healthy for weight loss?
faq.a: It can fit into a weight loss diet as a side dish, but it is not a free food. The coconut milk adds significant fat. Stick to one scoop, ask for less gravy, and pair it with a lean protein to keep the overall meal balanced.

faq.q: Which version of Sayur Lemak is lowest in calories?
faq.a: Labu (pumpkin) masak lemak is the lowest, coming in around 120 calories per serving. Pumpkin itself is low-calorie, so even with a standard santan gravy the overall dish comes in lighter than leafy green versions.

foods.name: Kailan Ikan Masin
foods.metaDescription: Kailan ikan masin is about 200 calories per hawker plate. Not bad for a stir-fry, but the wok oil does most of the damage. Here's the full breakdown.
foods.summary: Chinese kailan stir-fried with salted fish and garlic. A simple hawker side dish where the wok oil does most of the calorie heavy lifting.
foods.answer: Kailan ikan masin comes in at around 200 calories per hawker plate (roughly 150g). That sounds low for a stir-fry, but the kailan itself is basically free calories. The problem is the oil absorbed during wok frying adds about 110 calories on its own, and the salted fish throws in another 40. So yeah, 200 is a reasonable ballpark for a normal hawker scoop.
realTalk: Honestly, 200 calories is pretty decent for a stir-fried veg dish. The kailan itself costs you almost nothing, around 40 calories for 120g of cooked greens. Where it sneaks up on you is the oil. A wok fry absorbs roughly 14-15g of oil, and that alone is 110 calories. The salted fish adds another 40. So you're basically paying 150 calories just for the cooking method and flavour. Fair trade if you ask me. The ikan masin is genuinely tasty and you get 9g of protein from a veg dish, which is not bad at all. These numbers are ballpark estimates by the way, because there's not a lot of hard lab data on kailan ikan masin specifically. Different hawkers use different amounts of oil, and the ikan masin portion varies a lot. Treat this as a reasonable guide, not a precise count.

What actually changes the maths here is the oil, full stop. A hawker who woks hard and generous can easily push this past 250 calories. A lighter hand stays closer to 160. The size of your scoop matters too. A heaped plate versus a small side scoop can be a 50 to 70 calorie difference. Some places also add a bit of sugar or extra oyster sauce, which adds maybe 15 calories but a tonne of sodium on top of the already-salty ikan masin. If you're watching your calories, this is still one of the safer dishes to order at a mixed rice stall compared to masak lemak or rendang. Grab a big scoop of this instead of an oily gravy veg and you're already doing better lah.
lighter: Order it as a side, not a main. A hawker scoop is 150g. Two scoops and the oil doubles too.
Ask the uncle to go lighter on the oil. Not every hawker will do it, but the ones who care will.
Skip the extra oyster sauce drizzle some places add on top. That adds calories and a lot of sodium on top of the ikan masin.
Eat it with steamed chicken or plain tofu instead of a heavy gravy dish. Kailan ikan masin pairs well with simple proteins that don't add more oil.
If you're cooking at home, use 1 teaspoon of oil in a non-stick pan instead of the full wok fry. You can cut the oil calories from 110 down to around 40.

faq.q: How many calories in Kailan Ikan Masin?
faq.a: About 200 calories per hawker plate (150g). The kailan itself is very low calorie, but the wok oil and salted fish push the total up.

faq.q: Is kailan ikan masin good for weight loss?
faq.a: It can be, yes. Kailan is one of the better veg dishes you can order because the base ingredient is so low in calories. The issue is oil. If you eat a smaller portion or ask the uncle to go easy on the oil, you can get a decent plate of greens under 180 calories with a solid 8-9g of protein from the ikan masin.

faq.q: Why is a vegetable dish 200 calories?
faq.a: Because it's a wok stir-fry. The kailan itself is only about 40 calories. It's the absorbed cooking oil that adds 110 calories all by itself. This is true of almost every Chinese stir-fried veg at a hawker. The veg is not the problem. The wok and the oil are.

foods.name: Sawi / Broccoli Sos Tiram
foods.metaDescription: Sawi or broccoli in oyster sauce is about 100 calories a plate at the kopitiam. Here's what's actually in it and how to keep it light.
foods.summary: Blanched sawi (mustard greens) with oyster sauce and a garlic oil drizzle, one of the lightest sides you can order at any kopitiam or Chinese stall. Broccoli sos tiram is a different dish but similar in preparation and calorie range, so the numbers here apply to both as a rough guide.
foods.answer: One plate of sawi sos tiram from your average kopitiam comes in at around 100 calories for a 180g serving. Quick note: at a Malaysian kopitiam, sawi sos tiram means mustard greens in oyster sauce. Broccoli sos tiram is a separate dish, though the preparation is similar and the calorie count lands in roughly the same range. The estimate here is based on sawi. The vegetable itself is basically free calories at 42 kcal for 150g cooked; it's the oil (about 40 kcal from 9g) doing most of the work. So yes, this is one of the safest sides you can order when you're watching your intake.
realTalk: Honestly, 100 calories for a full plate of vegetables is pretty hard to beat. This is blanched sawi, so the veg itself only contributes about 42 kcal. The oyster sauce adds another 13 kcal, and the garlic oil drizzle is where the biggest chunk comes from, around 40 kcal from just 9g of oil. Total is ballpark 100 kcal, but I want to be upfront: solid nutrition data for this dish specifically is thin on the ground, so treat this as a reasonable estimate rather than a lab reading. That said, even if you're off by 20 to 30 calories either way, this is still one of the lightest sides on the menu. If you're the kind of person who used to skip vegetables to save room for more rice (yes, I was that person at 128kg), this is worth rethinking. Broccoli sos tiram ordered at the same stall will be very similar in calories, though broccoli is slightly denser so a 180g plate may land a little higher, closer to 110 kcal.

What actually changes the maths is almost always the oil. A stall that goes light on the garlic oil can drop the whole plate to around 50 calories. A stall that wok-fries instead of blanches, or is generous with the drizzle, can push it to 140 kcal or more. The sauce itself is not the villain here, 25g of oyster sauce is only 13 kcal. So if you want to order this guilt-free every single day, ask for less oil lah. Portion-wise, 180g is a standard plate. If you pile on a bigger serving, scale accordingly but even 300g of this side is still under 170 calories, which is basically nothing compared to what it does for keeping you full alongside your rice.
lighter: Ask the stall to go easy on the garlic oil, that single step can cut roughly 40 calories off the plate.
Choose a stall that blanches rather than stir-fries. Wok-fried versions absorb more oil during cooking and can hit 140 calories.
Skip asking for extra sauce. The oyster sauce is low calorie on its own but extra drizzles of garlic oil often come with it.
Order a bigger portion if you are still hungry. More vegetable volume for minimal extra calories is the whole point of a side like this.
Pair it with plain steamed chicken or fish instead of a heavier lauk. You stay full and the whole meal stays manageable.

variants.note: Home-style or health-conscious stall; very little oil, thin sauce

variants.name: Standard hawker (garlic oil drizzle)
variants.note: Typical kopitiam or Chinese stall preparation with garlic oil

variants.name: Stir-fried with extra oil
variants.note: Wok-fried rather than blanched; more oil absorbed during cooking

faq.q: How many calories in Sawi / Broccoli Sos Tiram?
faq.a: A standard hawker or kopitiam plate of sawi sos tiram is around 100 calories for 180g. That assumes a normal garlic oil drizzle and oyster sauce. Broccoli sos tiram is a slightly different dish but lands in a similar range, maybe 100 to 110 kcal. Ask for less oil and you can drop either version to around 50 calories.

faq.q: Is Sawi Sos Tiram good for weight loss?
faq.a: Bro, it's one of the best sides you can order. 100 calories for a full plate of vegetables, decent fibre, and it actually tastes good with rice. The only thing to watch is how much oil the stall uses.

faq.q: How does sawi compare to kangkung belacan for calories?
faq.a: Sawi sos tiram at around 100 kcal tends to be slightly lighter than kangkung belacan, which runs higher due to the sambal and oil used in stir-frying. Both are solid choices but if you want the absolute lowest calories, blanched sawi with light sauce wins.

foods.name: Taugeh Ikan Masin
foods.metaDescription: Taugeh Ikan Masin is about 290 calories per plate. Beansprouts are nearly free but the stir fry oil adds up fast. Here's the honest breakdown.
foods.summary: Beansprouts stir fried with salted fish and a generous amount of oil, a common side dish at Chinese kopitiams and hawker stalls.
foods.answer: Taugeh Ikan Masin comes in at around 290 calories per plate (roughly 210g). The beansprouts themselves are practically nothing, only 60 calories for a full 200g. What bumps the number up is the stir fry oil, which adds about 160 calories on its own, and the salted fish another 40. So yeah, this is one of those dishes that sounds healthy but the wok does most of the damage.
realTalk: So here's the thing about taugeh ikan masin. It looks like a virtuous vegetable dish, beansprouts kan, how bad can it be? And to be fair, 200g of beansprouts genuinely is only 60 calories. The problem is that nobody stir fries taugeh with love and a dry wok. The oil is where 160 of those 290 calories come from, more than half the plate. Add 20g of ikan masin for another 40 calories and you have a side dish that costs more than most people expect. To be straight with you though, this is a ballpark estimate. Hard calorie data for Malaysian hawker cooking is thin, and how much oil lands in your plate varies a lot depending on who's behind the wok that day.

What actually changes the maths is the oil, full stop. A home cook being careful might use 10ml instead of 20ml and save 80 calories. A hawker stall that keeps the wok blazing hot and pours generously could easily hit 350 calories for the same plate. The salted fish quantity also matters. Some versions are barely there, some have a proper pile of ikan masin and more than double that 40 calorie figure. The tofu variant adds about 30 calories and bumps it to 320. For a side dish this is still pretty reasonable bah, especially compared to something like kangkung belacan which often has a similar oil situation. Just don't fool yourself into thinking beansprouts equals diet food automatically.
lighter: Ask the cook to go easy on the oil. The 20ml used in a standard plate adds 160 calories on its own. Less oil is the single biggest lever here.
Eat it as a side with plain rice or congee rather than nasi lemak or fried rice, so the overall meal stays in check.
If you're ordering at a kopitiam, share it between two people as a side dish. A half portion is only around 145 calories and still feels satisfying.
Skip the tofu add-on if you're watching calories closely. The tofu variant bumps it to 320 calories.
Pair it with a protein source like steamed chicken or poached egg rather than deep fried items, so the full meal stays reasonable.

variants.name: With tofu (tauhu)
variants.note: Common hawker variant adds 1-2 pieces firm tofu, adds ~30kcal and extra protein

variants.name: With chives (daun kucai)
variants.note: Adds daun kucai (Chinese chives), negligible calorie difference but common pairing

faq.q: How many calories in Taugeh Ikan Masin?
faq.a: One plate of taugeh ikan masin (about 210g) is around 290 calories. The beansprouts are almost free at 60 calories, but the stir fry oil adds roughly 160 calories and the salted fish another 40.

faq.q: Is taugeh ikan masin a healthy choice when dieting?
faq.a: It depends on how it's cooked. The beansprouts are genuinely low calorie and high in water content. The problem is the cooking oil, which can push a small side dish close to 300 calories. Order it at a kopitiam where they go heavy on the oil and it can easily hit 350 or more.

faq.q: Does taugeh ikan masin have a lot of sodium?
faq.a: Yes, quite a lot. The ikan masin (salted fish) is the main culprit. Even 20g of salted fish carries a significant sodium hit. If you have blood pressure issues this is worth watching, but for general dieting it's the calories from oil you should track more than the salt.

foods.name: Tauhu Sumbat
foods.metaDescription: Tauhu Sumbat is 230 calories for 4 pieces. Fried tofu stuffed with cucumber and beansprouts. Lighter than most hawker snacks, but the oil in tau pok adds up.
foods.summary: Fried tofu puffs stuffed with crunchy cucumber and beansprouts, served with sweet chilli sauce, a classic Malaysian hawker snack that's lighter than it looks.
foods.answer: Tauhu Sumbat comes in at 230 calories for 4 pieces (about 170g), which makes it one of the lighter snacks you'll find at a hawker stall. The bulk of those calories come from the fried tofu puffs themselves at 165 calories, with sweet chilli sauce adding another 45. The cucumber and beansprouts filling is basically free at just 20 calories. Honestly not bad for something that actually fills you up a bit.
realTalk: 230 calories for 4 pieces of Tauhu Sumbat is honestly pretty decent. For a hawker snack, that's on the lighter side. The filling itself, cucumber and beansprouts, is basically zero calories, so you're not getting cheated there. The calories are coming from the tau pok (fried tofu puffs), which soak up oil during frying. 165 calories from just the tofu alone. That's worth knowing. The sweet chilli sauce adds 45 more, which is fine, but if your uncle at the stall goes heavy-handed with it, that number creeps up. Fair warning though, these numbers are a ballpark estimate because hard data on homemade hawker Tauhu Sumbat is thin. Different stalls fry their tau pok differently, some soak in a lot more oil than others, so treat 230 as a reasonable middle-ground figure, not a lab result.

What actually moves the maths here is the sauce choice. Swap sweet chilli for peanut sauce and you're jumping to about 290 calories, that extra 60 calories from peanut sauce adds up if you're having this as a side to a full meal. The tofu itself isn't going anywhere calorie-wise unless you eat fewer pieces, but if you're at a stall where they're selling yong tau foo style, you can mix in more filling-heavy pieces to stretch the volume. Protein is 12g for 4 pieces which is reasonable given the tofu. If you want more protein overall, just add a plain hard-boiled egg on the side instead, cheaper and more protein for fewer calories than a second serving of tau pok. For a snack that feels substantial and hits 230 calories with 12g protein, this is actually one of the smarter things you can grab at a hawker stall.
lighter: Ask for sauce on the side and dip lightly instead of having it drizzled all over. That alone can save you 20 to 30 calories.
Choose sweet chilli over peanut sauce. Peanut sauce adds about 60 extra calories per serving.
If the stall offers a baked or steamed tofu option, take it. Most don't, but worth asking.
Eat it as a main snack on its own rather than a side to rice. 230 calories works better as a standalone than stacked on top of a full nasi plate.
Stop at 4 pieces. Easy to mindlessly grab 6 or 8 when chatting at the stall, and that takes you to 345 to 460 calories without realising.

variants.name: With sweet chilli sauce only
variants.note: Standard hawker version with cucumber, beansprouts, sweet chilli

variants.name: With peanut sauce
variants.note: Peanut sauce adds ~60 cal per 2-tbsp serving vs sweet chilli

faq.q: How many calories in Tauhu Sumbat?
faq.a: 4 pieces of Tauhu Sumbat (about 170g with sweet chilli sauce) has 230 calories. The fried tau pok accounts for most of it at 165 calories, with the sweet chilli sauce adding 45. The vegetable filling is basically negligible at 20 calories.

faq.q: Is Tauhu Sumbat healthy for weight loss?
faq.a: It's one of the better hawker snacks if you're watching calories. 230 calories with 12g protein for a filling snack is a reasonable deal. The main thing working against it is the oil in the fried tofu. Stick to sweet chilli sauce over peanut sauce and keep it to 4 pieces and it fits fine into a calorie deficit.

faq.q: What is the difference between Tauhu Sumbat and Yong Tau Foo?
faq.a: Similar concept but different execution. Yong Tau Foo typically uses fish paste as the stuffing and is served in soup or with various sauces. Tauhu Sumbat is specifically fried tofu puffs stuffed with fresh raw vegetables like cucumber and beansprouts, served cold or room temp with sweet chilli or peanut sauce. Tauhu Sumbat is the snack version you find pre-made at hawker stalls.

foods.name: Ulam-Ulaman
foods.metaDescription: Ulam-ulaman with sambal belacan is only about 60 calories per plate. Raw herbs, petai, long beans, basically free calories. Here's the full breakdown.
foods.summary: A traditional raw herb and vegetable platter served with sambal belacan, one of the lowest-calorie things you will find at any nasi campur stall.
foods.answer: One plate of ulam-ulaman with sambal belacan is about 60 calories for a 160g serving. That covers a mix of raw herbs and leaves, some long beans and cucumber, a few pods of petai, and a couple tablespoons of sambal belacan as the dip. Without the petai it drops to around 40 calories. With a richer tempoyak dip instead of sambal, you are looking at around 80. Either way, this is one of the lowest-calorie things you can put on your plate at a warung or nasi campur stall.
realTalk: Sixty calories for a whole plate of food, bro. That is basically free. The raw herbs and leaves, the cucumber, the long beans, even the sambal belacan dip, none of it adds up to much. The petai contributes about 19 calories for a few pods, and the sambal belacan another 19, so those two together are actually the biggest calorie contributors on the entire plate. Everything else is just leaves and water. If you are trying to eat big volume on a deficit, ulam-ulaman is exactly the kind of side dish you want to load up on. It fills the plate, it takes time to chew, and it costs you almost nothing calorie-wise. To be honest though, these numbers are a ballpark estimate since there is not much hard nutrition data for traditional Malaysian ulam spreads, but the range is going to be in this territory.

What actually changes the maths here is the dip. Sambal belacan at 2 tablespoons is already 19 calories, but if you start doubling up or swap it for tempoyak, the plate climbs from 60 to 80 or beyond. The herbs themselves are so low in calories that portion size barely matters. Skip the petai and you are at 40 calories. The ulam leaves and long beans are genuinely close to zero. Where people accidentally turn this into a higher-calorie dish is by pairing it with a rich gravy side or by getting a plate that has been sitting next to oily dishes at the nasi campur counter, where a little of that cooking oil transfers over. As a standalone side with plain sambal belacan, this is one of the smartest things to put on your plate.
lighter: Keep the dip to 2 tablespoons of sambal belacan and skip requests for extra. That dip is doing almost a third of the calories here.
Skip the tempoyak option. Fermented durian tastes amazing but adds more calories than plain sambal for a much smaller dip portion.
Load up on the plain herb leaves and cucumber. They are so close to zero calories that eating twice as much changes almost nothing.
Skip the petai if you are really cutting hard. Saves you about 19 calories, which is small but it adds up if you are being precise.
Pair it with a lean protein like steamed fish or grilled chicken instead of a rich santan-based lauk, so the whole plate stays light.

faq.q: How many calories in Ulam-Ulaman?
faq.a: A standard plate of ulam-ulaman with sambal belacan is around 60 calories for about 160g. Without petai it is closer to 40 calories, and with a tempoyak dip it goes up to about 80. These are estimates since detailed nutrition data for traditional ulam spreads is thin, but the numbers are in this range.

faq.q: Is ulam-ulaman good for weight loss?
faq.a: It is honestly one of the best side dishes you can pick if you are watching calories. Sixty calories for a full plate of food is almost nothing. The raw herbs and vegetables are very low in calorie density, so you get actual volume and something to chew on without spending much of your daily calorie budget. The main thing to watch is the dip, since richer dips like tempoyak add more calories than plain sambal belacan.

faq.q: Why does ulam-ulaman smell after you eat it?
faq.a: That is the petai lah. Stink beans contain sulphur compounds similar to asparagus, and your body breaks them down in a way that carries through to your urine and sweat. It passes within a day. Totally harmless, just a bit antisocial.

foods.name: Cucur Udang
foods.metaDescription: One cucur udang from a hawker stall is 145 calories. Most of it is batter and frying oil, not the prawns. Here's what you need to know before you eat five.
foods.summary: A deep-fried prawn and vegetable fritter that's a staple at pasar malam and morning markets, cheap as anything but sneakier calorie-wise than it looks.
foods.answer: One piece of cucur udang from a hawker stall is around 145 calories. That's for a 55g fritter, so we're talking about the standard size you grab from a pasar malam or morning market stall. The bulk of those calories come from the flour batter (75 cal) and the oil absorbed during frying (50 cal), not from the prawns or vegetables. The prawn and veg bits barely add up to 20 calories between them. It's a snack, not a meal, but at 145 cal per piece it adds up faster than you'd think if you're standing there eating four in a row.
realTalk: Okay so 145 calories per piece sounds manageable, right? And it is, if you actually stop at one or two. The problem is nobody stops at one or two. These things are cheap, they come out hot and crispy, and you're standing at the stall chatting while the auntie fries them. Before you know it you've eaten five pieces and that's 725 calories for what is basically a snack. The calorie driver here is not the prawns (only 10 cal worth of prawn in each one) and definitely not the bean sprouts. It's the flour batter at 75 calories and the oil absorbed during frying at 50 calories. Batter plus oil is 125 calories before the actual filling even shows up.

What changes the maths is pretty simple: how many you eat and whether you dip. If you eat two pieces, you're at 290 calories, which is fine as a snack. Eat four and you're at 580, which is basically a full meal's worth for something that won't even fill you up properly. The dipping sauce they serve with it (sweet chilli, usually) adds maybe 20 to 30 calories per tablespoon so it's not the main issue. The bigger thing is the prawn-to-batter ratio at different stalls. Some stalls use a lot of batter and very little filling, some stuff it properly. More batter means more calories, and you honestly can't tell until you bite in. If you're tracking, 145 per piece is a safe estimate for a standard hawker piece, but at a stingy stall it could creep higher.
lighter: Stop at two pieces. Seriously. Two pieces is 290 calories and actually works as a light snack. It's the eating six while you wait for your other food that kills you.
Skip the dipping sauce or use just a small amount. The sweet chilli isn't the main calorie problem but it adds up if you're generous with it.
If you're buying from a stall, pick the ones with visible prawns and vegetables in the batter. More filling, less batter, slightly fewer calories per bite.
Eat it as the snack it's supposed to be, not as part of a bigger spread. If you've already got nasi lemak or mee goreng, skip the cucur udang that day.
Drink plain water with it instead of a sugary drink. The snack itself is manageable; it's the teh tarik sitting next to it that pushes your total over.

faq.q: How many calories in Cucur Udang?
faq.a: One standard cucur udang from a hawker stall is 145 calories per piece (about 55g). The main calorie contributors are the flour batter (75 cal) and absorbed frying oil (50 cal). The prawns and vegetables together only account for about 20 calories.

faq.q: Is cucur udang healthy?
faq.a: It's a deep-fried snack so it's not exactly a health food, but it's also not the worst thing you can eat. At 145 calories per piece with 5g of protein, it's decent if you keep it to one or two pieces. The issue is it's very easy to eat four or five without realising, and then you've had a 600-plus calorie snack that doesn't even fill you up for long.

faq.q: How does cucur udang compare to pisang goreng in calories?
faq.a: They're in a similar range. Both are batter-fried hawker snacks where most of the calories come from flour and absorbed oil rather than the filling. Cucur udang at 145 calories per piece is comparable to pisang goreng, though the exact number depends on size and how much oil the batter soaks up at each stall.

foods.name: Cucur Badak
foods.metaDescription: Cucur Badak is about 140 calories per piece. Here's what's actually inside that sweet potato fritter and how the numbers add up at the hawker stall.
foods.summary: A deep-fried sweet potato fritter stuffed with spiced grated coconut and dried shrimp, a classic Malaysian kuih found at pasar malam and hawker stalls.
foods.answer: One piece of Cucur Badak (medium, hawker-stall size, about 55g) comes in at 140 calories. That number breaks down as 3g protein, 20g carbs, and 5g fat. The bulk of the calories come from the sweet potato dough and the spiced coconut filling, with the absorbed frying oil quietly adding another 19 calories you probably never think about.
realTalk: One Cucur Badak sits at around 140 calories, which sounds reasonable until you realise the absorbed frying oil alone is 19 of those calories and most people eat two or three pieces without thinking. The sweet potato dough is the biggest chunk at 77 calories for 30g, and the spiced coconut filling adds another 35. To be honest, hard calorie data for this dish is pretty thin out there, so treat this as a solid ballpark estimate rather than a lab-certified number. The protein is only 3g, so it is not going to keep you full for long. If you are trying to lose weight, Cucur Badak is fine as an occasional snack, but it is basically a refined carb and fat bomb dressed up as a traditional kuih.

What actually moves the number up or down is how much oil the dough absorbed during frying and how generous the filling is. A stingy filling piece might be closer to 120 calories. A big fat one, freshly fried and sitting in a pool of oil, can easily hit 160. At pasar malam, where the pieces tend to be larger, you could be looking at 180 calories per piece without even knowing it. The protein is too low to count for satiety, so if you are trying to eat smart, pair it with something that has actual protein rather than grabbing four pieces lah and calling it a balanced snack.
lighter: Eat one, not three. At 140 calories a piece, the damage is the quantity, not the dish itself.
If you are buying from a stall, pick pieces that were fried recently and are not sitting in oil. Older pieces that have been reheated tend to be greasier.
Eat it as a snack on its own, not alongside nasi lemak or roti canai. It is 140 calories of carbs, so stack it with other carbs and the total adds up fast.
If you make it at home, use an air fryer. You can cut the absorbed oil contribution down significantly.
Drink plain water or teh-o ais kosong alongside, not a sugared drink. That one swap saves you 100-plus calories every time.

faq.q: How many calories in Cucur Badak?
faq.a: One medium piece from a hawker stall is about 140 calories. That covers roughly 55g of food: sweet potato dough, spiced coconut and dried shrimp filling, and some absorbed frying oil.

faq.q: Is Cucur Badak fattening?
faq.a: 140 calories per piece is not outrageous on its own. The problem is that nobody eats just one. Three pieces is already 420 calories as a snack, before you even think about your main meal. If you keep it to one or two, it fits fine.

faq.q: Why is there coconut in the filling and how much does it add?
faq.a: The classic filling is spiced grated coconut mixed with dried shrimp. That 10g of coconut filling alone contributes around 35 calories, mostly from fat. It is what makes Cucur Badak taste different from a plain sweet potato fritter.

foods.name: Lok Lok
foods.serving: 1 stick (average mixed item with sauce dip)
foods.metaDescription: One lok lok stick averages about 70 calories, but it adds up fast. Here's what actually matters for your calorie count at the lok lok stall.
foods.summary: Lok lok is the ultimate Malaysian street snack: skewers of fish balls, sausages, tofu, and veg boiled in a big pot and dunked in sauce, sold for a few ringgit per stick.
foods.answer: One average lok lok stick comes in at around 70 calories, based on a typical mixed item (fish ball, fish cake, sausage, or tofu puff) with a dip of peanut or chili sauce. That 70 cal figure covers roughly 27g of boiled skewered food plus about 11g of sauce. The range across stick types is wide though: a plain veggie stick is as low as 15 calories, while a deep-fried sausage stick with peanut sauce can hit 130 calories. So "how many calories is lok lok" really depends on what you pick and how generous you are with the sauce.
realTalk: Fair warning upfront: the calorie numbers here are ballpark estimates. Hard nutrition data for hawker lok lok basically does not exist, so treat the 70 cal per stick figure as a reasonable average, not a precise lab result. With that said, lok lok is genuinely one of the more manageable late-night snacks out there IF you pick sensibly. A boiled fish ball stick with light chili sauce is around 45 calories. Two of those and you have had a real snack for under 100 cal. The problem is that nobody stops at two sticks, kan. You get chatting, you keep pulling sticks out of the pot, and suddenly you have eaten 15 sticks and wonder why you are hungry again. The sauce is also sneaky: that 11g dip adds 22 calories per stick, and if you are ladling peanut sauce generously, that number goes up fast.

The thing that really changes the maths is the item type and whether it gets fried. A plain mushroom or leafy veg stick with no sauce is basically 15 calories. A sausage or squid ball stick with peanut sauce is 95. Deep-fried lok lok, which some stalls offer, can hit 130 per stick because the oil soaks right into the coating. So the same stall, same price per stick, can give you wildly different calorie totals depending on what you grab. If you are trying to keep it reasonable, load up on the fish balls, crab sticks, tofu, and veg sticks, go easy on the sausage and anything fried, and be stingy with the peanut sauce. It sounds obvious but most people just grab whatever looks good without thinking about it.
lighter: Stick to boiled items only and skip the fried option entirely. That single swap can save you 35 to 60 calories per stick.
Prioritise fish ball, crab stick, tofu, and veggie skewers over sausage and processed meat balls. You get more volume for fewer calories.
Use chili sauce instead of peanut sauce. Chili sauce is mostly chili and vinegar while peanut sauce has added fat and sugar.
Set a stick limit before you start, maybe 8 to 10 sticks, and stick to it. The danger with lok lok is that there is no natural stopping point.
Ask for the sauce on the side and dip lightly rather than dunking the whole stick in. You will use half as much sauce without even noticing.

faq.q: How many calories in Lok Lok?
faq.a: One average lok lok stick with sauce dip is around 70 calories. The range runs from about 15 calories for a plain veggie stick with no sauce all the way up to 130 calories for a deep-fried sausage stick with peanut sauce.

faq.q: Is lok lok okay to eat when you are trying to lose weight?
faq.a: It can be, bro. The boiled fish ball and veggie sticks are genuinely low calorie, around 15 to 45 calories each. The issue is portion control because it is too easy to lose count. Set a limit before you start, pick the lighter items, and go easy on the peanut sauce.

faq.q: Which lok lok dipping sauce has the least calories?
faq.a: Chili sauce is the lighter option compared to peanut sauce. Peanut sauce has added fat and sugar, which bumps the calorie count noticeably. Sweet dark sauce is somewhere in the middle. If you are counting, use chili sauce and dip lightly rather than coating the whole stick.

foods.name: Yong Tau Foo (Fried)
foods.metaDescription: Fried Yong Tau Foo is about 90 calories per piece. Sounds fine until you eat 8 pieces. Here's what actually drives the numbers and how to eat it smarter.
foods.summary: Deep-fried stuffed tofu and beancurd skin filled with fish paste, oilier than the soup version and dangerously easy to overeat one piece at a time.
foods.answer: One piece of fried Yong Tau Foo (stuffed tofu or beancurd skin) comes in at around 90 calories per piece. At 45g a piece, that sounds pretty reasonable until you realise nobody ever eats just one. A typical plate of six pieces sits around 540 calories, and that's before any gravy or dipping sauce. The calories here are split between the tofu wrapper (55 cal), the fish paste filling (15 cal), and the oil absorbed during frying (20 cal per piece). So yeah, frying is doing most of the heavy lifting on the calorie front.
realTalk: So here's the thing about fried YTF. Each piece is 90 calories, which on paper sounds very manageable. The problem is portion control is basically non-existent when you're standing at the stall pointing at stuff. Six pieces is 540 cal. Eight pieces with curry gravy is pushing 700 cal. The oil absorption is real, about 20 cal per piece just from frying, and that's a ballpark estimate because honest nutrition data for hawker YTF is basically nonexistent. Take these numbers as a reasonable guide, not gospel. The fish paste filling itself is actually decent protein at 6g per piece, so the macros aren't terrible. It's just that the frying packs in fat that the soup version doesn't have.

The soup version of the same piece is 60 cal versus 90 cal fried, so switching to the boiled version across a 6-piece serving saves you about 180 calories. That's not nothing, bro. A typical soup bowl with 5 pieces is around 300 cal, and if you stretch it to 8 pieces that's 480 cal, so the count really depends on how many you grab. If you're counting, skipping the curry gravy or sweet chilli sauce also saves 15 to 25 cal per piece. Order 6 pieces soup version with no sauce and you're at around 360 cal for a fairly filling plate with decent protein. Add a dipping sauce and go fried and suddenly you're at 600 plus. The maths changes fast. The actual piece count is where most people lose track, so count before you eat, not after.
lighter: Go soup version instead of fried. Same fish paste, same tofu, 30 cal less per piece. On 6 pieces that's 180 cal saved.
Skip or limit the dipping sauce. Curry gravy and sweet chilli add 15 to 25 cal per piece, which adds up across a full plate.
Count your pieces before you start eating. It is very easy to grab 10 pieces without noticing. Set a limit of 6 and stick to it.
Pick pieces with more fish paste filling relative to wrapper. More protein, more filling, less fried dough surface area to absorb oil.
Pair with a clear soup or plain vegetables to bulk up the meal so you feel full on fewer fried pieces.

variants.note: Same stuffed tofu or beancurd skin, poached in broth instead of deep fried; about one-third less fat. A 5-piece soup bowl is around 300 cal, an 8-piece bowl around 480 cal.

faq.q: How many calories in Yong Tau Foo (Fried)?
faq.a: One piece of fried Yong Tau Foo is approximately 90 calories. A typical 6-piece serving comes to around 540 calories before any sauces or gravy.

faq.q: Is fried Yong Tau Foo fattening?
faq.a: It depends on how many pieces you eat. Per piece the numbers are fine, but most people grab 8 to 10 pieces without thinking. At 90 cal a piece plus dipping sauce, a big plate adds up fast. The soup version at 60 cal per piece is meaningfully lighter if you're watching your intake.

faq.q: How much protein does Yong Tau Foo have?
faq.a: Each piece has about 6g of protein from the fish paste filling. A 6-piece serving gives you roughly 36g of protein, which is actually a decent amount. The issue is the oil from frying also pushes the fat content up, so soup version gives you similar protein for fewer calories.

foods.name: Kuih Bangkit
foods.metaDescription: Kuih Bangkit is about 40 calories per piece, but nobody stops at one. Here's the real calorie count and why these tiny cookies can quietly wreck your deficit.
foods.summary: A melt-in-mouth tapioca coconut cookie that's mostly eaten during Raya, small enough to feel harmless but easy to overeat by the dozen.
foods.answer: One piece of Kuih Bangkit is about 40 calories. It's a tiny 10g cookie, so on the surface it sounds harmless. But the catch is nobody eats one. You sit down during Raya, somebody shoves a tin in front of you, and before you realize it you've had 10 pieces and quietly eaten 400 calories of something that basically dissolved the moment it hit your tongue.
realTalk: Forty calories per piece sounds like nothing, right? The problem is Kuih Bangkit is engineered to be unfillable. It's 10 grams of tapioca flour, icing sugar, and coconut cream that literally melts before you finish chewing. There's no texture, no chew, no real sense of having eaten anything. Most people comfortably clear 8 to 12 pieces without blinking, and that's 320 to 480 calories gone during a Raya visit before you even get to the real food. Just to be upfront, these numbers are a ballpark estimate since there's no solid lab data on homemade kuih, and every household recipe is a bit different. But the rough range of 35 to 45 calories per piece is a fair working figure.

What moves the number most is the ratio of sugar and coconut cream in the recipe. Some older grandma recipes are heavier on the coconut, which bumps the fat up slightly. The cookie itself has almost zero protein, so it does nothing for satiety. If you're tracking, count about 40 calories per piece and be honest about how many you actually ate. The tin that lives on the coffee table during open house is basically a calorie trap, not because any one piece is bad, but because the portion is whatever you happen to grab without thinking. At a Raya spread lah, the trick is to take a few, move away from the tin, and fill your plate with actual food first.
lighter: Count them out before you start eating. Physically put 3 or 4 pieces on a small plate and walk away from the tin. You will not self-regulate from an open container.
Drink a big glass of water alongside. The cookies are so dry they disappear instantly, and water helps you actually feel like you consumed something.
Eat it after a proper meal, not as a standalone snack. If your stomach already has real food in it, you'll naturally stop after 2 or 3 pieces.
If you're baking your own batch, reduce the icing sugar by 20 to 30 percent. You lose maybe 2 to 3 calories per piece and most people honestly can't taste the difference.
Treat it like a dessert, not a snack. One or two pieces after lunch is fine. Half a tin while watching TV is not the move.

faq.q: How many calories in Kuih Bangkit?
faq.a: One piece of Kuih Bangkit is around 40 calories. At 10g per piece it sounds fine until you eat 8 to 10 pieces in one sitting, which puts you at 320 to 400 calories from what feels like literally nothing.

faq.q: Is Kuih Bangkit fattening?
faq.a: It depends entirely on how many you eat. The calorie per gram ratio is actually pretty high since it's mostly tapioca flour, icing sugar, and coconut cream. The problem is the melt-in-mouth texture tricks your brain into thinking you haven't eaten anything, so you just keep going.

faq.q: How does Kuih Bangkit compare to other Raya kuih?
faq.a: Kuih Bangkit is on the lighter end compared to richer kuih, but it's not low-calorie by any stretch. A piece of Kuih Lapis or Kuih Seri Muka can run 50 to 80 calories per piece depending on the recipe, so Bangkit at 40 calories is not the worst offender. Still, the small size makes it easy to massively overeat.

foods.name: Kuih Badak Berendam
foods.metaDescription: Kuih Badak Berendam is 100 calories per ball including the santan. Here is what is actually driving those numbers and how easy it is to overeat this one.
foods.summary: A soft glutinous rice ball stuffed with gula melaka and coconut, sitting in a pool of warm coconut milk santan.
foods.answer: Each piece of Kuih Badak Berendam comes in at 100 calories per ball (about 45g including the santan). That is not a lot on paper, but the calories stack fast because nobody eats just one. The glutinous dough accounts for 47 of those calories, the gula melaka and coconut filling adds 30, and the santan gravy sitting underneath contributes the last 23. So roughly 40% of the damage is from the sweet coconut sauce, which you are definitely spooning up.
realTalk: Kuih Badak Berendam is 100 calories a ball, which sounds harmless until you realise you just had four of them without thinking. The glutinous rice dough is dense with carbs (47 calories in just 20g of cooked dough), the gula melaka and coconut filling adds another 30 calories of pure sugar and fat, and then there is the santan pooled at the bottom that you are going to spoon up anyway. It is the kind of kuih that feels light because it is small, but the calorie density is actually pretty high for its size. If you are a regular kuih snacker, this is worth knowing about.

What changes the numbers most is the santan. A thin, diluted coconut milk sauce puts you at 80 calories per piece. A thick, festival-grade coconut cream version pushes you to 130. That is a 60% swing from the same basic kuih, just from how the gravy was made. The filling matters too: more gula melaka means more calories, obviously, but the coconut in the filling also carries fat. Nobody is saying avoid this lah, it is a genuinely good kuih. But if you are tracking, count the santan separately because that is where the invisible calories live.
lighter: Take just one ball and skip the extra santan poured on top. The sauce alone can add 20 to 30 calories per extra ladle.
Ask for thin or diluted santan if you are buying from a stall. Some aunties use coconut cream; the diluted version drops you closer to 80 calories per piece.
Stop at two pieces. Seriously, set the limit before you start eating, not after. Three pieces is already 300 calories from something that felt like a small bite.
Pair it with plain water or teh o kosong, not teh tarik. You do not need extra sugar calories alongside a sweet kuih.
If you are making it at home, reduce the gula melaka filling by a third and use light coconut milk for the santan. You will still get the flavour but save 15 to 20 calories per piece.

faq.q: How many calories in Kuih Badak Berendam?
faq.a: One piece is 100 calories for a 45g serving, which includes the glutinous ball, gula melaka filling, and the coconut milk santan. Eat three and you are at 300 calories from a snack that takes about 90 seconds to finish.

faq.q: Is Kuih Badak Berendam fattening?
faq.a: Not if you stick to one or two pieces. The problem is the santan gravy: thick coconut milk is calorie-dense and it is very easy to slurp up extra without realising. The balls themselves are not huge, but the sauce is where the calories quietly add up.

faq.q: Can I eat kuih like this and still lose weight?
faq.a: Yes, but portion control is real. Two pieces is 200 calories, which is totally manageable if you count it into your day. The issue is kuih are small and sweet, so your brain does not register them as a proper snack. Track them the same way you would track anything else.

foods.name: Kuih Kasturi
foods.metaDescription: Kuih Kasturi is 110 calories per piece. Here's where those calories actually come from and how easy it is to eat three without noticing.
foods.summary: A fried glutinous rice ball stuffed with sweetened grated coconut and rolled in sesame seeds, sold at pasar malam stalls across Malaysia.
foods.answer: One piece of Kuih Kasturi (about 45g) comes in at 110 calories. The glutinous rice shell is the main contributor at 50 calories, the sweet coconut filling adds 20, and the sesame coating brings another 25. The frying oil soaks up the remaining 15 calories. For a small kuih you can knock back in two bites, 110 calories is not terrible, but they are easy to stack up fast.
realTalk: Honestly, 110 calories for one piece is pretty reasonable. The problem with Kuih Kasturi is not the calorie count per piece, it is the fact that nobody eats just one piece. The sesame-coated shell is chewy, the coconut filling is warm and sweet, and before you know it you have cleared five pieces at a pasar malam and spent 550 calories on snacks before dinner even started. The calories here come mostly from the glutinous rice dough (50 calories) and the fried sesame coating (25 calories), with oil absorption adding another 15. Worth flagging upfront: hard nutrition data for traditional kuih like this is basically nonexistent, so these are ballpark estimates based on ingredients and cooking method. Treat the numbers as a reasonable guide, not a lab result.

What actually changes the maths is how many you eat and how much oil the kuih soaks up during frying. A well-fried batch at the right temperature absorbs less oil than a greasy, soggy one. At three pieces you are already at 330 calories for 135g of food that will not keep you full for long. If you are tracking calories, the safest move is to log one to two pieces and leave it there lah. There is no protein story here to speak of, only 2g per piece, so it does not contribute anything meaningful to satiety. Pair it with a proper meal rather than treating a bag of kuih as a meal replacement.
lighter: Eat one piece and stop. Two pieces is 220 calories, four pieces is 440, and suddenly your snack costs more than a full meal.
Go for freshly made ones over pre-packed versions. Freshly fried kuih tend to absorb less oil if the temperature is right, while reheated or badly fried ones are greasier.
Skip pairing it with teh tarik or sirap bandung. The kuih is already sweet, adding a sugary drink just doubles the hit for zero extra fullness.
If you are making it at home, reduce the sugar in the coconut filling. The coconut itself has natural sweetness and you will not miss the extra.
Treat it as a once-in-a-while kuih, not a daily snack. One piece occasionally fits any sensible calorie budget. A bag of five every afternoon does not.

faq.q: How many calories in Kuih Kasturi?
faq.a: One piece of Kuih Kasturi is around 110 calories for a 45g ball. That accounts for the glutinous rice shell, sweet grated coconut filling, sesame coating, and oil absorbed from frying.

faq.q: Is Kuih Kasturi fattening?
faq.a: A single piece at 110 calories is not going to ruin your day. The problem is portion control. At a pasar malam stall you will likely eat three or four pieces without thinking, which puts you at 330 to 440 calories from a snack. Eat one or two and move on.

faq.q: What is Kuih Kasturi made of?
faq.a: Kuih Kasturi is a fried glutinous rice ball filled with sweetened grated coconut and coated in sesame seeds. The dough is made from glutinous rice flour (tepung pulut), which gives it that chewy, stretchy texture when you bite in.

foods.name: Kuih Jala (Roti Jala)
foods.metaDescription: Kuih jala (roti jala) with chicken curry is about 240 calories for 2 pieces. Here's what actually drives those numbers and how to eat it without guilt.
foods.summary: Lacy net crepes served with chicken curry or sweet coconut kuah, a popular teatime snack and kenduri staple.
foods.answer: Two pieces of kuih jala with chicken curry comes in at around 240 calories for a 170g serving. The lacy crepes themselves are only about 100 calories for the pair, but the coconut milk curry gravy adds roughly 110 calories on top. So it is honestly a pretty reasonable snack, as long as you are not drowning the thing in extra gravy.
realTalk: Honestly, kuih jala is one of the more diet-friendly traditional kuihs out there, bro. Two pieces with curry sits at roughly 240 calories, which is not bad at all for a proper snack. The crepes themselves are thin and airy, only about 100 calories for the pair. The real calories come from the curry gravy, around 110 calories for 80g of coconut milk-based curry, and the small bits of chicken tucked in. Worth flagging: these numbers are a ballpark estimate, because detailed lab data for kuih jala specifically is basically nonexistent. We cross-referenced the crepe batter (egg, flour, coconut milk, turmeric) and standard chicken curry macros to get here. Treat it as a reasonable guide, not gospel.

What actually swings the calories is how much gravy you pour over. Go light on the curry and you are closer to 180-190 calories. Go heavy with a generous ladle, maybe add a second dip, and you are pushing past 300 easily. Switching to sweet kuah (coconut milk dipping sauce) instead of curry drops you to about 200 calories since the sweet sauce is thinner and has less fat overall. Going from 2 pieces to 3 pieces adds roughly 50 calories from the extra crepe plus a bit more gravy. If you are at a kenduri and someone piles on three pieces with a big scoop of curry, you are probably looking at 320 calories. Still not a disaster, but it adds up if you eat four rounds because the food is just sitting there.
lighter: Stick to 2 pieces and be deliberate about how much curry you ladle on. The gravy is where the calories hide.
Ask for sweet kuah instead of coconut curry if you are watching calories. Drops the serving by about 40 calories.
Use the curry as a dip rather than pouring it over. You end up using maybe half the gravy.
At kenduri or family meals, eat slowly. These crepes are filling faster than they look because the batter has egg and coconut milk.
Pair with teh o kosong or plain water instead of teh tarik. You do not want to add another 100-plus calories from a sweet drink on top.

variants.note: Lighter than curry; sweet coconut sauce has less protein, fewer calories overall

variants.note: Typical hawker serving; curry adds coconut-milk fat and chicken protein

faq.q: How many calories in Kuih Jala (Roti Jala)?
faq.a: Two pieces of kuih jala with chicken curry is approximately 240 calories for a 170g serving. The crepes themselves contribute about 100 calories, with the coconut milk curry gravy adding another 110 calories. Switching to sweet kuah instead of curry brings it down to around 200 calories.

faq.q: Is kuih jala fattening?
faq.a: Not really, especially compared to other Malaysian kuihs. Two pieces with curry is 240 calories, which is a reasonable snack. The fat content comes mainly from the coconut milk in the curry gravy. Control the gravy portion, stick to two pieces, and you are totally fine lah, just watch the gravy.

faq.q: What is the difference in calories between kuih jala with curry and with sweet kuah?
faq.a: About 40 calories. Two pieces with sweet coconut dipping sauce is around 200 calories, while two pieces with chicken curry is around 240 calories. The curry is heavier because of the coconut milk base and the protein from the chicken pieces.

foods.name: Kopi Tarik
foods.metaDescription: Kopi tarik has about 150 calories a glass, mostly from condensed milk. Here's what's actually in your morning kopitiam coffee and how to order it smarter.
foods.summary: Malaysia's classic pulled coffee, brewed from robusta beans and mixed with sweetened condensed milk and evaporated milk for that thick, caramelly kick.
foods.answer: A standard glass of kopi tarik at the kopitiam runs about 150 calories. That might not sound like much, but almost all of it is coming from roughly 40g of sweetened condensed milk, which alone clocks in at 120 calories. The coffee itself is practically nothing. So you are basically drinking dessert in a cup, just dressed up as your morning routine.
realTalk: Kopi tarik is 150 calories a glass, and before you say 'aiya that's nothing lah', just think about how many you drink in a day. One kopi tarik with breakfast, one after lunch, maybe one in the afternoon because your colleague belanja. That's 450 calories from drinks alone before you've even looked at your nasi. The calories here are almost entirely from the condensed milk. We're talking about 40g of the stuff per glass, which is 120 calories of pure sugar and fat. The evaporated milk adds another 20. The actual coffee? Ten calories. So the drink you think is 'just coffee' is mostly sweetened milk with a coffee flavour. To be fair, these numbers are ballpark estimates because there's no standardised recipe at the kopitiam. Uncle behind the counter pours by feel, and some hands are heavier than others.

The variant you order makes a massive difference. Swap to kopi O (black with sugar, no milk) and you drop to 45 calories. Kopi C, which uses evaporated milk instead of condensed, sits around 90 calories. That's a 60 to 105 calorie saving per cup just from changing how you order. If you're the type who drinks three coffees a day, switching from kopi tarik to kopi C could save you 180 calories daily without giving up your kopitiam habit. Kurang manis (less sweet) shaves off a bit more too, since the uncle uses slightly less condensed milk. None of these changes feel like dieting. You're still at the same table, same kopitiam, same uncle. Just a slightly different order.
lighter: Order kopi C instead of kopi tarik. Evaporated milk instead of condensed drops you from 150 to about 90 calories, and honestly the taste is still damn good.
Add 'kurang manis' to every order. Less condensed milk means fewer calories, and most kopitiams will do it without blinking.
Switch to kopi O on at least one of your daily coffees. Forty-five calories and you still get the caffeine hit you need.
Stop counting kopi tarik as a free item. It is not water. Three cups a day is 450 calories, which is basically a full meal.
If you like iced coffee, kopi peng has the same calories as hot kopi tarik, so there's no magic in the ice. The only win is if the extra water from ice melt makes you feel slightly fuller.

faq.q: How many calories in Kopi Tarik?
faq.a: A standard glass of kopi tarik at the kopitiam is about 150 calories. Almost all of that comes from the sweetened condensed milk, which makes up roughly 120 of those calories on its own.

faq.q: Is kopi tarik bad for weight loss?
faq.a: One cup is not going to ruin anything, but it adds up fast if you drink two or three a day. Three kopi tarik is 450 calories, which is more than some people's full meals. If you want to keep the habit without the calorie hit, switch to kopi C (about 90 cal) or kopi O (about 45 cal) for most of your daily coffees.

faq.q: What is the difference between kopi tarik and teh tarik calories?
faq.a: They are very close. Both use sweetened condensed milk as the main ingredient, so both land around 150 calories for a standard glass. The coffee versus tea base barely changes the number. If you want lower calories, the answer for both is the same: order C or O style instead.

foods.name: Sirap Bandung
foods.metaDescription: Sirap Bandung has about 190 calories per hawker glass. Mostly sugar from rose syrup. Here's what's actually in it and how to drink smarter.
foods.summary: The iconic pink drink at every mamak and kenduri: rose syrup mixed with evaporated milk over ice, sweet and creamy and deceptively calorie-dense for something that feels like just a drink.
foods.answer: Sirap Bandung comes in at 190 calories per standard hawker glass (300ml). Most of that comes from two things: rose syrup at around 90 calories and evaporated milk at around 95 calories. The ice and water make up the rest, bringing the total to roughly 190 calories for what is essentially a sweet pink drink. Not catastrophic, but definitely not free.
realTalk: 190 calories for a drink sounds okay until you realise you're ordering two of these with your nasi lemak and roti canai. The calories here come from both the rose syrup and the evaporated milk, and they contribute almost equally: about 90 calories from the syrup and 95 from the milk. Rose syrup alone is 90 calories for just 55g, which is basically cordial with red dye. Add evaporated milk at 95 calories per 100g and you've got a proper calorie bomb in a glass. The ice and water dilution save you a bit, but not enough to pretend this is a light choice. If you're counting, 190 calories for a drink is the same as a small bowl of plain rice, lah.

What actually changes the number is how heavy-handed the uncle is with the syrup and milk. Some hawkers go really generous with both, which can push this to 220 or even 250 calories easily. The soda version (Bandung Soda) swaps some of that evaporated milk for soda water or sarsi, bringing it down to around 160 calories, but the sugar stays roughly the same because the syrup doesn't change. If you're trying to cut calories without giving up the drink entirely, ask for less syrup, get the soda version, or just drink half and leave the rest. Both the syrup and the milk contribute roughly equally here, so cutting back on either one will make a real difference.
lighter: Ask the uncle to go light on the syrup. That alone can save 30 to 50 calories.
Order the soda version (Bandung Soda) instead. Around 160 calories versus 190, same drink experience.
Stop at one glass. Sounds obvious, but most people casually order a refill without thinking.
Skip the Sirap Bandung if you already have another sweet drink coming. Teh tarik plus Bandung in one meal is 400 calories just from drinks.
Drink it slow, make it last. You enjoy it more and you won't feel like you need a second one.

variants.name: Sirap Bandung Soda (with sarsi or soda water)
variants.note: Replaces some evaporated milk with soda or sarsi; less fat but similar sugar, slightly fewer calories overall

faq.q: How many calories in Sirap Bandung?
faq.a: A standard hawker glass of Sirap Bandung is about 190 calories. The main sources are rose syrup (90 cal) and evaporated milk (95 cal), with ice and water making up the rest of the 300ml glass.

faq.q: Is Sirap Bandung fattening?
faq.a: It depends on how many you drink. One glass at 190 calories is manageable. Two glasses with your meal is 380 calories from drinks alone, which adds up fast. The sugar content (36g of carbs per glass) is the bigger concern if you're watching your diet.

faq.q: What is the difference between Sirap Bandung and Bandung Soda?
faq.a: Bandung Soda replaces some or all of the evaporated milk with soda water or sarsi. It comes out lighter at around 160 calories because there's less fat from the milk. The sugar content stays similar since the rose syrup amount doesn't really change.

foods.name: Soya (Soy Milk)
foods.metaDescription: Sweetened hawker soya is 130 cal per 250ml. Order kosong and it drops to 85 kcal. Here's what's in your cup and how to make it work for weight loss.
foods.summary: Your classic hawker soy milk drink, anywhere from 85 calories kosong to 150 calories with cincau, depending on how much sugar makes it into your cup.
foods.answer: A standard hawker cup of sweetened soya (250ml) comes in at 130 calories. That's for the typical manis order you get at most mamak stalls or drink carts, where they add sugar syrup on top of the soy milk base. Order it kosong and you drop to about 85 calories. Add cincau for that classic "Michael Jackson" combo and you're looking at around 150 calories for the slightly bigger 300ml serve.
realTalk: Soya is genuinely one of the better drink options at the mamak, bro. At 130 calories for the standard sweetened cup, it is not bad at all. And unlike teh tarik which can hit around 130 to 160 calories and gives you basically zero nutrition, soya actually has 8g of protein per cup. That is real. The only thing bumping up the calories is the sugar syrup, which accounts for about 35 of those 130 calories. The soy milk base itself is sitting at 90 calories and doing all the nutritional work.

What actually changes the maths here is simple: sugar in or out. Kosong brings you down to 85 kcal, manis is 130 kcal, and the cincau version creeps up to 150 kcal partly because of the extra syrup and the slightly bigger 300ml serve. The soy base does not change much between stalls, but the amount of syrup the uncle pours in can vary a lot. Some places are heavy-handed with it. If you are having soya twice a day thinking it is health food but you are getting the sweetened version both times, that is 260 calories just from drinks before you even look at your food. Order kosong or siu tit lah, simple.
lighter: Order it kosong every time. You save 45 calories per cup and honestly the soy flavour still comes through fine.
If you need a little sweetness, ask for siu tit (less sweet) instead of going full manis.
Skip the cincau version if you are counting calories seriously. The grass jelly itself is near zero calories but the extra syrup brings the whole thing to 150 kcal for a bigger cup.
Drink it as your morning or post-workout protein source rather than pairing it with other sugary drinks at the same meal.
If you make it at home, use unsweetened soy milk from a packet, around 40 kcal per 100ml, and skip the syrup entirely.

variants.note: Plain unsweetened soy milk, ~250ml; Mr Bean data ~83 kcal

variants.note: Standard hawker order with sugar syrup added; most common default
