Use less sugar in the batter since ripe banana is already sweet
Swap to plain steamed or grilled banana when you just want the banana taste

faq.q: How many calories in one cekodok pisang?
faq.a: Around 75 calories per ball for a typical small size. Bigger ones from the stall can hit 90 plus.

faq.q: Is cekodok pisang healthy?
faq.a: It has real banana so some potassium and fibre, but it is fried and sugared, so treat it as a snack not a health food. Three is a reasonable portion.

faq.q: What is the difference between cekodok and cucur pisang?
faq.a: Cekodok is rolled into balls, cucur pisang is usually flatter with sliced banana. Calories are similar per gram since both are fried.

foods.name: Muruku
foods.metaDescription: Calories in muruku? About 155 kcal per 30g handful. Crispy fried rice flour snack that disappears fast. Real numbers and lighter tips.
foods.summary: One 30g handful of muruku is about 155 kcal. Crunchy, salty, impossible to stop at one.
foods.answer: A 30 gram handful of muruku is around 155 calories. It is rice flour and dhal flour mixed with spices, piped into spirals and deep fried, so it is basically crunchy fried carbs with a good amount of oil. The serving size is the killer here, nobody eats just 30 grams from a Deepavali tin.
realTalk: Muruku is the festive trap. The tin sits on the table, you walk past, you grab a piece, crunch crunch, you walk past again. Each 30g handful is 155 calories and you will do that handful five times in one afternoon without blinking.

Five casual handfuls is close to 800 calories of fried snack, more than a full meal, and you got zero satisfaction from it because you were watching TV. If you want muruku, put one handful on a small plate and close the tin lah.
lighter: Portion one handful onto a plate and put the tin away, out of sight
Pick baked or less oily brands if you can find them
Pair it with unsweetened tea so you are not adding sugar drink calories on top

faq.q: How many calories in muruku per 100g?
faq.a: Muruku runs roughly 500 calories per 100g because it is deep fried flour. A 30g handful is about 155.

faq.q: Is muruku good for a diet?
faq.a: Only in small, measured amounts. It is calorie dense and easy to overeat, so portion it on a plate instead of grazing from the tin.

faq.q: Is muruku high in protein?
faq.a: Not really. The dhal gives it a little, about 3g per handful, but it is mostly carbs and oil.

foods.name: Kacang Putih
foods.metaDescription: Calories in kacang putih? About 215 kcal per 40g packet. Fried chickpeas that feel like nothing but add up fast. Real numbers inside.
foods.summary: One 40g packet of kacang putih is about 215 kcal. Feels like air, actually fried and oily.
foods.answer: A small 40 gram packet of kacang putih is around 215 calories. It is chickpeas and lentils fried with salt and spices, so you do get a decent 8g of protein, but the frying oil pushes it up. The texture is so light you forget you are eating fried food, that is exactly the problem.
realTalk: Kacang putih feels like nothing bro, you just keep dipping your hand in. But that little packet is fried and oily, easily 215 calories before the movie even starts. The crunch tricks your brain into thinking it is healthy chickpeas.

It does have real protein, 8g a packet, which is more than most snacks here. But one packet at the cinema turns into two with your drink and now you are at 430 calories sitting in the dark. Stick to one packet and you are fine.
lighter: Choose roasted kacang putih over fried, you cut a chunk of the oil
Eat one packet and actually use the 8g protein as the win, do not double up
Skip the sugary cinema drink that usually comes with it, that is where it really stacks

faq.q: How many calories in a packet of kacang putih?
faq.a: A small 40g packet is roughly 215 calories. Bigger paper-cone servings can easily double that.

faq.q: Is kacang putih healthy?
faq.a: It has good protein and fibre from chickpeas, but it is fried so it is calorie dense. Roasted versions are the better pick if you can find them.

faq.q: Does kacang putih have protein?
faq.a: Yes, around 8g per 40g packet, which is solid for a snack. That is the one genuine plus point here.

foods.name: Kaya Pau (Steamed Kaya Bun)
foods.metaDescription: Calories in kaya pau? About 215 kcal for one steamed kaya bun. Soft, sweet, deceptively heavy. Real numbers and lighter tips inside.
foods.summary: One steamed kaya pau is about 215 kcal. Soft and sweet, but it is flour plus sugar coconut jam.
foods.answer: One kaya pau comes in around 215 calories. It is a steamed white flour bun filled with kaya, which is coconut jam made from sugar, egg, and coconut milk. Steamed means no frying oil, that is the good news, but the soft dough plus sweet filling is still a solid chunk of carbs and sugar.
realTalk: People think kaya pau is light because it is steamed and fluffy, not fried. Fair, no frying oil. But that fluffy bun is basically sweet white bread, and the kaya inside is pure sugar and coconut. One bun is 215 calories of mostly carbs.

It is not a disaster, it is actually one of the gentler snacks on this list since there is almost no frying involved. Just do not eat it thinking it is a free pass. One pau with your kopi is fine, two is creeping toward a meal worth of sugar.
lighter: Have one pau, not two, and skip the condensed milk in your kopi to balance it
Pick a smaller pau if the stall has different sizes, they vary a lot
Pair with a black coffee or plain tea so you are not stacking more sugar on top

faq.q: How many calories in a kaya pau?
faq.a: Roughly 215 calories for a standard bun. Larger ones or extra kaya can push it to 250 plus.

faq.q: Is kaya pau better than fried snacks?
faq.a: Calorie for calorie it is gentler because it is steamed, not fried, so the fat is lower. The catch is the sugar in the kaya filling.

faq.q: Can I eat kaya pau on a diet?
faq.a: Yes, one bun fits fine in a deficit, especially since it is steamed. Just count it as a real 215 calories, not a freebie.

foods.name: Sata (Terengganu)
foods.metaDescription: Calories in sata Terengganu? About 230 kcal for 2 sticks. Grilled spiced fish in banana leaf, decent protein. Real numbers inside.
foods.summary: 2 sticks of sata are about 230 kcal with 14g protein. Grilled fish, not fried, surprisingly solid.
foods.answer: Two sticks of sata land around 230 calories with a respectable 14g of protein. It is spiced fish meat mixed with grated coconut, wrapped in banana leaf and grilled over charcoal. Because it is grilled not fried, the calories come mostly from the fish and coconut rather than soaked oil, which makes it one of the better snack choices here.
realTalk: Sata is actually one of the smarter picks on this list, bro. It is fish, it is grilled over charcoal, and 2 sticks give you 14g of real protein. The coconut adds fat so it is not zero calorie, but you are getting actual nutrition, not just fried air.

The thing to watch is the grated coconut, that is where the fat comes from, about 16g across two sticks. Still, compared to muruku or kacang putih, sata fills you up and feeds your muscles. If you are choosing a snack on the east coast, this one is a green light.
lighter: It is grilled already, so just go easy on any sweet dipping sauce on the side
Pair 2 sticks with cut cucumber or ulam instead of rice if you want it lighter
Choose sticks with more fish and less coconut paste if the stall lets you see

faq.q: How many calories in sata?
faq.a: About 115 calories per stick, so 230 for two. It varies with how much coconut is packed in.

faq.q: Is sata good for weight loss?
faq.a: Pretty good actually. It is grilled fish with 14g protein per 2 sticks, so it is filling and not fried. The coconut adds fat but it is still a smart snack.

faq.q: Is sata high in protein?
faq.a: Yes, around 14g for 2 sticks since it is mostly fish. That is one of the highest protein snacks in this category.

foods.name: Akok (Kelantan Kuih)
foods.metaDescription: Calories in akok? About 180 kcal for 2 pieces. Baked Kelantan kuih of egg, coconut milk and palm sugar. Real numbers inside.
foods.summary: 2 pieces of akok are about 180 kcal. Baked egg and coconut kuih, sweet and rich.
foods.answer: Two pieces of akok come in around 180 calories, so roughly 90 each. It is a Kelantan kuih baked from eggs, coconut milk, and palm sugar, so it is soft, creamy, and sweet. It is baked not fried, but the coconut milk and sugar still make it richer than it looks for such a small piece.
realTalk: Akok is small and innocent looking, like a little flower shaped cake. But it is egg, coconut milk, and palm sugar baked together, so each piece is about 90 calories of rich sweet custard. Two pieces with your kopi is 180.

It is not the worst thing, it is baked so there is no frying oil, and the egg gives it a touch of protein. But the palm sugar and coconut milk mean it is denser than the size suggests. Enjoy two, do not sit there finishing the whole tray lah.
lighter: Stick to 2 pieces, the small size makes it easy to lose count fast
Pair with black coffee or plain tea, no extra sugar drink on the side
Treat it as your one sweet thing for the day, not an all-afternoon graze

faq.q: How many calories in akok?
faq.a: About 90 calories per piece, so 180 for two. Bigger or sweeter versions can run higher.

faq.q: Is akok fried?
faq.a: No, akok is baked, traditionally in special moulds over a fire. That means no soaked frying oil, the calories come from coconut milk and palm sugar.

faq.q: Is akok ok for a diet?
faq.a: In small amounts yes. It is baked and the egg gives a little protein, but the coconut milk and palm sugar make it rich, so keep it to 2 pieces.

foods.name: Pulut Panggang
foods.metaDescription: Calories in pulut panggang? About 290 kcal for 2 rolls. Grilled glutinous rice with spiced coconut filling. Real numbers inside.
foods.summary: 2 rolls of pulut panggang are about 290 kcal. Grilled sticky rice with spicy coconut inside.
foods.answer: Two rolls of pulut panggang come in around 290 calories, so roughly 145 each. It is glutinous rice cooked in coconut milk, wrapped around a spiced coconut or dried shrimp filling, then grilled in banana leaf. The grilling keeps oil out, but glutinous rice plus coconut milk is dense, so two rolls is a proper snack not a nibble.
realTalk: Pulut panggang smells amazing off the charcoal and the banana leaf char makes you want three immediately. But glutinous rice is heavy, bro, and it is cooked in coconut milk, so each roll is about 145 calories. Two rolls is 290, basically a small meal.

It is grilled so there is no frying oil, which is a plus, and the rempah filling actually gives it flavour and a little protein. Just know that two rolls fills you up like rice because it is rice. Treat it as a mini meal, not a between-meal snack you stack on top of lunch.
lighter: Count 2 rolls as part of a meal, not an extra on top of your rice
Pick rolls with more filling and a thinner rice layer if you can
It is grilled already, so just skip any sweet sauce and you are good

components.name: Banana leaf char and oil brush

faq.q: How many calories in pulut panggang?
faq.a: About 145 calories per roll, so 290 for two. Bigger rolls with more coconut filling go higher.

faq.q: Is pulut panggang fattening?
faq.a: It is calorie dense because glutinous rice and coconut milk are heavy, but it is grilled not fried. Treat 2 rolls like a small meal and it fits fine.

faq.q: Is pulut panggang a meal or a snack?
faq.a: Two rolls is really a light meal worth of carbs. If you eat it as a snack on top of full meals, that is where the calories pile up.

foods.name: Sweet and Sour Chicken
foods.metaDescription: Sweet and sour chicken runs about 540 calories a plate. The battered chicken and that sugary red sauce are the whole story. Breakdown inside.
foods.summary: Battered deep-fried chicken pieces tossed in a sweet, tangy red sauce with pineapple, onion and capsicum.
foods.answer: A standard zi-char plate of sweet and sour chicken comes in around 540 calories, with 26g protein, 52g carbs and 26g fat. The chicken itself is fine, but it gets battered and deep fried first, then drowned in a sauce that is basically sugar, ketchup and vinegar. That combo of fried batter plus sweet sauce is what pushes the carbs and fat up together.
realTalk: Sweet and sour chicken is one of those zi char plates everyone orders without thinking. Crispy battered chicken, that bright red glossy sauce, bits of pineapple and capsicum for show. Tastes great with rice, no argument. But here is the thing bro, the chicken is deep fried in batter before it even touches the sauce, so you are paying for the oil and the flour twice. Then the sauce itself is loaded with sugar to get that sweet tang. At around 540 calories for a plate, it is not a disaster, but it is also not the lean protein dish people pretend it is.

The sauce is the swing factor. Some shops make it light and tangy, some make it candy-sweet and thick enough to coat a spoon. The sweeter and glossier it looks, the more sugar is in there, and that can add 80 to 120 calories on its own. Portion matters too. A small plate shared between people is one thing, but a full plate to yourself with a mountain of rice and you are easily past 900 calories for that one corner of the table. If you want the flavour without the full hit, ask for the sauce on the side and dip instead of drowning.
lighter: Ask for the sauce on the side and dip the chicken instead of having it all poured over. You control how much sugar goes on.
Share it as a table dish, not a solo main. One or two pieces for taste, then get your protein from something steamed.
Pick the version with more visible veg and actually eat those, they bulk the plate for almost no calories.
Pair it with plain rice and a plate of sayur instead of stacking it next to another fried dish like butter prawns.

faq.a: A standard zi char plate is roughly 540 calories, with 26g protein, 52g carbs and 26g fat. Heavier sauce and thicker batter can push it past 600.

faq.q: Why is sweet and sour chicken so high in carbs?
faq.a: Two reasons. The chicken is coated in flour batter before deep frying, and the sauce is built on sugar and ketchup. Those two together are where most of the 52g of carbs come from, not the chicken.

faq.q: Is sweet and sour chicken a good protein choice?
faq.a: It gives you about 26g of protein per plate, which is decent, but it comes packaged with 26g of fat and a lot of sugar. If protein is the goal, a steamed or plain stir-fried chicken dish gets you more protein for fewer calories.

foods.name: Kung Pao Chicken
foods.metaDescription: Kung pao chicken is around 480 calories a plate. Leaner than most fried zi char dishes, but the oil and cashews add up. Full breakdown here.
foods.summary: Stir-fried chicken cubes with dried chili, peanuts or cashews, onion and a savoury-sweet kung pao sauce.
foods.answer: A plate of kung pao chicken sits around 480 calories, with 30g protein, 24g carbs and 29g fat. Compared to battered dishes it is actually one of the better zi char picks because the chicken is usually just diced and stir-fried, not deep fried in batter. The fat comes mostly from the wok oil and the nuts, and the sauce keeps the carbs moderate rather than crazy.
realTalk: Kung pao chicken is a solid order if you are watching things, and I do not say that about most zi char plates. The chicken is cubed and stir-fried, not battered and deep fried, so you skip that whole layer of flour and absorbed oil that wrecks dishes like sweet and sour. At around 480 calories with a genuine 30g of protein, the macros are actually not bad. The fat number looks high, but a good chunk of it is the wok oil and the handful of peanuts or cashews tossed in, which at least bring something to the table besides empty calories.

Where it goes wrong is oil-heavy versions and the nut load. Some shops are generous with the wok oil and the dish arrives swimming, which can add 100 calories easily. The cashew version is richer than the peanut one because cashews are denser. And like every dish here, the rice is the real trap, not the chicken. If you treat the kung pao as your protein anchor and keep the rice to one scoop, you are eating well. Pick this over butter prawns or marmite chicken any day if you want flavour without the deep-fry tax.
lighter: Choose kung pao over the battered dishes. Stir-fried beats deep fried every time on calories.
Ask them to go light on the oil. A drier wok finish can save you 80 to 100 calories per plate.
Eat the chicken and veg, go easy on scooping up the loose nuts and oil pooled at the bottom.
Use it as your protein main and keep rice to one scoop, that is where this meal stays reasonable.

faq.q: How many calories in kung pao chicken?
faq.a: A standard plate is about 480 calories, with 30g protein, 24g carbs and 29g fat. Oil-heavy or cashew versions can reach 520 to 560.

faq.q: Is kung pao chicken healthier than sweet and sour chicken?
faq.a: Generally yes. Kung pao chicken is stir-fried, not battered and deep fried, so you skip the flour coating and a lot of absorbed oil. It also has more protein and fewer carbs per plate.

faq.q: What makes kung pao chicken high in fat?
faq.a: Mostly the wok oil and the peanuts or cashews. The chicken itself is lean since it is diced and stir-fried, so if the plate arrives swimming in oil, that is where the extra fat is hiding.

foods.name: Marmite Chicken
foods.metaDescription: Marmite chicken comes in around 580 calories a plate. Deep fried then glazed in sweet marmite sauce, this one hits both fat and sugar. Breakdown inside.
foods.summary: Deep-fried chicken pieces coated in a sticky, sweet and savoury glaze made from Marmite, sugar and soy.
foods.answer: A zi char plate of marmite chicken lands around 580 calories, with 28g protein, 40g carbs and 32g fat. This one is a double hit. The chicken is deep fried first, then tossed in a glossy glaze built on Marmite, sugar, honey or maltose and soy. So you pay for the frying oil and the sugary glaze at the same time. Tasty as hell, but not light.
realTalk: Marmite chicken is one of those dishes that tastes way too good for what it does to your day. The chicken gets battered and deep fried until crispy, then it is tossed in that dark sticky glaze made from Marmite, sugar, honey or maltose and a bit of soy. That glaze is where the magic and the damage both live, because it is essentially caramelised sugar clinging to fried chicken. At around 580 calories a plate, it is one of the heavier zi char chicken dishes, with the fat coming from the deep fry and the carbs coming straight from the sweet glaze.

The glaze thickness is everything here. A light Marmite coating is one thing, but some shops drench it so thick and glossy that every piece is candied, and that easily adds 100 to 150 calories of pure sugar. Because it is deep fried, you also cannot pull skin or batter off to save much, the calories are baked into the whole piece. If you love it, the move is to treat it as a shared table dish, take two or three pieces for the taste, and not make it your personal protein main. Pair it with steamed veg and one scoop of rice and you keep the meal from running away from you.
lighter: Share it. Two or three pieces for the flavour hit, then get your actual protein from a steamed or plain stir-fried dish.
Go for the version with a thinner glaze. The thicker and glossier the coating, the more sugar you are eating.
Do not pour the leftover glaze from the plate over your rice, that pooled sauce is concentrated sugar and oil.
Balance the plate with a green veg like sawi or kangkung instead of ordering a second fried dish.

faq.q: How many calories in marmite chicken?
faq.a: A standard zi char plate is roughly 580 calories, with 28g protein, 40g carbs and 32g fat. A heavily glazed version can push past 650.

faq.q: Why is marmite chicken so high in calories?
faq.a: It is a double hit. The chicken is deep fried first, then coated in a glaze made from Marmite, sugar and honey or maltose. So you get the fat from frying and the sugar from the glaze in the same bite.

faq.q: Is marmite chicken worse than sweet and sour chicken?
faq.a: Slightly, yes. Both are battered and deep fried, but the marmite glaze tends to be richer and more sugar-heavy than the sweet and sour sauce, so the plate usually lands a bit higher at around 580 calories.

foods.name: Char Siew (BBQ Pork)
foods.metaDescription: Char siew is around 290 calories per 100g. That glossy red BBQ pork glaze is basically sugar. Here is the full breakdown.
foods.summary: Cantonese barbecued pork, marinated in a sweet honey-soy glaze and roasted until the edges caramelise.
foods.answer: 100g of char siew comes in around 290 calories, with 24g protein, 14g carbs and 15g fat. The pork gives you a solid protein hit, but two things bump the number up: char siew is usually made from fattier cuts like pork shoulder or belly, and that signature glossy red glaze is loaded with sugar and honey. The leaner the cut and the lighter the glaze, the better it sits.
realTalk: Char siew is that sweet, glossy red BBQ pork you see hanging in the Chinese roast meat shop window. 100g at around 290 calories is honestly not bad for a roast meat, and the 24g of protein is genuinely good. But two things are working against you bro. First, char siew is usually cut from pork shoulder or belly, which carries a fair bit of fat, so even before any sauce you are starting fattier than chicken. Second, that beautiful red lacquered glaze is basically a sugar bomb of honey, maltose, sugar and soy painted on layer by layer. That is where most of the 14g of carbs come from. The caramelised burnt edges everyone fights over taste incredible and are pure sugar.

Cut choice is the biggest lever. Lean char siew can drop the fat noticeably, while the fatty belly version with the white streaks can push 100g toward 340 calories. The other trap is portion. A char siew rice plate gives you way more than 100g, often 150 to 200g, so just doubling the meat alone can be 500 plus calories before the rice. If you are at the roast shop, ask for lean over fatty, eat it with rice and veg rather than stacking it with siu yoke, and you have got a reasonable high-protein meal.
lighter: Ask for the lean cut over the fatty belly version. The lean shoulder pieces save you a good chunk of fat per 100g.
Watch the portion. A roast shop plate is often 150 to 200g, not 100g, so the meat alone can be 500 plus calories.
Do not drench it in extra dark sauce. The glaze is already sweet, so adding the syrupy sauce on top is double sugar.
Pair it with rice and a plate of greens instead of ordering it alongside siu yoke and roast duck on the same plate.

faq.q: How many calories in char siew?
faq.a: Around 290 calories per 100g, with 24g protein, 14g carbs and 15g fat. Leaner cuts come closer to 230, while the fatty belly version can hit 340.

faq.q: Why does char siew have carbs if it is just pork?
faq.a: The carbs come from the glaze. That glossy red coating is made from honey, maltose, sugar and soy, painted on in layers and caramelised, which is where the 14g of carbs per 100g comes from.

faq.q: Is char siew a good protein source?
faq.a: Yes, 24g of protein per 100g is solid. Just be aware of two things: it is often a fattier cut of pork, and the sweet glaze adds sugar. Pick the lean cut and watch the portion size.

foods.name: Siu Yoke (Roast Pork)
foods.metaDescription: Siu yoke is around 400 calories per 100g. That crispy crackling skin is literally rendered fat. Worth it sometimes, just know the price.
foods.summary: Cantonese roast pork belly with shatteringly crispy crackling skin over layers of fat and meat.
foods.answer: 100g of siu yoke comes in around 400 calories, with 20g protein, basically no carbs, and a hefty 36g of fat. There is no sugary glaze here, the calories are all about the cut. Siu yoke is pork belly, which is layers of fat with some meat, topped by that crispy crackling skin that is literally rendered fat. Delicious, but it is one of the fattiest things in the roast shop.
realTalk: Siu yoke is the crispy roast pork everyone fights over at the table bro. That shattering crackling skin, the layers underneath, dipped in a bit of mustard or hoisin. Pure joy. But let us be honest about what it is: pork belly. That means alternating layers of fat and meat, topped by skin that has been roasted until the fat under it renders and crisps into that crackling. At around 400 calories per 100g with 36g of fat, it is one of the fattiest things you can order at a roast meat shop. Unlike char siew there is no sweet glaze, so the carbs are near zero, but you are not saving anything because the fat does all the work instead.

The thing to understand is that the crackling skin, as good as it is, is basically rendered fat with a crunch. There is no lean version of siu yoke, it is belly by definition, so you cannot really pick a lighter cut the way you can with char siew. Your only real levers are portion and frequency. 100g is already 400 calories, and a roast shop usually piles on more, so a generous serving can quietly be 600 plus before rice. The move is not to swear it off, it is to treat it as a sometimes thing. Take a few pieces for the taste, pair it with a leaner protein, and pile on the veg to balance it out. Worth it sometimes, just know the price.
lighter: Treat it as a taste, not a main. A few pieces alongside a leaner protein beats a full plate of siu yoke on its own.
Pair it with steamed veg and plain rice to balance the plate, do not stack it with roast duck and char siew at once.
If you want roast pork as your protein, char siew lean cut gives you more protein for a lot less fat than belly.
Blot the surface oil off with a tissue. It will not change the cut, but it shaves a little of the dripping fat.

faq.q: How many calories in siu yoke?
faq.a: Around 400 calories per 100g, with 20g protein and a heavy 36g of fat. There are almost no carbs since there is no sweet glaze, but the pork belly cut makes it one of the fattiest roast meats.

faq.q: Why is siu yoke so high in fat?
faq.a: Because it is pork belly, which is layers of fat and meat, topped with crackling skin. That crispy skin everyone loves is literally rendered fat, so the whole cut is fat-heavy by nature.

faq.q: Is siu yoke or char siew better for losing weight?
faq.a: Char siew, especially the lean cut, is the better pick. It has more protein and far less fat per 100g. Siu yoke is pork belly so it is much fattier, around 400 calories per 100g versus roughly 230 to 290 for char siew.

foods.name: Roast Duck (Siu Ngap)
foods.metaDescription: A quarter roast duck is around 480 calories. Great protein, but the skin and fat under it do the heavy lifting. Full breakdown here.
foods.summary: Cantonese roast duck, marinated with five-spice and roasted until the skin is crisp and the meat juicy.
foods.answer: A quarter roast duck (around 200g with the bone) comes in roughly 480 calories, with a big 40g of protein, almost no carbs, and 34g of fat. Duck meat is leaner than people think, but the skin and the layer of fat right under it are rich, and that is where most of the fat and calories come from. Eat it with the skin off and the numbers drop fast.
realTalk: Roast duck, siu ngap, is one of those roast shop orders that is actually a decent protein play if you are smart about it. A quarter duck gives you a massive 40g of protein, which is more than most lauk on this site. The duck meat itself is leaner than people assume, darker and more flavourful than chicken but not crazy fatty. The catch is the skin. That crispy five-spice skin and the fat layer right under it are where a big chunk of the 34g of fat hides. At around 480 calories for a quarter, it is a fair trade for the protein, but the skin is doing a lot of the calorie work.

Here is the useful part: roast duck is one of the few roast meats where you have a real lever, and that is the skin. Pull the skin off and you can cut the fat noticeably, dropping a quarter duck toward 350 calories while keeping almost all of that 40g protein. That is a genuinely good macro profile. Compared to siu yoke, duck is the smarter order because the protein is much higher and the fat is more removable. Bone weight also means the calories per actual bite of meat are lower than the gram count suggests. Eat the meat, go easy on the skin, pair with rice and greens, and a quarter duck is a solid meal.
lighter: Pull the skin off, or at least most of it. The crispy skin and the fat under it are where the bulk of the fat lives.
Pick duck over siu yoke if you want a roast meat. Way more protein, and the fat is more removable.
Remember the quarter includes bone, so eat the meat and do not feel you have to finish every fatty scrap.
Pair it with plain rice and greens instead of ordering it next to char siew and siu yoke all at once.

faq.q: Is roast duck healthier than roast pork?
faq.a: For protein, yes. A quarter duck gives you about 40g of protein, far more than siu yoke, and the fat sits mostly in the skin so you can remove it. Duck meat itself is leaner than most people expect.

faq.q: Where does the fat in roast duck come from?
faq.a: Mostly the skin and the layer of fat directly under it. The duck meat itself is reasonably lean, so if you pull the crispy skin off you cut a big share of the 34g of fat right away.

foods.name: Sotong Goreng Tepung (Fried Calamari)
foods.metaDescription: Fried calamari is around 460 calories a plate. Squid is super lean, but the flour batter and deep frying flip the script. Breakdown inside.
foods.summary: Squid rings coated in seasoned flour batter and deep fried until golden and crispy.
foods.answer: A plate of sotong goreng tepung comes in around 460 calories, with 24g protein, 34g carbs and 24g fat. Here is the irony: squid by itself is one of the leanest, lowest-calorie proteins you can eat. But the moment you coat it in flour batter and deep fry it, you stack on carbs from the coating and fat from the absorbed oil. The squid is innocent, the batter and fryer are not.
realTalk: Sotong goreng tepung is a real what-could-have-been dish bro. Plain squid is incredibly lean, like 90 calories per 100g lean, high protein, almost no fat. It should be a diet dream. But then you coat each ring in seasoned flour batter and drop it in the deep fryer, and suddenly that innocent squid is wearing a calorie jacket. The batter brings the carbs and the absorbed frying oil brings the fat. At around 460 calories a plate, it is not the worst thing on the table, but it is a long way from the lean protein the squid started as. The crispy coating is the entire story here.

The variables are batter thickness and how well it was drained. A light, thin tepung coating absorbs less oil and keeps the plate closer to 400, while a thick beer-batter style or a heavily clumped coating can push it past 550. Squid also goes rubbery fast if overcooked, so some places batter it thick to hide that, which works against you. Dipping it in mayo or thousand island sauce, which a lot of places serve it with, can quietly add another 100 calories. If you want the squid without the deep-fry tax, sotong masak gives you the same lean protein for far fewer calories. But if you are ordering the fried version, blot the oil, skip the mayo, and share it as a starter rather than a main.
lighter: If you can choose, get sotong stir-fried or in sambal instead of battered. Same lean squid, way fewer calories without the batter and oil.
Skip the mayo or thousand island dip. That sauce can add 100 calories fast and you do not need it.
Blot the rings with a tissue before eating. Surface oil removal genuinely shaves a bit off a deep-fried plate.
Share it as a starter for the table, not as your protein main, since the protein-to-calorie ratio gets wrecked by the batter.

faq.q: How many calories in fried calamari (sotong goreng tepung)?
faq.a: A standard plate is around 460 calories, with 24g protein, 34g carbs and 24g fat. A thin-coated version is closer to 380, while a thick batter can push past 550.

faq.q: Isn't squid supposed to be low calorie?
faq.a: It is. Plain squid is one of the leanest proteins around, roughly 90 calories per 100g. The calories in fried calamari come almost entirely from the flour batter and the oil absorbed during deep frying, not the squid itself.

faq.q: What is a lighter way to eat squid?
faq.a: Get it stir-fried or cooked in sambal instead of battered and fried. You keep the lean high-protein squid but skip the flour coating and the frying oil, which is where most of the calories come from.

foods.name: Telur Dadar (Malaysian Omelette)
foods.metaDescription: Telur dadar is around 290 calories. Solid cheap protein, but the cooking oil it fries in does more than you think. Breakdown here.
foods.summary: Malaysian-style fried omelette, eggs beaten with onion and chili and fried until puffy and crisp at the edges.
foods.answer: A telur dadar made with 2 to 3 eggs comes in around 290 calories, with 17g protein, 4g carbs and 23g fat. The eggs themselves are a cheap, solid protein, but telur dadar is fried in a decent slick of oil to get those crispy puffy edges, and that oil is where a lot of the fat comes from. The eggs alone would be a lot lighter.
realTalk: Telur dadar is the cheap, reliable lauk everyone has had a hundred times. Eggs beaten with sliced onion and a bit of chili, poured into hot oil and fried until the edges go crispy and the middle puffs up. At around 290 calories for a 2 to 3 egg version, it is honestly a decent protein-per-ringgit deal, 17g of protein for cheap. The thing people forget is the oil. To get that proper crispy fried-omelette texture, the kampung way uses a generous amount of oil, and the egg soaks a fair bit of it up. So a chunk of that 23g of fat is not the eggs, it is the frying oil.

The swing factor is purely how much oil it is fried in. A non-stick pan with a light film of oil keeps it close to 220, while the traditional deep-ish fry in a wok with plenty of oil for that lacy crispy edge can push it to 330 or more. Adding extras like minced meat, prawns or anchovies bumps it up too. The good news is this is one lauk where you genuinely control the outcome if you cook it at home: less oil, same protein. At a stall you have less say, but it is still a more honest protein choice than most fried dishes here. Pair it with rice and sambal and it is a simple, filling plate.
lighter: At home, fry it in a non-stick pan with just a thin film of oil. The eggs are the same, you just skip the soaked-up frying oil.
Use 2 eggs instead of 3, or 1 whole egg plus 2 whites, to keep the protein up while trimming fat.
Go easy on rich add-ins like minced pork or extra anchovies if you are watching it, the plain version is leaner.
Pair it with rice and a sambal or veg rather than stacking it next to another fried lauk on the same plate.

variants.name: Telur dadar, pan-fried with little oil
variants.note: Light film of oil in a non-stick pan, mostly just the eggs

variants.name: Telur dadar with minced meat or prawns
variants.note: Added protein and a bit more oil push it higher

faq.q: How many calories in telur dadar?
faq.a: A 2 to 3 egg telur dadar is around 290 calories, with 17g protein, 4g carbs and 23g fat. Pan-fried with little oil it drops toward 220, while a heavily oil-fried crispy version can hit 330.

faq.q: Why is telur dadar higher in calories than boiled eggs?
faq.a: The frying oil. To get those crispy puffy edges, telur dadar is fried in a generous amount of oil that the egg soaks up. That absorbed oil adds fat that you would not get from a boiled or poached egg.

faq.q: Is telur dadar a good cheap protein?
faq.a: Yes. For the price it gives you about 17g of protein per omelette. If you want to keep it lean, fry it in a non-stick pan with minimal oil, since the oil is what drives most of the fat.

foods.name: Ayam Kapitan (Kari Kapitan)
foods.metaDescription: Ayam kapitan is around 410 calories a serving. A rich, dry Nyonya chicken curry where the santan and oil do the work. Breakdown inside.
foods.summary: A rich, dry Nyonya chicken curry with a thick spice paste, coconut milk, lemongrass and lime.
foods.answer: A serving of ayam kapitan (kari kapitan) comes in around 410 calories, with 28g protein, 12g carbs and 28g fat. This is a rich, dry Nyonya curry, thicker and more intense than a normal kuah kari. The chicken brings the protein, but the thick spice paste is fried in oil and finished with coconut milk, so the santan and oil are what push the fat and calories up.
realTalk: Ayam kapitan is the fancy cousin of regular chicken curry. It is a Nyonya dish, a dry-style curry where the rempah, that thick paste of chili, lemongrass, galangal, candlenut and belacan, is fried down hard in oil before the chicken and coconut milk go in. The result is thick, clingy and intensely flavoured, finished with a squeeze of lime that cuts through the richness. At around 410 calories per serving, it sits in the same ballpark as a good ayam masak, with a solid 28g of protein from the chicken. The carbs stay low at 12g since there is no sugar glaze, but the fat is up at 28g, and that comes from two places: the oil the rempah is fried in, and the coconut milk that thickens it.

The richness is the whole point of this dish, which is also the calorie problem. Because it is a dry curry, the sauce clings to every piece rather than sitting watery at the bottom, so you eat more of the santan and oil per bite than you would with a thin curry. The amount of coconut milk is the big lever, a kapitan made with more santan and a heavier oil fry can climb toward 480, while a lighter hand keeps it nearer 360. Using chicken thigh with skin versus breast also moves it. If you are watching it, the move is the same as any curry: eat the chicken, do not spoon all the thick gravy and oil over your rice, and pair it with veg. The flavour is in the rempah clinging to the meat, you do not need to drink the oil.
lighter: Eat the chicken and go easy on spooning the thick gravy over your rice. That clingy sauce is where the santan and oil concentrate.
Pull the chicken skin off. The skin plus the oily rempah is a fat double-up you can trim.
Ask for or cook a version with less coconut milk. The santan is the main lever on the fat number.
Pair it with plain rice and a plate of ulam or sayur instead of a second rich lauk.

variants.name: Ayam kapitan, lighter santan
variants.note: Less coconut milk and a lighter oil fry on the rempah

variants.name: Ayam kapitan, rich restaurant style
variants.note: Heavy santan and a generous oil fry, the richest version

components.name: Rempah spice paste fried in oil

portions.label: A couple of pieces with gravy

faq.q: How many calories in ayam kapitan?
faq.a: A serving of ayam kapitan is around 410 calories, with 28g protein, 12g carbs and 28g fat. A lighter-santan version is closer to 360, while a rich restaurant style can reach 480.

faq.q: What is the difference between ayam kapitan and normal chicken curry?
faq.a: Ayam kapitan is a dry Nyonya curry with a thicker, more intense rempah fried hard in oil and finished with coconut milk and lime. Normal kari ayam is usually thinner and more soupy. The dry, clingy sauce means you eat more of the santan and oil per bite.

faq.q: Why is ayam kapitan high in fat?
faq.a: Two reasons. The rempah spice paste is fried in a fair amount of oil, and the curry is finished with coconut milk. Both the oil and the santan drive the 28g of fat, while the chicken itself supplies the protein.

foods.name: Nasi Campur (Economy Rice)
foods.metaDescription: A typical nasi campur plate with rice plus 3 dishes runs about 720 calories. Point at fried lauk and it climbs fast. Full breakdown here.
foods.summary: Rice plus 3 dishes lands around 720 kcal. Fried picks are the trap.
foods.answer: A standard nasi campur plate with rice and three dishes is around 720 calories. The rice alone is about 280, then your three lauk pile on the rest depending on what you point at. Pick fried chicken plus a fried egg plus a fried veg and you are quietly at 850. Go steamed fish, sayur, and tofu and you can drop it under 550.
realTalk: Economy rice is a trap dressed as a budget meal bro. The rice is cheap, sure, but you point at three lauk and half of them are deep fried, so your RM9 plate is quietly 800 calories before you even add the curry gravy on top.

The killer is the auntie ladle of kuah. That free splash of curry or masak lemak over your rice is pure coconut oil and easily adds 100 to 150 calories you never counted. You think it is free flavour but your waistline is paying for it.
lighter: Pick two veg dishes and one protein instead of three fried meats, easily saves 200 calories
Go steamed or grilled fish over fried chicken, that one swap alone is about 150 calories down
Skip the curry gravy ladle or ask for just a little, that drizzle is sneaky coconut oil

faq.q: Is nasi campur healthy?
faq.a: It can be if you choose well. Go for a steamed protein and two vegetable dishes and you land around 520 calories with decent protein. The problem is most people stack fried lauk and drown it in curry gravy, which pushes it past 800.

faq.q: Why does my economy rice cost so much?
faq.a: Because you pointed at the expensive fried stuff and the auntie eyeballed your portions. Funny enough the pricier plates are usually the more fattening ones since fried meat costs more and carries more oil. Cheaper veg picks are also lighter.

faq.q: How much protein is in nasi campur?
faq.a: Roughly 30g for a standard plate with one meat dish and an egg. If you want more, ask for a double portion of chicken or fish instead of a second veg, gets you to 40g plus without much extra fat.

variants.name: Veg-heavy plate
variants.note: rice, steamed fish, two vegetable sides

variants.name: Fried-loaded plate
variants.note: big rice, two fried meats, fried egg, curry gravy

foods.name: Yong Chow Fried Rice
foods.metaDescription: A restaurant plate of yong chow fried rice is about 620 calories. Char siew, prawn, and egg through wok-tossed rice. Full breakdown inside.
foods.summary: Wok-fried rice with char siew, prawn and egg, about 620 kcal a plate.
foods.answer: A full restaurant plate of yong chow fried rice is around 620 calories. It is white rice tossed in a hot wok with char siew, prawns, egg, and peas, so you get decent protein around 24g but also a fair bit of oil. Smaller cup-sized servings sit closer to 330, but nobody orders the cup at a zi char stall lah.
realTalk: Yong chow fried rice is actually not the worst fried rice on the menu bro, because the char siew and prawn and egg push the protein up to around 24g. Problem is the wok hei comes from a serious glug of oil, so a big plate still lands near 620.

The portion at a zi char place is the real issue. They plate it like it is feeding two people, so what looks like one serving is often 1.5 servings of rice and oil. Split it with someone and suddenly it is a sensible 310 calorie meal.
lighter: Share the plate, a zi char portion is basically 1.5 servings so halving it is the easy win
Ask for less oil when you order, most stalls will do it and it shaves 80 to 100 calories
Add a plate of steamed veg or stir-fried sayur so you fill up without ordering a second rice

faq.q: Is yong chow fried rice healthier than normal fried rice?
faq.a: Slightly, yes. The char siew, prawn and egg give it more protein than a plain nasi goreng, around 24g versus 15g. The calories are similar though because the wok oil is the same either way. It is the protein that makes it a better pick, not fewer calories.

faq.q: How many calories in a small bowl of yong chow fried rice?
faq.a: A small cup-sized serving of about 200g is roughly 330 calories. The catch is restaurants almost never serve it that small, the standard plate is 300g plus and lands around 620.

faq.q: Can I eat yong chow fried rice while losing weight?
faq.a: Yes, just respect the portion. Split a plate with someone or eat half and pack half, then add vegetables. Half a plate at 310 calories with 12g protein fits a deficit easily.

variants.note: ask the wok to go easy on oil

foods.name: Nasi Paprik
foods.metaDescription: A plate of nasi paprik runs about 680 calories. Spicy stir-fried chicken and veg over rice, decent protein but oily sauce. Breakdown inside.
foods.summary: Spicy paprik chicken and veg over rice, around 680 kcal a plate.
foods.answer: A plate of nasi paprik is around 680 calories. You get rice topped with paprik, which is chicken stir-fried with vegetables in a spicy thick sauce, so the protein is solid at about 32g. The catch is the sauce carries oil and a bit of sugar, and the wok-fry adds more, so it climbs higher than you would guess for a stir-fry.
realTalk: Nasi paprik is one of the better mamak rice plates honestly bro, because it is loaded with actual chicken and a pile of vegetables, so you walk away with 32g protein. That is more than most nasi goreng will ever give you.

The sauce is where it sneaks up on you though. That glossy spicy paprik gravy is wok oil plus a spoon of sugar to balance the chilli, and they pour it generously over the rice. The protein and veg are great, the sauce is the part quietly adding 150 calories.
lighter: Ask for less rice, the paprik chicken and veg already fill you up so half the rice still satisfies
Request less sauce or get it on the side, that thick gravy is the oil-and-sugar part
It is already protein and veg heavy, so just controlling the rice and sauce makes it a genuinely lean plate

faq.q: Is nasi paprik a good choice for dieting?
faq.a: Actually yes, it is one of the smarter mamak rice picks. It packs around 32g protein from the chicken and a real serving of vegetables. Just go easy on the rice and ask for less of the oily sauce and you have got a lean 520 calorie plate.

faq.q: Why is nasi paprik more calories than plain stir-fried chicken?
faq.a: The rice and the sauce. The paprik itself is reasonable, but a full scoop of rice is 280 calories and the glossy sauce is wok oil plus sugar, around 140 more. Together they push a healthy-looking stir-fry up to 680.

faq.q: How much protein is in nasi paprik?
faq.a: About 32g for a standard plate, which is genuinely good for a single rice meal. If you want more, ask for extra chicken, most stalls will load you up for a small top-up.

variants.name: Less rice, less sauce
variants.note: the lean way to order it

foods.name: Nasi Goreng Pattaya
foods.metaDescription: Nasi goreng pattaya is about 700 calories. Fried rice wrapped in an omelette with chilli sauce. The egg blanket adds fat. Breakdown inside.
foods.summary: Fried rice wrapped in an omelette, about 700 kcal a plate.
foods.answer: A plate of nasi goreng pattaya is around 700 calories. It is basically mamak fried rice wrapped in a thin omelette blanket with a squiggle of chilli sauce on top. The fried rice underneath is already 500 plus, then the egg omelette and the oil it is fried in add another 150 to 200 on top.
realTalk: Nasi goreng pattaya is just nasi goreng wearing a jacket bro. The fried rice inside is the same 500 calorie business as usual, and then they wrap it in a fried egg omelette which adds fat and another splash of oil from the pan.

The chilli sauce squiggle on top looks innocent but it is mostly sugar. Combine the oily fried rice, the omelette, and the sweet sauce and you are at 700, which is more than the plain nasi goreng you thought you were upgrading from.
lighter: Eat half the rice inside, the omelette and a smaller scoop of fried rice still feels like a full meal
Skip or scrape off the sweet chilli sauce drizzle, it is basically sugar syrup
Ask them to go light on oil for both the rice and the omelette, easily 100 calories saved

faq.q: Is nasi goreng pattaya more fattening than normal nasi goreng?
faq.a: A bit, yes. The omelette blanket and the extra oil to fry it add roughly 150 to 200 calories over a plain plate. You do get a little more protein from the egg, around 24g, but the calorie cost outweighs it if you are counting.

faq.q: How many calories is the omelette part alone?
faq.a: The egg wrap is about 160 calories, mostly from the two eggs and the oil used to fry the thin omelette. It is the main thing separating pattaya from regular fried rice on the calorie sheet.

faq.q: Can I make nasi goreng pattaya lighter at home?
faq.a: Yes. Use a non-stick pan with minimal oil for the omelette, load the fried rice with more vegetables and less rice, and skip the sweet sauce. You can bring it down near 450 to 500 with the same look and feel.

variants.note: less oil, more veg, no sweet sauce

foods.name: Lor Mee
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of lor mee is about 520 calories. Thick yellow noodles in a starchy dark gravy. The gravy is the real story. Breakdown inside.
foods.summary: Thick noodles in dark starchy gravy, around 520 kcal a bowl.
foods.answer: A bowl of lor mee is around 520 calories. It is thick yellow noodles sitting in a dark, cornstarch-thickened gravy with bits of pork, fish cake, and egg. The noodles and the starchy gravy are the bulk of it, and toppings like fried items or extra egg can push it past 600.
realTalk: The real culprit in lor mee is that seductive thick gravy bro. It looks harmless, like a thin soup, but it is thickened with starch and carries oil and a beaten egg through it, so that brown sauce is quietly a chunk of the 520 calories.

It is not the worst hawker bowl out there honestly, because there is no coconut milk and the protein from pork, egg, and fish cake lands around 20g. The trap is the fried toppings, throw in some fried fish or extra deep-fried bits and you jump to 650 fast.
lighter: Skip the deep-fried toppings, the fried fish and crispy bits are where the extra fat hides
Ask for more of the lean toppings like lean pork and egg, less of the fatty stuff
Add a side of vegetables or beansprouts to bulk the bowl without adding much to the count

faq.q: Is lor mee a healthy hawker choice?
faq.a: It is mid, leaning okay. There is no coconut milk and it gives you around 20g protein, which is decent. The downside is the starchy gravy and any deep-fried toppings. Order it with lean toppings and skip the fried fish and it is a reasonable 450 to 500 calorie bowl.

faq.q: Why is lor mee gravy so high in calories?
faq.a: It is thickened with cornstarch and usually has a beaten egg and some oil stirred through. That makes the dark gravy more than just flavoured water, it is carrying real calories, roughly 130 in a standard bowl.

faq.q: How much protein is in a bowl of lor mee?
faq.a: About 20g from the pork, fish cake, and egg toppings. You can push it higher by asking for extra egg or more lean meat, which also makes the bowl more filling without much added fat.

variants.name: Lean-topping bowl
variants.note: skip fried items, more egg and lean pork

foods.name: Sup Herba (Herbal Chicken Soup)
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of sup herba (herbal chicken soup) is about 300 calories. High protein, low carb, one of the cleaner Malaysian dishes. Breakdown inside.
foods.summary: Herbal chicken soup, about 300 kcal a bowl and high protein.
foods.answer: A bowl of sup herba is around 300 calories. It is chicken simmered in a herbal broth with ingredients like wolfberry, red dates, and dang gui, so you are basically eating lean protein in flavoured water. The protein lands around 28g and the carbs are tiny, which makes this one of the cleaner things you can order.
realTalk: Sup herba is genuinely one of the best things on this whole site bro. It is chicken in a herbal broth, so you get around 28g of protein for only 300 calories, with almost no carbs and no oily gravy to sabotage you. Order this and you are winning.

The only thing to watch is the skin and the fattier chicken parts. If your bowl is loaded with chicken skin and fatty drumstick the fat creeps up, but pick a leaner cut or skim the oil layer on top and this stays a lean, filling, high-protein bowl.
lighter: Go for chicken breast or thigh without skin to keep the fat down, drops it toward 240 calories
Skim the layer of chicken oil floating on top of the broth before you drink it
Pair it with vegetables instead of rice if you want a full meal that stays light

faq.q: Is sup herba good for weight loss?
faq.a: Honestly one of the best picks you can make. Around 28g protein for only 300 calories, low carb, and very filling thanks to the warm broth. Order this over a fried rice any day and your deficit thanks you.

faq.q: Why is herbal chicken soup low in calories?
faq.a: Because it is just chicken and herbs simmered in water. There is no coconut milk, no thickened gravy, no frying. Most of the calories come from the chicken itself, and the broth is basically flavoured water.

faq.q: Does sup herba have enough protein for after the gym?
faq.a: Yes, around 28g in a standard bowl, which is a solid post-workout amount. Add an extra piece of chicken or pair it with rice if you trained hard and need more total food.

foods.name: Teh O Ais
foods.metaDescription: Teh O Ais is about 60 calories a glass and every one of them is sugar. Order it kurang manis and it drops to 30. Full breakdown inside.
foods.summary: Iced black tea with sugar and nothing else. No milk, no condensed milk, which makes it the cheapest thing on most kopitiam drink lists.
foods.answer: A normal glass of teh o ais is around 60 calories, and effectively all of it is the sugar. The tea itself is about 2 calories, the ice is free, and roughly three teaspoons of sugar does the rest. That makes it one of the lightest drinks you can order anywhere in Malaysia. For comparison, teh ais with condensed milk is 150 and teh tarik is 130, so switching to teh o ais saves you 70 to 90 calories per glass without giving up your drink. Ask for kurang manis and you are at about 30. Ask for kosong and you are at 2.
realTalk: Teh o ais is the drink I switched to and never switched back. Teh means tea, O means no milk, ais means iced. That is the whole thing. No condensed milk, no evaporated milk, which is where basically every other kopitiam drink hides its calories. At 60 calories a glass it costs you almost nothing, and you still get something cold and sweet with your food instead of sitting there with plain water feeling sorry for yourself.

The number moves entirely with the sugar, so it depends completely on who is making it. Some stalls pour three teaspoons, some pour five. Five teaspoons puts you at 85 and you would not taste the difference at that point. These are estimates based on typical hawker sweetness, not lab numbers, so treat 60 as a fair middle.

Here is the maths that actually mattered for me. One teh ais a day for a year is about 55,000 calories. Switch to teh o ais and it is 22,000. That gap is roughly 4kg of body fat a year from changing one word in your order. I am not saying it did all the work, but it was the single easiest change I made in the whole 42kg.
lighter: Say kurang manis. Half the sugar takes you from 60 to about 30 calories and after a week you stop noticing.
Say kosong if you are serious. Teh o kosong is 2 calories a glass and it is genuinely fine once your palate adjusts.
Teh o ais over teh ais saves you 90 calories per glass. Same drink family, no milk.
Watch the free refills at banana leaf and nasi kandar places. Three glasses of normal sweet is 180 calories you did not count.
If you want it cold and sweet for almost nothing, add a squeeze of calamansi and go kosong. Flavour for about 10 calories.

variants.name: Teh O Ais kosong
variants.note: No sugar at all. Just tea and ice.

variants.name: Teh O Ais (normal)
variants.note: About three teaspoons of sugar, standard hawker pour

variants.name: Teh O Ais manis
variants.note: Heavy hand on the sugar, five teaspoons or so

variants.name: Teh O Ais Limau
variants.note: Same drink with calamansi lime added

faq.q: How many calories in Teh O Ais?
faq.a: About 60 calories for a standard hawker glass, almost all of it from roughly three teaspoons of sugar. Kurang manis is around 30 and kosong is about 2.

faq.q: Is Teh O Ais good for weight loss?
faq.a: It is one of the best drink swaps available. Teh ais is 150 calories and teh tarik is 130, so ordering teh o ais instead saves you 70 to 90 calories every glass for no real sacrifice. Go kurang manis and you save more.

faq.q: What is the difference between Teh O Ais and Teh Ais?
faq.a: Teh O has no milk. Teh ais has condensed milk, which is where the calories are. Teh o ais is about 60 calories, teh ais is about 150.

foods.name: Cucur Jagung
foods.metaDescription: Cucur jagung is about 120 calories a piece, and half of that is oil the batter soaked up. Nobody eats one. Full breakdown inside.
foods.summary: Sweetcorn folded into a flour batter and deep fried into a fritter. Cheap, hot, sold by the bag at every pasar and warung in the country.
foods.answer: One piece of cucur jagung is around 120 calories for a typical 40g hawker fritter. The batter and corn together are only about 60 of that. The other 60 is cooking oil the fritter absorbed on its way out of the wok, which is the part nobody thinks about. It sounds harmless because it is vegetable and it is small, but these are sold in bags of six or eight, and nobody in recorded history has eaten one cucur jagung. Six pieces is 720 calories, which is a full meal in fritter form.
realTalk: Cucur jagung feels like a safe snack because there is corn in it. The corn is fine. The problem is that a fritter is a sponge, and deep frying is how you get oil into a sponge. Roughly 7g of oil ends up in each piece, which is 60 calories on its own, so the fritter is about half oil by calories before you count the batter.

The real damage is the format. These are sold hot in a bag by the half dozen for a couple of ringgit. You buy a bag on the way home, you eat them in the car, and 720 calories are gone before you have parked. That is not a snack, that is dinner. If you ate a proper meal and then had the bag, you are 700 calories over for the day and you will not have registered eating anything.

Numbers here are estimates against a normal 40g hawker piece. Some stalls make them small and thin, some make them the size of your palm and soak them properly. A big greasy one is closer to 180 than 120, so use your eyes.
lighter: Buy by the piece, not by the bag. Two is 240 calories and it is a genuine snack. Six is a meal.
Take them off the pile that has been sitting and draining rather than straight out of the wok. Less oil clinging to the outside.
Ask for them on paper and blot them. It sounds fussy but it genuinely takes 10 to 20 calories off each piece.
If you want the corn without the oil, jagung rebus or a corn cup is about 330 calories for a big portion and it keeps you full much longer.
Eat them right after a high protein meal, not on an empty stomach at 4pm. You will stop at two instead of eight.

variants.note: Vegetable fritter version, usually with sayur and a little more batter

faq.q: How many calories in Cucur Jagung?
faq.a: About 120 calories for one standard 40g piece. A small pasar piece is nearer 90 and a large palm sized one can hit 180.

faq.q: How many calories in a bag of cucur jagung?
faq.a: A typical bag is six pieces, so around 720 calories. That is a full meal, not a snack, which is the thing worth knowing before you buy one on the way home.

faq.q: Is cucur jagung healthy?
faq.a: There is corn in it, but roughly half the calories are frying oil the batter soaked up. It is a fried snack with vegetables in it, not a vegetable dish. Two pieces fits in most days. Six does not.

foods.name: Bak Chor Mee
foods.metaDescription: A standard dry bowl of bak chor mee is about 511 calories. Here is where the lard, vinegar and mee pok add up, and how to order it lighter.
foods.summary: Bak chor mee is the Singapore hawker bowl of mee pok or mee kia tossed in vinegar, chilli, soy and pork lard, topped with minced pork, sliced pork, liver, mushrooms and a couple of meatballs, with a small soup on the side.
foods.answer: A standard dry bowl of bak chor mee is about 511 calories for a 311g serving, with roughly 23g of fat. The noodles alone are around 230 of those calories, and the lard and chilli dressing is another 90 to 100 before any meat goes in.
realTalk: The number that surprises people is not the pork, it is the dressing. A dry bowl gets a spoon of lard, a spoon of chilli oil, and the crispy lard bits on top. That is about 20g of fat right there, close to 90 calories, and the stall does it before you can say anything. The 150g of mee pok is another 230 calories. Meat, liver, mushrooms and two meatballs together come to only about 170. So a 511 calorie bowl is really 60 percent noodles and oil.

The soup version drops to around 420 calories because there is no lard dressing and the noodles sit in clear broth instead of oil. Same pork, same liver, same mushrooms. If you order dry, you are paying about 90 calories for the vinegar and lard taste. Some people think that is worth it. Just know the trade.

Price matters here too. The S$4 bowl at a normal hawker centre is the 511 calorie one. The S$6 or S$8 bowl at the famous stalls comes with extra meat, an extra ladle of lard and sometimes abalone, and it lands closer to 650 to 700 calories. Bigger bowl, more noodles, more oil. The fancier the stall, the heavier the bowl.
lighter: Order soup instead of dry and you save close to 90 calories from the lard and chilli oil.
Ask for less lard or no lard bits. Most stalls will do it and the bowl drops by 40 to 60 calories.
Get mee kia instead of mee pok. It is thinner and the portion by weight is usually a bit smaller, around 30 calories less.
Eat the pork, liver and meatballs first. About 20g of protein for under 200 calories is the good part of the bowl.
Skip the extra meatball order. Each pork ball is about 35 calories.

portions.label: Large with extra lard and meat

variants.name: Soup version
variants.note: No lard dressing, noodles in clear broth

variants.name: Signature bowl with abalone and extra pork
variants.note: The S$8 to S$10 famous stall bowl

faq.q: Is bak chor mee healthy?
faq.a: It is a decent protein bowl if you go soup. Dry bak chor mee at 511 calories with 23g of fat is heavier than it looks because of the lard dressing. Soup at around 420 with 20g of protein is one of the better hawker lunches.

faq.q: How many calories in bak chor mee soup?
faq.a: About 420 calories for a standard bowl. The noodles are still 230 of that, but there is no lard or chilli oil dressing, which is where the dry version picks up its extra 90 calories.

faq.q: Is mee pok or mee kia lower in calories?
faq.a: Mee kia by a small margin. A mee kia portion is usually 20 to 30g lighter, which is about 30 calories less. The dressing and toppings are identical, so the difference is minor.

faq.q: Can I eat bak chor mee while losing weight?
faq.a: Yes. A 511 calorie bowl fits into most 1,800 to 2,000 calorie days. Order it soup or with less lard, do not add extra meatballs, and it is a normal lunch.

foods.source: HPB iDAT via danielfooddiary.com 2015, KKH dietitians via HealthXchange.sg

foods.name: Kway Chap
foods.serving: 1 set for one (kway in soup + braised platter)
foods.metaDescription: A one person kway chap set is about 650 calories. The rice sheets are light. The braised pork belly, intestines and egg are where it climbs.
foods.summary: Kway chap is the Teochew hawker set of broad rice sheets in a dark herbal soy broth, served with a plate of braised pork belly, intestines, pig skin, tau kwa, tau pok and a braised egg.
foods.answer: A standard one person kway chap set is about 650 calories for a 611g serving, with around 26g of fat. The bowl of kway in broth is only about 190 calories. The braised platter with pork belly, intestines, egg and beancurd is the other 460.
realTalk: The bowl of kway is the cheap part of the calorie bill. 300g of flat rice sheets in braised broth is around 190 calories, and the broth itself adds very little. The plate next to it is the problem. Three slices of braised pork belly are about 250 calories on their own. Add 60g of intestines and pig skin at about 90, a braised egg at 75, and some tau kwa and tau pok at 50, and you are at 650 before you have finished counting.

The pork belly is the swing item. A S$5 set usually comes with 2 to 3 slices. Ask for lean meat or pork shoulder instead and the same set drops to roughly 520 calories. Ask for extra belly and it can pass 850. Nobody weighs it, so what lands on the plate depends on the auntie and how much she likes you.

One honest thing about kway chap. The offal gets blamed, but 60g of braised intestines is about 90 calories, less than one slice of belly. The intestines are mostly protein and some fat. If you like them, keep them. Drop a slice of belly instead and you will save more.
lighter: Ask for lean pork or pork shoulder instead of belly. That alone cuts around 130 calories from a standard set.
Get the kway plain with just tau kwa, egg and one piece of meat. A set like that is about 400 calories.
Skip the extra soup ladle over the platter. The braised sauce is salty and oily, roughly 30 calories per spoon.
Share the S$10 platter between two people and each order your own bowl of kway. Same taste, half the meat.

portions.label: Set with lean pork, no intestines

variants.name: Set with lean pork only
variants.note: Shoulder or lean cut, egg and tau kwa

variants.name: Full platter with pig skin, belly and extra intestines
variants.note: The S$10 to S$12 sharing plate eaten alone

faq.q: Is kway chap fattening?
faq.a: The braised pork belly is. A standard 650 calorie set has 26g of fat and most of it comes from 3 slices of belly. Swap to lean pork and the same set is around 520 calories with half the fat.

faq.q: How many calories in kway chap without meat?
faq.a: The bowl of kway in broth is about 190 calories. Add a braised egg and tau kwa and you are at roughly 310, which is a light meal with about 15g of protein.

faq.q: Are the intestines high in calories?
faq.a: Not really. 60g of braised intestines is about 90 calories. One slice of pork belly is around 85. The intestines are higher in cholesterol, but for calories they are not the main issue.

faq.q: How much protein is in kway chap?
faq.a: A standard set gives about 30g of protein from the pork, egg and beancurd. It is one of the higher protein hawker meals, which is the argument for eating it with the lean cuts.

foods.source: HPB iDAT via danielfooddiary.com 2015, KKH dietitians via HealthXchange.sg

foods.name: Hokkien Prawn Mee (Fried)
foods.metaDescription: A standard plate of Singapore fried Hokkien prawn mee is about 522 calories. Here is what the noodles, lard, egg and sambal each contribute.
foods.summary: Singapore Hokkien mee is yellow noodles and bee hoon fried in a rich prawn and pork stock with egg, prawns, squid and pork belly, finished with lard, lime and a spoon of sambal.
foods.answer: A standard plate of fried Hokkien prawn mee is about 522 calories for a 442g serving, with around 19g of fat. The 200g mix of yellow noodles and bee hoon makes up about 260 calories, and the lard, oil and sambal add another 80.
realTalk: This is the wet, braised style, not the dark KL version, so the calorie count is lower than people expect. A 442g plate has about 200g of noodles, which is 260 calories, then one egg at 75, four prawns at 50, and some squid and pork belly at 70. The stall fries it in lard and finishes it with a spoon of sambal, and that is the last 80. Total around 522, which is under a plate of char kway teow at 742.

The size jump is the real issue. The S$5 plate is the 522 calorie one. The S$8 plate at the popular stalls is not a little bigger, it is about 50 percent bigger, and it comes with more prawns, more lard and an extra egg. That plate is closer to 780 calories. Two people sharing a S$10 plate get about 500 each, which is a sensible way to do it.

The sambal is small but not free. A full spoon of hawker sambal is around 40 calories because it is fried in oil. The lime is free and does more for the taste than the sambal does. Squeeze the lime, use half the sambal, and you have lost nothing you will notice.
lighter: Order the S$5 plate, not the S$8 one. The bigger plate is about 260 calories more.
Ask for no pork lard bits on top. That is around 50 calories of pure fat.
Use half the sambal and all of the lime. Sambal is about 40 calories a spoon, lime is zero.
Share a large plate with one other person and each add a side of vegetables or a boiled egg for protein.
Eat the prawns and squid. They are the lowest calorie part of the plate and give most of the 24g of protein.

variants.name: Large plate with extra prawns
variants.note: S$8 to S$10 famous stall size

variants.name: Opeh leaf sharing plate for 2, eaten alone

faq.q: Is Singapore Hokkien mee healthier than char kway teow?
faq.a: Yes, by a good margin. A standard plate is about 522 calories against 742 for char kway teow. Hokkien mee is braised in stock, so it takes on less oil than a plate fried dry in lard.

faq.q: How many calories in Hokkien mee without the noodles?
faq.a: The prawns, squid, pork and egg together are about 195 calories. The noodles are the bulk of the plate at around 260, plus 80 from lard and sambal.

faq.q: How much protein is in Hokkien prawn mee?
faq.a: Around 24g per standard plate, from the egg, prawns, squid and pork. That is a reasonable amount for a 522 calorie lunch.

faq.q: Is the KL Hokkien mee higher in calories?
faq.a: Yes. KL Hokkien mee is thick noodles braised in dark soy and a lot of lard, at about 720 calories a plate. The Singapore version at 522 is the lighter of the two.

foods.source: HPB iDAT via danielfooddiary.com 2015, KKH dietitians via HealthXchange.sg

foods.name: Prawn Noodle Soup
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of prawn noodle soup is about 294 calories, one of the lightest hawker noodle bowls. The dry version with chilli and lard jumps to 461.
foods.summary: Singapore prawn noodle soup is yellow noodles or bee hoon in a deep prawn head and pork bone broth with prawns, kangkong and bean sprouts, served soup or dry with a side of broth.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of prawn noodle soup is about 294 calories for a 500g bowl, with only 5g of fat. The dry version tossed in chilli, lard and soy is about 461 calories. The 167 calorie difference is almost entirely the dressing.
realTalk: This is one of the best value hawker bowls for anyone counting. 150g of noodles is about 180 calories, five prawns about 60, and the broth, even though it tastes rich, is around 40 calories a bowl because the stall skims most of the fat off. Add kangkong and bean sprouts at 10 and some fried shallots at 15. That is 294 for a full bowl that keeps you full until dinner.

The dry version is a different dish for calorie purposes. Same noodles, same prawns, but tossed in chilli paste, lard, ketchup and soy. That dressing is about 150 to 170 calories, which takes the bowl to 461. The small bowl of broth on the side is still nearly free. So dry prawn mee costs you about 55 percent more than soup for the same amount of food.

Watch the add ons. Pork ribs are the usual upgrade and two ribs add around 150 calories. The S$8 jumbo prawn version is fine, because prawns are lean, and two big prawns are only about 60 calories more. Pig tail and intestines also stay under 100. The rule is simple. Add seafood, not pork fat.
lighter: Order soup, not dry. The dry dressing is about 167 calories for the same bowl.
Choose bee hoon over yellow noodles. It is about 30 calories lighter per bowl and takes less alkaline flavour.
Upgrade with prawns, not pork ribs. Two extra prawns are 30 calories, two ribs are around 150.
Ask for extra kangkong and bean sprouts. Most stalls give it free and it fills the bowl for under 20 calories.
Skip the fried shallots if the stall spoons them on heavily. It is a small saving, about 15 calories, but it is free to skip.

portions.label: Dry version with chilli and lard

variants.name: Dry with jumbo prawns and pork ribs

faq.q: Is prawn noodle soup good for weight loss?
faq.a: It is one of the better hawker choices. At 294 calories with 22g of protein and 5g of fat, a soup bowl is filling for the calories. Order dry and it becomes 461, which is still fine but no longer light.

faq.q: How many calories in dry prawn mee?
faq.a: About 461 calories for a standard bowl. The chilli, lard and soy dressing is about 167 calories on top of the 294 soup version.

faq.q: Is the prawn broth high in calories?
faq.a: No. Most stalls skim the fat, so a bowl of broth is about 40 calories. The richness comes from prawn heads and bones, which flavour the stock without adding much fat.

faq.q: How is Singapore prawn mee different from Penang Hokkien mee?
faq.a: Same idea, different details. Penang Hokkien mee at about 420 calories has a spicier broth with more chilli oil and often a hard boiled egg. The Singapore soup version at 294 is lighter and usually comes without egg.

foods.source: HPB iDAT via danielfooddiary.com 2014

foods.name: Mee Soto
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of mee soto is about 433 calories with a begedil on top, or around 370 without. The yellow noodles are most of it, the soup is light.
foods.summary: Mee soto is the Malay hawker bowl of yellow noodles in a spiced chicken broth with shredded chicken, bean sprouts and fried shallots, usually with a begedil potato patty dropped in and sambal kicap on the side.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of mee soto is about 433 calories for a 500g serving with a begedil. Without the begedil it is around 370 calories. The 180g of yellow noodles is about 230 calories, the chicken about 80, and the turmeric broth only 60.
realTalk: The broth looks oily because of the turmeric and fried shallot oil floating on top, but it is lighter than it looks. 250ml of soto broth is around 60 calories. The yellow noodles are the real weight at 230 calories for 180g. Shredded chicken adds 80, bean sprouts 8, sambal kicap 25 and shallots 20. Without the begedil you are at about 370, which is a good number for a bowl that big.

Then the begedil goes in. One fried potato patty is about 60 to 95 calories depending on the size and how much oil it took on, and most stalls give you one by default. That is the difference between 370 and 433. Two begedil and you are close to 500. The same stall usually sells lontong at 798, so mee soto is the light option on that menu by a long way.

Watch the sambal kicap. It tastes like it should be free because it is mostly chilli and sweet soy, but sweet soy is sugar. Two spoons is about 50 calories. Stir in one spoon, taste, and stop there. The broth already has enough going on.
lighter: Skip the begedil or ask for it on the side and eat half. That is up to 95 calories saved.
Ask for bee hoon instead of yellow noodles if the stall offers it. It is about 40 calories less per bowl.
Use one spoon of sambal kicap, not three. Each spoon of sweet soy chilli is about 25 calories.
Ask for extra chicken. Most stalls charge S$0.50 to S$1 and it adds protein for about 40 calories.
Order soto ayam, the version with rice cubes instead of yellow noodles, if you want it lighter. Same broth, about 60 calories less.

components.name: Bean sprouts, sambal kicap, fried shallots

portions.label: Large with 2 begedil and extra chicken

variants.name: Mee soto with 2 begedil and extra sambal

faq.q: Is mee soto healthy?
faq.a: It is one of the lighter Malay hawker dishes. About 370 calories without the begedil and 433 with it, with around 20g of protein from the chicken. The broth is spiced with turmeric and lemongrass, not coconut milk, so it stays low in fat.

faq.q: How many calories in a begedil?
faq.a: One hawker begedil is about 60 to 95 calories depending on size. It is a mashed potato patty fried in oil, so most of the calories come from the potato and the frying oil.

faq.q: Is mee soto lower in calories than mee rebus?
faq.a: Yes. Mee rebus is about 500 calories a plate because of the thick sweet potato gravy. Mee soto sits in clear broth and comes in at 370 to 433 depending on the begedil.

faq.q: Does mee soto have coconut milk?
faq.a: No. The broth is chicken stock with turmeric, galangal, lemongrass and shallots. That is why a 250ml serving of broth is only about 60 calories, compared with 260 for sayur lodeh gravy.

foods.source: HPB iDAT via danielfooddiary.com 2015 (433 with begedil), HealthHub.sg (370 without)

foods.name: Satay Bee Hoon
foods.metaDescription: A plate of satay bee hoon is about 462 calories. Nearly 200 of them are the peanut sauce, which is the whole point of the dish.
foods.summary: Satay bee hoon is a Singapore hawker dish of rice vermicelli, cuttlefish, cockles, pork slices, kangkong and bean sprouts, all covered in a thick spicy peanut satay sauce.
foods.answer: A standard plate of satay bee hoon is about 462 calories for a 350g serving, with around 18g of fat. The 150g of bee hoon is about 165 calories and the peanut sauce is close to 190. The cuttlefish, cockles and pork add under 110 together.
realTalk: The satay sauce is the dish, and it is also 40 percent of the calories. A hawker ladle is about 80g of ground peanuts, oil, chilli, sugar and tamarind, which is roughly 190 calories. The bee hoon underneath is 165 for 150g. Everything else on the plate is light. Cuttlefish and cockles are around 50 calories for 50g, the pork slices 55, and the kangkong and bean sprouts about 10. A 462 calorie plate that is mostly sauce and noodles.

Bee hoon is the noodle that helps you here. It is thin rice vermicelli, so a full plate by volume weighs less than the same plate of yellow noodles. If this were satay yellow mee it would be closer to 520. The stall is doing you a favour without meaning to.

The problem is extra sauce. It is normal to ask for more because the plate dries out fast, and a second ladle is another 190 calories. A S$5 plate with extra sauce and extra cuttlefish lands at about 600. If you want more flavour, ask for more chilli, which is 10 calories, not more sauce.
lighter: Ask for less sauce or sauce on the side. Half a ladle saves about 95 calories.
Ask for extra kangkong and bean sprouts. Most stalls will add them for free and it stretches the sauce for under 20 calories.
Add cuttlefish or cockles rather than pork slices. Seafood is about 1 calorie per gram, pork slices closer to 2.
Skip the tau pok if the stall adds it. Fried beancurd puffs soak up sauce and are about 30 calories each.
Eat it with a plain soup on the side rather than a sweet drink. A kopi c is 87 calories, a canned drink is 140.

portions.label: Large with extra sauce and cuttlefish

variants.name: Extra sauce and extra cuttlefish
variants.note: The usual S$5 to S$6 upgrade

faq.q: How many calories in satay sauce?
faq.a: About 190 calories per hawker ladle of roughly 80g. It is ground peanuts, oil, sugar, chilli and tamarind, so most of the calories are peanut fat with some sugar.

faq.q: Is satay bee hoon healthy?
faq.a: It is a middle of the road hawker plate at 462 calories with 18g of protein. The peanut sauce carries most of the fat. It is better than fried noodles like char kway teow at 742, but not as light as a soup.

faq.q: Is satay bee hoon the same as the satay skewers?
faq.a: Same sauce, different dish. Satay skewers are grilled meat at about 50 calories a stick. Satay bee hoon is noodles and seafood under the same peanut sauce, and a plate is around 462.

faq.q: Can I eat satay bee hoon on a diet?
