realTalk: Mung beans are the good part. 60g of cooked split mung beans is about 100 calories with 7g of protein and a fair amount of fibre. The soup is where it gets sweet. It is water, sugar, sweet potato starch and pandan, thickened until it coats the spoon, about 100 calories for 200ml, nearly all sugar. Then the you tiao, cut into pieces and dropped on top, about 95 for the usual half pair. That is 293 for a dessert most people think of as light because it is not coconut based.

It is still one of the lighter hawker desserts. Cheng tng is about 160, tau suan 293, bubur cha cha 360, and the coconut based ones like pulut hitam with santan are around 290 as well. The difference is where the calories come from. Tau suan is sugar and fried dough on a base of beans. Bubur cha cha is coconut milk. Neither is a problem once a week. Both are a problem after a 700 calorie lunch.

The you tiao is optional and the stall will leave it out. Without it a bowl is about 200 calories, and with a small spoon of you tiao on top rather than the full handful it is about 240. The beans are the same. If the stall uses less starch and the soup is thinner, that is another 20 to 30 saved without asking.
lighter: Order it without you tiao. That is about 95 calories gone and the beans and soup are unchanged.
Ask for less sugar. Most Teochew dessert stalls will do it and it saves about 40.
Order the small bowl. The S$1.50 bowl is about 220 with you tiao, the S$2.50 bowl is 293.
Choose cheng tng if it is on the same menu and you want something even lighter, at about 160.
Have it as an afternoon snack rather than after dinner. On its own it is a 293 calorie snack with 8g of protein, which is reasonable.

variants.name: Tau suan, no you tiao, less sugar
Tau suan with a full pair of you tiao

faq.q: How many calories in tau suan?
faq.a: About 293 calories for a standard bowl with you tiao. Without the you tiao it is about 200. The split mung beans are around 100 of that and the sweet soup about 100.

faq.q: Is tau suan healthy?
faq.a: It is one of the better hawker desserts. Mung beans give about 8g of protein and some fibre, and there is no coconut milk, so the fat is around 5g. The sugar in the soup, about 25g, is the main downside.

faq.q: Is tau suan or cheng tng lower in calories?
faq.a: Cheng tng at about 160 is lower. Tau suan at 293 has the starch thickened soup and the you tiao. Without you tiao, tau suan is about 200, closer to cheng tng.

faq.q: What is tau suan made of?
faq.a: Split mung beans, steamed until soft, in a soup of water, sugar and sweet potato starch with pandan leaf. It is served warm with pieces of you tiao on top.

foods.source: HPB iDAT via danielfooddiary.com 2015

foods.name: Oyster Omelette
foods.metaDescription: A hawker plate of oyster omelette is about 487 calories, and a large one about 645. The oysters are the smallest number on the plate. The oil is the biggest.
foods.summary: Orh luak is the Singapore hawker plate of eggs and a sweet potato starch batter fried in a lot of oil until crisp at the edges and gooey in the middle, with small oysters folded in at the end, served with a garlic chilli dip.
foods.answer: A standard plate of oyster omelette is about 487 calories for a 250g serving, with around 32g of fat. A large plate is about 645. The eggs are about 190 calories, the frying oil about 180, the starch batter 60, and the oysters themselves only about 45.
realTalk: The oysters are almost irrelevant to the number. 60g of small oysters is about 45 calories and 6g of protein. What makes orh luak 487 is the cooking. Two and a half eggs at 190 go into a wok with about 20g of oil, which is 180 on its own, and the starch batter that makes the crispy, sticky texture is another 60. The chilli dip is 12. So about two thirds of the plate is egg and oil, and the oysters are a garnish with a name.

The HPB numbers show the size problem. The 2014 survey put a plate at 487. The 2015 one, with a bigger plate from a different stall, put it at 645. That is the same dish and a 158 calorie gap, because the stall used more egg, more batter and more oil to fill a bigger plate. A S$6 plate is the first number. A S$10 plate is the second. There is no version of this dish where the cooking is light.

The crispy style takes more oil than the gooey style. Crispy orh luak is fried longer in more oil until the batter is like a lacy cracker, and it lands nearer 600 for a standard plate. The wetter, softer style with more egg and less batter is closer to the 487. If you have a choice, the messy looking one is the lighter one.
lighter: Order the small plate. The S$6 plate at 487 against the S$10 plate at 645 is the biggest single decision.
Ask for less oil. Some stalls will, and it takes off 60 to 90 calories.
Choose the soft style over the crispy style. Less time in the oil means less oil in the plate.
Share it. Half a plate at 245 with a bowl of soup or rice is a normal meal with 10g of protein.
Ask for extra oysters. They are about 8 calories each and they are the part you came for.

faq.q: How many calories in oyster omelette?
faq.a: About 487 calories for a standard hawker plate and about 645 for a large one. Around 180 of that is frying oil and 190 is egg. The oysters are only about 45.

faq.q: Is oyster omelette healthy?
faq.a: Not in the hawker form. It has 20g of protein from the eggs and oysters, which is fine, but 32g of fat from the oil and 30g of starch. It is a share plate, not a personal meal.

faq.q: Why is orh luak so oily?
faq.a: The starch batter needs a lot of oil to crisp up and not stick to the wok. Stalls use about 20g of oil per plate, which is 180 calories, more than the oysters and batter combined.

faq.q: How much protein is in oyster omelette?
faq.a: About 20g per standard plate, mostly from two and a half eggs. The 60g of oysters adds about 6g. It is a reasonable protein number for a plate that is 487 calories.

foods.source: HPB iDAT via danielfooddiary.com 2014 (487) and 2015 (645, larger plate)

foods.name: BBQ Chicken Wings
foods.metaDescription: Two hawker BBQ chicken wings are about 196 calories, so 98 each. Six wings with the chilli and lime is about 600. The chilli is what keeps you eating.
foods.summary: BBQ chicken wings are the charcoal grilled, soy and honey marinated whole wings sold by the piece at Singapore hawker centres, especially East Coast Lagoon and Chomp Chomp, with a green chilli and lime dip.
foods.answer: Two hawker BBQ chicken wings are about 196 calories for a 110g serving, with around 17g of protein and 13g of fat. Each wing is about 98 calories. The marinade of soy, honey and oil adds about 25 of that, and the chilli dip is nearly free.
realTalk: A chicken wing is about half skin and bone by weight, which is why two whole wings at 110g is only about 100g of edible meat and skin. Grilled over charcoal, the fat under the skin drips off, and what stays is about 85 calories of meat and skin per wing plus the marinade. The soy, honey and oil glaze is brushed on twice and adds about 13 per wing. So 98 each, 196 for two, with 17g of protein. As a source of protein at a hawker centre, it is one of the more honest options.

The problem is nobody eats two. The stalls sell them at S$1.50 to S$2 each and the normal order at East Coast is five or six per person with a plate of stingray and a beer. Six wings is about 590 calories and 51g of protein. That is not a disaster, but it is a full meal, and the stingray, the satay and the beer come on top of it.

Compared to the other grilled meats on the same row, wings are middle of the pack. A chicken satay stick is about 50, so four sticks with sauce match one wing without the chilli. A grilled stingray with sambal is about 430. A plate of six wings is about the same as the stingray with far more protein. Choose the wings over the sambal sotong if protein is the goal.
lighter: Order three, not six. Three wings is about 295 calories and 26g of protein, a proper protein serving.
Peel off the wing tip skin. It is the crispiest part and the fattiest, about 15 calories per wing.
Use the chilli and lime, not the sweet chilli sauce. The green chilli dip is about 5 calories, the bottled sweet chilli about 30 per spoon.
Pair with a plate of grilled vegetables or a bowl of clear soup rather than fried carrot cake.
Skip the beer. A large Tiger is about 220, more than two wings.

components.name: Chicken wing meat and skin, 2 wings

variants.name: Fried chicken wing
variants.note: Per wing, economy bee hoon stall, for comparison

faq.q: How many calories in one BBQ chicken wing?
faq.a: About 98 calories per hawker grilled wing, or 196 for two. That includes the honey soy marinade. Each wing gives about 8 to 9g of protein.

faq.q: Are BBQ chicken wings healthy?
faq.a: For a hawker centre, yes. Grilling over charcoal lets the fat drip off, and two wings give 17g of protein for under 200 calories. The issue is portion. Six wings is about 600.

faq.q: Is a grilled wing lower in calories than a fried wing?
faq.a: Yes, by a lot. A grilled hawker wing is about 98 calories. A fried wing from an economy bee hoon stall is about 190, because the batter and oil roughly double it.

faq.q: How many calories in chicken wings with rice?
faq.a: Two wings with a plate of white rice is about 520. Three wings with rice about 620. The rice is the bigger number, about 325 for a hawker scoop.

foods.source: HPB iDAT via danielfooddiary.com 2015 (196 per 2 pieces)

foods.name: Black Pepper Crab
foods.metaDescription: A serving of black pepper crab, about half a 1kg mud crab, is around 344 calories.
foods.summary: Black pepper crab is the Singapore seafood restaurant dish of mud crab wok fried in butter with a thick coating of coarse black pepper, garlic, oyster sauce and soy. The drier, spicier sibling of chilli crab, and usually ordered alongside it.
foods.answer: A serving of black pepper crab, about half a 1kg crab with its sauce, is around 344 calories for a 500g shell on portion, with about 24g of protein and 24g of fat. The crab meat itself is about 100 calories. The butter is around 145 and the pepper sauce about 60.
realTalk: A 1kg mud crab gives about 250g of meat once you have fought through the shell, so half a crab is about 120g of meat at roughly 100 calories. Crab meat is lean, about 85 calories per 100g. What you are eating on top of that is the coating. Black pepper crab is fried in a good amount of butter, about 20g per half crab at 145 calories, with oyster sauce, soy and a little sugar for another 60. That is 344 for half a crab. Most of the sauce stays on the shell, which is one of the quiet advantages of this dish.

Chilli crab is about 450 for the same half crab, because the gravy is thickened with egg and has a lot of sugar and tomato sauce, and it is made to be eaten by the spoon with fried mantou. Black pepper crab has no gravy to mop up. The pepper sauce is dry and clings to the shell, and after you have eaten the meat there is nothing left on the plate to drink. That is why it lands about 100 calories lower.

The mantou is the trap for both crabs. A fried mantou bun is about 130 calories and the basket comes with six or eight. Two fried mantou with the crab takes 344 to about 600. The steamed ones are about 80 each. Order steamed, and eat the crab with a plate of stir fried vegetables at about 150 instead of rice, and the whole meal for one person is around 500.
lighter: Choose black pepper over chilli crab. About 100 calories less per half crab, because there is no egg and sugar gravy.
Order steamed mantou, not fried. 80 calories each against 130.
Ask the restaurant to go easy on the butter. Some cze char stalls use margarine or oil instead, and less of it drops the dish to about 280.
Eat the crab with vegetables, not white rice. There is no gravy to justify the rice.
Share a 1kg crab between two people. That is the 344 serving. One person eating a whole crab is around 700 before mantou.

components.name: Crab meat, from half a 1kg crab
Black pepper, oyster sauce, soy and sugar

variants.name: Chilli crab
variants.note: Per half crab, with egg gravy

variants.name: Whole 1kg black pepper crab, eaten alone

faq.q: How many calories in black pepper crab?
faq.a: About 344 calories for half a 1kg crab with its sauce, which is a normal one person share. A whole crab eaten alone is around 690. The crab meat is only about 100 of that, the butter and sauce are the rest.

faq.q: Is black pepper crab healthier than chilli crab?
faq.a: Yes, by about 100 calories per serving. Black pepper crab has no egg and sugar gravy, so it is around 344 per half crab against 450 for chilli crab. Both have about 24g of protein.

faq.q: Is black pepper crab keto?
faq.a: Close to it. A serving has about 6g of carbs, mostly from the oyster sauce and the little sugar in the marinade. Skip the mantou and it fits a low carb meal.

faq.q: How many calories in fried mantou?
faq.a: About 130 calories per fried bun and 80 per steamed bun. The basket of six fried mantou that comes with the crab is around 780 on its own.

foods.source: estimate from components

foods.name: Cereal Prawns
foods.serving: 1 serving (4 to 5 prawns, one share of a cze char plate)
foods.metaDescription: A share of cereal prawns, 4 to 5 prawns with the cereal, is about 330 calories. The full cze char plate is about 600. The crunchy cereal is butter and sugar.
foods.summary: Cereal prawns is the Singapore cze char dish of large prawns deep fried in a light batter, then tossed in a wok with butter, curry leaves, chilli padi and sweetened Nestum cereal until the cereal turns golden and crisp. The cereal is the part everyone scoops up.
foods.answer: One share of cereal prawns, about 4 to 5 prawns with cereal, is about 330 calories for a 150g serving, with around 18g of protein and 18g of fat. A full cze char plate of 8 to 10 prawns is about 600. The prawns are about 90 calories of a share, the cereal 100, and the butter 85.
realTalk: The prawns are not the issue. Five large prawns at 90g of meat is about 90 calories with 18g of protein. Everything they are covered in is. The cereal is Nestum, a sweetened wheat and oat cereal, fried in butter with sugar and sometimes milk powder until it crisps. A share of that cereal is about 100 calories, the butter about 85, and the batter on the prawns plus the curry leaf oil and egg yolk another 50. That is 330 for a portion that fits on a saucer.

The full plate is what arrives at the table. A S$18 to S$25 cze char plate of cereal prawns is 8 to 10 prawns and a generous pile of cereal, about 600 calories. Two people sharing it is 300 each, which is fine. One person eating most of it because it is in front of them, with a bowl of rice at 325, is close to 900 for one dish of a five dish dinner.

The cereal is the thing to watch, and it is the thing everyone fights over. Once the prawns are gone, the crunchy sweet cereal at the bottom of the plate is about 40 calories a spoonful. Three spoons of leftover cereal is 120, the same as a prawn and a half. It is the best part of the dish. It is also butter and sugar in a crunchy shape.
lighter: Eat the prawns, leave the loose cereal at the bottom. That is about 100 calories of butter and sugar you do not need.
Order it as one of five dishes for a table of four, not as your dish. Four prawns is your share.
Ask for prawns without batter if the stall will do it. Some do, and it takes off about 30 calories a share.
Have it with steamed fish or a soup as the other dishes, not butter prawns and salted egg chicken. Those are the same trick three times.
Skip the rice. 325 calories of white rice is more than your share of the prawns.

components.name: Batter, egg yolk, curry leaves, chilli

variants.name: Full plate with rice
variants.note: One person, one dish, one rice

faq.q: How many calories in cereal prawns?
faq.a: About 330 calories for a share of 4 to 5 prawns with cereal, and about 600 for a full cze char plate. The prawns are about 90 of a share. The cereal, butter and batter are the rest.

faq.q: Is cereal prawns healthy?
faq.a: The prawns are, with 18g of protein per share. The cereal coating is Nestum fried in butter and sugar, about 185 calories per share. Eat the prawns, leave the pile of cereal, and it is a decent dish.

faq.q: What cereal is used for cereal prawns?
faq.a: Nestum, the sweetened wheat and oat instant cereal. It is fried in butter with curry leaves and chilli padi, and sometimes milk powder and sugar are added, which is why it tastes like a dessert.

faq.q: Is cereal prawns or butter prawns higher in calories?
faq.a: Butter prawns at about 580 per restaurant portion is heavier, because the egg floss soaks up more butter than the cereal does. Cereal prawns is about 330 per share and 600 per full plate.

foods.source: FatSecret Singapore (330 per serving), full plate estimate from components

foods.name: Pho Bo
foods.metaDescription: A street bowl of pho bo is about 450 calories. Most of it is the rice noodles, the broth is nearly free. Here is the full breakdown with tai, chin and nam.
foods.summary: Flat rice noodles in a clear beef bone broth with sliced beef, onion, and a plate of herbs on the side. Sold from 5am at every street corner in Hanoi and Saigon for 40,000 to 60,000 dong.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of pho bo is about 450 calories for roughly 500g of noodles, beef and broth. Rare beef (tai) lands around 430 and well done brisket (chin) around 455. Order it with fatty brisket, tendon and a side of quay and you are past 700.
realTalk: The 450 calories in a bowl of pho splits about like this: 200g of cooked banh pho noodles is 220, the 80g of beef is 160, and 300ml of broth is only 50 even with the fat floating on top. The herbs, onion and bean sprouts add maybe 10. So half the bowl is noodles. That is the part to control if you want to eat pho five mornings a week without gaining weight.

The beef cut changes the number more than people expect. Tai (rare sliced round) is lean, about 130 calories per 80g. Nam (flank) and gau (fatty brisket) run 200 to 230 for the same weight. A bowl of tai nam gau with a spoon of the rendered fat from the pot is closer to 600. The quay, those fried dough sticks, are 120 to 150 each and most people eat two.

Pho is one of the better street breakfasts if you order it plain. You get 28g of protein, the broth fills you up with almost nothing, and there is no oil beyond what is on the beef. The problem is a 60,000 dong bowl at a busy quan is often 250g of noodles, not 200, and the free refill of broth comes with more fat skimmed from the pot.
lighter: Ask for it bớt bánh (less noodles). That alone drops the bowl from 450 to about 350 with no loss of beef.
Order tai instead of gau or nam. Same protein, 60 to 90 fewer calories per bowl.
Skip the quay. Two sticks are 250 to 300 calories, more than half the pho itself.
Do not add the spoon of fat from the pot that some quan offer. It is 45 calories per teaspoon.
Load up on the herb plate and bean sprouts. They are basically free and slow you down.

portions.label: Large tai nam gau with pot fat

variants.name: Pho dac biet
variants.note: Everything, including tendon and fatty brisket

variants.name: Pho with 2 quay
variants.note: Fried dough sticks add 130 to 150 each

faq.q: Is pho good for weight loss?
faq.a: It can be. A plain bowl is 450 calories with 28g protein and a lot of water volume, which is a reasonable breakfast or lunch. Order less noodles and lean beef and it drops to about 350.

faq.q: How many calories in pho broth alone?
faq.a: About 15 to 20 calories per 100ml, so a full 300ml ladle is around 50. Almost all of it is from fat that rises to the top; skim it and the broth is close to zero.

faq.q: Does pho have a lot of sodium?
faq.a: Yes. One bowl typically carries 1,500 to 2,000mg of sodium from the broth and fish sauce, most of a day's limit. Not a calorie issue but worth knowing if you drink every drop.

faq.q: Pho bo or pho ga, which has fewer calories?
faq.a: Pho ga with breast meat is about 400 versus 450 for pho bo. The difference is small; the noodle portion matters more than the meat choice.

foods.source: Long Chau pharmacy dietitian page (431 tai, 456 chin) and Vinmec; component cross-check

foods.name: Pho Ga
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of pho ga is about 400 calories with shredded breast, closer to 450 with thigh and skin.
foods.summary: The chicken version of pho: rice noodles in a lighter chicken broth with shredded or sliced free range chicken, spring onion and lime leaf. Hanoi does it with skin on and a pile of fried shallots.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of pho ga is around 400 calories, built from 200g of rice noodles, 80g of chicken and 300ml of broth. Shredded breast keeps it near 380; a thigh with the skin on pushes it to about 450. The dry mixed version, pho ga tron, is 500 plus because of the oil and shallots.
realTalk: Pho ga is about 50 calories lighter than pho bo, and the difference is almost entirely the meat. Chicken breast is 110 calories per 80g against 160 for the same weight of beef. The noodles are identical at 220 for 200g, and chicken broth is a little leaner than beef broth, around 45 for the bowl. So you are looking at 400 for a normal quan portion.

The trap is the Hanoi style bowl. Many quan use ga ta, free range chicken, served with skin on and chopped into bone-in pieces. The skin on an 80g portion adds 60 to 80 calories. Then there is the spoonful of fried shallots in oil that goes on top, another 40. Ask for a lot of chicken and you often get 120g instead of 80, which is fine for protein but now the bowl is 480.

Pho ga tron, the dry version tossed in soy, chili oil and fried shallots with the broth on the side, is the one to watch. The dressing is 80 to 100 calories of oil and the noodle portion is usually bigger because there is no broth to fill the bowl. Expect 500 to 550 for the same price.
lighter: Ask for uc (breast) rather than dui (thigh). Same bowl, about 60 fewer calories and more protein.
Skip the skin. Most quan will happily give you skinless if you say khong da.
Order bớt bánh, less noodles. Takes the bowl to about 320.
Stick with the soup version. Pho ga tron adds 100 to 150 calories of dressing.
The lime, chili and herb plate are free. Use them instead of the shallot oil.

faq.q: Is pho ga healthier than pho bo?
faq.a: Marginally. Pho ga is about 400 calories versus 450 for pho bo, with similar protein around 26 to 28g. Both are decent meals if you control the noodles.

faq.q: How much protein is in a bowl of pho ga?
faq.a: About 26g from 80g of chicken plus a little from the broth. Ask for extra chicken and it climbs to 35g for around 480 calories.

faq.q: How many calories in pho ga tron?
faq.a: Roughly 500 to 550. The dry version uses more noodles and a dressing of oil, soy and fried shallots that adds over 100 calories compared with the soup version.

foods.source: FPT Shop health page and Long Chau range (300 to 500 per bowl); component estimate at 400 for breast

foods.name: Bun Cha
foods.metaDescription: A set of bun cha is about 500 calories: 200g bun, 100g grilled pork and the sweet fish sauce bowl. Add one nem cua be and you are at 640.
foods.summary: Charcoal grilled pork patties and slices of belly floating in a bowl of warm sweet and sour fish sauce, with a plate of bun noodles and a basket of herbs on the side. The Hanoi lunch that Obama and Bourdain made famous, 40,000 to 50,000 dong a set.
foods.answer: One set of bun cha is around 500 calories. The 200g of bun is 220, the 100g of grilled pork patties and belly is about 230, and the bowl of dipping sauce adds 40 once you count the sugar. Most people add a nem cua be, which is another 140.
realTalk: Bun cha sits at 500 calories for a standard set, and the split is roughly half noodles, half pork. The 200g plate of bun is 220 calories on its own. The pork is where the fat is: a normal quan gives you two or three patties of minced pork shoulder plus three or four slices of grilled belly, 100g in total and about 230 calories because belly is 30 percent fat and the patties are mixed with fat too.

The dipping bowl looks innocent because it is mostly liquid, but it is fish sauce, water, vinegar and around 10g of sugar, so 40 calories before you count the pork fat that drips into it off the grill. Most people drink or spoon the whole thing. The green papaya and carrot slices in it are the only free part.

The real number for most people is not 500. It is 640 to 780, because nem cua be (the square fried crab spring roll) is 140 calories each and quan sell them in pairs. A set with two nem and a second plate of bun, which the owner will bring without asking at a busy place, is over 850 calories for one lunch.
lighter: Skip the nem cua be. Each one is about 140 calories, mostly from frying oil.
Ask for cha bam (patties) only and leave the belly slices. Saves around 80 calories.
Do not accept the free noodle refill. The first plate of 200g is already 220 calories.
Eat the herb basket: perilla, lettuce, mint, all free and they fill you up.
Dip rather than drown. Spoon a little sauce over the noodles instead of drinking the bowl.

faq.q: How many calories are in bun cha with nem?
faq.a: About 640 with one nem cua be and 780 with two. The nem are deep fried and run 140 calories each, so they change the meal more than the pork does.

faq.q: Is bun cha healthy?
faq.a: It is a fair meal at 500 calories with 28g protein and a lot of fresh herbs. The downsides are the belly fat and the sugar in the sauce. Order patties only and it is a decent lunch.

faq.q: What is the difference between bun cha and bun thit nuong?
faq.a: Bun cha is the Hanoi version with pork served in a bowl of warm dipping sauce; bun thit nuong is the Saigon version with grilled pork on top of noodles and sauce poured over. Both land around 480 to 500 calories.

faq.q: How much sugar is in the bun cha sauce?
faq.a: A typical bowl uses about 10g of sugar per serving, roughly 40 calories, plus whatever fat drips in from the grilled pork.

foods.source: Long Chau pharmacy page (452 per set) and Pharmacity (400 to 500); component cross-check

foods.name: Bun Bo Hue
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of bun bo Hue is about 630 calories, nearly 200 more than pho. The pork hock, chili oil and thick bun are why.
foods.summary: Thick round rice noodles in a lemongrass and shrimp paste beef broth stained red with chili oil, topped with beef shank, a slab of pork hock, cubes of pig blood and crab paste cake. Hue's answer to pho, and a lot heavier.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of bun bo Hue is around 630 calories, with some quan serving bowls closer to 700. The 220g of thick bun is 240, the beef shank and pork hock together are about 300, and the chili oil floating on the broth is 30 to 60 on its own. It is about 180 calories more than a bowl of pho bo.
realTalk: Bun bo Hue is the heaviest of the big Vietnamese noodle soups, and three things drive the 630 calories. The noodles are thicker and the portion is bigger than pho, so 220g of bun is 240 calories. The gio heo, that slice of pork hock with the skin and fat attached, is 200 calories for an 80g piece. And the broth is finished with sate, chili fried in oil, which is 45 calories per tablespoon and every bowl gets at least one.

The beef itself is the healthy part. A 60g portion of sliced shank is about 100 calories and mostly protein. The cha cua (crab and pork paste) cube is 60, and the huyet (blood cubes) are almost nothing, maybe 20 for a couple of pieces. So if you removed the pork hock and skipped the chili oil, the bowl would be closer to 400.

A bowl dac biet at a good Hue quan comes with everything: shank, hock, blood, cha cua, sometimes a piece of beef tendon, and a second spoon of sate. That is 750 to 800 calories, and the broth is salty enough that you will drink a lot of it. The 45,000 dong price makes it feel like a light meal. It is not.
lighter: Order it khong gio, without the pork hock. That one piece is about 200 calories.
Ask for it it cay, less chili oil. Each tablespoon of sate is 45 calories.
Get bớt bún, less noodles. Drops the bowl by about 80.
Leave the top layer of broth. The oil floats, so the bottom half is far leaner.
Eat the banana blossom and bean sprouts on the side plate. They add crunch for nearly zero calories.

components.name: Crab paste cake and blood cubes

portions.label: Dac biet with extra hock and sate

faq.q: Is bun bo Hue higher in calories than pho?
faq.a: Yes, by a lot. A standard bowl is about 630 versus 450 for pho bo. The pork hock, the thicker noodles and the chili oil account for the difference.

faq.q: How much fat is in bun bo Hue?
faq.a: Around 28g per bowl, more than double a bowl of pho. Most of it comes from the pork hock skin and the sate chili oil on the broth.

faq.q: Can I eat bun bo Hue on a diet?
faq.a: Yes if you order it without the pork hock and with less chili oil, which brings it to about 450 with 30g of protein. As a standard bowl it is a full meal's worth of calories.

faq.q: How much sodium is in a bowl?
faq.a: Around 2,000mg, similar to pho. The shrimp paste and fish sauce in the broth push it high, so do not drink the whole bowl if that matters to you.

foods.source: Long Chau and Bazaar Vietnam (637 medium bowl, range 500 to 700)

foods.name: Bun Thit Nuong
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of bun thit nuong is about 480 calories. The grilled pork is 170, the bun 215, and the peanuts and scallion oil quietly add 45.
foods.summary: A Saigon lunch bowl: cold bun vermicelli, lettuce and herbs underneath, charcoal grilled pork slices on top, finished with crushed peanuts, scallion oil, pickled carrot and a pour of sweet fish sauce. Usually 35,000 to 45,000 dong.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of bun thit nuong is around 480 calories. The 200g of bun is 215, the 80g of grilled pork is about 170, and the sauce, peanuts and mo hanh (scallion oil) add another 95 between them. Order it with a cha gio on top and the bowl is 620.
realTalk: The 480 calories in bun thit nuong is fairly evenly spread, which is why people underestimate it. Nothing on the bowl looks heavy. The bun is 215 for 200g. The pork is thin sliced shoulder marinated in sugar, fish sauce and lemongrass, then grilled, so 80g is about 170 with the sugar glaze. The mo hanh spoon on top is 30 to 40 on its own, the peanuts are 15, and the sweet nuoc cham you pour over is around 40.

The marinade is the hidden bit. Vietnamese grilled pork gets a lot of sugar or honey in the marinade, which is what makes it caramelise on the charcoal. A quan may use 10g of sugar per portion of meat, another 40 calories that does not show up as fat. Combined with the sauce, one bowl can carry 20g of sugar.

The standard order in most Saigon quan is bun thit nuong cha gio, with one or two fried spring rolls chopped on top. Each cha gio is 130 to 140 calories, so the popular version of this bowl is really 620 to 750, not 480. Add the second ladle of sauce that comes when the bowl gets dry and you are at a full dinner's worth.
lighter: Order it without cha gio. Each roll is about 135 calories of oil and wrapper.
Ask them to hold the mo hanh. The scallion oil is 30 to 40 calories a spoon.
Pour half the nuoc cham and taste before adding more. Most of the sugar is in the sauce.
Ask for extra rau (herbs and lettuce). It is free and makes the bowl bigger.
Extra pork is a better upgrade than extra bun: 40g more pork is 85 calories and adds 10g of protein.

variants.name: Bun thit nuong 2 cha gio, extra sauce

faq.q: How many calories in bun thit nuong cha gio?
faq.a: About 620 with one cha gio and 750 with two. The spring rolls are the biggest single add-on at roughly 135 calories each.

faq.q: Is bun thit nuong healthy?
faq.a: It is a decent balanced bowl at 480 calories with 24g of protein and a lot of raw vegetables. The sugar in the marinade and sauce is the main downside, around 20g per bowl.

faq.q: Bun thit nuong vs bun cha, which is lighter?
faq.a: They are close: about 480 for bun thit nuong and 500 for bun cha. Bun cha has more fat from the belly slices; bun thit nuong has more sugar from the marinade and sauce.

foods.source: Bazaar Vietnam and Long Chau (470 to 500 per full bowl)

foods.name: Hu Tieu Nam Vang
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of hu tieu Nam Vang is about 400 calories per Vinmec. The dry version with the sauce and fried garlic is closer to 480.
foods.summary: Chewy tapioca and rice noodles in a clear pork bone broth with minced pork, sliced pork, a prawn, a slice of liver and a quail egg on top. The Saigon breakfast that came via Phnom Penh, 35,000 to 50,000 dong.
foods.answer: A bowl of hu tieu Nam Vang is about 400 calories according to Vinmec, with 180g of noodles making up 200 of that and the mixed pork, prawn, liver and quail egg toppings about 140. The dry version (hu tieu kho) with soy, oil and fried garlic tossed through is closer to 480.
realTalk: Hu tieu Nam Vang is one of the lighter noodle soups in Saigon at about 400 calories, and it is a decent protein bowl because of the mixed toppings. The 180g of hu tieu noodles is 200 calories. The toppings are a spoon of minced pork, three or four slices of lean pork, one or two prawns, a slice of liver and a quail egg, about 90g together and 140 calories. The broth is clear pork bone stock, around 50 for 300ml.

The version matters. Vinmec lists plain hu tieu thit heo at 351 calories, Nam Vang at 400, hu tieu mi (with egg noodles mixed in) at 410, hu tieu bo kho at 538 and hu tieu xao (stir fried) at 646. The dry hu tieu kho is not on their list but the dressing of dark soy, sugar, pork fat and fried garlic adds about 80 calories over the soup version.

The thing that makes hu tieu bigger than the number suggests is the free bowl of broth that comes with the dry version and the pile of fried garlic in oil on top. At a busy quan the topping bowl of toi phi (fried garlic) sits on the table and people spoon it on freely. One tablespoon is around 50 calories. Two spoons of that plus a squeeze of chili sauce and the 400 calorie bowl is 520.
lighter: Stick to the soup version. Hu tieu kho adds about 80 calories of dressing.
Go easy on the fried garlic bowl on the table. One tablespoon is about 50 calories.
Ask for extra lean pork or prawns instead of extra noodles. Better protein for the calories.
Skip the hu tieu mi option. Mixing egg noodles in adds noodles, not toppings.
The bean sprouts, chives and lettuce on the side plate are free. Eat all of them.

components.name: Minced pork, sliced pork, prawn, liver, quail egg

portions.label: Hu tieu kho with extra toppings

variants.name: Hu tieu Nam Vang
variants.note: Mixed pork, prawn, liver, quail egg

variants.name: Hu tieu kho (dry)
variants.note: Soy and pork fat dressing, broth on the side

faq.q: How many calories in hu tieu kho?
faq.a: About 480 for the dry version. The soup version is 400; the difference is the dressing of dark soy, sugar, pork fat and fried garlic tossed through the noodles.

faq.q: Is hu tieu healthier than pho?
faq.a: Slightly. Hu tieu Nam Vang is about 400 calories versus 450 for pho bo, with similar protein around 26 to 28g. Both are reasonable meals.

faq.q: What is in hu tieu Nam Vang?
faq.a: Tapioca rice noodles, minced pork, sliced pork, prawn, pork liver, a quail egg and clear pork bone broth, topped with chives, fried garlic and bean sprouts.

faq.q: How many calories in hu tieu go?
faq.a: The cheaper street cart version with just noodles, a little pork and broth is around 350 calories for a smaller bowl.

foods.source: Vinmec hospital (400 per bowl Nam Vang; variants 351 to 646)

foods.name: Mi Quang
foods.metaDescription: A medium bowl of mi Quang is about 415 calories; a large one at a Da Nang quan can hit 680. The turmeric noodles, peanuts and rice cracker explained.
foods.summary: Wide yellow turmeric rice noodles with just a ladle of rich broth, not a soup, topped with pork, prawns, a quail egg, crushed peanuts and a toasted sesame rice cracker. The signature of Quang Nam and Da Nang, 30,000 to 40,000 dong.
foods.answer: A medium bowl of mi Quang is around 415 calories. Because there is only 100ml of broth, most of the weight is 150g of noodles (190 calories) and about 70g of pork and prawn (110). The peanuts and rice cracker on top are 65 more. A large bowl at a Da Nang quan can reach 680.
realTalk: Mi Quang is a dry-ish noodle bowl, which changes the math compared with pho. The 100ml of broth is concentrated and cooked with annatto oil and pork fat, so it is 40 calories for a small ladle even though there is hardly any of it. The 150g of turmeric noodles is 190. The pork and prawn topping, usually a piece of pork belly or rib and two prawns, is about 110 for 70g. The bowl is 415 in total for a medium portion.

Two toppings are easy to forget. The crushed roasted peanuts are about 30 calories for a tablespoon and the banh trang me, the black sesame rice cracker you crumble into the bowl, is another 35 for one cracker. Some quan give you two crackers. They are the reason a bowl that looks like noodles and broth reaches 415 rather than 350.

The size difference between quan is huge with this dish. A small bowl from a street stall in Hoi An is about 320. A large bowl at a sit-down quan in Da Nang with an extra rib, three prawns and a whole chicken thigh (mi Quang ga) can be 600 to 680. The published range of 300 to 500 covers the common sizes; the big bowls go past it.
lighter: Ask for one rice cracker only, or none. Each one is about 35 calories.
Mi Quang ga with breast meat is the leanest topping, about 400 for a medium bowl.
Skip the extra ladle of broth. It is cooked with annatto oil and is 40 calories per 100ml.
Choose prawn over pork belly if given the option. Same weight, half the calories.
The banana blossom, herbs and lettuce underneath are free. Mix them through instead of asking for more noodles.

portions.label: Large Da Nang bowl, extra rib and prawns

variants.name: Mi Quang tom thit (prawn and pork)
Mi Quang dac biet
variants.note: Everything plus quail eggs and extra cracker

faq.q: Is mi Quang high in calories?
faq.a: A medium bowl is about 415 calories, similar to pho, but large bowls with extra rib and prawns can reach 680. Portion size varies more than with other noodle dishes.

faq.q: Why is mi Quang yellow?
faq.a: The noodles are made with turmeric and the broth is cooked with annatto seed oil. The turmeric adds nothing to the calories; the annatto oil adds about 40 per ladle of broth.

faq.q: How many calories in mi Quang ga?
faq.a: About 400 for a medium bowl with chicken, marginally less than the prawn and pork version because chicken is leaner than pork belly.

foods.source: FPT Shop health and Long Chau (415 medium, 680 large, range 300 to 500)

foods.name: Bun Rieu
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of bun rieu cua is about 480 calories, per the Vietnam National Institute of Nutrition figure of 465 to 500.
foods.summary: Rice vermicelli in a tomato broth made from pounded freshwater paddy crab, with a floating raft of crab and egg paste, fried tofu cubes, blood cubes and sometimes a pork hock. A Hanoi morning staple sold from tiny alley stalls for 30,000 to 40,000 dong.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of bun rieu cua is around 480 calories, in line with the National Institute of Nutrition estimate of 465 to 500 for a 300g bowl of noodles and toppings plus broth. The 200g of bun is 220, the crab paste raft and fried tofu are 130 together, and the tomato broth cooked with annatto oil adds 70.
realTalk: Bun rieu looks lighter than pho because it is a tomato soup, but the broth is where the calories hide. The rieu cua, pounded paddy crab, is simmered with tomato and then finished with annatto seeds fried in oil, which gives the red colour. That oil is 40 to 50 calories a bowl, and the 300ml of broth ends up around 70. The 200g of bun is 220, the biggest chunk.

The toppings vary by quan and each one adds. The crab and egg raft is about 80 calories for a 60g piece. Two cubes of fried tofu are 50. Huyet, the blood cubes, are close to zero. Cha (pork paste) or gio (pork hock) add 60 to 140 depending on which and how many. A basic Hanoi bowl is 400; a Saigon style bun rieu with tofu, cha, hock and a snail or two is 620.

Then there is the mam tom. A teaspoon of fermented shrimp paste stirred into the broth is only 10 calories but it makes you drink every last spoonful, which means all the annatto oil goes in. And the basket of shredded morning glory, banana blossom and perilla that comes with it is free, so at least the volume is on your side.
lighter: Ask for it khong dau phu, no fried tofu. Two cubes are about 50 calories.
Skip the gio heo (pork hock) add-on, which is another 140 or so.
Leave the last third of the broth. The annatto oil floats and collects at the top.
Order bớt bún. Dropping to 150g of noodles saves about 55 calories.
Fill the bowl with the free morning glory and banana blossom before the noodles run out.

components.name: Crab paste raft and fried tofu
Tomato crab broth with annatto oil

faq.q: How many calories in bun rieu cua?
faq.a: About 480 for a standard bowl. The National Institute of Nutrition puts a 300g bowl of noodles and toppings plus broth at 465 to 500, and some Saigon style bowls with extra toppings run to 530 or more.

faq.q: Is bun rieu good for weight loss?
faq.a: It is a reasonable meal at 480 calories with 24g of protein and a lot of vegetables in the side basket. Skip the fried tofu and pork hock and it drops to about 400.

faq.q: Does bun rieu contain a lot of fat?
faq.a: Around 20g per bowl. The fried tofu and the annatto oil in the broth are the main sources; the crab itself is lean.

foods.source: Huggies VN quoting Vietnam National Institute of Nutrition (465 to 500 per 300g bowl); Bach Hoa Xanh (530 full bowl)

foods.name: Banh Canh Cua
foods.metaDescription: A full bowl of banh canh cua is about 520 calories. The thick tapioca noodles and starchy broth do most of it; the crab is the lean part.
foods.summary: Fat, chewy tapioca noodles in a thick, gluey pork and crab broth coloured with annatto, topped with crab meat, a whole crab claw, fish cake, quail eggs and fried shallots. A Saigon evening bowl, 45,000 to 70,000 dong depending on how much crab.
foods.answer: A full bowl of banh canh cua is around 520 calories. The 180g of thick tapioca noodles is 265, the thickened broth is about 120 because it is made with tapioca starch and pork fat, and the crab, fish cake and quail eggs add about 135 together. A basic bowl without the extras is closer to 380.
realTalk: Banh canh is heavier than it looks because of the noodle itself. Banh canh strands are tapioca and rice, thick like udon, and they hold water without absorbing broth, so a 180g portion is 265 calories, about 20 percent more than the same weight of bun. The broth is the other surprise: it is thickened with tapioca starch until it coats the noodles, and 250ml of it is around 120 calories. Together that is 385 before any topping.

The crab is the good news. Real crab meat is 100 calories per 100g, so the 40g you get in a normal bowl is only 40 calories and mostly protein. The claw is decorative, maybe 15 calories of meat inside. The fish cake slice is 55 for 30g, and two quail eggs are 35. So a basic bowl is 380 and a full one with everything is 520; the published figures span exactly that range.

What pushes it past 600 is the extras that Saigon quan pile on. Cha (pork paste), a piece of gio heo, extra crab at 20,000 dong a scoop, and a tablespoon of fried shallots that is 40 calories on its own. A bowl dac biet with a crab claw, two kinds of cha and hock is 640 and it comes with a bread roll to mop up the broth, another 190.
lighter: Order the basic bowl with crab and quail eggs only. About 380 versus 520 for the full version.
Ask for it it nuoc, less broth. The thickened broth is 120 calories per bowl.
Skip the bread roll on the side. One roll is around 190 calories.
Extra crab is a better add-on than extra cha: 40g of crab is 40 calories, 40g of pork paste is 70.
Go easy on the fried shallots. One tablespoon is about 40 calories.

portions.label: Basic bowl, crab and quail egg
Dac biet with claw, cha and hock

faq.q: How many calories in a bowl of banh canh cua?
faq.a: About 380 for a basic bowl and 520 for a full one with crab, fish cake and quail eggs. The thick tapioca noodles and starchy broth make up most of it.

faq.q: Is banh canh higher in calories than pho?
faq.a: Yes. A full banh canh cua is around 520 versus 450 for pho bo, mainly because the thick noodles are denser and the broth is thickened with starch.

faq.q: Is banh canh cua healthy?
faq.a: It has decent protein at 26g and the crab is lean, but the bowl is high in refined starch from both the noodles and the thickened broth. Fine as a meal, not as a snack.

foods.source: Bazaar Vietnam (380 basic bowl) and Lemon8 component table (560 full bowl); chose 520 as a standard Saigon quan bowl

foods.name: Bun Dau Mam Tom
foods.metaDescription: A single met of bun dau mam tom is about 700 calories, and the full one with cha com, pork and offal can hit 1,000. The fried tofu is the reason.
foods.summary: A bamboo tray of pressed bun noodle cakes, golden deep fried tofu, boiled pork belly, cha com (green rice pork sausage), herbs and a bowl of fermented shrimp paste whipped with lime, sugar and hot oil. Hanoi's lunch on a plastic stool, 35,000 to 60,000 dong.
foods.answer: A standard single met of bun dau mam tom is around 700 calories. The 200g of bun is 220, the 90g of deep fried tofu is 210, the cha com is 110 and the boiled pork belly is 120, with the mam tom dip and its spoon of hot oil adding 30. A full met with lòng (offal), dồi (blood sausage) and extra cha com goes to 1,000.
realTalk: People think of bun dau as a light tofu lunch. It is 700 calories for one person, and the tofu is the problem, not the pork. Deep fried tofu absorbs oil: 90g of fried dau comes out at around 210 calories, more than the 50g of boiled pork belly at 120. The cha com, a pork sausage mixed with young green rice and then fried, is 110 for two pieces. The pressed bun is 220 for 200g.

The mam tom bowl is 30 to 40 calories, which is nothing, but it is mixed with a spoon of the hot oil from the tofu pan to make it foam. That is what you are tasting. Some quan add a full tablespoon, 90 calories, and if you dip every piece of tofu and bun you get all of it. The herbs, cucumber and perilla on the tray are the only free part.

The real order at most Hanoi quan is the met day du, the full tray, for two people to share. It adds lòng (boiled intestine), dồi (blood sausage), cha quay (fried pork) and sometimes a fried nem. Split in two, each person eats 900 to 1,000 calories. The quan will also refill the tofu without asking if the tray looks empty. Each refill of three cubes is about 100.
lighter: Ask for dau it chien, tofu fried briefly, or half the tofu. Each fried cube is about 70 calories.
Order bun dau thit luoc only, tofu and boiled pork, and skip cha com and dồi. About 550.
Mix your mam tom without the oil. Ask for khong mo and squeeze extra lime instead.
Eat all the cucumber and herbs first. They fill you up for close to zero.
Do not accept the tofu refill. Three more cubes is another 100 calories.

components.name: Mam tom with oil and sugar

portions.label: Basic bun dau (tofu and pork only)
Full met with offal and blood sausage

variants.name: Met day du (full tray, per person)

faq.q: How many calories in bun dau mam tom?
faq.a: About 700 for a standard single tray with tofu, pork belly and cha com. Published estimates range from 465 for a basic tray to 800 or more for the full version.

faq.q: Is bun dau mam tom healthy?
faq.a: It has good protein at 32g but is high in fat at 40g, almost all from the deep fried tofu and cha com. Ordering tofu and boiled pork only brings it to a reasonable 550.

faq.q: How many calories in fried tofu?
faq.a: About 230 per 100g once fried, versus 80 for the same weight of plain tofu. The oil absorbed during frying nearly triples it.

faq.q: Does mam tom have calories?
faq.a: The shrimp paste itself is about 10 calories a tablespoon. The sugar and the spoon of hot oil whipped into it add another 20 to 90 depending on the quan.

foods.source: Long Chau (around 700 per full serving) and FPT Shop; range 465 to 800 across sources

foods.name: Com Tam Suon
aka: Broken Rice with Grilled Pork Chop
foods.metaDescription: A plate of com tam suon bi cha is about 700 calories; sources put it between 627 and 767. Add a fried egg and it is 820. Every topping broken down.
foods.summary: Broken rice grains topped with a charcoal grilled pork chop, shredded pork skin with toasted rice powder (bi), a steamed egg and pork loaf (cha), scallion oil and a bowl of sweet fish sauce. Saigon's all-day plate, 35,000 to 60,000 dong.
foods.answer: A plate of com tam suon bi cha is around 700 calories. The 220g of broken rice is 290, the grilled chop is about 220 for a 90g piece with its sugary marinade, the bi is 55, the cha is 80, and the mo hanh and nuoc mam add 40. Add op la (a fried egg) and it is 820.
realTalk: Com tam is a 700 calorie plate and it does not look like one. The rice is the biggest part: com tam plates are generous, 220g of cooked broken rice is 290 calories, and the grains soak up the fish sauce. The chop is a thin cut pork shoulder or rib marinated in sugar, honey, fish sauce and oil, then grilled over charcoal. A 90g chop is 220 once you count the marinade, and a lot of quan serve 120g chops now.

The sides add up quietly. Bi, the shredded pork skin tossed with thinh (toasted rice powder), is 55 for a small handful. Cha trung, the steamed pork and egg loaf, is 80 for a 40g slice. The spoon of mo hanh (scallion oil) on top is 30. The nuoc mam is sweet, about 15g of sugar per bowl if you pour it all, so 40 calories. None of these feel like food, and together they are 200.

The full plate at a proper Saigon com tam quan is suon bi cha op la, with a fried egg, sometimes a second cha, plus the free bowl of canh (clear soup). That is 820 to 900 calories. The published figures range from 627 to 767 for suon bi cha depending on the size of the chop and rice; 700 is a fair middle for what you actually get on the plate.
lighter: Order com tam suon only, chop and rice. About 550 versus 700 for suon bi cha.
Ask for it it com, less rice. Cutting 70g of rice saves 90 calories.
Skip op la. A fried egg in oil is 110 to 120.
Hold the mo hanh. The scallion oil spoon is about 30.
Pour half the nuoc mam. The sauce has about 15g of sugar per bowl.

components.name: Bi (shredded pork skin with rice powder)
Scallion oil and sweet fish sauce

variants.name: Com tam suon bi cha op la
Com tam dac biet (2 chops, cha, egg, lap xuong)

faq.q: How many calories in com tam suon bi cha?
faq.a: About 700 for a standard plate. Published figures range from 627 to 767 depending on the size of the pork chop and the rice portion.

faq.q: Is com tam fattening?
faq.a: It is a full meal at 700 calories with 32g of fat, mainly from the chop marinade, scallion oil and cha. Eating it every day without adjusting the rest of your intake will add up.

faq.q: How many calories in the grilled pork chop alone?
faq.a: About 220 for a 90g chop, or around 290 for the larger 120g chops many quan now serve. The sugar and oil in the marinade add 40 to 50 on top of the meat.

faq.q: What is bi in com tam?
faq.a: Shredded boiled pork skin and lean pork mixed with thinh, toasted rice powder. A small serving is about 55 calories and mostly protein and collagen.

foods.source: Huggies VN (767) and Long Chau (627); component cross-check settled on 700

foods.name: Xoi Xeo
aka: Vietnamese Sticky Rice with Mung Bean
foods.metaDescription: A packet of xoi xeo is about 600 calories, around 330 per 100g. The turmeric sticky rice, mung bean and shallot oil add up fast. Every xoi variant compared.
foods.summary: Turmeric yellow glutinous rice pressed into a banana leaf, topped with shaved steamed mung bean paste, a drizzle of liquid pork fat and a handful of fried shallots. Hanoi's 10,000 to 15,000 dong breakfast from a basket on the pavement.
foods.answer: A standard packet of xoi xeo is around 600 calories, based on the published figure of about 332 per 100g for a 180g portion. The sticky rice is 330, the mung bean paste 80, and the fat drizzle and fried shallots together nearly 190. Add cha or ruoc (pork floss) and it is over 700.
realTalk: Xoi xeo is the densest breakfast on the street and the cheapest, which is a bad combination. Glutinous rice cooked with turmeric is about 235 calories per 100g cooked, so the 140g of rice in a normal packet is 330. The mung bean shaved on top is 80 for 30g. Then the seller ladles on mo, liquid rendered pork fat, and a spoon of fried shallots that were cooked in more of it: 190 calories for 25g of topping. Total 600 for something the size of your fist.

Per 100g, xoi xeo is 332 calories, which puts it in the same league as fried rice and well above pho at around 90 per 100g. The problem is there is no water in it. A bowl of pho weighs 500g and is 450 calories; a packet of xoi weighs 180g and is 600. You will be hungry again by 10am because 180g of anything does not stretch the stomach.

The xoi man version from Saigon carts is worse. Plain white sticky rice with cha lua, lap xuong (Chinese sausage), pate, quail eggs and pork floss runs 650 to 750 for a similar size packet, and the sellers pack them bigger. The one lighter option is xoi gac or xoi lac, sticky rice with gac fruit or peanuts and no fat drizzle, at about 380 to 450.
lighter: Ask for khong mo, no pork fat drizzle. That alone saves about 130 calories.
Xoi gac or xoi dau xanh without shallots is 380 to 400 for the same packet.
Ask for a small packet (10,000 dong) instead of the 15,000 one. About 450 versus 600.
If you want protein, add a boiled egg (75) rather than cha or lap xuong (100 to 150).
Treat it as a meal, not a snack. At 600 calories it is bigger than a bowl of pho.

variants.name: Xoi man (Saigon style)
variants.note: Cha, lap xuong, pate, quail egg

faq.q: How many calories in 100g of xoi?
faq.a: About 330 for xoi xeo with its toppings, and around 235 for plain steamed glutinous rice. The fat drizzle and fried shallots are what push xoi xeo higher.

faq.q: Is xoi good for weight loss?
faq.a: Not really. A 180g packet is 600 calories with only 12g of protein, so it is dense and not filling for long. Xoi gac or xoi lac without the fat is a better choice at around 400.

faq.q: Is xoi healthier than banh mi?
faq.a: A packet of xoi xeo (600) has more calories than a banh mi thit (500) and less protein. Banh mi is the better breakfast of the two on numbers.

faq.q: Why is sticky rice so high in calories?
faq.a: Glutinous rice is not higher per gram than normal rice; it is that it is eaten compressed with no water, so a small packet holds a lot of rice, and it is topped with fat.

foods.source: Long Chau (664 per serving, 332 per 100g); scaled to a 180g street packet

foods.name: Banh Cuon
foods.metaDescription: A plate of banh cuon with cha lua is about 300 calories. Plain rolls are 200; add a fried egg or nem and it is 450. One of the lighter Vietnamese breakfasts.
foods.summary: Paper thin steamed rice sheets rolled around minced pork and wood ear mushroom, cut up, showered with fried shallots and served with slices of cha lua (pork loaf) and a bowl of warm nuoc cham. Hanoi breakfast, 25,000 to 35,000 dong.
foods.answer: A plate of banh cuon with cha lua is around 300 calories. The 200g of rice rolls with their pork and mushroom filling is about 220, the two slices of cha lua are 60, and the fried shallots and dipping sauce add 45. Plain banh cuon with only mushroom is about 200 a plate.
realTalk: Banh cuon is one of the lightest things you can eat at a Hanoi breakfast stall, and the reason is water. The rice batter is steamed on cloth into sheets a millimetre thick, so a 200g plate of rolls is only about 220 calories even with the pork and wood ear filling. Compare that with 180g of xoi at 600. The filling is minced pork shoulder, maybe 30g per plate, so 60 of the 220 is meat.

The sides are where the plate goes up. Cha lua, the smooth boiled pork loaf, is 130 calories per 100g, so the two slices you get are about 60. Fried shallots are 25 for a teaspoon and most sellers are generous. The nuoc cham is warm, sweet and diluted, around 20 calories a bowl. Some stalls add a drop of ca cuong essence, which is just aroma. That is 300 for the standard plate.

The heavier orders are banh cuon trung, with a soft egg steamed inside the roll, and banh cuon with nem chua ran (fried fermented pork) or a fried banh tom on the side. Egg adds about 80 per roll. A plate with cha, egg and two fried nem is around 450 to 500. The published range of 200 to 600 per plate covers plain rolls at the bottom and minced pork with all the extras at the top.
lighter: Order banh cuon chay or nhan moc nhi, mushroom filling only. About 200 a plate.
Ask for it hanh phi, less fried shallots. Each teaspoon is about 25 calories.
Skip the nem chua ran or banh tom on the side. Each fried piece is 80 to 120.
One slice of cha lua instead of two saves 30 and you still get the taste.
A plate of banh cuon plus a boiled egg is a decent 375 calorie breakfast with 20g of protein.

components.name: Steamed rice rolls with pork and mushroom

variants.name: Banh cuon full set with nem chua ran
variants.note: Two fried nem on the side

faq.q: How many calories in banh cuon?
faq.a: About 200 for a plain plate and 300 with cha lua. Versions with egg inside or fried nem on the side run 380 to 500.

faq.q: Is banh cuon good for weight loss?
faq.a: Yes, it is one of the lighter street breakfasts at 300 calories with 14g of protein. Add a boiled egg for protein and skip the fried sides.

faq.q: Banh cuon or pho, which is lighter?
faq.a: Banh cuon at 300 versus pho at 450. Pho has more protein though, 28g against 14g, so it keeps you full longer.

faq.q: What is banh cuon made of?
faq.a: A thin batter of rice flour and tapioca starch steamed into sheets, filled with minced pork and wood ear mushroom, and served with cha lua and diluted fish sauce.

foods.source: Pharmacity and Long Chau (200 plain, 300 with egg, up to 590 with pork and extras); component estimate at 300 for the standard plate

foods.name: Chao Ga
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of chao ga is about 250 calories, 60 to 80 per 100g. The quay on the side is another 150 each.
foods.summary: Rice simmered in chicken stock until it breaks down, topped with shredded chicken, spring onion, coriander, black pepper and fried shallots. The late night and sick day food of Vietnam, 20,000 to 35,000 dong a bowl.
foods.answer: A standard 400g bowl of chao ga is around 250 calories. Congee is 60 to 80 calories per 100g because it is mostly water, so the porridge itself is about 150, the 50g of shredded chicken adds 75, and the fried shallots and oil on top add 25. Two quay (fried dough sticks) on the side would double it.
realTalk: Chao ga is about as cheap as calories get on a Vietnamese street: a 400g bowl for 250 calories, and 18g of that is protein. The rice porridge itself is 60 to 80 calories per 100g depending on how thick the quan makes it, so around 150 for the bowl. The chicken is usually 50g of shredded boiled ga ta, 75 calories. Spring onion, coriander, pepper and a small spoon of fried shallots make up the rest.

The reason it works for weight loss is volume. 400g of warm liquid stretches the stomach the same way a bowl of pho does, for half the calories. The catch is you will be hungry in two hours because 32g of carbs and 18g of protein is not a lot of food. Ask for extra chicken, 100g instead of 50, and it becomes a 325 calorie bowl with 30g of protein, which holds you much longer.

The trap is the side order. Quay, the fried dough sticks, are 130 to 150 each and every chao quan sells them. Two quay torn into the bowl is 280 extra, more than the chao itself. The other one is chao long, the offal version, where the fried intestine and liver take a 250 bowl to 400 or more. And a raw egg cracked in, common at late night stalls, adds 75.
lighter: Skip the quay. Each fried dough stick is 130 to 150, more than half the bowl.
Ask for them ga, extra chicken. Doubles the protein for 75 more calories.
Ask for it hanh phi, less fried shallots. The oil is 25 to 40 per spoon.
Chao ga breast (uc) is leaner than thigh. Ask if they have a choice.
Order chao ga rather than chao long. The offal version is 150 to 200 higher.

faq.q: How many calories in a bowl of chao ga?
faq.a: About 250 for a 400g bowl. Congee is only 60 to 80 calories per 100g, and the chicken adds around 75.

faq.q: Is chao ga good for weight loss?
faq.a: Yes, it is one of the lowest calorie hot meals available, as long as you skip the quay. Ask for extra chicken to get 30g of protein for about 325 calories.

faq.q: How many calories in quay?
faq.a: About 130 to 150 per stick. Two quay with your chao adds more calories than the chao itself.

faq.q: Chao ga or pho ga, which is lighter?
faq.a: Chao ga at 250 versus pho ga at 400. Pho ga has more protein and more noodles; chao is mostly water.

foods.source: FPT Shop and bTaskee (60 to 80 per 100g, 160 to 200 per 200g bowl); scaled to a 400g quan bowl with 50g chicken

foods.name: Bo Kho
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of bo kho with one banh mi is about 550 calories: 360 for the stew, 190 for the bread. Hu tieu bo kho is 538. The full breakdown and the leaner order.
foods.summary: Beef brisket and tendon braised with lemongrass, star anise, annatto and tomato until the sauce is thick and red, with chunks of carrot, served with a baguette for dipping or over hu tieu noodles. A Saigon breakfast, 40,000 to 60,000 dong.
foods.answer: A bowl of bo kho with one banh mi is around 550 calories. The 120g of braised brisket and tendon is about 260, the oily broth and carrot together about 105, and the baguette is 190. Order it over noodles as hu tieu bo kho and Vinmec puts it at 538. With two loaves of bread it is 740.
realTalk: Bo kho is a proper protein meal, 34g in a bowl, and the beef is the good part. Brisket and tendon braised for two hours come out at about 215 calories per 100g, so the 120g in a normal bowl is 260. The broth is the tricky bit: it is finished with annatto oil for colour and the fat from the brisket renders into it, so 220ml of that red gravy is around 90 calories. The carrot is 15.

The bread is the other 190. A standard Saigon banh mi loaf is 80g, and dipping it into the gravy is the whole point, so the bread soaks up another 30 or 40 calories of fat. Most quan put two loaves on the table. If you eat both, the meal is 740. If you order hu tieu bo kho or mi bo kho instead, the noodles take the place of the bread at roughly the same calories, 538 for hu tieu per Vinmec.

The 360 calorie stew on its own is a decent thing to eat. What makes bo kho a heavy breakfast is the format: the bread, the second bread, and the fact that a quan bowl uses fattier brisket than the 100g at 350 to 400 you see quoted for home versions. Skim the orange layer of oil off the top before you start and you save 40 to 50.
lighter: One banh mi, not two. The second loaf is 190 calories plus whatever gravy it soaks up.
Skim the orange oil layer off the top of the bowl. About 40 to 50 calories.
Ask for nam (brisket) rather than gan (tendon) and gau (fatty brisket). Leaner cut, same protein.
Order bo kho with a side of bun instead of bread and eat half the noodles. About 460.
The Vietnamese basil, onion and lime on the side plate are free. Use them.

components.name: Bo kho gravy with annatto oil

faq.q: How many calories in banh mi bo kho?
faq.a: About 550 with one baguette and 740 with two. The stew on its own is around 360.

faq.q: Is bo kho healthy?
faq.a: It is high in protein at 34g per bowl and the vegetables are real, but the gravy carries a lot of fat from the brisket and annatto oil. Skim the top layer and limit the bread and it is a solid meal.

faq.q: How many calories in 100g of bo kho?
faq.a: Around 200 to 220 for the beef in gravy. Sources quoting 350 to 400 per 100g are measuring the fattiest cuts with a lot of oil.

faq.q: Bo kho or pho bo, which is lighter?
faq.a: Pho bo at 450 versus bo kho with bread at 550. Bo kho has more protein, 34g against 28g.

foods.source: Vinmec (hu tieu bo kho 538) and Bibi Healthy Bread (bo kho 350 to 500 plus bread 150 to 200); component cross-check

foods.name: Canh Chua
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of canh chua ca is about 150 calories: pineapple, tomato, okra, tamarind broth and a piece of fish. Almost no fat.
foods.summary: A sweet and sour tamarind broth with chunks of fish, pineapple, tomato, okra, elephant ear stem and bean sprouts, finished with fried garlic and rice paddy herb. Southern Vietnam's everyday soup, served next to a bowl of rice and a clay pot of ca kho.
foods.answer: A bowl of canh chua ca is around 150 calories for 350ml with a 60g piece of fish. The fish is about 65, the pineapple, tomato and vegetables about 30, the tamarind broth with its sugar about 30, and the spoon of fried garlic oil on top 25. Without the fish, a ladle of the soup is about 60.
realTalk: Canh chua is the lowest calorie thing on a Vietnamese table that still tastes like a meal. A full bowl is 150 calories. The broth is water, tamarind, fish sauce and about a teaspoon of sugar per bowl, so 30 calories. The vegetables, 100g of pineapple, tomato, okra and bac ha stem, are another 30. The piece of fish, usually ca loc (snakehead) or ca dieu hong (tilapia), is 65 for 60g and it is lean.

The published range is 90 to 180 per bowl and the fish is the variable. Canh chua with ca hu or ca basa, the fatty catfish cuts with the belly on, is 250 to 280 because catfish belly is 15 percent fat. With prawns it is about 120. Vegetarian canh chua with tofu is 100. The fried garlic on top is the one thing to watch: a teaspoon of toi phi in oil is 25 calories and some quan use a tablespoon.

At a com binh dan quan the soup comes as part of a set: a plate of rice at 300, a clay pot of ca kho at 300, and canh chua at 150. The soup is the part you should eat more of. Ask for a second bowl and the meal is 900 calories with an extra 14g of protein and a lot more volume, versus adding a second helping of rice at 150 for nothing.
lighter: Pick ca loc or prawn over ca basa. The catfish belly version is nearly double.
Ask for it toi phi, less fried garlic. Each spoon of the oil is about 25.
Have a second bowl of canh instead of a second plate of rice. 150 calories versus 150 for rice, but with protein and fibre.
Eat the pineapple and okra. Most people leave them and they are the fibre.
Drink the broth. It is 30 calories and mostly water; the sourness kills appetite for a while.

components.name: Pineapple, tomato, okra, elephant ear stem

variants.name: Canh chua ca basa / ca hu

faq.q: How many calories in canh chua ca?
faq.a: About 150 for a bowl with a piece of lean fish. The published range is 90 to 180; catfish belly versions go higher, around 270.

faq.q: Is canh chua healthy?
faq.a: Yes. It is low calorie, low fat, has 14g of protein per bowl and a lot of vegetables. The only additions to watch are the sugar in the broth and the fried garlic oil.

faq.q: Does canh chua have sugar?
faq.a: About a teaspoon per bowl, 15 to 20 calories, to balance the tamarind. Some quan use more; if it tastes noticeably sweet it is probably two.

faq.q: Can I eat canh chua for weight loss?
faq.a: It is one of the best dishes for it. A bowl of canh chua and a small plate of rice is about 450 calories with 20g of protein and a lot of volume.

foods.source: Pharmacity and Long Chau (100 to 180 per bowl; 90 to 120 with lean catfish); component estimate at 150 with snakehead

foods.name: Ca Kho To
aka: Vietnamese Caramelised Fish in Clay Pot
foods.metaDescription: A clay pot of ca kho to with two pieces of fish is about 300 calories, roughly 120 per 100g of fish. The caramel sauce is 60 of that.
foods.summary: Fish steaks braised in a small clay pot with nuoc mau (burnt sugar caramel), fish sauce, black pepper, shallots and a little pork fat until the sauce is dark and sticky. Eaten with white rice and canh chua at every com binh dan quan in the south.
foods.answer: A clay pot of ca kho to with two pieces of fish, about 150g of meat plus sauce, is around 300 calories. The fish is 190, the caramel and fish sauce reduction is about 60 because it has 20 to 25g of sugar in it, and the pork fat or oil used to start the braise adds 45. Made with fatty ca basa instead of ca loc it is over 400.
realTalk: Ca kho to is 300 calories for a normal quan pot and 30g of it is protein, which makes it one of the better lauk on the tray. The published figure is about 120 calories per 100g of braised fish, and a two piece pot holds 150g of fish, so 190 from the fish alone. The rest is the sauce: nuoc mau is sugar cooked to caramel, and a pot uses about 20g of it plus fish sauce, so 60 calories of sauce that you will pour over your rice.

The fish choice changes the number a lot. Ca loc (snakehead) and ca ro (climbing perch) are lean, around 100 calories per 100g cooked. Ca basa and ca hu, the catfish cuts with the belly and skin, are 180 to 200 per 100g because the fat renders into the sauce. Same size pot, 300 versus 420. Ca kho with thit ba chi, where cubes of pork belly are braised in with the fish, is 480 or more.

The meal is the issue more than the fish. Ca kho is so salty and sweet that it is designed to push rice: most people eat 300g of rice with one pot, which is 390 calories, plus the sauce soaked into it. A pot of ca kho, a big plate of rice and a bowl of canh chua is 850. Take a small plate of rice and the same meal is 650 with the same 45g of protein.
lighter: Order ca loc or ca ro over ca basa. Lean fish is about 100 per 100g versus 180 to 200.
Do not pour all the sauce over your rice. Half the pot's sauce is 30 calories of sugar and fat.
Ask for a small plate of rice (it com). The sauce makes you want to eat more rice than you need.
Skip the ca kho thit ba chi version. The pork belly adds 150 to 200.
Have it with canh chua rather than a fried side dish. The soup fills you up for 150.

variants.name: Ca bong kho tieu (goby with pepper)

faq.q: How many calories in ca kho to?
faq.a: About 300 for a two piece clay pot with lean fish, or around 120 per 100g of braised fish. Fatty catfish versions are 400 or more.

faq.q: Is ca kho healthy?
faq.a: The fish is lean and high in protein. The downside is the sauce, which has 20 to 25g of sugar and a lot of salt per pot. It is fine as the protein on a rice plate.

faq.q: How much sugar is in ca kho?
faq.a: Around 20 to 25g per pot from the nuoc mau caramel, about 80 to 100 calories, though a lot of it stays in the pot if you do not scrape the sauce out.

faq.q: What fish is used for ca kho to?
faq.a: Snakehead (ca loc) is the classic; ca basa, ca hu, tilapia and small goby (ca bong) are common. The fattier the fish, the higher the calories.

foods.source: Long Chau (about 120 per 100g braised fish); component estimate for a 2 piece quan pot

foods.name: Bo La Lot
aka: Grilled Beef Wrapped in Lolot Leaf
foods.metaDescription: A plate of 5 bo la lot rolls is about 580 calories, around 115 each. The mince is fatty and the scallion oil on top adds 80.
foods.summary: Seasoned minced beef and pork fat rolled in lolot leaves and grilled over charcoal until the leaves char, then topped with scallion oil and crushed peanuts. Served with banh hoi, rice paper, herbs and mam nem at street grills from 4pm. Around 50,000 to 70,000 dong a plate.
foods.answer: A street plate of five bo la lot rolls is around 580 calories, about 115 per roll. The mince is beef mixed with pork fat, so a 40g roll is 90 to 110 before the mo hanh and peanuts on top add another 30 per roll. The full set with banh hoi, rice paper and dipping sauce is about 850.
realTalk: Bo la lot is a fat bomb hiding behind a leaf. The mince is beef mixed with pork fat or pork mince, usually 20 to 30 percent fat, because lean beef dries out on the grill. So a 40g roll is about 90 to 110 calories, and the published range for a 50 to 60g roll is 120 to 180. Five rolls on a plate is 440 to 550 before toppings. The lolot leaf is nothing, about 1 calorie each.

Then the seller pours mo hanh over the plate, scallions fried in oil, a tablespoon is 80 calories, and sprinkles peanuts, another 60. That is how a plate of five reaches 580. It comes with mam nem, fermented anchovy sauce with pineapple and sugar, about 40 calories for a small bowl, and most tables have two.

The way it is actually eaten is the problem: as a set with banh hoi (fine rice vermicelli sheets, 200 calories for a normal serving), rice paper (60 for two sheets), and a plate of herbs and cucumber. Wrapped and dipped, the full bo la lot banh hoi is 850 to 900 calories, and it is usually an appetiser at a bia hoi table before the main dishes. Two beers on top is another 300.
lighter: Ask for khong mo hanh, no scallion oil. That is 80 calories off a plate of five.
Wrap in rice paper with lots of herbs and skip the banh hoi. Saves 200 and you still get the bite.
Three rolls, not five, as a side dish. About 350.
Dip lightly. The mam nem has sugar and pineapple, about 40 per bowl if you finish it.
Some quan grill bo la lot with lean beef only, which is drier but 30 fewer calories a roll. Ask.

components.name: Beef and pork fat mince, 5 rolls

portions.label: Full set with banh hoi and rice paper

variants.name: Cha la lot (pan fried, lean pork)
Bo la lot banh hoi set
Bo la lot with bo mo chai
variants.note: Add caul fat wrapped beef, per set

faq.q: How many calories in one bo la lot roll?
faq.a: About 90 to 115 for a 40g street roll with toppings. Larger 50 to 60g rolls are 120 to 180 each.

faq.q: Is bo la lot healthy?
faq.a: It is high in protein, 30g per plate of five, but also high in fat at 44g because the mince is cut with pork fat and topped with scallion oil. Fine occasionally, not a diet food.

faq.q: How many calories in bo la lot banh hoi?
faq.a: About 850 for a full set of five rolls with banh hoi, rice paper, herbs and mam nem. The banh hoi alone is around 200.

faq.q: What is the leaf used for bo la lot?
faq.a: Lolot leaf (la lot, Piper sarmentosum), a relative of betel. It adds aroma and almost no calories.

foods.source: Long Chau (120 to 180 per 50 to 60g piece); component estimate for a 5 roll street plate

foods.name: Nem Nuong
foods.serving: 1 set (4 sticks with rice paper, greens, sauce)
foods.metaDescription: A set of nem nuong Nha Trang is about 650 calories: 4 grilled pork sticks, rice paper, banh hoi, fried ram and the peanut dipping sauce.
foods.summary: Sweet, springy pork sausage grilled on skewers over charcoal, rolled up in rice paper with fine vermicelli, a crispy fried wrapper (ram), green mango, cucumber and herbs, then dunked in a thick peanut and pork liver sauce. Nha Trang's signature, 50,000 to 70,000 dong a set.
foods.answer: A full set of nem nuong Nha Trang is around 650 calories. The four grilled pork sticks are about 300, the rice paper and banh hoi 170, the fried ram strips 60, the peanut dipping sauce 90, and the plate of greens 25. Published estimates run 600 to 700 per set.
realTalk: Nem nuong is 650 calories for a set, and it is spread across five things so no single one looks bad. The pork sticks are the biggest: nem nuong is minced pork with pork fat, sugar and garlic, so 100g of grilled sticks is about 300 calories, and a set gives you four sticks. The sugar in the mince caramelises on the grill, which is why they taste sweet and why 10g of that 100g is sugar.

The wrapping is the second 230. Two sheets of rice paper are 60, the banh hoi or bun that goes inside is 110, and the ram chien, the deep fried rice paper strips that give the crunch, are 60 for a small handful. Then the sauce. Nem nuong sauce is peanuts, pork liver, glutinous rice, sugar and oil cooked into a thick dip, about 90 calories for a 50ml bowl, and many people go through two bowls.

Ordering a second round is the normal move because four sticks does not feel like dinner. Two sets is 1,300 calories. The lighter play is one set of nem plus extra greens and rice paper rather than a second set of everything: each extra stick is 75 and each extra sheet of rice paper is 30, so you can build a bigger meal for about 200 more instead of 650.
lighter: Skip the ram chien. The fried strips are about 60 per set and add nothing except crunch.
Wrap with more greens and less banh hoi. The vermicelli sheets are 110 per set.
One bowl of sauce, not two. Each is around 90 calories of peanut, liver and sugar.
Order extra nem sticks (75 each) instead of a second full set if still hungry.
The green mango and cucumber are free and cut the sweetness. Use a lot.

components.name: Peanut and pork liver dipping sauce

portions.label: Set with extra sauce and ram

variants.name: Two sets
variants.note: What two hungry people usually order per person

faq.q: How many calories in nem nuong?
faq.a: About 300 for four grilled sticks on their own, and 650 for a full Nha Trang set with rice paper, banh hoi, ram and dipping sauce.

faq.q: Is nem nuong healthy?
faq.a: The pork is high in protein at 30g per set but also carries a lot of fat and sugar, and the sauce adds more. It is a reasonable dinner at 650 if you stop at one set.

faq.q: What is nem nuong sauce made of?
faq.a: Ground peanuts, pork liver, glutinous rice, sugar, garlic and oil simmered into a thick paste. A 50ml bowl is around 90 calories.

faq.q: Nem nuong or bo la lot, which has more calories?
faq.a: Similar per plate. A nem nuong set is 650; a plate of five bo la lot is 580, or 850 with the banh hoi set. Both are fatty minced meat over charcoal.

foods.source: Long Chau (600 to 700 per set) and Vua Ga Nuong (600 to 667 for 4 sticks, 2 rice paper, greens, sauce)

foods.name: Banh Xeo
foods.metaDescription: A medium banh xeo is about 350 calories; a small central style one is 250 and a big Mekong plate size one is 500.
foods.summary: A crisp turmeric rice flour and coconut milk crepe fried in a hot pan with pork belly, prawns and bean sprouts folded inside, torn up and wrapped in mustard leaf and herbs, then dipped in nuoc cham. Big and thin in the south, small and thick in the centre. About 20,000 to 40,000 dong each.
foods.answer: A medium banh xeo is around 350 calories. The batter is rice flour with coconut milk and turmeric, about 170 for one pancake, and it is fried in enough oil to make it crisp, which adds 90. The prawn and pork inside are about 70, the bean sprouts 15. Small central Vietnam ones are 250; the huge southern ones are 500.
realTalk: Banh xeo looks like a light, vegetable heavy snack and it is really a fried pancake. The batter for one medium pancake is about 60g of rice flour and 40ml of coconut milk, 170 calories before it hits the pan. Then it hits the pan with a ladle of oil, because the crispness comes from shallow frying, and a medium pancake absorbs about 10g, 90 calories. That is 260 before the filling.

The filling is the healthy bit. Two or three prawns and a few slices of pork belly are about 70 calories for 40g, and the bean sprouts are 15. The published figure of 315 to 350 for a medium pancake with 11g fat, 40g carbs and 14g protein lines up with that. What changes it is size. A Hue or Da Nang banh xeo is palm size and 250; a Mekong style one is the size of the pan and 450 to 500.
