Nobody eats one. The typical order at a banh xeo quan is two per person, with a plate of mustard greens and herbs and a bowl of sweet fish sauce, about 40 calories per bowl. Two medium pancakes plus sauce is 740. Two southern ones is 1,000. The greens are free and the pancake is meant to be wrapped in them, so at least the meal has volume.
lighter: Order the central style small ones. About 250 each versus 350 for medium and 500 for the big southern kind.
Wrap every piece in a large mustard leaf with herbs. The greens are free and slow you down.
Ask for it dau, less oil, at a quan that cooks to order. Saves 30 to 50 per pancake.
One pancake plus a bowl of canh or a goi cuon is a lighter meal than two pancakes.
Ask for more tom (prawn) and less ba chi (pork belly) in the filling.

components.name: Rice flour and coconut milk batter

faq.q: How many calories in one banh xeo?
faq.a: About 350 for a medium pancake with prawn and pork. Small central Vietnam ones are around 250 and the large Mekong style ones about 500.

faq.q: Is banh xeo healthy?
faq.a: It has some protein and comes with a lot of raw greens, but the pancake is fried in oil and made with coconut milk, so 15g of fat per medium piece. One is fine; two or three is a heavy meal.

faq.q: Is banh xeo gluten free?
faq.a: Usually yes. The batter is rice flour, turmeric and coconut milk. Some stalls add a little wheat flour or beer for crispness, so ask if it matters.

faq.q: How much oil is in banh xeo?
faq.a: A medium pancake absorbs about 10g of frying oil, roughly 90 calories, which is a quarter of the total.

foods.source: Long Chau and Huggies VN (315 to 350 medium, 250 small); component cross-check

foods.name: Banh Mi Thit
foods.metaDescription: A standard banh mi thit is about 500 calories: 240 for the bread, 120 for pate and butter, 90 for the cold cuts. A stuffed Huynh Hoa style loaf is 900.
foods.summary: A crackly, airy baguette split and spread with pate and butter or mayo, layered with cha lua, head cheese, roast pork or cold cuts, then stuffed with pickled carrot and daikon, cucumber, coriander, chili and a splash of Maggi. 20,000 to 35,000 dong from a cart, more at the famous shops.
foods.answer: A standard banh mi thit is around 500 calories. The 90g baguette is 240, the pate and butter or mayo spread is about 120, the 50g of cold cuts and cha lua is 90, and the pickles, cucumber and sauce make up the rest. Published figures range from 380 for a lightly filled cart banh mi to 900 for a fully stuffed one.
realTalk: A banh mi is 500 calories and the bread is half of it. A Vietnamese baguette is lighter than a French one because it is part rice flour and mostly air, but a 90g loaf is still 240 calories. The other big piece is the spread. Pate is 320 calories per 100g and butter or mayo is 700, and a cart puts about 15g of pate and 10g of fat on each loaf, so 120 calories that you never see.

The meat is less than you think. A typical cart gives 50g of mixed cha lua, cold pork, and head cheese, around 90 calories. Roast pork (thit nuong) or xiu mai (meatballs in tomato sauce) are heavier, 130 to 150 for the same weight. Then the pickles, cucumber and coriander are 15, and the Maggi and chili sauce about 20. That is your 500.

The variance between banh mi is huge. A 15,000 dong banh mi chả with two slices of cha lua is 380. A banh mi from Huynh Hoa in Saigon, stuffed with 150g of meat, pate and a thick layer of butter, weighs 350g and is 900 or more. The published 300 to 350 figures are for the thin cart versions; a real banh mi dac biet from a shop is 500 to 600.
lighter: Ask for it bo, khong pate: no butter, less pate. Saves 80 to 120 calories.
Banh mi thit nuong (grilled pork) or ga (chicken) gives more protein for the calories than cold cuts.
Ask for extra do chua (pickles) and cucumber. They are free and add crunch.
Skip the extra Maggi and chili sauce. About 20 calories and a lot of sodium.
Banh mi op la (fried egg) is about 420 and has 13g of protein, a decent breakfast option.

variants.name: Banh mi op la (fried egg)
variants.note: One or two eggs, no cold cuts

faq.q: How many calories in a banh mi?
faq.a: About 500 for a standard banh mi thit. A lightly filled cart banh mi cha is 380 and a heavily stuffed shop version can be 900.

faq.q: Is banh mi healthy?
faq.a: It is a reasonable meal at 500 calories with 20g of protein and fresh vegetables. The pate and butter add 20g of fat, so ask for less if you eat one daily.

faq.q: How many calories in the bread alone?
faq.a: About 240 for a 90g Vietnamese baguette. It is lighter than a French baguette because it is airier and part rice flour.

faq.q: What is the lowest calorie banh mi?
faq.a: Banh mi op la with one egg and no pate at about 380, or banh mi ga (chicken) without butter at around 420.

foods.source: Pharmacity (about 500 for a full banh mi thit) and Long Chau (380 to 400 with 50 to 60g meat)

foods.name: Goi Cuon
foods.metaDescription: Two goi cuon with peanut sauce are about 200 calories, roughly 65 per roll. The fried version, cha gio, is double.
foods.summary: Soft rice paper wrapped around prawns, a slice of boiled pork, bun vermicelli, lettuce and herbs, served cold with a peanut hoisin dip or nuoc cham. Sold by the pair from street carts for 10,000 to 15,000 dong each.
foods.answer: Two goi cuon with a small bowl of peanut sauce are around 200 calories. Each roll is about 65 to 70: the rice paper is 30, the bun inside 20, the prawn and pork together 30, and the greens almost nothing. The peanut hoisin sauce is 35 for a 20ml pour; the nuoc cham option is about 15.
realTalk: Goi cuon is one of the few street snacks where the number is actually low: 65 to 70 calories per roll, 200 for two with sauce. A sheet of rice paper is about 30 calories, the 20g of bun inside is 20, and a prawn and a slice of boiled pork come to 30. There is no oil anywhere in the roll. The published figures of 49 for a prawn only roll and 67 for a pork and prawn roll match that.

The sauce is where it moves. The peanut hoisin sauce is hoisin, peanut butter, sugar and sometimes coconut milk, about 35 calories for the 20ml a cart gives you, and 90 if a restaurant gives you a full bowl and you finish it. The alternative, nuoc cham with lime, is 15. The difference over four rolls is 150 calories, which is more than two of the rolls.

The comparison people want is with cha gio, the fried version. A cha gio is 130 to 150 calories, double a goi cuon, because it is fried in oil. Four goi cuon is 260 before sauce and makes a real light lunch with 22g of protein. Four cha gio is 540. Most menus put them side by side at the same price.
lighter: Choose nuoc cham (15) over peanut sauce (35 to 90). Or dip, do not pour.
Ask for goi cuon tom, prawn only. About 50 per roll versus 67 with pork.
Four rolls with nuoc cham is a 280 calorie meal with 22g of protein.
Skip the bun inside if the cart makes them to order. Saves 20 per roll.
Goi cuon over cha gio, every time. Half the calories for the same filling.

faq.q: How many calories in one goi cuon?
faq.a: About 65 to 70 for a prawn and pork roll, or 50 for prawn only. Sauce adds 15 to 45 per roll depending on type and amount.

faq.q: Are goi cuon good for weight loss?
faq.a: Yes. They are about the lightest thing on a Vietnamese menu, with protein from the prawns and no oil. Four rolls with nuoc cham is under 300 calories.

faq.q: Goi cuon or cha gio, which is healthier?
faq.a: Goi cuon. A fresh roll is about 65 calories and a fried cha gio is 130 to 150, with most of the difference being frying oil.

faq.q: How many calories in peanut sauce for spring rolls?
faq.a: About 35 for a 20ml cart portion and up to 90 for a full restaurant bowl. Nuoc cham is about 15.

foods.source: Long Chau (49 prawn, 67 pork and prawn per roll) and Pharmacity (40 to 70 per roll); sauce estimated from components

foods.name: Chicken Adobo
foods.metaDescription: A carinderia plate of chicken adobo with 1 cup rice is about 520 calories. Here is where the number comes from and how to trim it.
foods.summary: Chicken braised in soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaf and peppercorns, then spooned over a cup of white rice. The default lunch at every carinderia in the country.
foods.answer: A carinderia plate of chicken adobo with 1 cup of rice is about 520 calories. That is roughly 255 calories from 180g of adobo (thigh with sauce) and 260 calories from 200g of rice. Skip the rice and the adobo alone is closer to 250.
realTalk: The adobo itself is not the problem. FatSecret puts chicken adobo at 141 calories per 100g, which is modest for a meat dish because the sauce is soy, vinegar and garlic with almost no sugar and only a spoon of oil. A 180g carinderia scoop with one thigh and some sauce lands around 255 calories. The rice is what doubles the plate. One cup of steamed rice is 200g and 260 calories, and most people order a second cup for 55 pesos more.

The variable nobody tracks is the cut. Thigh with skin is what most carinderias use, because it survives 40 minutes of simmering without drying out. A skinless breast piece of the same weight drops the adobo portion from 255 to about 170 calories. Pork adobo made with liempo goes the other way, closer to 400 calories for the same scoop, because pork belly is 50 percent fat by weight.

Watch the sauce. Adobo sauce reduces down to a thin layer of chicken fat and soy, and the habit of spooning extra sauce over the rice adds 40 to 60 calories per ladle. If the carinderia adds a spoon of oil or fries the chicken first (adobong pritong manok), add another 80 calories. The 520 figure assumes standard simmered adobo, one thigh, one cup of rice.
lighter: Ask for breast or ask the cook to leave the skin off. Same sauce, about 85 calories less per plate.
Order half rice. Half a cup is 130 calories and adobo sauce covers it just fine.
Skip the extra sauce ladle. Each one is mostly chicken fat and soy, about 50 calories.
Pair it with a plain vegetable side like ensaladang talong or steamed okra instead of a second ulam.

variants.name: Standard chicken thigh adobo with rice
Pork belly adobo with rice
variants.note: Liempo is half fat by weight

faq.q: How many calories in chicken adobo without rice?
faq.a: About 250 calories for a 180g carinderia scoop of thigh adobo with sauce. FatSecret lists 141 calories per 100g. A single thigh with sauce (152g) is listed at 107 calories, but that figure counts bone weight.

faq.q: Is chicken adobo good for weight loss?
faq.a: Yes, as far as ulam goes. It is high in protein (about 25g per scoop), has no sugar and no coconut milk, and the sauce is mostly vinegar and soy. Just control the rice, since 1 cup is 260 calories on its own.

faq.q: Is chicken adobo or pork adobo higher in calories?
faq.a: Pork adobo, by a wide margin. The same 180g scoop of pork belly adobo is about 400 calories versus 255 for chicken thigh. Chicken breast adobo is lowest at around 170.

faq.q: How many calories in a cup of adobo sauce?
faq.a: About 100 to 150 calories per cup, mostly from rendered chicken fat and the tablespoon of oil used to sauté the garlic. One ladle over rice is about 50 calories.

foods.source: FatSecret generic chicken adobo (141 kcal/100g), rice and sauce from components

foods.name: Sinigang na Baboy
foods.metaDescription: A carinderia bowl of sinigang na baboy is about 320 calories. The broth is nearly free, the pork belly is the whole number. Full breakdown inside.
foods.summary: Sour tamarind soup with pork ribs or belly, kangkong, radish, string beans and tomato. The one dish every Filipino asks for on a rainy day.
foods.answer: A 350g carinderia bowl of sinigang na baboy is about 320 calories. FatSecret lists sinigang at 222 calories per cup (240g), and a real bowl with 90g of pork is about 1.5 cups. Nearly all of that is the pork. The sour broth and vegetables together are under 60 calories.
realTalk: The broth is water, tamarind, tomato and fish sauce, so a cup of it is about 15 calories before the pork goes in. That is why sinigang is one of the better carinderia soups if you are counting. The number only moves when the cook uses liempo instead of ribs. Pork belly is around 350 calories per 100g cooked, so a bowl loaded with three thick belly slices can hit 450 to 500 while a bowl with two rib pieces stays near 300.

The rice is where sinigang gets expensive. Nobody eats it without at least 1 cup of rice (260 calories), and sinigang broth on rice is the specific reason people go back for a second cup. A standard lunch of one bowl and two cups of rice is 840 calories. The soup did not do that, the refill did.

The oil floating on top is real. Belly fat renders into the broth during the 45 minutes of simmering and forms a layer of about 15 to 20g in a family pot, which is 130 to 180 calories spread across the servings. Some carinderias skim it, most do not. Ask for a bowl from the bottom of the pot with more vegetables and less of the top layer.
lighter: Order sinigang na hipon or bangus instead. Shrimp brings the bowl down to about 190 calories, milkfish to about 240.
Ask for more kangkong and labanos. The vegetables are under 30 calories per handful and they soak up the sour broth.
Stick to 1 cup of rice and let the broth do the flavouring instead of pouring more soup on a refill.
Skim the fat layer off the top of your bowl with a spoon. That alone can save 50 to 80 calories.

faq.q: How many calories in sinigang na baboy with rice?
faq.a: About 580 calories for one bowl and 1 cup of rice. Two cups of rice pushes it to 840. The soup itself is only 320 of that.

faq.q: Is sinigang healthy?
faq.a: The broth and vegetables are, at under 60 calories per bowl. The pork is the only heavy part. Pick ribs or shrimp over belly and it is one of the leanest full meals at a carinderia.

faq.q: How many calories in sinigang broth only?
faq.a: About 15 to 25 calories per cup if it has been skimmed, up to 60 if the pork fat layer is still on top. Tamarind, tomato and fish sauce add almost nothing.

faq.q: Which sinigang has the least calories?
faq.a: Sinigang na hipon at about 190 calories per bowl, then bangus at 240. Pork belly sinigang is the heaviest at 400 plus.

foods.source: FatSecret generic sinigang (222 kcal per cup) scaled to a 350g bowl

foods.name: Lechon
foods.metaDescription: A fiesta serving of lechon (about 120g with skin) is around 380 calories. The skin is 150 of that. Here is the math per slice and per kilo.
foods.summary: Whole pig roasted over charcoal for hours until the skin blisters. Sold by the kilo at fiestas, weddings and every Cebu lechon house.
foods.answer: A typical fiesta plate of lechon, about 120g or 3 to 4 slices with skin, is around 380 calories. Roast pork with skin runs 300 to 330 calories per 100g. A 250g lechon house serving with sarsa is closer to 800. The skin alone is about 500 calories per 100g.
realTalk: The skin is the whole story. Lechon skin is rendered pork rind, essentially chicharon that never left the pig, and it runs about 500 calories per 100g. The meat underneath, once the fat cap is trimmed, is about 220 calories per 100g. So a 120g plate with 30g of skin and 90g of meat is 380 calories, but the same weight of pure skin would be 600. At a fiesta, the people fighting over the crispy bits are eating twice the calories of the ones taking meat from the loin.

Lechon houses sell by the kilo, and a quarter kilo (250g) is a normal single order for one hungry person. That is about 800 calories before rice and before the Mang Tomas. The liver sauce is 40 calories per 30g spoon, which sounds small until you use four spoons. Cebu lechon skips the sauce entirely because it is stuffed with lemongrass and salt, so the count is a bit lower per plate.

The morning-after version matters too. Leftover lechon becomes lechon paksiw (simmered in vinegar and liver sauce) at about 350 calories per cup, or gets fried into lechon kawali style pieces at 500 plus. Most fiesta lechon is eaten three times over two days, and the 380 figure is only the first plate.
lighter: Go for the loin and shoulder slices, skip the belly cuts. Belly lechon is about 30 percent higher per slice.
Take one piece of skin, not a handful. Each 10g shard is about 50 calories.
Use Mang Tomas sparingly or squeeze calamansi and vinegar instead, which is close to zero.
Fill half the plate with atchara or ensalada before adding meat. It slows you down.

portions.label: Fiesta plate, 3 to 4 slices with skin
Quarter kilo from a lechon house

faq.q: How many calories in 100g of lechon?
faq.a: About 300 to 330 calories with skin, or 220 without. The skin alone is around 500 calories per 100g.

faq.q: How many calories in a kilo of lechon?
faq.a: Roughly 3,000 to 3,300 calories per kilo as served, skin included. A quarter kilo order is about 800.

faq.q: Is lechon or lechon kawali higher in calories?
faq.a: Lechon kawali, because it is belly only and deep fried. Gram for gram it is about 400 calories per 100g against 320 for roast lechon.

faq.q: How many calories in Mang Tomas lechon sauce?
faq.a: About 40 calories per 30g serving, mostly sugar and breadcrumbs. Four spoons at a fiesta is 160 calories on top of the meat.

foods.source: estimate from components

foods.name: Lechon Kawali
foods.metaDescription: A carinderia serving of lechon kawali (130g) is about 520 calories, almost all of it pork belly fat. Numbers per piece, with rice, and lighter swaps.
foods.summary: Pork belly boiled until tender, then deep fried until the skin puffs and cracks. Served chopped with lechon sauce or toyomansi.
foods.answer: A carinderia serving of lechon kawali, about 130g or 6 to 8 chopped pieces, is around 520 calories. Deep fried pork belly runs about 400 calories per 100g. With 1 cup of rice the plate is 780. The dipping sauce adds another 20 to 40.
realTalk: Pork belly is about half fat by weight before it touches the pan. Boiling it first renders some of that out, then frying puts oil back in, and you end with roughly 400 calories per 100g. A 130g carinderia scoop is 520 calories, which is more than a Jollibee Chickenjoy with rice. Each chopped cube is around 70 calories, so counting cubes is the honest way to track it.

Bagnet, the Ilocano version, is fried twice and comes out even drier and crunchier. The second fry pushes it past 450 calories per 100g. Lechon kawali houses in Manila usually serve 200g portions for 180 to 220 pesos, which is 800 calories before rice. Add the standard cup and the sizzling plate crowd is at 1,060 for lunch.

The sauce choice moves the number less than people think. Mang Tomas is 40 calories per 30g, toyomansi is about 10, spiced vinegar is nearly zero. What actually matters is whether the pieces came from the thin end of the belly (more meat) or the thick end (more fat). Ask for the leaner end if the cook lets you pick.
lighter: Order the small portion (90g) and pair it with a vegetable ulam like pinakbet. That keeps the plate under 600 with rice.
Dip in spiced vinegar or toyomansi instead of liver sauce.
Blot the pieces on a paper napkin. Surface oil on fried belly is 30 to 50 calories per serving.
Make it at home in an air fryer after boiling. The skin still puffs and it drops to about 320 calories per 100g.

components.name: Pork belly, boiled then deep fried

faq.q: How many calories in lechon kawali with rice?
faq.a: About 780 calories with 1 cup of rice, or 1,040 with 2 cups. The pork alone is 520 for a 130g serving.

faq.q: How many calories in one piece of lechon kawali?
faq.a: About 70 calories per chopped cube (roughly 18g). A 6 to 8 piece serving is 420 to 560.

faq.q: Is bagnet higher in calories than lechon kawali?
faq.a: Yes, by about 15 percent. Bagnet is fried twice and loses more water, so it lands near 450 calories per 100g versus 400 for regular lechon kawali.

faq.q: Can I eat lechon kawali on a diet?
faq.a: Occasionally, in small portions. A 90g serving is 350 calories and gives you about 20g of protein. It is the size, not the dish, that breaks a calorie budget.

foods.source: estimate from components

foods.name: Kare-Kare
foods.metaDescription: A restaurant serving of kare-kare with oxtail and peanut sauce is around 500 calories before rice. Here is what the sauce, oxtail and bagoong each add.
foods.summary: Oxtail and tripe stewed in a thick peanut and annatto sauce with banana heart, string beans, eggplant and pechay. Always eaten with bagoong alamang on the side.
foods.answer: A single restaurant serving of kare-kare, about 250g with oxtail, vegetables and peanut sauce, is around 500 calories. The peanut sauce alone is about 200 of that. Add 1 cup of rice and a spoon of bagoong and the full plate reaches 800.
realTalk: Kare-kare is a peanut butter dish. A family-size pot uses 150 to 200g of ground peanuts or peanut butter, which is 900 to 1,200 calories of sauce spread across 6 servings. Your 80g ladle of sauce is about 200 calories before the meat. Then oxtail, which is fatty even after skimming, adds 260 calories per 100g. That is how a dish full of eggplant, string beans and banana heart still lands at 500.

The bagoong is small but not free. A tablespoon of sautéed shrimp paste is about 30 calories, and most people take three because kare-kare without it tastes flat. Sautéed bagoong has oil and sugar in it, so it is not the same as raw alamang. Count 90 to 100 calories for a normal amount at a restaurant.

Restaurant kare-kare in Manila runs 350 to 600 pesos for a serving meant for two, and it usually gets finished by one. That is 1,000 calories of ulam before rice. The crispy kare-kare trend, where lechon kawali or bagnet replaces the oxtail, adds another 300 calories per serving because you are putting deep fried belly into peanut sauce.
lighter: Ask for more vegetables and less sauce. The banana heart, eggplant and string beans are about 25 calories a handful.
Choose the seafood or vegetable-only version, which lands at 250 to 380 instead of 500.
One tablespoon of bagoong, not three. That is 60 calories saved.
Share the restaurant order. It is portioned for two and priced for two.

components.name: Banana heart, string beans, eggplant, pechay

portions.label: Large serving with 1 cup rice and bagoong

variants.name: Crispy kare-kare
variants.note: Lechon kawali or bagnet on top

faq.q: How many calories in kare-kare with rice?
faq.a: About 760 calories for one serving with 1 cup of rice, or around 800 once you add bagoong. Two cups of rice takes it past 1,000.

faq.q: Why is kare-kare so high in calories?
faq.a: The sauce is ground peanuts or peanut butter, at about 600 calories per 100g, and the meat is oxtail, one of the fattier cuts. The vegetables are only about 25 calories per serving.

faq.q: How many calories in bagoong alamang?
faq.a: About 30 calories per tablespoon when sautéed with oil and sugar. Raw alamang is closer to 10 per tablespoon.

faq.q: Is kare-kare healthy?
faq.a: It has protein and vegetables, but the peanut sauce and oxtail make it one of the heaviest Filipino ulam at 500 calories per serving. The seafood or vegetable version at 250 to 380 is the better pick if you are cutting.

foods.source: estimate from components

foods.name: Sisig
foods.metaDescription: A sizzling plate of pork sisig with egg and mayo is about 530 calories. FatSecret lists 215 kcal per 100g before toppings.
foods.summary: Chopped pig face, ears and belly, boiled, grilled, then fried on a sizzling plate with onion, chili, calamansi, a raw egg and a squeeze of mayonnaise. Pampanga's gift to every beer house.
foods.answer: A standard sizzling plate of pork sisig, about 200g with egg and mayo, is around 530 calories. FatSecret puts plain pork sisig at 215 calories per 100g, and the egg (70) and mayo (100) push a restaurant plate past 500. With 1 cup of rice it is 790.
realTalk: Sisig is pig face. Ears, jowl and snout are mostly skin, fat and cartilage, and the belly some cooks add is half fat. FatSecret lists pork sisig at 515 calories per cup, with 35g of fat and 39g of protein, and that is before the sizzling plate toppings. The protein is real, which surprises people, but the fat is higher.

The toppings are 170 of the 530. A raw egg cracked on top is 70 calories. The squiggle of mayonnaise most restaurants add is 15g, and mayo is 100 calories per 15g. Chicharon crumbled on top is another 55 per 10g. A plain sisig with just calamansi and onion is about 360 calories for the same 200g, which is a meaningful difference for the same dish.

A sisig plate in a Manila beer house is 150 to 250 pesos and is priced as pulutan for a group. In practice one person clears it with 2 cups of rice, which is 1,050 calories, plus two San Miguel Pale Pilsens at 150 each. That is a 1,350 calorie sitting. The sisig was never the whole problem, the setting was.
lighter: Order it without mayo and without egg. Same flavour from the calamansi and chili, 170 calories less.
Try chicken sisig (about 380) or bangus sisig (about 330). Same plate, half the fat.
Stick to 1 cup of rice. Sisig is salty and pushes you toward a second cup.
Make it at home with pork shoulder instead of face. Lean pork sisig is about 300 calories per 200g.

components.name: Chopped pork face and belly, grilled and fried

portions.label: Standard sizzling plate with egg and mayo

variants.name: Pork sisig with extra mayo and chicharon

faq.q: How many calories in sisig with rice?
faq.a: About 790 calories for a standard plate with 1 cup of rice, or 1,050 with 2 cups. Sisig alone is around 530.

faq.q: How many calories in sisig without mayo and egg?
faq.a: About 360 calories for a 200g plate. The egg is 70 and the mayo is 100, so leaving both off saves 170.

faq.q: Is sisig high in protein?
faq.a: Yes, about 34g per plate. FatSecret lists 39g of protein per cup of pork sisig. The catch is the 35g of fat that comes with it.

faq.q: Is chicken sisig healthier than pork sisig?
faq.a: It is lower in calories, about 380 versus 530 for the same plate, because thigh meat has far less fat than pig face and belly.

foods.source: FatSecret generic pork sisig (215 kcal/100g) plus egg and mayo from components

foods.name: Pancit Canton
foods.metaDescription: A plate of pancit canton from a carinderia is about 450 calories. The noodles are 210 of that, the oil is 100. Full breakdown and the bihon comparison.
foods.summary: Flour stick noodles stir-fried with soy sauce, pork or chicken, shrimp, cabbage and carrot. The birthday noodle, the fiesta noodle, and the Friday carinderia special.
foods.answer: A carinderia plate of pancit canton, about 250g, is around 450 calories. That is 60g of dry canton noodles (210 calories), a tablespoon of oil (105), and about 130 calories of meat, shrimp and vegetables. A bilao slice at a party is closer to 600.
realTalk: Canton noodles are flour and egg noodles that have already been fried once at the factory, which is why they are 350 calories per 100g dry compared to 360 for bihon but with three times the fat. Then the cook adds a tablespoon of oil to the wok, sometimes two. A standard plate ends up with 17g of fat, most of it from the noodle and the pan rather than the pork.

The fiesta bilao is the version that catches people. A large bilao is about 3kg of pancit for 900 to 1,200 pesos and gets cut into 10 to 12 portions, so each is 250 to 300g. Except nobody takes one slice at a birthday, they take one, then a second because it is there. Two bilao portions with a slice of lechon and rice is a 1,300 calorie plate.

Instant pancit canton is its own category. A pack of Lucky Me Pancit Canton is listed at 280 to 290 calories on FatSecret, which is less than the carinderia plate because the pack is only 60g of noodles. The problem is the 1,000mg plus of sodium and the fact that one pack is never enough, so people cook two, which is 580.
lighter: Order pancit bihon instead. Rice noodles absorb less oil, about 70 calories less per plate.
Ask for extra repolyo and carrots. Vegetables in pancit are about 20 calories a handful.
One portion, no rice on the side. Pancit is already a carbohydrate, the rice is a second one.
At home, use half the oil the recipe says and a splash of chicken stock to keep the noodles moving.

variants.name: Pancit canton with lechon kawali topping

faq.q: How many calories in pancit canton per cup?
faq.a: About 300 calories per cup (roughly 170g). A standard carinderia plate is one and a half cups, or 450 calories.

faq.q: Is pancit canton or pancit bihon healthier?
faq.a: Bihon is lower, at about 380 calories per plate versus 450. Rice noodles have almost no fat and absorb less oil in the wok than pre-fried canton noodles.

faq.q: How many calories in Lucky Me Pancit Canton?
faq.a: About 280 to 290 calories per pack according to FatSecret, depending on the flavour. Two packs, which is what most people cook, is 570.

faq.q: How many calories in a bilao of pancit canton?
faq.a: A large bilao (about 3kg) is roughly 5,400 calories in total, or about 600 per party slice if it is cut into 9 or 10.

foods.source: estimate from components; instant pack figure from FatSecret Lucky Me entry

foods.name: Pancit Bihon
foods.metaDescription: A plate of pancit bihon guisado is about 380 calories, the lightest of the common pancit.
foods.summary: Thin rice vermicelli stir-fried with soy sauce, chicken or pork, cabbage, carrot and celery. The noodle that shows up at every birthday because it is cheap and feeds a crowd.
foods.answer: A carinderia plate of pancit bihon, about 250g, is around 380 calories. Dry bihon is 60g of that at 215 calories, plus about 70 calories of oil and 95 from chicken, vegetables and soy. It is roughly 70 calories lighter than the same plate of pancit canton.
realTalk: Bihon is rice flour and water, nothing else. Dry, it is 360 calories per 100g with less than 1g of fat, which is why it is the lightest pancit on the menu even after the wok. The 60g of dry noodles in a plate swells to about 170g cooked. The oil is the only fat source, and a careful cook uses one tablespoon (about 70 to 100 calories) for a family batch, while a careless one uses a quarter cup.

The toppings are where carinderia bihon and party bihon differ. Carinderia bihon has 40g of shredded chicken and cabbage, about 80 calories of extras. Party bihon from a caterer gets pork belly slices, shrimp, chicharon crumbs and a boiled egg per bilao, which pushes a slice to 500. Same noodle, different economics.

A plate of bihon at a carinderia is 35 to 50 pesos and comes with a pandesal or a cup of rice if you ask. The pandesal adds 138, the rice adds 260. Bihon with rice is a carb-on-carb plate at 640 calories with about 18g of protein, which is a poor deal. Bihon alone with an egg on the side is a better lunch at 450.
lighter: Ask for it without rice or pandesal. The noodles are the carbohydrate.
Add a boiled egg or a piece of grilled chicken for protein. Bihon on its own is low at 14g.
Squeeze calamansi over it instead of adding more soy sauce. It brightens the plate with zero calories.
At home, swap half the noodles for shredded cabbage. The texture holds and the plate drops to about 280.

portions.label: Party bilao slice with pork and egg

faq.q: How many calories in pancit bihon per cup?
faq.a: About 250 calories per cup (170g cooked). A carinderia plate is about 1.5 cups, or 380 calories.

faq.q: Is pancit bihon good for weight loss?
faq.a: It is one of the lower calorie pancit at 380 per plate, but it is light on protein at about 14g. Add an egg or chicken and skip the rice to make it a proper meal.

faq.q: How many calories in pancit bihon with rice?
faq.a: About 640 calories with 1 cup of rice. Bihon is already noodles, so the rice is a second carbohydrate with no extra protein.

faq.q: Which pancit has the least calories?
faq.a: Pancit bihon at 380 per plate, then sotanghon at a similar level, then canton at 450. Palabok and malabon are higher because of the shrimp sauce and toppings.

foods.source: estimate from components

foods.name: Pancit Palabok
foods.metaDescription: A carinderia plate of pancit palabok is about 440 calories. Jollibee's Palabok Fiesta is listed at 305. Where the shrimp sauce, chicharon and egg land.
foods.summary: Rice noodles under a thick orange shrimp and annatto sauce, topped with crushed chicharon, smoked fish flakes, shrimp, boiled egg and spring onion. The pancit that looks like a party.
foods.answer: A carinderia plate of pancit palabok, about 300g, is around 440 calories. The bihon base is 215, the shrimp sauce about 90, and the toppings (chicharon, egg, tinapa, shrimp) add 140. Jollibee's Palabok Fiesta is listed on FatSecret at 305 calories for their smaller serving.
realTalk: Palabok sauce is shrimp stock thickened with flour and coloured with annatto oil, so a 100g ladle is about 90 calories. That is lighter than a peanut or coconut sauce, and the plate would be modest if it stopped there. It does not. The toppings are the point of palabok, and chicharon (55 calories per 10g), half a boiled egg (35) and tinapa flakes (30) are what push a carinderia plate to 440.

The Jollibee number is useful as a reference. FatSecret lists Jollibee Palabok Fiesta at 305 calories, and it is a smaller serving with a lighter sauce than what a Malabon carinderia puts down. A fiesta-size plate from a Pancit Malabon specialist, with extra shrimp, squid, egg and a heavy chicharon topping, runs 600 or more and costs 90 to 120 pesos.

Pancit Malabon is the same idea with thicker noodles and a richer sauce that uses more shrimp fat and sometimes crab fat. Count 10 to 15 percent more than palabok for the same plate. Pancit luglug is the Pampanga name and uses the thickest noodles of the three. All of them get finished with a squeeze of calamansi, which is the one free ingredient on the plate.
lighter: Ask for less chicharon on top. It is the single heaviest topping at 55 calories per small handful.
Keep the egg, skip the extra sauce. The egg gives protein, the sauce is flour and oil.
Order the Jollibee size (305) if you want palabok without committing to a 440 calorie plate.
Do not add rice or pandesal. Palabok is already a full carbohydrate serving.

faq.q: How many calories in Jollibee palabok?
faq.a: About 305 calories for a Palabok Fiesta according to FatSecret. It is a smaller serving than a carinderia plate, which is closer to 440.

faq.q: Is pancit palabok healthy?
faq.a: The base is fine at about 300 calories for noodles and shrimp sauce. The chicharon and extra toppings are what push it to 440 plus. Ask for light chicharon and keep the egg.

faq.q: How many calories in pancit malabon?
faq.a: About 500 calories per plate, roughly 10 to 15 percent more than palabok, because the sauce uses more shrimp fat and the noodles are thicker.

faq.q: What is the difference between palabok and luglug?
faq.a: Same sauce and toppings. Palabok uses thin bihon, luglug uses thick noodles and is the Pampanga name. Calories are close, within about 30 per plate.

foods.source: estimate from components; Jollibee figure from FatSecret Jollibee Pancit Palabok entry (305 kcal)

foods.name: Lumpia Shanghai
foods.metaDescription: Five pieces of lumpia shanghai are about 280 calories, or 55 each. FatSecret lists 110 for two. Numbers per piece, per party plate, and the sweet chili dip.
foods.summary: Thin spring rolls filled with ground pork, carrot and onion, rolled tight and deep fried. Served with sweet chili sauce or banana ketchup at every birthday, fiesta and Jollibee party.
foods.answer: Five pieces of lumpia shanghai, about 100g, are around 280 calories, or roughly 55 calories per small piece. FatSecret lists lumpia at 110 calories for 2 pieces. Add 2 tablespoons of sweet chili sauce and the plate is 320. Nobody stops at five.
realTalk: Each piece is a 20g roll: about 12g of pork filling (30 calories), a 5g wrapper (14), and the oil it soaks up in the fryer (about 12). That is 55 each, and the wrapper-to-filling ratio is what makes lumpia cheaper per calorie than a meatball. The oil is the swing factor. A thin roll fried in fresh oil absorbs about 2g, a fat roll in tired oil absorbs 4g, which doubles that part of the count.

The problem is the plate, never the piece. A party tray of 50 pieces costs 350 to 500 pesos and a normal adult clears 10 to 15 across an afternoon without noticing, which is 550 to 830 calories. At a carinderia, lumpia shanghai as ulam is 4 to 5 pieces with a cup of rice, 540 calories, and the pieces there are usually larger, around 30g each.

The dip is sugar. Sweet chili sauce is about 15 calories per tablespoon, banana ketchup about 12, spiced vinegar is under 5. Two tablespoons of sweet chili on 10 pieces adds 30 calories, which is not dramatic, but it is a lot of sugar for a savoury snack. Vinegar with garlic and chili is the traditional pairing and it happens to be the lightest.
lighter: Air fry or bake them after rolling. Five pieces drop from 280 to about 200 with no oil in the pan.
Use ground chicken or a half-pork, half-minced-vegetable filling. Chicken lumpia is about 45 calories each.
Count them out before you start eating. Ten on a plate is a decision, fifteen from a tray is an accident.
Dip in spiced vinegar instead of sweet chili sauce.

components.name: Ground pork filling with carrot and onion

variants.name: Lumpiang sariwa, 1 roll
variants.note: Fresh, not fried, with peanut sauce

faq.q: How many calories in one lumpia shanghai?
faq.a: About 55 calories for a standard 20g piece. FatSecret lists lumpia at 110 calories per 2 pieces. Jumbo carinderia pieces are closer to 85.

faq.q: How many calories in 10 pieces of lumpia?
faq.a: About 560 calories for 10 standard pieces, or around 590 with sweet chili sauce. That is more than a plate of chicken adobo with rice.

faq.q: Is lumpia shanghai healthy?
faq.a: It is fried pork in a wrapper, so no, but at 55 calories a piece it is manageable in fives. The wrapper is thin and the filling is real meat. The issue is the party tray, not the roll.

faq.q: How many calories in lumpiang sariwa?
faq.a: About 220 calories per fresh roll with peanut sauce. The crepe wrapper is not fried, and the filling is mostly vegetables, so it is lighter than 4 pieces of shanghai.

foods.source: FatSecret generic lumpia (110 kcal per 2 pieces), scaled to 5 pieces

foods.name: Tapsilog
aka: Beef Tapa with Garlic Rice and Egg
foods.metaDescription: A plate of tapsilog is about 650 calories: 230 from the beef tapa, 320 from garlic rice, 90 from the fried egg. Numbers for every silog plate inside.
foods.summary: Cured beef tapa fried until the edges crisp, a mound of garlic fried rice, and a sunny-side-up egg. The original silog, served 24 hours a day at every tapsihan.
foods.answer: A standard tapsilog plate is about 650 calories. That is 100g of beef tapa (230 calories), 200g of sinangag garlic rice (320), one fried egg (90) and a spoon of atchara (10). A tapsihan that gives extra rice with the meal pushes it to 900.
realTalk: The rice is the biggest item, and it is not plain rice. Sinangag is day-old rice fried in garlic oil, and a 200g cup carries about 8g of oil, so it lands at 320 calories versus 260 for the same cup steamed. Then the egg is fried in more oil, 90 calories rather than the 70 of a boiled one. Between them, the oil on a tapsilog plate is about 150 calories before the beef.

The tapa itself is the leanest part of the plate. Beef tapa is thin-sliced sirloin or round cured with soy, garlic, sugar and vinegar, and 100g cooked is about 230 calories with 25g of protein. A tapsihan that uses fattier cuts or fries the tapa in lard will run higher, and some places add a spoon of the cooking oil over the rice as a finish. That spoon is 40 calories.

The silog family runs from about 520 to 700 for a standard plate. Cornsilog (corned beef) and bangsilog (fried bangus) are at the low end, tapsilog and tosilog sit in the middle at 650 to 660, and longsilog is the heaviest at 700 because sweet longganisa is a fatty sausage. The rice and egg are fixed at about 410, so the ulam alone decides the range.
lighter: Ask for plain steamed rice instead of sinangag. That is 60 calories less and you lose nothing except garlic.
Ask for the egg boiled or poached. About 20 calories less and no extra frying oil.
Half rice. Tapa is salty and the atchara is sweet, so half a cup carries the flavour fine.
Skip the extra oil drizzle some tapsihan spoon over the rice. Ask for it dry.

faq.q: How many calories in tapsilog without egg?
faq.a: About 560 calories for tapa and garlic rice only. The fried egg adds 90.

faq.q: How many calories in beef tapa alone?
faq.a: About 230 calories per 100g cooked, with roughly 25g of protein. It is the leanest part of the plate.

faq.q: Is tapsilog good for breakfast on a diet?
faq.a: It has 34g of protein, which is good. The 650 total is high for one meal, so the fix is plain rice instead of sinangag and a boiled egg, which brings it to about 570.

faq.q: Which silog has the lowest calories?
faq.a: Cornsilog at around 520, then bangsilog at 560. Longsilog is the highest of the common ones at about 700.

foods.source: estimate from components

foods.name: Longsilog
aka: Longganisa with Garlic Rice and Egg
foods.metaDescription: A longsilog plate with 2 longganisa is about 700 calories, the heaviest of the silog breakfasts. Where the sausage, garlic rice and egg each land.
foods.summary: Two sweet Filipino pork sausages, a mound of garlic fried rice and a fried egg. The silog with the most sugar and the most fat, and the one most people order.
foods.answer: A standard longsilog plate with 2 pieces of longganisa is about 700 calories. Two sweet longganisa (90g) are around 290 calories, the 200g of sinangag is 320, and the fried egg is 90. Three sausages with extra rice, a common tapsihan order, is 1,100.
realTalk: Longganisa is pork, pork fat, sugar and garlic in a casing. The sweet Pampanga style (hamonado) is about 320 calories per 100g cooked, and a lot of that is sugar, 8 to 10g per sausage. The fat renders out in the pan and most tapsihan cooks tip it back over the rice. That is why longsilog beats tapsilog by 50 calories even though the sausages weigh less than the tapa.

The style of longganisa changes the plate a lot. Vigan longganisa is garlicky, sour and leaner, about 240 calories per 2 pieces. Lucban is similar at 260. The skinless sweet ones sold at supermarkets are small, about 110 each, so 2 pieces is only 220. The tapsihan default is the plump sweet kind at 145 each, and the plate assumes that.

A longsilog at a Manila tapsihan is 75 to 110 pesos and usually comes with a cup of sinangag that is more like 250g than 200g. If the plate looks generous, count 400 for the rice instead of 320. Add a cup of 3-in-1 coffee at 90 calories and breakfast is close to 900 before 8am.
lighter: Order 1 longganisa instead of 2 and add a second egg. That drops the plate to about 630 with more protein.
Choose Vigan or Lucban longganisa when the tapsihan has it. About 50 calories less per pair, and less sugar.
Plain rice instead of sinangag saves 60. Ask them not to drizzle the sausage fat over it.
Skip the 3-in-1 coffee. Black kape barako is 5 calories.

faq.q: How many calories in one longganisa?
faq.a: About 145 calories for a standard sweet longganisa (45g cooked). Skinless supermarket ones are about 110, Vigan about 120.

faq.q: Is longsilog or tapsilog higher in calories?
faq.a: Longsilog, at about 700 versus 650 for tapsilog. Longganisa has more fat and sugar than beef tapa, and its rendered fat usually ends up on the rice.

faq.q: How much sugar is in longganisa?
faq.a: Sweet hamonado longganisa has about 8 to 10g of sugar per piece. Vigan and Lucban styles have almost none, which is why they taste sour and garlicky instead.

faq.q: How many calories in longsilog without rice?
faq.a: About 380 calories for 2 longganisa and a fried egg. The 200g of sinangag is 320 of the standard plate.

foods.source: estimate from components

foods.name: Halo-Halo
foods.metaDescription: A regular tall glass of halo-halo is about 450 calories, and the special with ice cream is 560.
foods.summary: Shaved ice over sweetened beans, jackfruit, kaong, nata de coco, sago and banana, topped with evaporated milk, leche flan, ube halaya and sometimes ice cream. Stir before eating.
foods.answer: A regular tall glass of halo-halo, about 400g, is around 450 calories. The sweetened fruits and beans are 200 of that, the leche flan 100, the ube halaya 90, and the evaporated milk 80. A special with a scoop of ice cream is closer to 560. The ice is zero.
realTalk: Every layer under the ice is preserved in sugar syrup. Sweetened red beans, garbanzos, kaong, nata de coco, macapuno and minatamis na saging are all about 150 to 200 calories per 100g in their syrup. A regular glass has around 120g of them, which is 200 calories before any topping goes on. The ice is doing nothing except making it feel light.

The toppings decide whether it is 450 or 650. A slab of leche flan is 100 calories for 40g. Ube halaya is 90 for the same weight because it is mashed purple yam cooked with condensed milk and butter. A scoop of ube ice cream is 100 to 120. A carinderia halo-halo for 50 pesos skips the flan and ice cream and lands around 300. A restaurant special for 150 to 200 pesos has all three and lands past 550.

It is a dessert most people eat after a full meal. A lunch of sinigang with rice at 580 and then a special halo-halo at 560 is 1,140 calories. The 3pm merienda version on its own is easier to fit, because it replaces a snack instead of following a meal. The sugar hit is about 70g either way, roughly the same as two cans of Coke.
lighter: Order mais con yelo or saba con yelo instead. Same shaved ice and milk, about 220 to 260 calories.
Ask for it without leche flan and ube halaya. That takes 190 calories off a special.
Skip the ice cream scoop. Ube ice cream is 100 to 120 on its own.
Ask for less evaporated milk, or ask for fresh milk. Evap is 80 calories per 60ml pour.

components.name: Sweetened beans, jackfruit, kaong, nata, banana in syrup

portions.label: Small cup, no flan or ube

faq.q: How many calories in a halo-halo special?
faq.a: About 560 calories with ice cream, leche flan and ube halaya. A regular glass without ice cream is around 450.

faq.q: How much sugar is in halo-halo?
faq.a: Roughly 65 to 75g in a regular glass, from the syrup-preserved beans and fruit, the evaporated milk and the flan. That is about the same as two 330ml cans of soft drink.

faq.q: Is halo-halo healthy?
faq.a: No, it is a sugar dessert. The one thing in its favour is volume: 400g of ice and fruit fills you up more than a 450 calorie slice of cake would.

faq.q: How many calories in mais con yelo?
faq.a: About 220 calories for a glass of sweet corn, shaved ice, sugar and evaporated milk. It is the lightest of the con yelo desserts.

foods.source: estimate from components

foods.name: Bulalo
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of bulalo with shank and marrow is about 520 calories. The marrow alone is 170 of that.
foods.summary: Beef shank simmered for hours until the meat slides off the bone, served in clear broth with corn on the cob, cabbage and pechay. The marrow is the prize.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of bulalo, about 450g with beef shank, a marrow bone, corn and vegetables, is around 520 calories. The shank meat is 260, the marrow about 170, and the broth, corn and cabbage together under 100. The Tagaytay bowl-for-two is closer to 1,000.
realTalk: Bone marrow is about 780 calories per 100g, almost entirely fat. A single bulalo bone gives 20 to 25g of marrow, which is 160 to 200 calories that most people slurp out in ten seconds. The shank meat around it is honest beef at 260 calories per 120g with 30g of protein. So a bowl is 520 if you eat the marrow and about 350 if you leave it, which nobody does.

The Tagaytay version is a different animal. Bulalo houses along the ridge sell a bowl for 400 to 600 pesos meant for 2 to 3 people, with two or three bones and 300g of meat. Split in two, each person is at 800 to 1,000 calories of soup, then the rice, then the tawilis. The broth also carries a fat layer from 4 hours of simmering that adds 40 to 80 calories per bowl unless it was skimmed.

Nilagang baka is bulalo without the marrow bone and is the sensible choice at about 400 calories a bowl with the same meat and vegetables. Kansi, the Ilonggo sour cousin, is around 480 because it uses the same bone but the batuan fruit and less corn. Corn on the cob in bulalo is about 45 calories for a 50g chunk, so it is not the issue.
lighter: Order nilagang baka. Same shank, same cabbage and corn, no marrow bone, about 120 calories less.
Eat the marrow from one bone only if the bowl has two. Each bone is roughly 170 calories.
Skim the fat from the top of the broth. In a long-simmered bulalo that layer is 40 to 80 calories per bowl.
Fill up on the pechay and cabbage before the rice. They are under 15 calories a handful in this broth.

portions.label: Tagaytay bowl, half of a sharing order

faq.q: How many calories in bulalo with rice?
faq.a: About 780 calories for a standard bowl with 1 cup of rice. With 2 cups, which is normal in Tagaytay, it is 1,040.

faq.q: How many calories in bone marrow from bulalo?
faq.a: About 160 to 200 calories per bone. Marrow is roughly 780 calories per 100g and a bulalo bone holds 20 to 25g.

faq.q: Is bulalo healthy?
faq.a: The broth, shank and vegetables are fine, about 350 calories with 30g of protein. The marrow and the fat layer on top are what push it to 520. Nilaga is the same dish without them.

faq.q: What is the difference between bulalo and nilaga?
faq.a: Bulalo uses the shank cut with the marrow bone, nilaga uses cheaper beef cuts without it. Nilaga is about 400 calories a bowl versus 520 for bulalo.

foods.source: estimate from components

foods.name: Tinola
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of tinolang manok with one chicken piece, green papaya and malunggay is about 300 calories. The lightest of the big three Filipino soups.
foods.summary: Chicken simmered in ginger broth with green papaya or sayote, malunggay or chili leaves, and fish sauce. The sick-day soup, the rainy-day soup, and the cheapest ulam at the carinderia.
foods.answer: A carinderia bowl of tinolang manok, about 400g with one bone-in chicken piece, papaya and leaves, is around 300 calories. The chicken is 200 of that, the ginger broth about 30, the papaya 30, and the oil used to sauté the ginger and garlic 45. It is the lightest of tinola, sinigang and bulalo.
realTalk: Tinola broth is water, ginger, garlic, onion and patis. A cup of it is about 15 calories, and even after the chicken simmers in it for 30 minutes it stays under 30 because chicken thigh does not shed fat the way pork belly does. The one place calories sneak in is the start, when the cook fries the ginger and garlic in a tablespoon of oil (about 90 calories for the pot, 45 per bowl if the pot serves two).

The chicken piece is the whole number. A bone-in thigh or leg with skin, about 120g cooked, is 200 calories with 22g of protein. A skinless breast piece of the same weight is 140. Native chicken (manok na bisaya) is leaner and tougher and lands around 160 for the same piece, which is why the long-simmered Visayan tinola tastes different and runs lighter.

The green papaya and malunggay are practically free, about 30 calories per 80g of papaya and 10 per handful of leaves, and they carry most of the volume. A 400g bowl is mostly broth and vegetable by weight. With 1 cup of rice the meal is 560, which is one of the better carinderia lunches you can order for 60 to 80 pesos.
lighter: Ask for the breast piece or take the skin off. About 60 calories less per bowl.
Ask for extra papaya or sayote. It is 30 calories a serving and it fills the bowl.
One cup of rice. Tinola broth on rice is good enough that people go back, and that second cup is 260.
Squeeze calamansi and add fresh chili instead of extra patis. Zero calories, more flavour.

components.name: Chicken thigh or leg, bone-in with skin
Oil for sautéing ginger and garlic

faq.q: How many calories in tinola with rice?
faq.a: About 560 calories for a standard bowl with 1 cup of rice. The soup alone is around 300.

faq.q: Is tinola good for weight loss?
faq.a: It is one of the best carinderia choices. About 300 calories a bowl with 26g of protein, and most of the volume is broth, papaya and leaves. Pick the breast piece and it drops to 230.

faq.q: How many calories in tinola broth only?
faq.a: About 15 to 30 calories per cup. Ginger, garlic, onion and fish sauce add almost nothing, and chicken thigh sheds very little fat into it.

faq.q: Which is lower in calories, tinola or sinigang?
faq.a: Tinola, at about 300 per bowl versus 320 for pork sinigang. The gap widens if the sinigang uses pork belly, which can push it past 400.

foods.source: estimate from components

foods.name: Pineapple Bun (Bo Lo Bao)
foods.metaDescription: A pineapple bun from a Hong Kong bakery is about 310 calories. No pineapple inside, just a sugar crust on a sweet bun. Here is the full breakdown.
foods.summary: The bo lo bao is a soft sweet bun with a cracked sugar-and-lard crust on top that looks like pineapple skin. Every Hong Kong bakery and cha chaan teng sells them, usually for HK$5 to HK$12.
foods.answer: One standard pineapple bun (about 80g) is around 310 calories. Roughly 200 of that is the sweet bread itself and the other 95 or so is the crunchy topping, which is basically sugar, flour and lard baked into a shell.
realTalk: There is no fruit in this thing. The name comes from the way the crust cracks in the oven. What you are actually eating is 48g of carbs, most of it refined flour and sugar, packed into something you finish in four bites. A bun at 310 calories is more than a bowl of rice, which sits around 260, and it comes with far less staying power. Most people who buy one at 3pm are hungry again by 5.

The topping is where the fat hides. That 15g crust adds around 95 calories on its own because it is made with lard or shortening plus a big hit of sugar. The Centre for Food Safety tested pineapple buns in its bread survey and found them low in sodium and moderate in fat compared to cocktail buns and croissants, so among Hong Kong bakery items this is actually one of the tamer choices at roughly 10g of fat.

Size varies a lot between shops. A small bakery bun can be 65g and closer to 250 calories. The big fluffy ones from the famous cha chaan tengs in Mong Kok and Central push 100g and land near 380 calories. If the bun is warm and the crust is thick and glossy, assume the high end. Add a slab of butter (bo lo yau) and you are looking at around 390 calories before your milk tea arrives.
lighter: Eat it as a snack on its own, not as a side to a full breakfast set. One bun plus a hot milk tea is about 420 calories, which is a reasonable light breakfast.
Skip the butter slab. That single 10g piece adds 75 calories and most of the extra fat.
Pick the smaller buns from neighbourhood bakeries. The difference between a 65g bun and a 100g bun is about 130 calories.
If you want the crust, pull it off and eat that part, then leave half the plain bread. You keep the good bit for about 180 calories.

components.name: Sweet bun dough (flour, milk, sugar, egg)

variants.name: Pineapple bun with pork chop
variants.note: Fried bone-in chop inside the bun

faq.q: Is there pineapple in a pineapple bun?
faq.a: No. The name refers to the cracked golden crust, which looks like pineapple skin. The bun is plain sweet bread with a sugar and lard topping, about 310 calories.

faq.q: How many calories in a pineapple bun with butter?
faq.a: A bo lo yau with a 10g butter slab is roughly 390 calories. The butter alone is about 75 calories and doubles the fat content of the bun.

faq.q: Is a pineapple bun a healthy breakfast?
faq.a: It is 310 calories with about 7g of protein and 48g of refined carbs, so it will not keep you full for long. It is fine as an occasional breakfast but pair it with something with protein, like an egg or a glass of milk.

foods.source: am730 HK dietitian bread ranking (310 kcal per bun); CFS Hong Kong bread survey for fat and sodium context

foods.name: Bo Lo Yau (Pineapple Bun with Butter)
foods.metaDescription: A bo lo yau (pineapple bun with a cold slab of butter) is about 390 calories. The butter alone adds 75. Here is what you are actually eating.
foods.summary: Bo lo yau is a warm pineapple bun split open with a thick slice of cold butter pushed inside so it half melts. It is the signature cha chaan teng snack, usually HK$12 to HK$20 with a milk tea set.
foods.answer: One bo lo yau is around 390 calories: about 310 from the pineapple bun and 75 from the 10g butter slab. Fat nearly doubles compared to a plain bun, going from 10g to about 19g, because butter is almost pure fat.
realTalk: The butter is the whole point and also the whole problem. A cha chaan teng slab is usually 10g, sometimes 15g at the generous places, and butter is 7.2 calories per gram. That means the slab is 75 to 110 calories with zero protein and zero carbs. It is the easiest calorie you will ever eat because it melts into the bun and you barely notice it is there.

A bo lo yau plus a hot milk tea is the classic afternoon tea set, and it lands at about 500 calories. That is a quarter of a normal adult's day in a snack that takes 5 minutes to eat. Compare it to a bowl of century egg congee at 260 calories, which will keep you full for three hours. The bun set will not.

Not all bo lo yau are equal. The famous places in Mong Kok and Sai Wan use bigger 100g buns and thicker butter, so those push 450 to 480 calories. A basic bakery bun with a thin slice is closer to 350. The tell is how much butter is visible when they bring it out. If you can see a yellow slab thicker than a HK$10 coin, assume the high end.
lighter: Ask for half the butter. Most cha chaan tengs will do it and you save about 40 calories without losing the taste.
Order it with a hot lemon tea (36 calories) instead of milk tea (110) and the set drops to under 430.
Share one bun and each have a boiled egg or a small bowl of congee instead. You get the taste and some actual protein.
Treat it as a once a week snack rather than a daily 3pm habit. Five bo lo yau a week is nearly 2,000 calories, which is more than half a kilo of body fat per month if nothing else changes.

variants.name: Bo lo yau with condensed milk
Bo lo yau with pork chop

faq.q: How much butter is in a bo lo yau?
faq.a: Usually a 10g slab, sometimes 15g at generous places. That is 75 to 110 calories of pure fat added to a 310 calorie bun.

faq.q: Is bo lo yau worse than a croissant?
faq.a: About the same. A plain croissant is around 270 calories with 14g fat; a bo lo yau is 390 with 19g fat but is also bigger. Per gram they are close.

faq.q: Can I eat bo lo yau while losing weight?
faq.a: Yes, as long as it fits your day. At 390 calories it is a snack, not a meal. Have it and eat lighter at dinner, or skip the butter and save 75 calories.

foods.source: Estimate from components: am730 dietitian figure for pineapple bun (310 kcal) plus 10g butter

foods.name: Egg Waffle (Gai Daan Zai)
foods.metaDescription: One full sheet of gai daan zai (Hong Kong egg waffle) is about 390 calories, and the big ones hit 525. It looks light but it is mostly sugar and flour.
foods.summary: Gai daan zai is the honeycomb-shaped egg waffle sold from street carts and hole-in-the-wall shops across Hong Kong. One sheet has about 30 little egg-shaped bubbles, crisp outside and cakey inside, for HK$15 to HK$25.
foods.answer: A standard sheet of egg waffle is about 390 calories, based on the HK Department of Health figure of 389.5 kcal per piece. Larger sheets from the popular shops weigh more and land around 525 calories. Almost all of it is carbohydrate, about 70g, from flour and sugar.
realTalk: This is the snack that fools people. It is airy, it is not greasy to the touch, and it feels like nothing. But the batter is flour, sugar, egg, evaporated milk and custard powder, and one sheet carries 70g of carbs. That is the same carb load as a bowl and a half of rice, eaten standing on the pavement in Mong Kok in about 6 minutes.

Sugar is the main driver. A typical batter uses around 30g of sugar per sheet, which is 115 calories before the flour even counts. That is why the outside caramelises and goes crisp. Fat is actually modest at about 8g, which is why it scores better than a Belgian style waffle (格仔餅) with butter, peanut butter and condensed milk, which the same data puts at 440 calories.

The trendy versions are worse. A matcha or chocolate chip sheet adds 40 to 80 calories. Roll it around a scoop of ice cream and you are at 550 or more. The plain original from a cart is the lowest calorie way to eat this, and at 390 it is still a full meal's worth of energy with only 9g of protein.
lighter: Share one sheet between two people. Half a sheet is 195 calories, which is a fair snack.
Stick to the original flavour. Chocolate chip, cheese and matcha versions add 40 to 80 calories each.
Skip the ice cream roll. That version is over 550 calories, closer to a meal than a snack.
Eat it instead of dinner carbs, not on top of them. A sheet of egg waffle after a plate of siu mei rice is a 1,300 calorie evening.

faq.q: How many calories in one gai daan zai?
faq.a: About 390 calories for a standard sheet, according to HK Department of Health data. The larger shop versions weigh more and reach 525 calories.

faq.q: Is egg waffle healthier than a Belgian waffle?
faq.a: Slightly. Egg waffle is about 390 calories with 8g fat. A Hong Kong style grid waffle with butter, peanut butter and condensed milk is around 440 calories with 21g fat.

faq.q: Why is egg waffle so high in calories if it is not fried?
faq.a: Because the batter has roughly 30g of sugar and 50g of flour per sheet. That is 70g of carbs, which is the bulk of the 390 calories. No oil needed.

foods.source: HK Department of Health / HK Food Exchange Handbook via healthyD.com (389.5 kcal per piece); HKET dietitian figure 525 kcal for large sheets

foods.name: Hong Kong Milk Tea
foods.metaDescription: A hot Hong Kong milk tea is about 110 calories per cup according to the Centre for Food Safety. Iced is 130. The evaporated milk is where the fat comes from.
foods.summary: Hong Kong milk tea is strong black tea pulled through a cloth filter and mixed with evaporated milk and sugar. Every cha chaan teng serves it, hot in a cup or iced in a glass, for about HK$18 to HK$25.
foods.answer: One cup of hot Hong Kong milk tea (240ml) is about 110 calories, based on Centre for Food Safety data. An iced milk tea (300ml) is around 130 calories at normal sweetness and 100 if you order it less sweet. The evaporated milk contributes most of the fat, about 5g per cup.
realTalk: Milk tea on its own is not a big problem. At 110 calories a cup it is less than a can of Coke (140) and it comes with about 3g of protein from the evaporated milk. The problem is frequency. A lot of office workers in Central drink two a day, one at breakfast and one at 3:15pm with the afternoon tea set. That is 220 calories a day, over 1,500 a week, from a drink they do not count.

The evaporated milk is the calorie driver, not the tea. Black tea is about 2 calories per cup. A cha chaan teng adds around 50 to 60ml of evaporated milk, which is 70 to 80 calories and nearly all the fat. Then 7 to 8g of sugar adds another 30. If you order cha jau (茶走), where condensed milk replaces both the evaporated milk and the sugar, the cup goes up to around 170 calories because condensed milk is roughly 50 calories a tablespoon.

Iced is a bit higher than hot because the glass is bigger and needs more sugar to taste right over the ice. CFS puts iced milk tea at 130 calories at regular sweetness with about 22g of sugar, which is more than half of the daily 40g limit the WHO suggests. Order it siu tim (少甜, less sweet) and it drops to 100 calories and 15g sugar.
lighter: Order siu tim or jau tim (少甜 / 走甜). Less sweet saves about 30 calories per glass; no sugar saves nearly 50.
Choose hot over iced. The hot cup is 240ml and 110 calories; iced is 300ml and 130.
Avoid cha jau. Condensed milk pushes the cup to about 170 calories.
If you drink two a day, make one of them a hot lemon tea at 36 calories. That single swap saves over 500 calories a week.

variants.name: Cha jau (condensed milk)
variants.note: Condensed milk replaces evaporated milk and sugar

variants.name: Iced milk tea with pearls
variants.note: Bubble tea shop version, less sweet

faq.q: How many calories in a Hong Kong milk tea?
faq.a: About 110 calories for a hot 240ml cup and 130 for a 300ml iced glass at regular sweetness, according to the Centre for Food Safety.

faq.q: Does Hong Kong milk tea have a lot of sugar?
faq.a: A hot cup has about 7g of sugar. An iced glass at regular sweetness has about 22g, which is over half the WHO daily suggestion of 40g.

faq.q: Is milk tea worse than coffee for weight loss?
faq.a: Only slightly. A cha chaan teng hot coffee with milk is about 100 calories and milk tea is 110. Black coffee is 29. The milk and sugar matter more than the tea or coffee.

foods.source: Centre for Food Safety Hong Kong, Nutrient Content of Non-Prepackaged Beverages (110 kcal hot, 130 kcal iced)

foods.name: Yuenyeung (Coffee Milk Tea)
foods.metaDescription: A hot yuenyeung is about 130 calories and the iced version is 160, according to the Centre for Food Safety.
foods.summary: Yuenyeung is Hong Kong milk tea mixed with coffee, roughly 7 parts tea to 3 parts coffee, with evaporated milk and sugar. It is a cha chaan teng standard, hot or iced, for about HK$20.
foods.answer: A hot cup of yuenyeung (240ml) is about 130 calories. The iced version (300ml) is around 160 calories at regular sweetness or 120 less sweet. It runs about 20 calories higher than plain milk tea because the coffee bitterness gets balanced with a bit more sugar.
realTalk: People assume yuenyeung and milk tea are the same calorie-wise. They are close but not identical. CFS data puts hot milk tea at 110 and hot yuenyeung at 130, with the difference being sugar: 7g in milk tea versus 12g in yuenyeung. Cha chaan tengs add more because coffee makes the drink more bitter and customers complain if it is not sweet enough.

The iced version is where it climbs. At 160 calories and 24g of sugar per 300ml glass, an iced yuenyeung is more than a can of Coke. Two of those a day, which is not unusual for anyone working long hours in Kwun Tong or Tsim Sha Tsui, is 320 calories and nearly 50g of sugar before you count any food.

The fat side is the same as milk tea: about 5g per cup, all from the 50ml or so of evaporated milk. That is not much on its own. The reason to care about this drink is really the sugar, which is why the less sweet order (少甜) knocks 40 calories off the iced version and brings it to 120, the same as a hot milk tea.
lighter: Order iced yuenyeung less sweet (少甜). It drops from 160 to 120 calories and sugar goes from 24g to 17g.
Hot over iced. The 240ml hot cup is 130 calories versus 160 for the iced glass.
If you want the caffeine hit without the sugar, a hot cha chaan teng black coffee is about 29 calories.
Do not pair it with a bo lo yau every afternoon. That set is around 520 calories.

faq.q: How many calories in an iced yuenyeung?
faq.a: About 160 calories for a 300ml glass at regular sweetness, or 120 calories if you order it less sweet, based on Centre for Food Safety figures.

faq.q: Is yuenyeung higher in calories than milk tea?
faq.a: Yes, by about 20 to 30 calories. Hot yuenyeung is 130 versus 110 for milk tea, mostly because more sugar is added to balance the coffee.

faq.q: How much caffeine is in yuenyeung?
faq.a: Roughly 100 to 150mg per cup, since it combines strong tea and coffee. That is similar to a regular cup of brewed coffee.

foods.source: Centre for Food Safety Hong Kong, Nutrient Content of Non-Prepackaged Beverages (130 kcal hot, 160 kcal iced)

foods.name: Hong Kong Iced Lemon Tea
foods.metaDescription: A cha chaan teng iced lemon tea is about 140 calories and 25g of sugar per glass. Order it less sweet and it drops to 90. The hot version is only 36.
foods.summary: Iced lemon tea is black tea over ice with three or four lemon slices you crush with a long spoon, sweetened with syrup. It is the most ordered cold drink in Hong Kong cha chaan tengs, about HK$18 to HK$22.
foods.answer: One 300ml glass of iced lemon tea at regular sweetness is about 140 calories, all from roughly 25g of sugar syrup. Order it less sweet (少甜) and it drops to around 90 calories. The hot version with half a teaspoon of sugar is only 36 calories.
realTalk: This drink has a health halo it does not deserve. No milk, has lemon, looks light. But the tea and lemon contribute almost nothing; CFS data shows the 140 calories come entirely from about 25g of sugar syrup, which is 6 teaspoons. That is more sugar than a glass of iced milk tea (22g). It just does not taste as sweet because the lemon masks it.

The gap between hot and iced is huge. Hot lemon tea at a cha chaan teng is 36 calories because they give you a small cup and half a teaspoon of sugar. Iced is a 300ml glass and the syrup goes in by the ladle. Same ingredients, nearly four times the calories. If you are drinking it for the lemon, the hot one gives you that for basically nothing.

Less sweet actually works here more than with milk drinks. Because there is no milk fat, the sugar is the only variable. CFS puts less-sweet iced lemon tea at 90 calories and 18g sugar. Ask for no sugar (走甜) and it is under 15 calories, and you can still crush the lemon in and have a drink that tastes like something.
lighter: Order it 走甜 (no sugar). You get the same tea and lemon for under 15 calories.
If no sugar is too harsh, 少甜 (less sweet) brings it to 90 calories, saving 50.
Go hot instead of iced when you can. Hot lemon tea is 36 calories.
Crush the lemon slices hard and let the drink sit a minute. The stronger lemon flavour makes the reduced sugar version taste fine.

variants.name: Iced lemon honey
variants.note: Honey instead of syrup, still 21g sugar

faq.q: How much sugar is in a Hong Kong iced lemon tea?
faq.a: About 25g at regular sweetness, roughly 6 teaspoons. That is more than half the WHO daily suggestion of 40g, in one glass.

faq.q: Is iced lemon tea healthier than milk tea?
faq.a: Barely. Iced lemon tea is 140 calories and iced milk tea is 130. Lemon tea has no fat but more sugar. Order either one less sweet and the difference shrinks to nothing.

faq.q: Does iced lemon tea help with weight loss?
faq.a: Only the no-sugar version. At 140 calories a glass, the regular version is a small snack's worth of pure sugar. Order 走甜 and it becomes a near-zero calorie drink.

foods.source: Centre for Food Safety Hong Kong, Nutrient Content of Non-Prepackaged Beverages (140 kcal regular, 90 kcal less sweet, 36 kcal hot)

foods.name: Red Bean Ice
aka: Iced Red Bean with Evaporated Milk
foods.metaDescription: Red bean ice is the highest calorie drink on the cha chaan teng menu at about 260 calories and 36g sugar per glass. Here is why and what to order instead.
foods.summary: Red bean ice is a tall glass of sweetened red beans, crushed ice, evaporated milk and syrup, eaten with a long spoon. It is the classic Hong Kong summer drink, about HK$22 to HK$28 at a cha chaan teng.
foods.answer: One 300ml glass of red bean ice is about 260 calories with 36g of sugar, according to Centre for Food Safety testing. That makes it the highest calorie drink on a typical cha chaan teng menu, roughly double an iced milk tea (130). Ordering it less sweet only brings it down to about 240.
realTalk: Red bean ice tops every cha chaan teng drink ranking in Hong Kong. CFS measured it at 87 calories per 100ml, which is more than a cola (about 42). The reason is that the red beans are cooked in sugar before they go in, then the drink gets syrup, then evaporated milk on top. There are three separate sugar sources in one glass. A 300ml glass ends up around 260 calories, equal to a bowl of rice.

The evaporated milk is the only thing giving you any nutrition. About 50ml adds 70 calories, 4g of protein and most of the 5g of fat. The beans themselves have some fibre, but 100g of sweetened red bean paste is about 150 calories, and that is what the bottom third of the glass is. So a drink that looks like a snack is really dessert.

Less sweet barely helps here. CFS found the less-sweet version still lands at 240 calories and 30g sugar, because the beans are pre-sweetened and the shop cannot take that out. This is one drink where the 少甜 order does very little. If you want it, have it as your dessert, not as your drink with lunch.
lighter: Treat it as dessert. If you order red bean ice, skip the tong sui or the egg tart after.
Share it. Two spoons in one glass is a 130 calorie treat each.
If you want something cold and milky for fewer calories, an iced milk tea is 130 and an iced lemon tea less sweet is 90.
Ask for less syrup (少糖水), not just less sweet. Some shops will hold back the extra syrup and that saves around 40 calories.

faq.q: How many calories in a red bean ice?
faq.a: About 260 calories per 300ml glass, with 36g of sugar, based on Centre for Food Safety data. It is the highest calorie drink on most cha chaan teng menus.

faq.q: Is red bean ice healthy because of the beans?
faq.a: The beans add a little fibre and protein, but they are cooked in sugar. A glass has as many calories as a bowl of rice. It is closer to a dessert than a healthy drink.

faq.q: Does ordering red bean ice less sweet help?
faq.a: Only a little. Less sweet drops it from 260 to about 240 calories because the beans are already sweetened before they go in the glass.

foods.source: Centre for Food Safety Hong Kong, Nutrient Content of Non-Prepackaged Beverages (260 kcal regular, 240 kcal less sweet per 300ml)

foods.name: Macaroni in Soup with Ham
foods.metaDescription: A cha chaan teng bowl of macaroni in soup with ham is about 320 calories, one of the lightest breakfasts on the menu.
foods.summary: Macaroni in clear chicken broth with a few slices of ham is the standard Hong Kong cha chaan teng breakfast, usually served in a set with buttered toast and a hot drink for about HK$30 to HK$40.
foods.answer: One bowl of ham macaroni soup is around 320 calories, based on a Hong Kong dietitian tally of cha chaan teng breakfasts. About 200 of that is the macaroni, 50 is the ham, and the broth is nearly free. It is one of the lowest calorie hot breakfasts on the menu.
realTalk: Of everything on the cha chaan teng breakfast board, this is the one to order. Ham macaroni soup at 320 calories beats satay beef noodles (667), luncheon meat and egg instant noodles (785) and a buttered toast with fried egg (427). The macaroni is boiled, not fried, and the ham is lean. The broth is mostly water with a bit of chicken stock powder, around 40 calories a bowl.

The set is the trap. The macaroni bowl comes as a breakfast set with two slices of buttered toast (about 250 calories) and a hot milk tea (110). That takes a 320 calorie bowl to a 680 calorie breakfast. Ask for the toast without butter and it drops by about 100, or skip the toast and the whole thing stays under 450 with the tea.

Watch the protein swap. Ham gives you about 14g of protein for 50 calories. Change it to luncheon meat (餐肉) and the same two slices are 190 calories with double the fat. Change it to a fried egg on top (煎蛋) and add another 110. The 餐蛋通粉 version, with both, is closer to 600 calories and is one of the most popular orders in Hong Kong.
lighter: Order the macaroni with ham, not luncheon meat. That single swap saves about 140 calories.
Ask for the toast dry (多士走油) or skip it. Buttered toast in the set is about 250 calories.
Add a boiled egg instead of a fried one for 70 calories and an extra 6g of protein.
Do not drink all the soup. It is low in calories but a cha chaan teng broth can carry over 1,000mg of sodium.

portions.label: Full set with buttered toast and milk tea

faq.q: How many calories in a cha chaan teng macaroni breakfast?
faq.a: The ham macaroni bowl alone is about 320 calories. The full set with buttered toast and milk tea is around 680.

faq.q: Is macaroni soup a good breakfast for weight loss?
faq.a: Yes, relative to the other options. At 320 calories with 14g protein it is lighter than almost everything else on a cha chaan teng menu. Just skip the buttered toast.

faq.q: What is the difference between ham and luncheon meat in calories?
faq.a: Two slices of ham are about 50 calories. Two slices of fried luncheon meat are about 190. Luncheon meat has roughly four times the fat.

foods.source: HK01 registered dietitian ranking of 12 cha chaan teng items (ham macaroni 320 kcal)

foods.name: Curry Fish Balls
foods.metaDescription: A skewer of Hong Kong curry fish balls is about 120 calories with the sauce. The balls are only 65 to 75; the curry coating adds the rest.
foods.summary: Curry fish balls are the number one Hong Kong street snack: bouncy fried fish balls simmered in a spicy curry gravy, served 5 to 7 on a bamboo skewer for about HK$10 to HK$15 from carts in Mong Kok, Sham Shui Po and outside every MTR exit.
foods.answer: One skewer of six curry fish balls with sauce is about 120 calories. The fish balls themselves are 65 to 76 calories for 5 or 6 pieces, according to Hong Kong Department of Health figures, and the curry gravy clinging to them adds roughly 45 more. Protein is around 8g per skewer.
realTalk: Fish balls are the cheapest calories on the street in the good sense. Six balls without sauce are about 76 calories, which is less than a single egg tart (195). The Centre for Health Protection lists them at the very bottom of its street snack ranking, under stinky tofu (174 a piece), fried intestine (160 a skewer) and egg waffle (390 a sheet). Two skewers is still under 250 calories.

The sauce is where it moves. Hong Kong curry gravy at a street cart is oil, curry powder and a lot of starch to make it stick. A tablespoon is about 51 calories. Most skewers pick up two to three tablespoons of coating, so the sauce can be worth more than the fish balls. If the cart lets the skewer drain before handing it over, you are closer to 100. If it comes dripping, closer to 150.

The real issue is sodium, not calories. One skewer of six with curry gravy carries around 600mg of sodium, nearly a third of the 2,000mg daily limit. Add the sweet sauce and chili that most people squeeze on top and it goes higher. So while this is the lightest thing on the cart for calories, it is one of the saltiest, which matters if you have blood pressure to watch.
lighter: Let the skewer drain over the pot before you take it. That knocks the sauce down by about a third.
Skip the sweet sauce and chili on top. Each squeeze is 15 to 20 calories and more sodium.
Pick fish balls over siu mai at the same cart. Six siu mai are about 294 calories, four times the fish balls.
One skewer plus a bottle of water is a fine 120 calorie snack. Two skewers and a soft drink is 400.

portions.label: Cup of 12 balls with extra sauce

variants.name: Fish balls, plain in clear soup
Curry fish balls with sweet sauce and chili
Fish siu mai (6 pieces)
variants.note: Same cart, four times the calories

faq.q: How many calories in a skewer of curry fish balls?
faq.a: About 120 calories for six balls with curry sauce. The fish balls alone are around 76 calories according to HK Department of Health data; the sauce adds the rest.

faq.q: Are curry fish balls healthy?
