variants.note: Same beef and sauce, lighter noodle

variants.name: Satay beef noodles with fried egg
Luncheon meat and egg instant noodles
variants.note: The other cha chaan teng classic

faq.q: How many calories in satay beef noodles?
faq.a: About 670 calories per bowl, according to a Hong Kong registered dietitian's cha chaan teng breakfast ranking. Some estimates run to 700 or 800 for bigger bowls.

faq.q: Why are satay beef noodles so high in calories?
faq.a: The instant noodle cake is deep fried at the factory and carries about 470 calories on its own. The satay sauce is oil based and adds another 80.

faq.q: Is satay beef noodles healthy for breakfast?
faq.a: Not really. It has good protein (28g) but 35g of fat and about 1,300mg sodium. Swapping to rice vermicelli brings it down to around 420 calories.

foods.source: HK01 registered dietitian ranking of 12 cha chaan teng items (satay beef noodles 667 kcal); FWD HK health blog cites about 700 kcal

foods.name: Tonkotsu Ramen
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of tonkotsu ramen is about 525 calories at Ichiran. The kaedama refill adds 236 more. Here is where the calories actually sit.
foods.summary: Thin straight noodles in a cloudy pork bone broth that has been boiled for 12 hours or more, topped with chashu, spring onion and sometimes a soft egg. The Hakata style bowl is smaller than most people expect.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of tonkotsu ramen is about 525 calories. That is Ichiran's own figure for its classic bowl with noodles, broth, chashu and the red sauce. A kaedama noodle refill adds another 236 calories, so one bowl plus one refill is 761.
realTalk: The number surprises people because tonkotsu looks heavy. It is the cloudiest, fattiest looking broth on the menu, yet Ichiran's bowl comes in at 525 calories, lower than a miso ramen at 621. The reason is portion size. Hakata style noodles are thin and the standard serving is only about 110g cooked, roughly 236 calories worth, which is why the shop lets you order kaedama refills for 210 yen. The broth itself is where the fat lives, around 150 calories for 300ml, but you are not eating a giant pile of noodles with it.

The trap is the refill culture. One kaedama is 236 calories. Two kaedama and you are at 997 calories for what still feels like one bowl of ramen. Add a marinated egg for 80 calories and extra chashu for another 150 and a single Ichiran visit lands at 1,200 calories, which is more than half of most people's daily target. The bowl costs about 1,080 yen, and every add-on is cheap, so the bill stays small while the calories do not.

Drinking the soup matters more here than with shoyu ramen. A shoyu broth is mostly water and salt. A tonkotsu broth is emulsified pork fat, which is why it is white. If you finish the bowl to the bottom you get the full 150 or so calories of broth, plus about 5g of salt. Leaving half the soup saves around 75 calories and 2.5g of salt, and most Japanese ramen eaters leave it anyway.
lighter: Order the noodles at standard portion and skip kaedama. That alone keeps you at 525 instead of 761.
Ask for 'abura sukuname' (less oil) when the shop offers it. Ichiran's order sheet has a richness setting, and 'light' drops the fat noticeably.
Leave the broth. Half a bowl of tonkotsu soup is about 75 calories you never taste as food.
Add the egg, skip the extra chashu. The egg is 80 calories and 6g of protein. Extra chashu is 150 calories and mostly fat.
If you want to feel full, order the bean sprout topping. It is under 20 calories and doubles the volume.

components.name: Tare, red pepper sauce, spring onion

variants.name: Basic Hakata stall bowl
variants.note: Smaller noodle portion, no red sauce

variants.name: Extra chashu
variants.note: 3 to 4 extra slices of pork belly

faq.q: Is tonkotsu ramen higher in calories than other ramen?
faq.a: Per bowl, usually not. Ichiran's tonkotsu is 525 calories, while a typical miso ramen is 621. The broth is fattier, but the noodle portion is smaller. Where tonkotsu wins is per refill: each kaedama is 236 calories.

faq.q: How many calories are in Ichiran ramen?
faq.a: Ichiran lists its classic tonkotsu bowl at about 525 calories. A kaedama is 236 calories, the half-boiled egg is about 80, and extra chashu adds about 150.

faq.q: Can I eat tonkotsu ramen and still lose weight?
faq.a: Yes, as long as one bowl means one bowl. At 525 calories it fits a 1,800 calorie day easily. The problem is the 761 or 997 calorie version with refills, plus gyoza on the side.

faq.q: How much salt is in a bowl of tonkotsu ramen?
faq.a: Around 5 to 6g if you drink all the broth, which is most of the 6g daily limit Japan's health ministry suggests. Leaving the soup cuts that roughly in half.

foods.source: Ichiran published figure (525 kcal, kaedama 236) via menuramen.com

foods.name: Shoyu Ramen
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of shoyu ramen is about 421 calories. It is the lightest of the classic ramen styles, and this page shows why, topping by topping.
foods.summary: Clear brown chicken or pork broth seasoned with soy sauce, medium curly noodles, one slice of chashu, menma, half an egg and spring onion. The old Tokyo standard, and the lightest bowl on most ramen menus.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of shoyu ramen is about 421 calories, based on Japan's calorie.slism.jp reference for a 726g bowl. Roughly 300 of those calories are the noodles. The clear soy broth is only about 40 calories, which is why shoyu is the lowest calorie ramen style.
realTalk: Shoyu ramen is 421 calories because the broth is nearly empty. A clear chicken and soy stock is around 40 calories for 300ml, compared with about 150 for the same amount of tonkotsu. So the whole bowl is basically 200g of cooked noodles at about 300 calories, plus one slice of chashu at 50, plus the toppings. At a neighbourhood shop this bowl costs 800 to 900 yen and it is the one to pick if you eat ramen more than once a week.

The gap between shops is bigger than the gap between styles. A back-street Tokyo chuka soba with a thin slice of chashu is 421 calories. A modern shop that finishes the bowl with a spoon of chicken oil (chi-yu) and a thick 40g slab of pork belly is closer to 600. The oil floating on top is the tell: a thick golden layer is 50 to 100 calories on its own before you touch the noodles.

The set meal is where shoyu ramen stops being light. Half fried rice on the side is about 300 calories. A plate of 6 gyoza is about 300. The 'ramen set' at a chain like Hidakaya for 900 yen is therefore around 1,000 calories, not 421. If you want a bigger meal, add a second egg (80 calories) instead of the rice.
lighter: Pick shoyu over miso or tonkotsu. Same noodle volume, about 200 fewer calories per bowl.
Skip the ramen set. Ramen plus half chahan is 700 calories; ramen alone is 421.
Ask for no chicken oil, or 'abura nuki'. Some shops add it by default and it is 50 to 100 calories of pure fat.
Extra menma or spring onion is nearly free. Extra chashu is about 50 calories per slice.

components.name: Menma, half egg, naruto, spring onion

variants.name: Plain chuka soba
variants.note: Old style, one thin slice of pork

variants.name: With chicken oil finish
variants.note: Modern shops add chi-yu on top

faq.q: Which ramen has the fewest calories?
faq.a: Shoyu and shio (salt) are the lightest at roughly 400 to 420 calories a bowl. Miso is around 620 and tonkotsu around 525, with the gap coming from broth fat.

faq.q: How many calories are the noodles alone in ramen?
faq.a: About 300 calories for a standard 200g cooked serving. Noodles are 70 percent of a shoyu ramen's calories, which is why kaedama refills add so much.

faq.q: Is shoyu ramen good for a diet?
faq.a: It is one of the better restaurant meals in Japan at 421 calories with 20g of protein. The weak point is salt, around 5g per bowl if you drink the soup.

foods.source: calorie.slism.jp 醤油ラーメン 1杯 726g 421 kcal

foods.name: Miso Ramen
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of miso ramen is about 621 calories, the heaviest of the classic styles. The butter and corn version pushes past 700. Full breakdown inside.
foods.summary: Thick curly noodles in a rich miso broth, usually with stir-fried bean sprouts, cabbage, ground pork and a knob of butter. Sapporo's winter ramen, and the biggest bowl on the menu.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of miso ramen is about 621 calories, based on the calorie.slism.jp reference for an 839g bowl. That is roughly 200 calories more than a shoyu ramen. The miso broth is cooked with lard, the noodles are thicker, and the stir-fried topping adds another 100.
realTalk: Miso ramen is 621 calories because everything in it is bigger. The noodles are thick Sapporo style and the standard serving is about 230g cooked, around 340 calories. The broth is miso paste blended into pork stock and finished with lard, about 130 calories for 350ml. Then the wok topping of bean sprouts, cabbage and ground pork is fried in oil, another 60 to 70. Compare that with a shoyu bowl where the broth is 40 calories and you can see where the extra 200 comes from.

The Sapporo classic adds butter and corn. A 10g pat of butter is 75 calories and a spoon of sweet corn is 40, so the famous 'miso butter corn ramen' is about 735 calories for around 1,100 yen. It is still a normal meal, but it is close to a McDonald's Big Mac set. Order it once in winter, not every Friday.

The bowl is 839g, which is why it fills you up for hours. About 400g of that is broth. If you eat the noodles and toppings and leave the soup, you drop to around 500 calories and cut the salt from roughly 6g to about 3g. The miso broth tastes good enough that people finish it, so decide before you start.
lighter: Skip the butter. That single 10g pat is 75 calories.
Ask for extra bean sprouts (moyashi mashi). Many shops do it free and it adds volume at about 15 calories per 100g.
Leave the broth. Half the bowl's weight is soup and it carries about 130 calories and most of the salt.
Choose the standard noodle portion. Sapporo shops offer 'omori' for 100 yen extra, which is about 170 more calories.
Have miso ramen as the whole meal, not with gyoza and rice. The set version is over 900.

faq.q: Why is miso ramen higher in calories than shoyu?
faq.a: Three reasons: the broth is made with lard (about 130 calories versus 40), the noodles are thicker and the portion larger (340 versus 300), and the topping is wok-fried in oil. Together that is a 200 calorie gap.

faq.q: How many calories are in miso butter corn ramen?
faq.a: About 735 calories. The butter is 75 and the corn about 40 on top of the 621 base bowl.

faq.q: Is miso ramen healthier because of the miso?
faq.a: Miso adds a bit of protein and some fermented soy, but the bowl is still 621 calories with 22g of fat and around 6g of salt. Treat it as a full meal, not a health food.

faq.q: How much protein is in a bowl of miso ramen?
faq.a: About 26g, from the noodles, the ground pork and the chashu. Adding an egg brings it to around 32g.

foods.source: calorie.slism.jp 味噌ラーメン 1杯 838.9g 621 kcal

foods.name: Tempura Udon
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of tempura udon is about 370 calories with one shrimp tempura. Add kakiage and it doubles. Real numbers from Marugame and Japan's calorie tables.
foods.summary: Thick white wheat noodles in a light dashi and soy broth, topped with a shrimp tempura and spring onion. A standing-soba-shop classic and one of the cheapest hot meals in Japan.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of tempura udon with one shrimp tempura is about 370 calories, per the calorie.slism.jp reference for a 596g bowl. Marugame Seimen's kake udon (regular) is 299 calories, and adding one ebi ten at 110 puts you at 409. The noodles are most of it; the broth is under 30.
realTalk: Tempura udon is one of the lighter hot meals in Japan at 370 calories. The udon is 250g cooked, about 240 calories, and the dashi broth is nearly nothing at 25. The one thing with real fat in it is the shrimp tempura, which is about 95 to 110 calories for one piece because the batter soaks up oil. Marugame Seimen publishes 299 for its kake udon regular size and 110 for an ebi ten, and that 409 total is a normal lunch for about 500 yen.

The number climbs fast at a self-serve counter. Marugame's vegetable kakiage is 490 calories on its own, more than the bowl of udon it sits on. A chikuwa ten is about 140, a kashiwa (chicken) ten 143, and a half-boiled egg tempura around 110. Two pieces of tempura on a large udon and you are at 700 calories, which is a katsu curry territory bill for what feels like a light noodle lunch.

Udon is almost all carbohydrate. A 370 calorie bowl has about 62g of carbs and only 14g of protein, so it is fine for calories but it will not keep you full past 2pm on its own. Adding one kashiwa ten or a soft egg gives you 10 more grams of protein for about 100 to 140 calories, which is a better trade than a second shrimp.
lighter: One shrimp tempura, not two. Each is about 110 calories, mostly from the batter.
Never the kakiage. Marugame's is 490 calories, more than the udon itself.
Choose kake or kitsune udon when you want something under 400. Kitsune's fried tofu is about 90 calories.
Regular size (nami). Marugame's large is about 450 calories before toppings.
Add a soft-boiled egg for protein instead of a second piece of tempura.

variants.name: Kitsune udon
variants.note: Sweet fried tofu instead of tempura

faq.q: How many calories is Marugame udon?
faq.a: Kake udon regular is 299 calories, large about 450. Toppings: ebi ten 110, kashiwa ten 143, kakiage 490. All published by Marugame Seimen.

faq.q: Is udon lower in calories than ramen?
faq.a: Yes. Tempura udon is 370 calories against 421 for shoyu ramen and 621 for miso, mainly because the dashi broth has almost no fat.

faq.q: How many calories is one piece of shrimp tempura?
faq.a: About 95 to 110 calories depending on size. The shrimp is around 25 of that; the rest is batter and absorbed oil.

foods.source: calorie.slism.jp 天ぷらうどん 1杯 596.3g 370 kcal; Marugame Seimen published kake udon 299, ebi ten 110

foods.name: Zaru Soba
foods.metaDescription: A plate of zaru soba is about 362 calories with dipping sauce. Only 2g of fat, 16g protein. The lightest noodle meal in Japan, with numbers.
foods.summary: Cold buckwheat noodles on a bamboo tray with a soy and dashi dipping sauce, nori strips, wasabi and spring onion. The summer standard at every soba shop.
foods.answer: A standard plate of zaru soba is about 362 calories, per calorie.slism.jp for a 411g serving including the dipping sauce. It has 16g of protein and only about 2g of fat. Almost the entire count is the noodles themselves, around 240g cooked.
realTalk: Zaru soba is about as light as a full noodle meal gets: 362 calories, 2g of fat, and 16g of protein because buckwheat has more protein than wheat. The dipping sauce (tsuyu) is about 40 calories for the small cup, and the nori and wasabi are nothing. A plate at a standing shop costs around 400 yen, and at a proper soba restaurant 900 to 1,200.

The catch is that it is not very filling for the calories. A 362 calorie plate is 71g of carbohydrate and almost nothing else, so you are hungry again in two hours. That is why soba shops sell the 'ten zaru' set with a plate of tempura, which is 532 calories per calorie.slism.jp, or the 'ni-mai mori' double portion at about 700. Most people do not stop at one plate.

The sobayu at the end is worth knowing about. It is the cloudy water the noodles were boiled in, poured into your leftover tsuyu and drunk like a soup. It is only about 15 to 20 calories and it turns a plate of noodles into something that feels like a finished meal. Drink that instead of ordering a second plate.
lighter: Order zaru or mori, not ten zaru. The tempura plate adds about 170 calories.
One plate, then sobayu. The hot soba water is under 20 calories and closes the meal.
If you need protein, add a cold onsen egg for 80 calories rather than kakiage.
Watch the tsuyu. Dipping only the tip of the noodles is the traditional way, and it saves salt more than calories.

faq.q: Is soba good for weight loss?
faq.a: It is one of the best restaurant noodle choices at 362 calories a plate with 2g of fat. The weakness is low fullness, so pair it with an egg or tofu side rather than a second plate.

faq.q: How many calories are in soba noodles per 100g?
faq.a: Cooked soba is about 130 calories per 100g per the Japanese food composition tables. A standard plate is 240g cooked, so around 312 calories before sauce.

faq.q: Does zaru soba have gluten?
faq.a: Usually yes. Most shop soba is 'ni-hachi', 80 percent buckwheat and 20 percent wheat flour. Only 'juwari' soba is 100 percent buckwheat.

foods.source: calorie.slism.jp ざるそば 1人前 411g 362 kcal

foods.name: Yakisoba
foods.metaDescription: A plate of sauce yakisoba is about 469 calories. Festival packs with mayo run higher. Here is the noodle, pork and sauce breakdown.
foods.summary: Steamed wheat noodles stir-fried with pork belly, cabbage and a thick sweet Worcestershire style sauce, finished with aonori and pickled ginger. The matsuri stall and konbini staple.
foods.answer: A standard plate of sauce yakisoba is about 469 calories, based on a typical single-serve recipe with pork, cabbage and carrot. The steamed noodle pack alone is about 300 calories. The sauce adds 25 and the pork and frying oil make up the rest.
realTalk: Yakisoba is 469 calories for what is really a fairly small plate, about 290g. The steamed noodle pack is 150g and roughly 300 calories on its own, then 30g of pork belly, cabbage, 5g of oil to fry it and 20g of sauce. At a festival stall you pay 500 to 600 yen for that. The sauce is only 25 calories, so it is not the villain here. The noodles are.

The festival version drifts higher. Stall cooks use more oil because the griddle is dry and hot, and they finish with a squeeze of mayonnaise. Mayo is 100 calories per tablespoon, so the 'mayo yakisoba' from a stall is about 570 to 600. Konbini yakisoba is around 500 to 550 for the standard tray and closer to 700 for the 'omori' double packs, with the number printed on the label.

Yakisoba pan is the same thing stuffed into a hot dog bun, and it is the classic 'carbs on carbs' snack. The bun is about 150 calories, so a yakisoba pan is 350 to 400 calories, which is not terrible for a snack but it has almost no protein, about 9g. If you are choosing between that and an onigiri with a boiled egg, take the onigiri and egg.
lighter: Skip the mayo. One squeeze is about 100 calories on a 469 calorie plate.
Double the cabbage. It is 23 calories per 100g and the noodles taste the same with more of it.
Use pork shoulder or chicken thigh instead of pork belly at home. That saves about 60 calories per plate.
At the konbini, pick the standard tray, not omori. The label difference is usually 150 to 200 calories.

variants.name: Omori with mayo and egg
variants.note: Double noodles, fried egg on top

faq.q: Is yakisoba healthy?
faq.a: It is a normal 469 calorie carb-heavy meal with 15g of protein and 18g of fat. Not a health food, not a disaster. The mayo and double noodle versions are where it gets heavy.

faq.q: How many calories are in a konbini yakisoba?
faq.a: Usually 500 to 550 for the standard tray and 650 to 750 for the omori size. The exact number is printed on the label.

faq.q: How many calories is yakisoba pan?
faq.a: About 350 to 400 calories. A hot dog bun is around 150 calories and it holds roughly half a plate of noodles.

foods.source: health2sync.com sauce yakisoba 1 serving 469 kcal; calorie.slism.jp 焼きそば 157 kcal/100g

foods.name: Gyudon
foods.metaDescription: A regular Yoshinoya gyudon is 633 calories, published by Yoshinoya. Sukiya's is higher. Sizes, toppings and the cheese version, all with numbers.
foods.summary: Thin sliced beef and onion simmered in a sweet soy and dashi sauce, ladled over a bowl of rice. Japan's fast food, served in under a minute at Yoshinoya, Sukiya and Matsuya.
foods.answer: A regular (namimori) gyudon at Yoshinoya is 633 calories, according to Yoshinoya's own nutrition data, with 19.6g of protein, 23.6g of fat and 88.2g of carbs in a 342g bowl. About 390 of those calories are the rice. The beef and sauce are the other 240.
realTalk: A regular gyudon is 633 calories at Yoshinoya and about 730 at Sukiya, because Sukiya serves a bit more rice. For around 500 yen that is one of the cheapest full meals in Japan, and the numbers are all published, which makes it easy to plan around. The rice is 250g and about 390 calories. The beef is fatty short plate cooked in sugar and soy, roughly 200 calories for the meat and 45 for the onion and sauce.

The size ladder is steep. Yoshinoya's small (komori) is about 490 calories, regular 633, atamono-omori (extra beef, same rice) about 740, omori about 850, and tokumori around 1,000. The 'mega' bowl at Sukiya is over 1,200. The chains price these only 100 to 200 yen apart, so people go up a size without thinking, and each step is roughly a bowl of miso soup's worth of rice or a burger's worth of beef.

Toppings change the picture. A raw egg is about 80 calories and 6g of protein, which is a reasonable add. Cheese is about 120. Kimchi is 20. The 'tsuyudaku' extra sauce order is mostly free in calories but adds salt. If you want the bowl to do more for you, the egg or the extra beef head is the better spend than the bigger rice.
lighter: Order 'atama no omori' (extra beef, normal rice) instead of omori. More protein, about 100 fewer calories than the big rice version.
Add the miso soup and salad set for about 60 calories total. It slows you down and fills the bowl-sized gap.
Skip the cheese. That is 120 calories on top of 633.
Ask for 'gohan sukuname' (less rice). Yoshinoya does it free and it drops about 80 calories.
Yoshinoya's 'gyudon on yasai' swaps some rice for vegetables and lands around 480.

variants.name: Yoshinoya gyudon on yasai
variants.note: Vegetables replace part of the rice

faq.q: How many calories in a Yoshinoya gyudon?
faq.a: Regular is 633 calories per Yoshinoya's own data. Small is about 490, large about 850 and tokumori around 1,000.

faq.q: Is Sukiya or Yoshinoya gyudon lower in calories?
faq.a: Yoshinoya at 633 versus Sukiya at about 733 for regular. Sukiya's bowl carries more rice.

faq.q: Is gyudon good for building muscle?
faq.a: It has about 20g of protein per regular bowl, which is average. Adding an egg brings it to 26g. The 'atama no omori' extra beef version reaches about 30g.

faq.q: How much rice is in a gyudon?
faq.a: About 250g cooked rice in a regular bowl, which is roughly 390 calories on its own. Large bowls hold 350g or more.

foods.source: Yoshinoya published nutrition: 牛丼並盛 633 kcal, P19.6 F23.6 C88.2, 342g

foods.name: Katsudon
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of katsudon is about 866 calories, the heaviest of the common donburi. Here is what the cutlet, egg and rice each add up to.
foods.summary: A breaded fried pork cutlet simmered with onion and beaten egg in sweet dashi soy, then slid over a bowl of rice. The soba shop and teishoku-ya heavyweight.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of katsudon is about 866 calories, per calorie.slism.jp for a 504g bowl. The fried pork cutlet is roughly 390 of that, the rice about 360, and the egg, onion and sweet sauce make up the last 130. It is the highest calorie of the classic donburi.
realTalk: Katsudon is 866 calories, which puts it above gyudon (633) and oyakodon (631) by a wide margin, and the reason is simple: you are eating a whole tonkatsu, breading and oil included, and then it gets simmered in a sauce with sugar. A 120g cutlet is about 390 calories, the 230g of rice under it is 360, and the egg and sweet dashi bring it home. A bowl at a soba shop or Katsuya is 900 to 1,000 yen.

The egg is the part people underestimate. One beaten egg is 80 calories, and shops often use one and a half. The sauce it cooks in has sugar and mirin, so the onion and sauce together are 50 to 60 calories rather than the near zero you get with a clear dashi. That is why katsudon runs 130 calories above a plain tonkatsu plus rice even though it looks like the same ingredients.

The size problem is that katsudon is often the 'treat' order after a hard day, and it usually comes with a small bowl of soba or udon on the side at a soba shop. That set is around 1,100 calories. If you want the cutlet, katsudon at 866 is still a better deal than the katsu curry at CoCo Ichibanya, which is 1,116 for a regular rice serving.
lighter: Order hire (fillet) katsudon when it exists. The lean cutlet saves 80 to 100 calories against rosu (loin).
Ask for less rice. Dropping from 230g to 150g saves about 125 calories and the cutlet is still the same size.
Skip the side noodle set. The mini soba or udon adds 200 to 250 calories.
Eat it as the only heavy meal of the day. At 866 calories it is half of an 1,800 calorie budget.

components.name: Onion and sweet dashi soy sauce

variants.name: Sauce katsudon (Fukui style)
variants.note: No egg, cutlet dipped in sauce

faq.q: Which donburi has the most calories?
faq.a: Katsudon at 866 calories tops the common ones. Unaju is about 879 but it is usually a special occasion. Gyudon is 633 and oyakodon 631.

faq.q: How many calories are in the tonkatsu inside a katsudon?
faq.a: About 390 for a 120g loin cutlet. The breading and absorbed oil are roughly 40 percent of that.

faq.q: Is katsudon high in protein?
faq.a: Fairly high at about 33g per bowl from the pork and egg. The issue is the 36g of fat and 100g of carbs that come with it.

foods.source: calorie.slism.jp カツ丼 1人前 503.6g 866 kcal

foods.name: Oyakodon
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of oyakodon is about 631 calories with 30g of protein. It is the leanest of the big donburi. Breakdown and lighter orders inside.
foods.summary: Chicken thigh and onion simmered in sweet dashi soy, bound with soft egg and poured over rice. The 'parent and child' bowl, cheap at every soba shop and family restaurant.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of oyakodon is about 631 calories, per calorie.slism.jp for a 460g bowl. It carries about 30g of protein from the chicken and egg, with only 16g of fat because nothing is fried. The rice is about 390 of the calories.
realTalk: Oyakodon is the donburi to pick when you want to stay on plan. It is 631 calories, nearly the same as a gyudon, but with 30g of protein instead of 20 and 16g of fat instead of 24. Nothing in it is fried. The chicken thigh is about 70g, the eggs are one and a half, and the rest is rice and a sweet dashi sauce. At Nakau or a soba shop it costs 500 to 700 yen.

The rice is still 60 percent of the bowl. At 250g and 390 calories, the rice outweighs the chicken and egg combined. Ordering 'gohan sukuname' or eating half the rice takes the bowl down to 430 to 500 calories with the same protein, which is a very good lunch. The egg and chicken on top are only about 230 calories together.

Home versions and restaurant versions differ mostly in sugar. A restaurant warishita has sugar and mirin, about 30 calories per serving. Some shops also finish with a third egg yolk on top for richness, another 55 calories. Neither is a big deal. The bigger jump is the 'omori' rice, which adds about 150 calories, and the pickles and miso soup set, which adds about 50.
lighter: Ask for less rice or leave a third of it. The chicken and egg are only 230 of the 631 calories.
Order oyakodon over katsudon every time. Same shop, about 235 fewer calories, similar protein.
Skip the extra yolk topping some shops offer. It is 55 calories of pure fat.
Add the miso soup. It is 40 calories and it stretches the meal without adding rice.

variants.name: With extra yolk
variants.note: Some shops add a raw yolk on top

faq.q: Is oyakodon healthy?
faq.a: It is one of the better donburi at 631 calories, 30g protein and 16g fat, because the chicken is simmered rather than fried. The main weakness is 88g of carbs from the rice.

faq.q: Oyakodon or gyudon, which has fewer calories?
faq.a: They are close: oyakodon 631, Yoshinoya gyudon 633. Oyakodon has 10g more protein and 8g less fat, so it is the better pick.

faq.q: How much protein is in oyakodon?
faq.a: About 30g per bowl, from roughly 70g of chicken thigh and one and a half eggs.

foods.source: calorie.slism.jp 親子丼 1杯 460.5g 631 kcal

foods.name: Unagi Don
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of unagi don is about 671 calories at Sukiya. A full unaju at a specialist runs 879. Eel, rice and tare, broken down with real numbers.
foods.summary: Grilled eel glazed with a sweet soy tare and laid over rice, dusted with sansho pepper. Unadon comes in a bowl, unaju in a lacquer box with more eel. The midsummer 'Doyo no Ushi' tradition.
foods.answer: A regular unagi don at Sukiya is 671 calories, per Sukiya's published data, with about 80g of kabayaki eel on 260g of rice. A full unaju at an eel specialist is about 879 calories per calorie.slism.jp, because the box holds nearly double the eel.
realTalk: Unagi don is 671 calories at Sukiya for around 1,000 yen, which is the cheap end. The eel itself is fatty, about 293 calories per 100g as kabayaki, so an 80g piece is 234. The rice is 260g and about 405. The tare is sugar and soy, around 30 calories for the drizzle. Compared with a gyudon, you pay double and get about 40 more calories and 10g more protein, but the eel has omega-3 fat rather than beef tallow.

The specialist unaju is a different portion. A proper eel shop lays a whole 150g fillet across the box, and calorie.slism.jp puts that at 879 calories with 42g of protein. Those meals cost 3,500 to 5,000 yen, so people eat them once a year in July. The calories are high but the protein is real, and the fat in eel is largely unsaturated. As a once-a-year meal it is one of the more honest 900 calories in Japanese food.

The extras are small here. Kimosui, the clear soup with eel liver, is about 20 calories. Pickles are 5. Sansho pepper is nothing. So the number you order is the number you eat, unless you go 'omori' rice at Sukiya, which takes the bowl to 817 published. The eel does not change; only the rice does.
lighter: Order regular rice, not omori. At Sukiya the difference is 671 versus 817.
Pick unadon over unaju if you are watching calories. The box holds about 70g more eel, roughly 200 calories.
Eat the kimosui. It is 20 calories and it makes the meal feel complete.
Share a specialist unaju and add a second bowl of plain rice between two people rather than ordering two boxes.

variants.name: Hitsumabushi
variants.note: Nagoya style, chopped eel with extra rice and broth

faq.q: How many calories is unaju?
faq.a: About 879 calories for a standard box per calorie.slism.jp, with 42g of protein and 32g of fat. The cheaper unadon at chains is about 671.

faq.q: Is eel high in fat?
faq.a: Yes, kabayaki eel is about 293 calories per 100g with around 21g of fat, but much of that is unsaturated and includes omega-3. It also has 23g of protein per 100g.

faq.q: How many calories in Sukiya unagi don?
faq.a: Regular is 671 calories and the large rice version is 817, both published by Sukiya.

foods.source: Sukiya published unadon 並盛 671 kcal; calorie.slism.jp うな重 879 kcal for unaju variant

foods.name: Katsu Curry
foods.metaDescription: A CoCo Ichibanya rosu katsu curry is 1,116 calories with regular rice. That is the published figure. See how the rice, cutlet and sauce split it.
foods.summary: Japanese curry sauce over a plate of rice with a breaded fried pork cutlet on top. The CoCo Ichibanya bestseller and one of the highest calorie standard orders in Japanese chain food.
foods.answer: A rosu (pork loin) katsu curry at CoCo Ichibanya is 1,116 calories with the regular 300g rice, per CoCo Ichibanya's published nutrition sheet. The rice is about 470 of that, the cutlet about 400, and the curry sauce roughly 230. Chicken katsu curry is 1,115, nearly identical.
realTalk: Katsu curry is the plate people search after they have eaten it, because 1,116 calories is more than a Big Mac set and it does not feel like it at the time. CoCo Ichibanya publishes everything: the plain pork curry with 300g rice is 701 calories, and the rosu katsu adds about 415. The plate costs around 1,000 yen. For the same money you could have a tonkatsu teishoku at 873 and get a salad and miso soup with it.

Rice is the lever. CoCo Ichi lets you pick rice by 100g steps. Dropping from 300g to 200g takes the plate to about 960 calories. Going up to 400g is 1,272, and the 'mega' 600g plate with katsu passes 1,500. The cutlet is the same size at every rice level, so the small rice order is the same amount of meat for 156 fewer calories.

The sauce level and toppings are where it gets silly. Cheese is about 120 calories, cream croquette 200, and a half boiled egg 80. Spice level costs nothing. The 'katsu curry with cheese and egg' that a lot of people order after the gym is about 1,320 calories, which is a full day of food for a small woman. If you need it, order it as your one meal and make the rest of the day protein and vegetables.
lighter: Rice at 200g. That alone saves 156 calories and the cutlet is untouched.
Order the plain pork or chicken curry (701 or so) and add a boiled egg for protein. That is half the calories of the katsu version.
Hire (fillet) katsu instead of rosu when the shop has it. Leaner cut, roughly 80 to 100 fewer calories.
No cheese, no croquette. Those two toppings are 320 calories together.
Eat the pickles and salad first. It slows the plate down and you may not finish the rice.

variants.name: Katsu curry with cheese and egg

faq.q: How many calories in CoCo Ichibanya katsu curry?
faq.a: Rosu katsu curry with 300g rice is 1,116 calories per CoCo Ichibanya's nutrition sheet. Chicken katsu is 1,115. Each 100g of rice up or down is about 156 calories.

faq.q: Is Japanese curry high in calories without the katsu?
faq.a: A plain pork curry with 300g rice is 701 calories at CoCo Ichibanya. The sauce is about 230 of that because it is a roux made with flour and fat.

faq.q: Can I eat katsu curry on a diet?
faq.a: Once in a while, as the only big meal of the day. At 1,116 calories it is 60 percent of an 1,800 calorie budget. The 200g rice version at 960 is a bit easier to fit.

faq.q: What is the lowest calorie curry at CoCo Ichibanya?
faq.a: Plain curries with 200g rice come in around 550 calories. Vegetable curry is close to that. Anything with a fried topping jumps past 900.

foods.source: CoCo Ichibanya published nutrition PDF (ichibanya.co.jp): ロースカツカレー ライス300g 1116 kcal

foods.name: Kimchi Jjigae
foods.metaDescription: Kimchi jjigae with a bowl of rice is about 555 calories. The stew itself is only 244. Here is where the rest comes from and how to trim it.
foods.summary: Kimchi jjigae is the sour, spicy pork and kimchi stew that every Korean lunch spot serves in a black stone pot with a bowl of rice and a few banchan.
foods.answer: A standard kimchi jjigae set is about 555 calories: 244 for a 400g pot of stew (MFDS restaurant nutrition data) plus around 310 for a 210g bowl of white rice. The stew on its own is light. The rice and the pork belly are what add up.
realTalk: The stew itself is 244 calories for a full 400g pot. That is less than a bowl of rice. Old kimchi has almost nothing in it, the tofu is 60 to 70 calories, and the broth is mostly water and gochugaru. The pork belly is the only heavy thing in the pot, around 165 calories for the 50g most lunch places put in. If the cook is generous with belly, you can add another 100.

The 555 figure assumes one bowl of rice, about 210g. Most 8,000 to 9,000 won lunch sets give you free rice refills, and a second bowl takes you to 865 before you touch the banchan. The gyeran-mari or fish cake on the side is another 80 to 150. It is easy to walk out of a kimchi jjigae lunch at 900 calories while thinking you ate soup.

Tuna kimchi jjigae runs lower, around 104 calories per 200g portion according to FatSecret Korea, because canned tuna in water has a fraction of the fat of belly. Budae-style versions with spam and ramyeon added are a different dish entirely and can double the number. Ask what is in the pot before you assume it is the light option.
lighter: Ask for tuna (참치) instead of pork belly. The stew drops from around 244 to about 200 for the same pot.
Stop at one bowl of rice, or ask for half. That single decision is worth 150 to 300 calories.
Eat the kimchi, tofu and pork, and leave a third of the broth. The broth carries most of the sodium (around 1,960mg per pot) and some of the fat that renders off the pork.
Skip the fried banchan. A single slice of gyeran-mari is fine, the fried fish cake and japchae are where the extra 150 hides.

portions.label: Stew with 2 bowls rice and banchan

variants.name: Pork belly kimchi jjigae, no rice

faq.q: Is kimchi jjigae good for weight loss?
faq.a: The stew is, at 244 calories for a full pot with 15g protein. The rice is what decides the total. One bowl and it is a 555 calorie meal, which fits most deficits.

faq.q: How many calories in kimchi jjigae without rice?
faq.a: About 244 calories for a 400g restaurant pot with pork belly, based on Korean MFDS restaurant data. Tuna versions are closer to 200.

faq.q: Why is kimchi jjigae so salty?
faq.a: One pot has about 1,960mg of sodium, close to the full daily limit, because both the kimchi and the broth are salted. Leaving some broth helps.

faq.q: Kimchi jjigae vs doenjang jjigae, which is lower?
faq.a: Doenjang jjigae is lower at about 145 calories per pot because it uses less meat and no chili oil. Kimchi jjigae is 244.

foods.source: MFDS restaurant nutrition data (김치찌개 400g 244 kcal) via pillyze.com and geniet.co.kr, plus 210g rice

foods.name: Sundubu Jjigae
foods.metaDescription: A pot of sundubu jjigae is about 260 calories before rice. Soft tofu, one egg, a little chili oil. Here is the full breakdown.
foods.summary: Sundubu jjigae is a bubbling pot of silken tofu in a red chili broth, cracked with a raw egg at the table and served with rice and banchan.
foods.answer: One restaurant pot of sundubu jjigae is about 260 calories (FatSecret Korea lists the generic serving at 259). Add the bowl of rice that always comes with it and the meal is around 570. The tofu and egg supply 16g of protein, so it is one of the more filling stews for the calories.
realTalk: The pot is mostly water and silken tofu. A 200g block of soft tofu is about 110 calories, the egg cracked in is 70, and whatever seafood or minced pork the kitchen adds is 40 to 60. The rest of the 260 is the chili oil the broth is built on, which is the one ingredient that varies wildly between shops.

That chili oil matters more than people think. A kitchen that starts the pot with 2 tablespoons of gochu-gireum is adding about 240 calories before anything else goes in. Most lunch places use a lot less, which is why the average lands around 260, but a very red, glossy surface on the broth is a sign you are at the higher end.

The rice is the bigger lever. A 210g bowl is around 310 calories, more than the stew. Order the stew with half rice and you are at roughly 415 for a complete lunch with 20g of protein. The Gangneung-style versions with beef and extra fat listed by packaged brands run 450 to 475 per serving, closer to a full meal on their own.
lighter: Order the seafood (해물) version rather than beef or pork. It typically lands 40 to 60 calories lower.
Ask for less chili oil (기름 적게). It is a normal request and can save 100 calories.
Half rice instead of full. The stew is filling enough that most people do not miss it.
Do not drink all the broth. The flavour is in the top half, the oil settles there too.

variants.name: Kimchi sundubu
variants.note: Extra fat from pork and kimchi

faq.q: Is sundubu jjigae healthy?
faq.a: It is one of the better stews: about 260 calories, 16g protein, and most of the volume is tofu and water. The only thing to watch is the chili oil and the sodium.

faq.q: How many calories in sundubu jjigae with rice?
faq.a: About 570 calories with a standard 210g bowl of rice. The rice is more than half the total.

faq.q: Is sundubu jjigae high in protein?
faq.a: Decent, not high. The tofu and egg give around 16g. Add a side of gyeran-mari or order the beef version to push it past 25g.

faq.q: Does the egg add a lot of calories?
faq.a: About 70. It also adds 6g of protein, so it is worth keeping.

foods.source: fatsecret.kr generic 순두부찌개 259 kcal per serving

foods.name: Doenjang Jjigae
foods.metaDescription: Doenjang jjigae is about 145 calories for a full 400g pot. It is the lightest stew on the Korean menu, and here is why.
foods.summary: Doenjang jjigae is the fermented soybean paste stew with tofu, zucchini, potato and onion that turns up next to almost every Korean rice meal.
foods.answer: A 400g pot of doenjang jjigae is about 145 calories, according to Korean MFDS restaurant nutrition data. That is the lowest number of any common jjigae. With a bowl of rice the meal comes to around 455, and with a grilled fish on the side you are still under 700.
realTalk: There is barely anything in it. The doenjang paste is about 40 calories for the 30g a pot uses, tofu is 60, and the vegetables (zucchini, potato, onion, chili) come to 35. The anchovy stock is close to zero. That is how a full pot that fills you up lands at 145, about the same as one slice of bread.

Because the stew is so light, it is the rice and the sides that decide your lunch. A 210g bowl of rice is 310, more than double the stew. The typical 8,000 won doenjang jjigae set comes with rice, a fried egg or gyeran-mari, and 3 to 4 banchan, so a realistic total is 500 to 600. Still one of the cheapest, lowest-calorie set meals you can order.

The versions that go higher are the ones with meat. Chadol doenjang jjigae with beef brisket adds 80 to 120 calories, and some gogi-jip serve it as a rich, oily finisher after samgyeopsal where the pork fat from the grill ends up in the pot. That version is closer to 250. On its own, at a lunch place, it is 145.
lighter: It is already light. The single biggest saving is stopping at one bowl of rice instead of taking the refill.
Ask for extra tofu (두부 추가). Most places do it free and it adds protein for about 60 calories.
Pair it with grilled mackerel (고등어구이) rather than fried pork cutlet. The fish set lands near 650, the cutlet set near 1,000.
The chadol (brisket) version is nice but adds about 100. Order it when you want the meat, not by default.

faq.q: Is doenjang jjigae good for dieting?
faq.a: Yes. At about 145 calories per pot with 10g protein and a lot of volume, it is the best stew on the menu for a calorie deficit. Just watch the rice.

faq.q: How many calories in doenjang jjigae with rice?
faq.a: About 455 with a standard 210g bowl of rice. With the usual banchan and an egg, plan on 550 to 600.

faq.q: Is doenjang jjigae high in sodium?
faq.a: Yes, roughly 1,500 to 2,000mg per pot from the fermented paste. Drinking less of the broth is the easy fix.

faq.q: Doenjang jjigae or kimchi jjigae for fewer calories?
faq.a: Doenjang, at 145 versus 244 for kimchi jjigae. Both are low; the difference is the pork belly in kimchi jjigae.

foods.source: MFDS restaurant nutrition data (된장찌개 400g 145 kcal) via gazilab.co and pillyze.com

foods.name: Samgyetang
foods.metaDescription: Samgyetang is about 918 calories for the full pot. A whole young chicken, rice stuffing and broth. Here is where every calorie sits.
foods.summary: Samgyetang is a whole young chicken stuffed with glutinous rice, ginseng, jujube and garlic, simmered in a stone pot and eaten on the hottest days of summer.
foods.answer: A full pot of samgyetang is about 918 calories for a 1,000g serving, the highest single-serving figure in the Korean MFDS restaurant survey of 130 dishes. Most of that is the whole chicken (around 600 calories with the skin) and the glutinous rice stuffing (around 210). The broth itself is only about 70.
realTalk: This is a whole bird. A young chicken of about 500g, skin on, bones in, gives you roughly 300g of edible meat and skin and comes to 600 calories. The skin is the swing factor: eat it and you get the fat, peel it and you drop about 150 calories while keeping nearly all of the 70g of protein. Nobody at a samgyetang restaurant will judge you for peeling.

The stuffing is the surprise. The 60g of raw glutinous rice packed into the cavity swells into a thick porridge inside the bird and is about 210 calories on its own. Then the restaurant usually brings a side bowl of rice too, which most people do not need. Skip the extra rice and you are already saving 300.

At 15,000 to 20,000 won a pot, samgyetang is a meal, not a soup course. 918 calories with 70g of protein is honestly a fine lunch if it is your main meal of the day. The problem is treating it as a soup and adding rice, a plate of kkakdugi, and a shot of insamju on the side, which pushes a hot summer lunch to 1,200.
lighter: Peel the skin off the chicken. That is about 150 calories gone, and you keep nearly all the protein.
Do not order or eat the extra bowl of rice. The stuffing is already 210 calories of rice.
Eat the meat and half the broth. The broth has chicken fat floating on top, and half a bowl less saves 30 to 40.
Skip the insamju shot. It is only 50 to 60 calories but it is easy to make it two.

components.name: Whole young chicken, skin on, bone in

portions.label: Whole pot plus side bowl of rice

faq.q: Is samgyetang healthy?
faq.a: It is a whole meal with about 70g of protein. The 918 calorie total is a lot for a soup but fine for a main meal. The real question is whether you also eat the extra rice.

faq.q: How many calories in samgyetang without the skin?
faq.a: Roughly 770. The skin on a 500g young chicken is about 150 calories of mostly fat.

faq.q: Why is samgyetang so high in calories?
faq.a: Because it is an entire chicken plus 60g of glutinous rice in one pot. The broth is only about 70 calories; the bird and stuffing are the rest.

faq.q: Is samgyetang good for building muscle?
faq.a: Yes, 70g protein in one sitting is hard to beat. Eat the meat, go easy on the rice, and it is a solid post-gym meal.

foods.source: MFDS restaurant nutrition survey (삼계탕 1,000g 918 kcal) via hidoc.co.kr

foods.name: Seolleongtang
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of seolleongtang is about 425 calories with the meat and noodles, or around 735 once you add the rice. Milky broth, real numbers.
foods.summary: Seolleongtang is a milky white ox bone broth simmered for hours, served with sliced brisket, thin somyeon noodles, spring onion, and salt on the table so you season it yourself.
foods.answer: A bowl of seolleongtang with brisket slices and noodles is about 425 calories, with 33g of protein. Most people tip the bowl of rice into the soup, which takes it to around 735. The broth looks rich but is only about 170 calories for 500ml; the meat and the rice are the rest.
realTalk: The milky colour fools people. That white comes from bone collagen and emulsified marrow fat, and a 500ml bowl of broth is about 170 calories. Not nothing, but not cream either. The 70g of sliced brisket is 150 and the small tangle of somyeon noodles at the bottom is about 80. That is your 425.

Then the rice arrives. Almost everyone in a seolleongtang house tips the whole 210g bowl into the soup, and that is the moment it goes from 425 to 735. If you are trying to keep the number down, tip half in and leave the rest. The soup is 650g on its own and nobody leaves hungry.

Watch the salt. The broth is unseasoned when it lands, and the standard move is a heaped teaspoon of salt plus a big scoop of kkakdugi juice. That is where the 1,500mg of sodium comes from, not the kitchen. Season lightly, eat the kkakdugi rather than pouring its brine in, and you fix most of the problem for free.
lighter: Tip in half the rice, not the whole bowl. Saves about 155 calories.
Order the 특 (special) only if you want more meat. It adds 60 to 80g of brisket for about 130 calories and 25g protein, a fair trade.
Skim the fat that pools on top once the soup sits a minute. It is 40 to 60 calories of pure beef fat.
Go easy on the salt spoon. It changes nothing about calories but a lot about how you feel after.

portions.label: Bowl with full rice tipped in

faq.q: Is seolleongtang healthy?
faq.a: It is a decent meal: 425 calories, 33g protein, plenty of volume. The two things to manage are the rice you tip in and the salt you add yourself.

faq.q: How many calories in seolleongtang with rice?
faq.a: About 735 with a full 210g bowl of rice stirred in. Half rice brings it to around 580.

faq.q: Is the white broth high in fat?
faq.a: Moderately. About 500ml of broth carries 12 to 15g of fat, roughly 130 calories, from the emulsified marrow. Skimming the top layer removes a good chunk of it.

faq.q: Seolleongtang or samgyetang for fewer calories?
faq.a: Seolleongtang by a wide margin: 425 versus 918. Samgyetang is a whole chicken plus rice stuffing.

foods.source: geniet.co.kr 설렁탕 424 kcal per serving; weight set to a typical 650g restaurant bowl, macros from components

foods.name: Budae Jjigae
foods.serving: 1 serving (share of the pan, no rice)
foods.metaDescription: Budae jjigae is about 630 calories per person before rice. Spam, sausage, ramyeon and cheese in one pan. The full breakdown here.
foods.summary: Budae jjigae is the army base stew: spam, hot dogs, baked beans, kimchi, tofu and a brick of ramyeon boiled in a shallow pan of red broth at the table, usually shared between two or more.
foods.answer: One person's share of budae jjigae is about 630 calories before rice, based on the FatSecret Korea generic serving of 626. The spam and sausage are about 300 of that, the ramyeon brick another 240. Add the bowl of rice most people order and you are at roughly 940.
realTalk: This is the one Korean stew where the meat is processed and the noodles are instant. A 50g slab of spam is 155 calories, two slices of sausage around 150, and the half brick of ramyeon that goes in per person is 240. That is 545 from three ingredients before the kimchi, tofu, beans and broth even register. Nothing in this pan is a vegetable in disguise.

The 2-person pan at a Uijeongbu-style restaurant is around 18,000 to 22,000 won and comes with rice. The trick most people miss is that the ramyeon is often free to add, so tables order a second brick. Each extra brick is about 480 calories split between whoever eats it. A slice of American cheese melted on top is another 60 to 70.

Packaged versions from Bibigo and Pulmuone run 295 to 405 per 460g serving, which sounds better until you notice they contain about half the spam and no added ramyeon. The restaurant pan with everything in it is the 630 figure, and 630 with a bowl of rice and a can of cider is a 1,100 calorie dinner.
lighter: Skip the second ramyeon brick. Each one is about 480 calories shared across the table.
Ask for extra tofu and kimchi instead of extra spam. Same volume, a fraction of the fat.
No cheese slice on top. It is 65 calories that melts into the broth and disappears.
Go without rice. With ramyeon in the pan you already have your carbs, and it saves 310.

portions.label: Share with ramyeon, cheese and rice

faq.q: Is budae jjigae unhealthy?
faq.a: It is the heaviest common jjigae: about 630 calories per person, 36g fat, and around 2,500mg sodium from spam and sausage. Fine occasionally, not a weekday lunch habit.

faq.q: How many calories in budae jjigae with rice?
faq.a: About 940 for one share with a 210g bowl of rice. With ramyeon in the pan the rice is genuinely optional.

faq.q: How much of budae jjigae is the ramyeon?
faq.a: About 240 calories per half brick. Tables that add two full bricks are adding close to 1,000 calories to the pan.

faq.q: Is there protein in budae jjigae?
faq.a: About 28g per share, mostly from spam and sausage. It is protein with a lot of fat and salt attached.

foods.source: fatsecret.kr generic 부대찌개 626 kcal per serving; packaged range 295 to 455 cross-checked

foods.name: Gamjatang
foods.metaDescription: A single bowl of gamjatang is about 600 calories with the pork bones, potato and greens. Add rice and it is 900. Numbers and tips here.
foods.summary: Gamjatang is the pork spine bone stew with potato, ugeoji greens and perilla seed powder, sold as a big shared pot or as a single ppyeo-haejangguk bowl at 24-hour joints.
foods.answer: A single-serve bowl of gamjatang (ppyeo-haejangguk) is about 600 calories: two or three pork neck bones with around 150g of meat, a potato, ugeoji greens and a thick perilla broth. Packaged versions from Korean brands run 535 to 810 per 600 to 900g serving, which brackets the restaurant bowl. With rice it is about 910.
realTalk: The meat on the bones is the whole story. Pork neck and spine meat is fatty, around 220 calories per 100g once it has simmered in its own fat, and a single bowl carries about 150g of it if you pick the bones clean. That is 330 calories. The potato is 80, the greens with perilla powder about 60, the broth 80. Nothing exotic, just a lot of fatty pork.

The 2-person pot at a proper gamjatang place is a different animal. It comes with 6 to 8 bones, more potato, and the table almost always finishes with bokkeumbap fried in the leftover broth. That fried rice at the end is about 450 calories per person on top of the stew, and it is the reason a gamjatang dinner can quietly hit 1,300.

It is also a 3am food. Ppyeo-haejangguk at a 24-hour place after drinking, with rice tipped in and a soju finish, is closer to 1,000 than 600. The protein is real (about 40g) and the bowl is filling, but hangover eating is not where anyone is counting.
lighter: Order the single bowl, not the 2-person pot, and skip the fried rice finish. That alone is 450 calories.
Eat the meat and the greens, leave the fattiest bits on the bone. The fat that clings to spine bones is a lot of the 33g.
Half rice. The bowl already has a potato in it.
Skim the perilla broth once. A visible oil layer forms in about a minute, and it is 50 to 80 calories.

components.name: Pork neck bone meat, edible portion
Ugeoji greens with perilla seed powder

faq.q: Is gamjatang healthy?
faq.a: It is a high-protein, high-fat bowl: about 600 calories, 40g protein, 33g fat. Good as a main meal, heavy as a side to drinking.

faq.q: How many calories in gamjatang with rice?
faq.a: About 910 for a single bowl with a 210g bowl of rice tipped in.

faq.q: Does gamjatang have a lot of potato?
faq.a: Usually one medium potato per bowl, about 90 calories. The name refers to the pork bone cut as much as the potato.

faq.q: What about the fried rice at the end?
faq.a: Bokkeumbap made in the leftover pot is roughly 450 calories per person because it soaks up the fatty broth. It is the most expensive part of the meal calorie-wise.

foods.source: estimate from components; fatsecret.kr packaged gamjatang range 535 to 810 kcal per 600 to 900g used as a bracket

foods.name: Bibimbap
foods.metaDescription: Bibimbap is about 610 calories a bowl. The vegetables are almost free; the rice, sesame oil and gochujang are not. Full breakdown.
foods.summary: Bibimbap is a bowl of rice topped with seasoned vegetables, a little beef, a fried egg and a spoon of gochujang, mixed at the table with sesame oil.
foods.answer: A restaurant bowl of bibimbap is about 610 calories. Korean MFDS data via Pillyze lists a 450g bowl at 638, while Geniet has 553 to 586, so 610 is a fair middle. Half of it is the 210g of rice (about 310); the vegetables are only 60. The sesame oil and gochujang add about 90 together.
realTalk: Everyone assumes the vegetables make it light. They do, but the vegetables were never the problem. Spinach, bean sprouts, carrot, zucchini and mushroom come to about 60 calories for 150g. The rice underneath is 310. So a bowl with the same toppings on 140g of rice instead of 210g drops to about 510 without you noticing much.

The sesame oil is the sneaky one. The kitchen drizzles about 5g on top and you probably add another 5g from the bottle on the table. Each teaspoon is 45 calories. The gochujang is another 45 for a full tablespoon, most of it sugar. Together the oil and the sauce can be 130 calories for something that takes up no space in the bowl.

Dolsot bibimbap is the higher version. The stone bowl is brushed with oil so the rice crisps, which adds 50 to 80 calories, and it usually comes with a raw egg yolk rather than a fried egg (about the same, 70). Yukhoe bibimbap with raw beef is similar in calories to the standard, since the beef replaces the fried egg rather than adding to it.
lighter: Ask for less rice (밥 적게) and more namul. Most places will do it and it saves 100 to 150.
Use the gochujang that comes on the bowl and do not add more from the tub. A second tablespoon is 45 calories of mostly sugar.
Do not add extra sesame oil from the table bottle. The kitchen already put some on.
Skip dolsot unless you really want the crispy rice. The oiled stone bowl adds 50 to 80.

variants.name: Vegetable bibimbap, no meat or egg

faq.q: Is bibimbap healthy?
faq.a: It is a balanced plate: 610 calories, 24g protein, and 150g of vegetables. The calories come from rice and oil, not the toppings. Cutting the rice makes it a strong diet meal.

faq.q: How many calories in dolsot bibimbap?
faq.a: About 690. The stone bowl is oiled before the rice goes in, which adds 50 to 80 calories over a regular bowl.

faq.q: Is bibimbap high in carbs?
faq.a: Yes, about 88g, almost all from the 210g of rice. Asking for less rice brings it under 60g.

faq.q: How many calories in the gochujang?
faq.a: About 45 per tablespoon (25g), roughly half of it sugar. Most bowls come with 1 to 2 tablespoons.

foods.source: MFDS 2020 food composition data via pillyze.com (450g bowl 638 kcal) and geniet.co.kr (553 to 586 kcal); 610 used as a restaurant middle

foods.name: Kimbap
foods.metaDescription: One roll of basic kimbap is about 400 calories. Tuna kimbap is closer to 520. Here is what is in the roll and which fillings add the most.
foods.summary: Kimbap is the seaweed and rice roll filled with egg, ham, pickled radish, carrot and spinach, sold sliced into 8 to 10 pieces at every bunsik shop and convenience store.
foods.answer: A standard roll of kimbap is about 400 calories. FatSecret Korea lists Barunkim Seonsaeng at 393 for a 230g roll and CU vegetable kimbap at 356 for 272g, while a Kimbap Cheonguk roll is 485 for 300g. Each slice is 40 to 50 calories. Tuna kimbap with mayo runs about 520, and cheese or bulgogi rolls 550 to 570.
realTalk: About 150g of the roll is rice, and that rice is seasoned with sesame oil and salt before it goes anywhere near the seaweed. That is 220 calories from rice plus 45 from the sesame oil, so 265 of the 400 is there before a single filling. The egg strip, ham and crab stick together are about 95. The pickled radish, carrot and spinach are 20.

Fillings change the number a lot. Tuna kimbap is tuna mixed with mayonnaise, and the mayo alone is 90 to 100 calories, which is why Kimbap Cheonguk lists it at 570 for a 300g roll. Cheese kimbap adds a 60 calorie slice. Bulgogi kimbap adds sweet marinated beef for about 150. Vegetable kimbap with no ham or egg is the low end at 355.

The trap is the second roll. At 3,500 to 4,500 won a roll it is cheap enough that two rolls with a cup of tteokbokki is a normal order, and that is 1,170 calories for a snack that felt light because it was cold and cut into pieces. One roll and a bowl of eomuk broth is 500 and does the same job.
lighter: Order vegetable (야채) kimbap. It is about 355 versus 400 for standard and 520 for tuna.
One roll, not two. The second roll is the whole problem.
Skip the tuna mayo and cheese versions. Each is 100 to 150 more than the basic roll for the same size.
Pair it with eomuk broth or a plain soup rather than tteokbokki. Tteokbokki on the side is another 370.

faq.q: Is kimbap good for weight loss?
faq.a: One roll is a reasonable 400 calorie meal with 13g protein. The problem is that it is easy to eat two, and tuna or cheese versions add 100 to 170 each.

faq.q: How many calories in one piece of kimbap?
faq.a: About 40 to 50 per slice, with 8 to 10 slices in a standard roll.

faq.q: Which kimbap has the most calories?
faq.a: Tuna mayo, cheese and bulgogi kimbap are the highest at 520 to 570 per roll. Vegetable kimbap is the lowest at around 355.

faq.q: Is convenience store kimbap lower in calories?
faq.a: Usually, because the rolls are smaller: CU and GS25 rolls are 200 to 270g and 290 to 360 calories, versus 400 to 485 for a bunsik shop roll.

foods.source: fatsecret.kr: 바르다김선생 393 kcal/230g, CU 야채김밥 356 kcal/272g, 김밥천국 485 kcal/300g; 400 used for a standard 240g roll

foods.name: Kimchi Bokkeumbap
foods.metaDescription: Kimchi fried rice is about 525 calories a plate with a fried egg on top. The kimchi is nearly free; the oil, spam and rice are not.
foods.summary: Kimchi bokkeumbap is day-old rice fried with chopped kimchi, a bit of spam or pork and butter or oil, topped with a fried egg and a sprinkle of seaweed.
foods.answer: A plate of kimchi bokkeumbap is about 525 calories, based on the Geniet figure of 523 per serving. The rice is 310 of that, the spam or pork about 110, the cooking oil 45, and the fried egg on top 70. The kimchi itself is under 20 calories.
realTalk: Kimchi fried rice sounds like leftover food, and it is, but a 210g portion of rice is still 310 calories no matter how old it is. The kimchi is 15 calories for a big handful. So the difference between a light plate and a heavy one is entirely what the cook fries it in and what protein goes in.

Most bunsik places use spam. A 40g dice of spam is 110 calories, and if it is a gogi-jip finishing the meal with bokkeumbap in the samgyeopsal pan, the rice is frying in rendered pork fat and the plate goes past 650. Butter is the other common fat. One tablespoon (14g) is 100 calories, about double the neutral oil most home cooks use.

The egg on top is 70 calories and 6g of protein, and it is the best thing on the plate. The seaweed flakes and sesame seeds are a rounding error. If you want it as a real meal, a second egg is a better addition than more spam: 70 more calories for another 6g of protein.
lighter: Ask for tuna instead of spam. Canned tuna in water is about 40 calories for the same 40g, versus 110 for spam.
Less rice, more kimchi. The kimchi is 15 calories a handful and carries all the flavour.
Two eggs on top, no cheese. Cheese kimchi bokkeumbap is around 100 calories higher.
If it is the end-of-meal bokkeumbap at a barbecue place, share one portion between two people.

portions.label: Standard plate with spam and egg

variants.name: Tuna kimchi bokkeumbap
variants.note: Tuna in water instead of spam

faq.q: Is kimchi fried rice healthy?
faq.a: It is an average plate: 525 calories, 15g protein, high in carbs. Swapping spam for tuna and adding a second egg makes it a much better meal for the same size.

faq.q: How many calories in kimchi fried rice without egg?
faq.a: About 455. The fried egg on top is roughly 70 calories.

faq.q: Does kimchi lose its benefits when fried?
faq.a: Some of the live bacteria die with heat, but the fibre and the flavour stay. It is still 15 calories a handful.

faq.q: Is kimchi bokkeumbap lower in calories than bibimbap?
faq.a: Slightly: about 525 versus 610. Bibimbap has more vegetables and more protein though, so it is the better bowl per calorie.

foods.source: geniet.co.kr 김치볶음밥 523 kcal per serving

foods.name: Jajangmyeon
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of jajangmyeon is about 797 calories according to Korean MFDS data. Thick noodles, black bean sauce, a lot of carbs. Details here.
foods.summary: Jajangmyeon is the Korean-Chinese bowl of thick wheat noodles under a glossy black bean sauce with diced pork, onion and potato, the default delivery meal for moving day.
foods.answer: A restaurant bowl of jajangmyeon is about 797 calories for a 650g serving, the figure from the Korean MFDS restaurant nutrition survey. Around 420 of that is the 300g of cooked noodles, with the rest in the chunjang sauce, the pork and the oil the sauce is fried in. It carries about 129g of carbohydrate.
realTalk: Jajangmyeon is a carb bowl. 300g of cooked noodles is 420 calories on its own, and the sauce adds another 130g of stuff that is mostly onion and potato cooked in black bean paste. The pork dice is small, maybe 40g. So you get 27g of protein and 129g of carbs, roughly the ratio of a plate of plain pasta with a spoon of sauce.

The oil is where restaurants differ. Chunjang is fried in oil before the vegetables go in, and a generous kitchen uses 2 tablespoons per portion, which is 240 calories of oil in the sauce. The MFDS survey found bowls ranging from 400g to 840g across shops, so a big-portion place can be serving you 1,000 calories in one bowl for 7,000 won.

Ganjajang (the dry, freshly stir-fried version) is listed at 825 in the same survey, slightly higher because the sauce is cooked with more oil to order. Jjajangbap swaps the noodles for rice and lands around the same. The set that really adds up is the half-and-half with tangsuyuk on the side, which turns lunch into a 1,300 calorie sitting.
lighter: Ask for less noodles (면 적게). Every 100g of noodles you leave is 140 calories.
Eat the sauce, onion and pork, and leave the last third of the noodles. The sauce is where the flavour and the protein are.
Skip the tangsuyuk set. Adding a small tangsuyuk is another 480 per person.
Order it with a side of danmuji and raw onion, and stop there. The onion is free and helps you slow down.

components.name: Black bean sauce with pork, onion, potato

faq.q: Is jajangmyeon unhealthy?
faq.a: It is a high-carb, moderate-fat bowl at about 797 calories with 129g of carbs. Not a diet meal, but fine as an occasional lunch if you skip the tangsuyuk.

faq.q: How many calories in jajangbap?
faq.a: About the same as the noodle version, 750 to 800, because a full bowl of rice replaces the noodles.

faq.q: Jajangmyeon or jjamppong for fewer calories?
faq.a: They are close: 797 versus 764 in the MFDS survey. Jjamppong has slightly less oil and more seafood, so it edges it on protein too.

faq.q: How much protein is in jajangmyeon?
faq.a: About 27g, mostly from the small pork dice and the wheat noodles. It is not a protein meal.

foods.source: MFDS restaurant nutrition survey (짜장면 650g 797 kcal) via hidoc.co.kr

foods.name: Nasi Padang
foods.serving: 1 plate (rice, rendang, gulai gravy, cassava leaves, sambal ijo)
foods.metaDescription: A plate of nasi padang with rendang is about 690 calories. The rice and the gravy poured over it do most of the damage, not the meat.
foods.summary: Nasi padang is the rice plate from a Minang restaurant: a mound of white rice, one main dish like rendang, a ladle of gulai gravy, boiled cassava leaves and green chili sambal.
foods.answer: A standard nasi padang plate with one piece of rendang comes to about 690 calories. That is roughly 250g of rice at 325 calories, 100g of rendang at 200, and about 165 calories of gravy, cassava leaves and sambal ijo poured on top.
realTalk: The rice is the biggest number on the plate, and the Padang restaurant knows it. A normal scoop is 250g, about 325 calories, and the free kuah gulai they ladle over it adds another 80 or so because it is coconut milk and oil. Before you even touch the rendang you are at 400 calories. One piece of rendang, usually around 100g with a bit of the dark paste, is about 200 more.

Where people get into trouble is the pick-and-mix. Order at the counter and you take one lauk, that is 690. Sit down and let them stack 12 plates on your table, and you eat the rendang, half a piece of ayam pop, a spoon of dendeng balado and some perkedel. That plate is now 1,100 to 1,300 calories, and it happens without you deciding anything.

The cassava leaves are basically free at 60 calories for a decent handful, and sambal ijo is only about 25 calories per spoon. Those two are the parts you can pile on. The kerupuk jangek (fried cow skin cracker) on the table is not free, one big piece is around 90 calories and it goes down in three bites.

Price check: a nasi padang with rendang is Rp 20,000 to 35,000 in Jakarta, so it is one of the better value meals for the calories if you keep it to one lauk. The protein is decent at 30g. The problem is only when you treat the table like a buffet.
lighter: Ask for nasi setengah (half rice). That alone takes 160 calories off the plate.
Say 'tanpa kuah' or 'kuahnya sedikit'. Skipping the gravy pour saves 60 to 80 calories and you lose nothing in flavour because rendang has its own paste.
Pick one lauk and stick to it. Rendang at 200, ayam bakar at about 290, or ikan bakar at about 300. Two lauk is where it becomes a 1,000 calorie lunch.
Load up on daun singkong. It is fibre and water, and it fills the same space on the plate as another spoon of rice.
Leave the kerupuk jangek and the sambal lado merah (the red one is cooked in a lot of oil, the green one much less).

portions.label: Two lauk plus perkedel and kerupuk jangek

variants.name: With ikan bakar instead of rendang
variants.note: Grilled fish is slightly leaner than rendang

variants.name: With ayam pop
variants.note: Pale fried chicken, oil soaked skin

variants.name: Bungkus (takeaway)
variants.note: Takeaway gets noticeably more rice and gravy

faq.q: How many calories in nasi padang with rendang?
faq.a: About 690 calories for a normal plate: 250g rice, one piece of rendang, a ladle of gravy, cassava leaves and green sambal.

faq.q: Is nasi padang bungkus more calories than eating in?
faq.a: Usually yes. The takeaway wrap is known for extra rice, often 300g or more, plus more gravy. Expect 800 to 850 calories for the same rendang order.

faq.q: Can I eat nasi padang while losing weight?
faq.a: Yes, once or twice a week fits fine if you order one lauk, half rice and skip the gravy. That version is around 470 calories with 30g protein.

faq.q: Which Padang dish has the fewest calories?
faq.a: Ikan bakar or ayam bakar as the lauk, with daun singkong on the side. Avoid gulai tunjang, gulai otak and anything swimming in santan.

foods.source: estimate from components (rendang figure aligned with existing rendang record, rice and gravy from standard values)

foods.name: Nasi Uduk
foods.serving: 1 plate (nasi uduk, telur balado, tempe orek, bihun goreng, kerupuk)
foods.metaDescription: A plate of nasi uduk with telur balado, tempe orek and kerupuk is about 600 calories. The coconut rice alone is 325 of that.
foods.summary: Nasi uduk is Jakarta's coconut rice, sold from morning stalls with a lineup of side dishes: telur balado, tempe orek, bihun goreng, fried chicken and kerupuk.
foods.answer: A typical breakfast plate of nasi uduk is about 600 calories: 200g of coconut rice at 325 calories, a telur balado at about 70, tempe orek at 90, a spoon of bihun goreng at 60 and one kerupuk at 50. Add fried chicken and you pass 900.
realTalk: FatSecret Indonesia lists plain nasi uduk at 260 calories for a 160g bowl, which works out to about 163 per 100g. Plain white rice is 130 per 100g. So the coconut milk costs you roughly 25% more per scoop, and a stall scoop is closer to 200g than 160g. That is why the rice alone on this plate is 325 calories before any side dish.

The side dishes are where the plate swings. The default Rp 12,000 to 15,000 breakfast set with egg, tempe orek, bihun and kerupuk is around 600 calories. Swap the egg for a piece of ayam goreng and you add about 390 calories. Add semur jengkol and another 150. The nasi uduk with ayam goreng, telur and everything is easily 1,000 calories and it is 7am.

Tempe orek looks innocent but it is fried tempe tossed in kecap manis and sugar. A small spoon of 40g is about 90 calories, and a lot of that is sugar. Bihun goreng is 60 calories per spoon, again mostly oil. Neither one is the enemy on its own, they just stack.

For 600 calories you get only 18g of protein, which is the actual weak point. The rice and bihun are 80g of carbs. If you want this to hold you until lunch, the fix is more egg or more tempe, not more rice.
lighter: Ask for half rice (nasi setengah). Coconut rice is dense, and cutting 100g saves 160 calories.
Take two telur balado instead of the fried chicken. Two eggs are about 140 calories with 14g protein; a piece of ayam goreng is 390.
Skip the bihun goreng. It is rice noodles fried in oil sitting next to rice, so you are paying twice for the same carb.
One kerupuk, not three. Each one is about 50 calories and they are all air and oil.
Ask for the sambal kacang on the side. The peanut sauce is about 40 calories per spoon and the stall tends to be generous.

portions.label: Half rice with telur balado only
Standard plate (egg, tempe orek, bihun, kerupuk)

variants.name: With telur balado and tempe orek

faq.q: How many calories in nasi uduk komplit?
faq.a: Around 600 calories for the usual set with telur balado, tempe orek, bihun goreng and one kerupuk. With fried chicken it is closer to 1,000.

faq.q: Is nasi uduk more fattening than white rice?
faq.a: Per 100g, nasi uduk is about 163 calories versus 130 for plain rice, because it is cooked in coconut milk. It is about 25% more, so half rice is the easy fix.

faq.q: How many calories in nasi uduk with ayam goreng?
faq.a: About 990 calories once you add a bone-in piece of fried chicken (around 390 calories) to the standard 600 calorie plate.

faq.q: Is nasi uduk good for breakfast on a diet?
faq.a: It can work at half rice with two eggs, around 370 calories and 16g protein. The full plate with chicken is a whole day's worth of fat before 8am.

foods.source: FatSecret Indonesia (nasi uduk 163 kcal/100g, telur balado 71 kcal/egg) plus component estimate for sides

foods.name: Nasi Kuning
foods.serving: 1 plate (yellow rice, shredded fried chicken, sliced omelette, kering tempe, serundeng)
foods.metaDescription: A plate of nasi kuning komplit is about 640 calories. The turmeric coconut rice is 320 of it, the toppings do the rest.
foods.summary: Nasi kuning is rice cooked with turmeric and coconut milk, served at breakfast stalls and on birthdays with fried chicken, sliced omelette, kering tempe and serundeng on top.
foods.answer: A standard plate of nasi kuning komplit is about 640 calories. That is 200g of turmeric coconut rice at 320 calories, a small piece of fried chicken at 150, sliced omelette at 55, sweet kering tempe at 75 and a spoon of serundeng at 40.
realTalk: The rice is not plain rice. It is cooked in coconut milk with turmeric, and it lands at about 160 calories per 100g against 130 for white rice. A stall scoop of 200g is 320 calories. FatSecret lists a smaller 150 calorie bowl, but that is a 100g lab portion, nobody gets served that at a warung.

The toppings are small but every one of them is fried or sweet. Kering tempe is tempe shreds fried and glazed in palm sugar, 75 calories for a spoon that weighs 30g. Serundeng is grated coconut toasted with sugar, 40 calories for 15g. Sliced telur dadar is 55 calories. None of them look like much on the plate, and together they are 170 calories.

The Manado version with cakalang (skipjack) and sambal roa is actually leaner than the Javanese one: the fish is grilled or shredded rather than fried, so the plate comes out around 560 calories with more protein. The tumpeng birthday version is the opposite, because the cone means more rice, often 300g, and the plate hits 800 without trying.
At Rp 12,000 to 20,000 this is a decent breakfast at 26g protein. The issue is it is 78g of carbs and most stalls pile the rice, so ask for less before they scoop.
lighter: Half rice. The rice is half the calories, and the toppings taste the same on 100g as on 200g.
Ask for ayam suwir (shredded chicken, usually not fried) instead of ayam goreng. Saves about 60 to 80 calories.
Double the telur dadar and skip the kering tempe. Egg gives you protein; kering tempe gives you sugar and oil.
The Manado version with cakalang fufu is the leaner order if you can find it, about 560 calories.
Skip the kerupuk and emping on the side. Emping is around 50 calories for a small handful.

faq.q: How many calories in nasi kuning?
faq.a: About 320 calories for 200g of the rice itself, and about 640 for a full komplit plate with chicken, egg, kering tempe and serundeng.

faq.q: Is nasi kuning healthier than nasi uduk?
faq.a: They are nearly the same. Both are coconut rice at roughly 160 calories per 100g. Nasi kuning just has turmeric for colour. What matters is the toppings you pick.

faq.q: Is nasi kuning high in fat?
faq.a: The rice has about 5g of fat per 200g from the coconut milk. Most of the plate's 25g of fat comes from the fried chicken, kering tempe and serundeng.

faq.q: How many calories in nasi kuning Manado?
faq.a: Around 560 calories with cakalang and sambal roa, because the fish is not deep fried. Add fried perkedel and it climbs to 700.
