Skip larb moo tod (the fried version), which doubles the calories to around 400.

components.name: Shallots, mint, coriander, lime, fish sauce, chili flakes

variants.name: Larb moo tod (fried)
variants.note: Shaped into balls and deep fried

faq.q: Is larb moo good for weight loss?
faq.a: Yes. At about 200 calories and 20g of protein per plate with no cooking oil, it is one of the best protein to calorie ratios at any Thai stall. Keep the sticky rice to one bag.

faq.q: How many calories in larb moo with sticky rice?
faq.a: About 450 calories for a 150g plate of larb with a 150g bag of khao niao. Add som tam and it is around 600 for a very full meal.

faq.q: Larb vs nam tok, which has fewer calories?
faq.a: They are close. Larb moo is about 200 a plate with minced pork; nam tok moo is about 250 because it uses grilled pork neck, which is fattier.

foods.source: sanook.com Thai food calorie table larb moo 150g = 220 kcal; hdmall.co.th 119 kcal per small plate; picked 200 for a 150g stall plate

foods.name: Tom Saap
aka: ต้มแซ่บกระดูกหมู
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of tom saap with pork ribs is about 270 calories, nearly all of it from the meat. The broth is close to zero. Rib, chicken and hot pot numbers.
foods.summary: The Isan cousin of tom yum: a clear, sour and very spicy broth with pork ribs or soft bones, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaf, lime juice, chili, toasted rice powder and a handful of sawtooth coriander. No coconut milk, no chili paste, no oil.
foods.answer: A 350g bowl of tom saap kraduk moo is about 270 calories, with 22g of protein. The broth is essentially free at under 20 calories; the pork ribs, roughly 90g of edible meat and fat once the bone is out, are around 230. Tom saap gai (chicken) is about 200 a bowl, and the big hot pot version served on a burner is closer to 400 per person.
realTalk: Tom saap is the lightest soup on an Isan menu that still counts as a meal. The broth is water, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaf, lime juice, fish sauce and chili, which comes to maybe 15 calories per bowl. Compare tom kha at 320 a bowl, where 180 calories are coconut milk, or tom yum nam khon with its chili paste and evaporated milk. Everything in a tom saap bowl that has calories is the meat.

The meat is pork ribs or kraduk on (soft cartilage bones). A stall bowl carries around 180g of bone in ribs, which gives roughly 90g of edible meat and fat at about 230 calories. Ribs are a fatty cut, so the fat number for the bowl is 18g even though nothing was fried. Pick tom saap moo sam chan (belly) and the bowl climbs to 380; pick the chicken version and it falls to about 200.

The catch is the rice. Tom saap comes with a bag of khao niao or a plate of rice, and that is where a 270 calorie bowl becomes a 520 calorie lunch. Still fine. The bowl also comes with toasted rice powder and chili flakes stirred in at the table, about 20 calories combined, so the numbers above already include them.
lighter: Order tom saap gai or tom saap kraduk on (soft bone) instead of belly or thick ribs; that saves 70 to 110 calories a bowl.
Eat all the meat and mushrooms and drink the broth; it is nearly free and very filling on a hot day.
Pair it with a small bag of sticky rice (160 calories) or half a plate of rice rather than a full plate.
Ask for extra sawtooth coriander and mushrooms; they add volume and about 10 calories.

components.name: Clear broth with lemongrass, galangal, lime, fish sauce, chili
Toasted rice powder and chili flakes

portions.label: Hot pot on a burner, per person

variants.name: Tom saap kraduk on (soft bone)
variants.note: Cartilage bones, less fat than ribs

variants.name: Tom saap moo sam chan (pork belly)

faq.q: Is tom saap healthy?
faq.a: It is one of the leaner soups in Thai food. A bowl is about 270 calories with 22g of protein and no cooking oil or coconut milk. The sodium is high from fish sauce, but for calories it is a good choice.

faq.q: Tom saap vs tom yum, which has fewer calories?
faq.a: A clear tom yum gai is about 100 to 150 a bowl because it uses less meat. Tom saap is about 270 because it is built around pork ribs. Tom yum nam khon with chili paste and evaporated milk is about 250 to 300, so tom saap and creamy tom yum are close.

faq.q: How many calories in tom saap with rice?
faq.a: About 520 for a rib bowl with a 150g bag of sticky rice, or about 500 with a small plate of steamed rice.

foods.source: estimate from components; no published Thai figure found for tom saap kraduk moo

foods.name: Khao Kha Moo
foods.metaDescription: A plate of khao kha moo with braised egg is about 690 calories. Skip the skin and egg and the Department of Health figure drops to 438. Here is the breakdown.
foods.summary: Pork leg braised for hours in soy, palm sugar and five spice until the skin turns to jelly, sliced over rice with a half braised egg, pickled mustard greens, blanched kale and a ladle of the sweet gravy. A 50 to 70 baht plate at every Thai market and night bazaar.
foods.answer: A standard 350g plate of khao kha moo with half a braised egg is about 690 calories. The Thai Department of Health lists a smaller 289g plate without egg at 438 calories, and Thai nutrition sites put a normal plate with skin and gravy at 600 to 800. The difference between those numbers is the skin, the egg and how heavy the gravy ladle is.
realTalk: Two numbers get quoted for this dish and both are right. The Department of Health figure is 438 calories for 289g, which is a modest plate of rice, lean pork leg and a little gravy with no egg. The common street figure is 690, which is what you actually get at a market stall: 220g of rice, 100g of pork including skin and fat, half a braised egg and a generous ladle of gravy. Order nueng ping (skin and fat included) and you are on the 690 plate, not the 438 one.

The skin is where it moves. Pork leg meat alone is about 200 calories per 100g. With the jelly skin and the fat layer attached it is closer to 300. Thai nutrition sites note that leaving out the skin and fat drops a plate from 600 to 800 down to 450 to 550, which matches the components: about 100 calories of skin and fat, another 40 for the half egg.

The gravy matters more than people think. It is the braising liquid reduced with palm sugar and soy, and a stall ladle is 40 to 50g and 50 to 60 calories, plus a lot of sodium. Some stalls sell a khao kha moo piset (special) with extra pork, a whole egg and a few pieces of intestine or sam chan belly, which lands at 850 or more. That is a dinner, not a lunch.
lighter: Order it mai ao nang, mai ao man (no skin, no fat); the plate drops by around 150 calories and the meat is still tender.
Ask for nam rad noi (little gravy); each ladle is about 55 calories and a lot of salt.
Take the full portion of pickled mustard greens and blanched kale; they are under 20 calories and cut the richness.
Skip the egg if you had one for breakfast, or skip the extra 10 baht piset upgrade, which is mostly skin.

components.name: Braised pork leg with skin and fat
Pickled mustard greens and blanched kale

portions.label: Small plate, no egg (Department of Health, 289g)
Piset with extra pork, whole egg and skin

variants.name: Khao kha moo, lean meat only, no egg
Khao kha moo with half egg
Kha moo only, no rice (100g with skin)
variants.note: Meat and gravy as a side

variants.name: Khao kha moo piset
variants.note: Extra pork, whole egg, often sam chan or intestine

faq.q: Why do khao kha moo calorie figures vary so much?
faq.a: Because the skin, the egg and the gravy are optional. The Department of Health figure of 438 is a 289g plate with lean meat and no egg. A real stall plate with skin, half an egg and a full ladle of gravy is closer to 690.

faq.q: How many calories in kha moo without rice?
faq.a: About 300 for 100g of pork leg with skin and gravy, or around 200 for lean meat only. The rice under it is another 290.

faq.q: Is khao kha moo or khao man gai higher in calories?
faq.a: Khao man gai is 596 for a 300g plate in the Department of Health table. A standard khao kha moo with egg at 690 is higher, but a lean, no skin khao kha moo at 438 is lower.

foods.source: hdmall.co.th khao kha moo 1 plate = 690 kcal; Thai Department of Health via health.kapook.com 289g plate = 438 kcal; joomyak.com 600 to 800 kcal for a normal plate with skin and gravy. Picked 690 for a 350g plate with half a braised egg

foods.name: Khao Pad Poo
foods.metaDescription: A plate of khao pad poo is about 560 calories, and the crab is the cheapest part. The rice and the oil carry it. Stall, restaurant and extra crab numbers.
foods.summary: Fried rice with lump crab meat, egg, garlic and spring onion, seasoned lightly with fish sauce and white pepper so the crab comes through. The most expensive fried rice at a Thai seafood restaurant, 120 to 300 baht depending on how much crab goes in.
foods.answer: A 300g plate of khao pad poo is about 560 calories, using the Thai table figure of 300 calories per 160g scaled up to a full plate. Crab meat is lean at about 90 calories per 100g, so a plate with 50g of crab gets only 45 calories from the crab. The rice is about 260 and the wok oil and egg are around 210 between them.
realTalk: People assume crab fried rice is the light option because crab is lean, and the crab part is: 50g of crab meat is 45 calories and 10g of protein. But it is still fried rice. A plate uses about 200g of cooked rice at 260 calories, one egg at 75, and a tablespoon or more of oil at 135. The Department of Health lists pork fried rice with egg at 557 for 315g, and crab fried rice lands in the same place, about 560 for 300g.

The price tells you the crab weight. A 60 baht stall plate has maybe 30g of crab, often mixed with crab stick, and is closer to 500 calories with a bit less protein. A 250 baht restaurant plate can carry 100g of lump crab, which adds protein (20g from crab alone) but only about 45 extra calories. If you are going to eat fried rice, the expensive one is the better deal per calorie.

The side plate matters too. Khao pad poo comes with cucumber, spring onion and a lime wedge, which is free, and a small bowl of prik nam pla (fish sauce with chili), which is about 5 calories. What is not free is the fried egg some places put on top for 10 baht: another 100 calories. Order the plate plain and the lime and prik nam pla do the work.
lighter: Order a plate with more crab and no extra egg on top; the crab adds protein for almost nothing.
Ask for nam man noi (less oil) at a seafood restaurant; they usually cook fried rice with a heavy hand.
Share one plate of khao pad poo between two people alongside a steamed fish or a clear tom yum.
Squeeze the whole lime wedge over it and use the prik nam pla instead of adding sugar or extra sauce.

components.name: Garlic, spring onion, fish sauce, cucumber, lime

variants.name: Khao pad goong (prawn fried rice)
variants.note: Prawns are as lean as crab

variants.name: Khao pad moo sai kai (pork with egg)
Khao pad poo with fried egg on top

faq.q: Is crab fried rice healthier than regular fried rice?
faq.a: Marginally. It is about 560 calories a plate against 557 for pork fried rice, but it has less saturated fat and the same protein. The rice and oil are the same in both.

faq.q: How many calories in crab meat?
faq.a: About 90 calories per 100g, with 19g of protein and almost no fat. The 50g in a typical plate is only 45 calories.

faq.q: How much protein is in khao pad poo?
faq.a: About 22g in a standard plate: roughly 10g from the crab, 6g from the egg and 5g from the rice. A restaurant plate with 100g of crab is closer to 32g.

foods.source: sanook.com Thai food calorie table khao pad poo 160g = 300 kcal, scaled to a 300g restaurant plate; Thai Department of Health khao pad moo sai kai 315g = 557 kcal for comparison

foods.name: Yen Ta Fo
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of yen ta fo is about 290 calories, one of the lightest noodle soups in Thailand. The pink sauce is fermented tofu, not sugar. What pushes it up.
foods.summary: Thai noodle soup coloured pink with fermented red bean curd sauce, loaded with fish balls, fish tofu, squid, morning glory and a fried wonton or two. Sold at noodle shops for 50 to 70 baht, usually with sen yai (wide rice noodles).
foods.answer: A bowl of yen ta fo with sen yai is about 290 calories, the figure both the Thai Department of Health based tables and hdmall use for a standard bowl. The noodles are 130 of that, the fish balls and squid about 70, and the red fermented tofu sauce around 20. It is lower than most Thai noodle soups because there is no pork fat and no coconut.
realTalk: The pink colour scares people who assume it is sugar syrup. It is nam yen ta fo, a sauce made from fermented red bean curd, garlic, vinegar and a little sugar, and a bowl uses about 20g of it for around 20 calories. The broth itself is a light pork or fish stock at maybe 15 calories per bowl. So the two things that make yen ta fo look unusual add up to less than 40 calories.

Where the calories sit is the noodles and the toppings. 120g of sen yai is about 130 calories. A standard bowl carries 60g of fish balls, fish tofu and squid at about 70 calories, which is lean protein. The fried wonton skins and fried tofu on top are the one fatty part: 20g of fried wonton is around 50 calories, and a shop that piles them on can add 100 more.

The version to watch is yen ta fo with extras. Add pork cracklings (kaeb moo), extra fried wonton and a couple of pieces of pork blood jelly and a 290 calorie bowl becomes a 400 calorie one. The dry version (yen ta fo haeng) tossed with garlic oil is another 60 to 80 on top. Order it nam (soup), standard toppings, and it is about as light as a Thai noodle lunch gets.
lighter: Order sen woon sen (glass noodles) or sen mee (thin rice vermicelli) instead of sen yai; either saves 30 to 40 calories a bowl.
Ask for mai ao kiao tod (no fried wonton); that is 50 to 100 calories of fried flour you do not need.
Take extra pak boong (morning glory); it is under 10 calories a handful and fills the bowl.
Order it nam (soup), not haeng (dry with garlic oil), which adds 60 to 80 calories.

portions.label: Special with extra fried wonton and pork cracklings

variants.name: Yen ta fo with glass noodles
Yen ta fo with sen yai
Yen ta fo piset with cracklings

faq.q: Is yen ta fo healthy?
faq.a: For a noodle soup it is one of the lighter ones at about 290 calories a bowl with 16g of protein from fish balls and squid. The fried wonton is the only real fat source, and the sauce is fermented tofu, not syrup.

faq.q: What is the pink sauce in yen ta fo made of?
faq.a: Fermented red bean curd blended with garlic, vinegar and a little sugar. A bowl uses around 20g, which is about 20 calories.

faq.q: Yen ta fo vs boat noodles, which is lower in calories?
faq.a: They are close. A small boat noodle bowl is about 300 calories, but boat noodle bowls are half the size, so per gram yen ta fo is much lighter.

foods.source: hdmall.co.th and health.kapook.com Thai calorie tables: sen yai yen ta fo nam 1 bowl = 290 kcal

foods.name: Kanom Jeen Nam Ya
aka: ขนมจีนน้ำยา
Thai Rice Noodles with Fish Curry
foods.metaDescription: A plate of kanom jeen nam ya is about 330 calories per the Thai Department of Health. The noodles are 150 of that. What the fish curry adds.
foods.summary: Fresh fermented rice noodles (kanom jeen) topped with nam ya, a thin fish curry made from pounded fish, krachai (fingerroot) and a little coconut milk, served with a table of raw and pickled vegetables you pile on yourself. A 30 to 40 baht market breakfast.
foods.answer: A 350g plate of kanom jeen nam ya is about 330 calories, the figure in the Thai Department of Health food table. About 150 calories are the 150g of rice noodles, around 150 are the fish curry, and the vegetables on the side are close to zero. A hard boiled egg on top adds 75.
realTalk: Kanom jeen looks like a lot of food for 330 calories, and it is. Fresh rice noodles are about 100 calories per 100g because they are mostly water, so the 150g nest on a plate is only 150 calories. The nam ya is a thin curry, not a thick coconut one: a stall ladle of about 150g is around 150 calories, and most of that is the fish and the small amount of coconut milk. That is the whole plate.

The type of nam ya changes the number. Nam ya pa (Isan style, no coconut) is about 100 calories a ladle, so the plate drops to 280. Nam ya kati (southern style, thick with coconut milk) is closer to 220 a ladle, so the plate climbs to 400. Nam ngiao from the North and gaeng keow wan (green curry) over kanom jeen both run 380 to 450 a plate because of the coconut and pork.

The best part is the vegetable table. Bean sprouts, long beans, cabbage, Thai basil, pickled mustard greens and cucumber are all sitting there for free, and a big pile adds about 20 calories. Load half the plate with vegetables and it eats like 600 calories of food. The one thing to be careful with is the fried dried chili and the fish sauce; the chili is fried in oil, and 5 pieces are around 30 calories.
lighter: Order nam ya pa (no coconut) where it is available; it is about 50 calories lighter per plate than standard nam ya.
Take one nest of noodles, not two; each extra nest is about 100 calories.
Pile on the raw vegetables and pickled mustard greens from the side table; they are almost free.
Skip the green curry and nam ngiao toppings if you want the light option; they add 80 to 120 calories over nam ya.

components.name: Raw vegetables and pickled mustard greens

portions.label: Small plate, nam ya pa (no coconut)
Standard plate, nam ya (Department of Health, 350g)
With boiled egg and second nest of noodles

variants.name: Kanom jeen nam ngiao
variants.note: Northern tomato and pork rib curry

faq.q: Is kanom jeen fattening?
faq.a: The noodles are not; 150g of fresh kanom jeen is about 150 calories, less than the same weight of cooked rice. The topping decides the plate: 280 for nam ya pa, 330 for nam ya, up to 450 for green curry.

faq.q: How many calories in kanom jeen nam ya with a boiled egg?
faq.a: About 405 calories: the 330 calorie plate plus a 75 calorie hard boiled egg. The egg adds 6g of protein, which the plate is a bit short on.

faq.q: Kanom jeen vs pad thai, which is lower in calories?
faq.a: Kanom jeen nam ya at 330 for 350g is far lighter than pad thai at 577 for 244g in the Department of Health table.

foods.source: Thai Department of Health (กรมอนามัย) via health.kapook.com kanom jeen nam ya 350g = 330 kcal; hdmall.co.th 332 kcal per plate

foods.name: Kuay Jab
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of Yaowarat style kuay jab with crispy pork is about 350 calories. The plain offal version is 240. Where the broth, noodles and moo krob land.
foods.summary: Rolled rice noodle sheets in a peppery clear broth (nam sai) with pork offal, a boiled egg and a scatter of crispy pork belly, the Chinatown Bangkok classic. There is also a dark, thick nam khon version with five spice. 50 to 80 baht a bowl, more with extras.
foods.answer: A 350g bowl of kuay jab nam sai with crispy pork is about 350 calories. Thai tables list a plain kuay jab bowl at 240 calories; the 30g of moo krob on a Yaowarat style bowl adds roughly 110. The rolled noodles are about 110 calories, the offal 80, and the black pepper broth around 25.
realTalk: The broth is the surprise here. Nam sai kuay jab is a clear pork stock loaded with white pepper, and it comes in at about 25 calories per bowl. It is one of the most warming things you can eat in Bangkok for almost nothing. The rolled noodle sheets are 100g and about 110 calories, so before any topping goes in you are at 135. That is why the plain hdmall figure of 240 is so low: it is noodles, broth and a modest amount of offal.

The toppings are where a Chinatown bowl earns its 350. Pork intestine, liver and a piece of blood jelly are about 80 calories for 50g, and they are decent protein. Then the moo krob: a standard scatter is 30g and about 110 calories, more than the whole broth and offal put together. A piset bowl with extra crispy pork and a boiled egg lands around 480.

Nam khon (the dark version) is a different animal. The broth is thickened with tapioca starch and flavoured with five spice and soy, and the noodles are usually a bit more, so a bowl runs 380 to 420 even before crispy pork. If you want the lightest kuay jab, it is nam sai, offal only, no moo krob, at about 240.
lighter: Order it mai ao moo krob (no crispy pork); that single change saves about 110 calories.
Pick nam sai (clear) over nam khon (thick); the thickened broth adds 40 to 70 calories.
Ask for extra offal or a boiled egg instead of moo krob for protein; the egg is 75 calories and the offal is lean.
Drink the broth; at about 25 calories a bowl it is the part that fills you up.

Standard Yaowarat bowl with moo krob
Piset with extra moo krob and boiled egg

variants.name: Kuay jab nam sai, offal only
Kuay jab nam sai with moo krob
Kuay jab Ubon (Vietnamese style)
variants.note: Round noodles, minced pork, fried garlic

faq.q: Is kuay jab high in calories?
faq.a: Not especially. A plain bowl is about 240 calories and a Chinatown bowl with crispy pork is about 350. The crispy pork is a third of the total.

faq.q: What is in kuay jab broth?
faq.a: Pork stock with a lot of white pepper, garlic and coriander root. A 170g ladle is about 25 calories. The nam khon version adds tapioca starch and five spice.

faq.q: How many calories in kuay jab nam khon?
faq.a: About 400 a bowl. The starch thickened broth and slightly larger portion add 40 to 70 calories over the clear version.

foods.source: hdmall.co.th kuay jab 1 bowl = 240 kcal (plain); estimate adds 30g moo krob (about 110 kcal) for the standard Yaowarat style bowl

foods.name: Khao Mok Gai
aka: ข้าวหมกไก่
foods.metaDescription: A plate of khao mok gai is about 534 calories, lighter than a Malaysian briyani because the rice is drier and the chicken is one piece. Full breakdown.
foods.summary: Thai Muslim biryani: rice cooked in chicken stock with turmeric, ghee and whole spices, with a bone in chicken thigh buried in it, served with crispy fried shallots, cucumber, a sweet and sour green chili sauce and a small bowl of clear chicken soup. 50 to 70 baht at halal stalls.
foods.answer: A 350g plate of khao mok gai is about 534 calories, the figure listed by hdmall. The spiced rice is about 330 of that, the chicken thigh with skin around 190, and the sauce and shallots the rest. It is around 200 calories lighter than a Malaysian nasi briyani with chicken because the Thai version uses less ghee and a single chicken piece.
realTalk: Thai khao mok is built lighter than the briyani it descends from. The rice is cooked with turmeric, a spoon of ghee or butter and stock, then steamed, so 220g of it is about 330 calories against 400 or more for oily Indian style rice. The chicken is one bone in thigh, about 130g raw, cooked in the rice, so it does not get fried. That thigh with skin is about 190 calories and 20g of protein.

The green sauce (nam jim khao mok) is sugar, vinegar, green chili, mint and coriander blended. A small dish is about 25g and 20 calories, almost all sugar. The fried shallots on top are 5g and 20 calories. And the bowl of clear soup on the side is about 15 calories and worth drinking. None of these move the plate much; the rice is two thirds of the total.

Portions vary more than most Thai plates. A stall that serves a small thigh and a modest scoop of rice is around 420. A restaurant plate with a big leg quarter and a heaped rice mound is 680 or more. Khao mok nuea (beef) is a bit higher because the beef is braised in fat, and khao mok pae (goat) higher still at around 620 for the standard plate.
lighter: Ask for khao noi (less rice); the rice is 330 of the 534 calories, so a two thirds scoop saves about 110.
Peel the skin off the thigh and you save around 60 calories with all the protein left.
Use the green sauce sparingly; it is sugar and vinegar, about 20 calories a dish.
Drink the clear soup and eat the cucumber first; they fill space for under 20 calories.

components.name: Turmeric rice cooked with ghee and stock
Chicken thigh, bone in, with skin

portions.label: Restaurant plate with leg quarter and extra rice

variants.name: Khao mok pae (goat)
variants.note: Goat on the bone, richer rice

faq.q: Is khao mok gai healthy?
faq.a: It is a reasonable one plate meal at 534 calories with 28g of protein. The rice is two thirds of the calories, so asking for less rice is the single most useful change.

faq.q: Khao mok gai vs khao man gai, which has fewer calories?
faq.a: Khao mok gai at 534 is a little lower than khao man gai at 596 for a 300g plate, mainly because khao man gai rice is cooked in chicken fat.

faq.q: How many calories in khao mok gai without the rice?
faq.a: The chicken thigh with skin, sauce and shallots is about 230 calories. The rice on its own is about 330.

foods.source: hdmall.co.th khao mok gai 1 plate = 534 kcal

foods.name: Khao Kai Jeow
aka: ข้าวไข่เจียว
foods.metaDescription: A plate of khao kai jeow with minced pork is about 500 calories per the Thai Department of Health. The omelette drinks the oil. One and two egg numbers.
foods.summary: The cheapest meal in Thailand: a fluffy, crisp edged omelette fried in a lot of hot oil, usually with a spoon of minced pork, over a plate of rice with prik nam pla (fish sauce with chili and lime) and sriracha. 35 to 45 baht at any tam sang stall.
foods.answer: A 380g plate of khao kai jeow moo sap (omelette with minced pork over rice) is about 500 calories, the Thai Department of Health figure. The rice is about 290, the two eggs 150, the minced pork 35 and the oil the omelette soaks up around 40. A plain single egg version is closer to 400.
realTalk: A Thai omelette is not a French omelette. The eggs are beaten with fish sauce and a splash of lime, then poured into a wok of oil so hot the edges puff and go brown. That is what makes it good, and it is also why two eggs at 150 calories become an omelette of about 220: the puffed edges hold oil. The Department of Health figure of 500 for the plate with pork reflects that, and hdmall lists a plain khao kai jeow at 445.

For 40 baht this is a decent protein plate. Two eggs and 20g of minced pork give you about 18g of protein, and with the rice it reaches 22g. The problem is the ratio: 220g of rice is 290 calories, more than the omelette, and it disappears under sriracha in about 4 minutes. Ask for kai song (two eggs) and khao noi (less rice) and you flip the ratio to more protein than starch.

Toppings are cheap here, calorie wise. Prik nam pla is fish sauce, chili and lime at about 5 calories a spoon. Sriracha is about 15 calories a tablespoon. The one that adds up is when a stall drops a second omelette on for 10 baht: that is another 220 calories, and a two omelette plate is over 700. Kai jeow with crab meat (kai jeow poo) at a seafood restaurant is around 550 as a plate.
lighter: Order kai jeow with khao noi (less rice); the rice is 290 of the 500 calories.
Ask for nam man noi (less oil) for the omelette; a thin omelette absorbs about half the oil of a puffy one.
Get moo sap (minced pork) or extra egg rather than a second full omelette for more protein.
Use prik nam pla instead of sriracha; both are low but prik nam pla has no sugar.

components.name: Frying oil absorbed by the omelette

portions.label: Standard, two eggs with minced pork (Department of Health, 380g)

variants.name: Khao kai jeow moo sap
variants.note: Two eggs with minced pork, the standard

faq.q: How many calories in a Thai omelette?
faq.a: About 220 for a two egg kai jeow fried in a wok, or around 140 for a single egg one. The oil the puffed edges absorb adds 40 to 70 over the eggs themselves.

faq.q: Is khao kai jeow good for weight loss?
faq.a: It can be. A two egg plate with less rice is about 400 calories with 18g of protein for 40 baht. The default plate with a full scoop of rice is 500.

faq.q: How much oil is in kai jeow?
faq.a: The wok holds a lot, but the omelette only keeps about 4 to 8g of it, which is 36 to 72 calories. Thin omelettes absorb less than puffy ones.

foods.source: Thai Department of Health (กรมอนามัย) via health.kapook.com khao kai jeow moo sap 380g = 500 kcal; hdmall.co.th khao kai jeow 1 plate = 445 kcal

foods.name: Khao Tom
aka: ข้าวต้มหมู
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of khao tom moo is about 300 calories. Plain khao tom is only 120 a cup; the minced pork, garlic oil and fish version take it up. Numbers for each.
foods.summary: Thai rice soup: whole grains of jasmine rice simmered in stock until soft but not broken down, with minced pork or fish, garlic oil, celery, spring onion and white pepper. The late night and hangover meal of Thailand, 40 to 60 baht a bowl.
foods.answer: A 400g bowl of khao tom moo (with minced pork) is about 300 calories. Thai tables list plain khao tom at 120 calories per cup and khao tom pla (fish) at 325 per cup. The rice and stock are about 200 of the bowl, the minced pork 70, and the fried garlic oil on top around 30.
realTalk: Khao tom is rice stretched with water, which is why it is light. A bowl holds about 60g of dry rice equivalent, roughly the same as a small plate, but it comes as 300g of soup that takes 15 minutes to eat. That 300g of rice soup is about 200 calories. Plain khao tom in a Thai table is 120 per cup, and a stall bowl is about two and a half cups.

The toppings are the variable. Minced pork (40g, about 70 calories) is the standard. Khao tom pla uses about 60g of fish and lands at 325 per cup in the hdmall table because it comes with a bigger dose of garlic oil and celery. The garlic oil is the sneaky part: a stall spoons 8 to 10g of it on top, and that is 70 to 90 calories if they are generous, 30 if they are not.

The other version of khao tom is the khao tom kui restaurant, where you get a bowl of plain rice soup (about 200 calories) and order side dishes: salted egg, stir fried morning glory, omelette, pork with garlic. That is where a 200 calorie bowl becomes a 900 calorie dinner, but each side is a choice. Two lean sides (salted egg at 90 and stir fried greens at 120) keep it under 450.
lighter: Ask for mai sai nam man krathiem (no garlic oil); that alone can save 50 to 90 calories.
Choose khao tom goong (prawn) or khao tom gai (chicken) over pork; both are around 260 a bowl.
At a khao tom kui restaurant, order one plain khao tom with a salted egg and a plate of pak boong; that is about 410 total.
Skip the pa tong go (fried dough) on the side; a pair is 124 calories.

variants.note: Rice soup only, the base at khao tom kui shops

variants.name: Khao tom pla (fish)
variants.note: hdmall figure per cup, fish and garlic oil

faq.q: Is khao tom good for weight loss?
faq.a: Yes. A 400g bowl is about 300 calories with 14g of protein, and the volume of water makes it filling. Ask for less garlic oil and it is closer to 250.

faq.q: Khao tom vs jok, which has fewer calories?
faq.a: Similar. Khao tom moo is about 300 a bowl; jok with egg is about 250 and jok moo without egg about 160. Jok is thinner, so it has slightly less rice per bowl.

faq.q: How many calories in plain khao tom?
faq.a: About 120 calories per cup in Thai tables, or roughly 200 for a full restaurant bowl with no toppings.

foods.name: Jok
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of jok moo with egg is about 250 calories. Without the egg it is 160. The pa tong go on the side is what turns breakfast into 400. Breakdown inside.
foods.summary: Thai congee: rice broken down to a smooth porridge, with minced pork balls, a soft egg cracked in, ginger threads, spring onion, white pepper and a splash of soy. The 30 to 45 baht breakfast at every morning market, often with a pair of pa tong go for dipping.
foods.answer: A 400g bowl of jok moo sai kai (pork congee with egg) is about 250 calories, matching the Thai table figure of 250 per cup with egg. Without the egg it is about 160. The congee base is around 130 calories, the pork balls 55, the egg 70 and the toppings about 5. A pair of pa tong go on the side adds 124.
realTalk: Jok is even thinner than khao tom. The rice is cooked until it breaks apart completely, so a 300g ladle of congee only holds about 35g of dry rice, or roughly 130 calories. That is why a full bowl with pork and egg comes in at 250, lower than almost any other Thai breakfast. Jok moo without egg is 160 in the Thai tables, about the same as a cup of milk tea.

The pork is minced and rolled into small balls, about 35g per bowl and 55 calories. The egg cracked in adds 70 calories and 6g of protein, so a bowl with egg reaches about 14g of protein. That is not a lot, which is why jok stalls also sell kai yiao ma (century egg), pork liver and extra pork balls. Each extra portion of pork balls is 55 calories; a century egg is 80.

The number that matters is the pa tong go. Jok on its own is 250 calories. Jok with a pair of fried dough sticks is 375. Jok with two pairs, which is what many people actually eat, is 500 and half of it is fried flour. If you want the crunch, one pair is plenty. The other add on to watch is the drizzle of garlic oil at some shops, about 30 calories.
lighter: Skip the pa tong go, or take one pair (124 calories) instead of two.
Order jok with egg and extra pork balls rather than plain; the protein is what makes 250 calories hold you until lunch.
Ask for no garlic oil on top; it is about 30 calories that you will not miss under the ginger and pepper.
Add the century egg if you like it; 80 calories and 6g of protein is a fair trade.

components.name: Ginger, spring onion, pepper, soy sauce

portions.label: With egg, century egg and a pair of pa tong go

variants.name: Jok with pa tong go
variants.note: Plus one pair of fried dough

faq.q: Is jok healthy for breakfast?
faq.a: At 250 calories a bowl with egg and 14g of protein, it is one of the lighter Thai breakfasts. The pa tong go on the side is the part to limit; each pair is 124 calories.

faq.q: Jok vs khao tom, which is lower in calories?
faq.a: Jok. A bowl of jok with egg is about 250 against 300 for khao tom moo, because the congee is thinner and has less rice per bowl.

faq.q: How many calories in jok without pork?
faq.a: Plain jok is about 130 to 150 calories a bowl. Add an egg and it is around 200.

foods.source: hdmall.co.th and health.kapook.com Thai calorie tables: jok moo 1 cup = 160 kcal, jok sai kai (with egg) 1 cup = 250 kcal

foods.name: Sinangag
foods.metaDescription: One cup of sinangag (garlic fried rice) is about 300 calories, roughly 40 more than plain rice. Here is where the extra comes from and how to cut it.
foods.summary: Day-old rice fried in oil with a lot of crushed garlic and salt. It is the sin in tapsilog, longsilog and every other silog plate in the Philippines.
foods.answer: One cup of sinangag is about 300 calories for a 200g carinderia scoop. That is 260 calories from the rice itself and about 40 from the tablespoon of oil and the fried garlic. It is only a little more than plain steamed rice, but the oil adds up fast if the cook is generous.
realTalk: The rice is the whole story. A cup of cooked white rice is 200g and about 260 calories before anything touches it. Sinangag adds roughly 1 tablespoon of oil per cup, which is another 120 calories in the pan, but only part of that sticks to the rice. Kawaling Pinoy's recipe card puts it at 247 calories per cup with a quarter cup of oil across 4 cups of rice. A carinderia uses more oil than a home cook, so 300 is the fair number.

Where people go wrong is the second cup. Silog plates come with 1 cup, and an extra cup of sinangag is 20 to 25 pesos. That second scoop turns a 650 calorie tapsilog into a 950 calorie tapsilog, and the tapa did not change at all. The garlic and salt make it very easy to keep eating, which is the point of the dish and the problem with it.

The oil varies a lot by cook. Some carinderias fry the garlic in lard or in the fat left over from frying longganisa, which makes the rice taste better and pushes a cup closer to 350 calories. If the rice looks shiny and leaves a film on the plate, count it as 350, not 300.
lighter: Ask for plain rice instead of sinangag. You save about 40 to 90 calories per cup and the ulam still tastes the same.
Order half rice. A half cup of sinangag is about 150 calories and is plenty next to a fried egg and tapa.
If you make it at home, use 1 teaspoon of oil per cup instead of 1 tablespoon. That is 260 plus 40 instead of 260 plus 120.
Skip the extra scoop. The second cup is where a silog plate goes from lunch to two lunches.

variants.name: Sinangag fried in lard or longganisa fat

faq.q: Is sinangag higher in calories than plain rice?
faq.a: Yes, but not by much. A cup of plain rice is about 260 calories and a cup of sinangag is about 300. The difference is the oil and garlic. The problem is usually the portion, not the frying.

faq.q: How many calories in a silog plate?
faq.a: Between 550 and 750 depending on the ulam. Tapsilog is about 650, longsilog about 700. Sinangag is 300 of that and the fried egg is about 90.

faq.q: Can I eat sinangag while losing weight?
faq.a: Yes. Keep it to 1 cup, which is 300 calories, and pair it with a lean ulam like chicken inasal or tinola. The second cup is what breaks the budget.

faq.q: Is sinangag the same as fried rice?
faq.a: It is the plainest version of fried rice. No egg, no vegetables, no soy sauce, just garlic, oil and salt. That makes it lower in calories than Chinese fried rice, which is about 400 to 450 per cup.

foods.source: Kawaling Pinoy recipe card (247 kcal per cup), adjusted for carinderia oil; rice from USDA

foods.name: Chicken Inasal
foods.metaDescription: A leg quarter of chicken inasal is about 450 calories, and the annatto oil you pour on the rice is a big part of it. Numbers for paa, pecho and unli rice.
foods.summary: Chicken marinated in vinegar, calamansi, lemongrass and ginger, grilled over charcoal and basted with annatto oil. Bacolod's dish, now on every corner through Mang Inasal.
foods.answer: One leg quarter (paa) of chicken inasal is about 450 calories for a 250g bone-in piece. Around 370 of that is the grilled thigh and drumstick with skin, and the rest is the annatto oil basting and the sugar in the marinade. Add 1 cup of rice and the plate is about 710 calories.
realTalk: The chicken itself is not the issue. Grilled thigh and drumstick with skin is about 220 calories per 100g of edible meat, and a paa gives you around 170g of meat off the bone, so about 375 calories. What pushes inasal past a plain grilled chicken is the atsuete oil. It is chicken fat rendered with annatto seeds, brushed on during grilling and then served in a little dish for your rice. Kawaling Pinoy's recipe card lands at 450 calories per quarter and uses a full pound of chicken skin to make the oil.

The pour matters more than the piece. Each tablespoon of chicken oil over your rice is about 120 calories. Two tablespoons, which is what most people do without thinking, adds 240 calories to a plate that already has 260 calories of rice in it. The pecho (breast quarter) is a bit leaner at around 380 calories, but the difference is smaller than you would guess because the skin comes with it.

At Mang Inasal a paa with rice costs about 140 pesos and the unli rice is the trap. Every refill is another 260 calories. One paa, one cup of rice and a spoon of chicken oil is about 830 calories. One paa with three cups of rice and chicken oil on each is about 1,450. Same order slip, twice the calories.
lighter: Order the pecho instead of the paa and take the skin off. That drops the chicken portion to about 250 calories.
Skip the chicken oil dish or use 1 teaspoon instead of pouring. That alone saves 100 to 200 calories.
One cup of rice, not unli. Say it when you order so the refill never shows up.
Use the sinamak (spiced vinegar) and soy calamansi for flavour instead of the oil. Both are close to zero calories.

components.name: Grilled chicken leg quarter with skin (edible meat)

portions.label: Paa with 1 cup rice and 1 tbsp chicken oil

variants.name: Paa with rice, no chicken oil
Paa with unli rice (3 cups) and chicken oil

faq.q: How many calories in Mang Inasal paa with rice?
faq.a: About 710 calories for the paa plus 1 cup of rice, and around 830 if you pour a tablespoon of chicken oil on the rice. Mang Inasal does not publish nutrition facts, so this is built from the components.

faq.q: Is chicken inasal healthy?
faq.a: The chicken is. A paa gives you about 38g of protein and it is grilled, not fried. The chicken oil and the unli rice are what turn a 450 calorie piece into a 1,400 calorie meal.

faq.q: Paa or pecho, which is lower in calories?
faq.a: Pecho. The breast quarter with skin is about 380 calories versus 450 for the paa. Without skin the pecho drops to about 250.

faq.q: How many calories in the inasal chicken oil?
faq.a: About 120 calories per tablespoon. It is rendered chicken fat with annatto, so it is nearly pure fat. The little saucer they give you holds 2 to 3 tablespoons.

foods.source: Kawaling Pinoy recipe card (450 kcal per quarter); grilled chicken from USDA; Mang Inasal publishes no nutrition data

foods.name: Crispy Pata
foods.metaDescription: One share of crispy pata (a quarter of the leg) is about 560 calories, and a whole pata is over 2,200. Skin, fat and meat broken down.
foods.summary: A whole pork leg boiled until tender, dried, then deep fried until the skin blisters. Served with soy, vinegar and chili, and meant to be shared by 4 people.
foods.answer: A quarter share of crispy pata is about 560 calories for roughly 200g of skin, fat and meat. A whole pata as served in a restaurant is around 2,200 to 2,500 calories before the rice. The skin and the fat under it carry most of that, since crispy pork skin is close to 550 calories per 100g.
realTalk: Crispy pata is one of the few Filipino dishes where the skin is the main event, and pork skin fried until it shatters is about 550 calories per 100g. A whole front leg gives you around 800g of edible skin, fat and meat after frying, which is where the 2,200 plus figure comes from. Kawaling Pinoy's recipe card lands at 560 calories per serving when a leg is split 4 ways, and that matches what you get at a restaurant table.

The meat underneath is actually fine. Pork leg meat with the fat trimmed is about 180 calories per 100g, similar to a pork chop. The problem is that nobody eats it that way. A typical share is a piece of skin, the fat layer under it and the meat, and the ratio is roughly 30 percent skin, 30 percent fat, 40 percent meat. That is how 200g lands at 560 calories instead of 360.

A whole crispy pata costs 600 to 900 pesos in a restaurant and is usually eaten by 3 or 4 people with a platter of rice. Four people, one pata, one cup of rice each: about 820 calories per person. Two people finishing it, which happens, is about 1,100 calories each before rice. The soy-vinegar dip adds almost nothing, maybe 15 calories, so use as much as you like.
lighter: Take the meat and a small piece of skin, leave the fat layer. That alone cuts a 560 calorie share to about 380.
Share it 4 ways as intended. A whole pata between 2 people is 1,100 calories each before rice.
Order pata tim or paksiw na pata instead if you want the leg. The braised versions are about 400 per serving because nothing is deep fried.
Pair it with a vegetable dish like ensaladang talong or pinakbet instead of a second fried ulam.

portions.label: Meat only with a bit of skin

variants.name: Pata tim or paksiw na pata, 1 serving

faq.q: How many calories in a whole crispy pata?
faq.a: About 2,200 to 2,500 calories for a whole front leg after frying, with roughly 800g of edible skin, fat and meat. Split 4 ways that is about 560 each.

faq.q: Is crispy pata worse than lechon kawali?
faq.a: Per serving they are close. Lechon kawali is about 520 per serving and crispy pata about 560. Lechon kawali uses belly so it has a bit more fat per bite, but pata has more skin.

faq.q: How many calories in crispy pata skin?
faq.a: About 550 calories per 100g. A single piece of skin the size of your palm is about 30g, so around 165 calories.

faq.q: Can I eat crispy pata on a diet?
faq.a: As an occasional shared dish, yes. Stick to the meat, keep the skin to one piece and stop at 1 cup of rice, and you are around 500 calories for the meal.

foods.source: Kawaling Pinoy recipe card (560 kcal per quarter serving); pork skin and leg meat from USDA

foods.name: Liempo
foods.metaDescription: A carinderia serving of inihaw na liempo is about 600 calories for 150g of grilled pork belly. Why it is so high and what to order instead.
foods.summary: Pork belly slabs marinated in soy, calamansi, garlic and a little sugar, grilled over charcoal. The most ordered ulam at any ihaw-ihaw stall.
foods.answer: One serving of inihaw na liempo is about 600 calories for a 150g grilled slab. Pork belly is roughly half fat by weight, and even after some drips into the coals, cooked belly sits near 400 calories per 100g. Add 1 cup of rice and the plate is about 860.
realTalk: Pork belly is the fattiest cut most people eat, and grilling does not fix that. Raw belly is about 50 percent fat. On the grill maybe a fifth of that renders out and drips away, which leaves cooked liempo around 400 calories per 100g. A 150g serving, which is one decent slab or 5 to 6 slices, is 600 calories. Kawaling Pinoy's recipe card goes even higher at 830 per serving because it counts the whole marinade.

The marinade adds less than people think. Soy sauce, calamansi, garlic and 2 tablespoons of brown sugar across 2 pounds of pork works out to maybe 20 calories per serving that actually clings to the meat. The banana ketchup glaze some stalls brush on adds another 20 to 30. The calories are in the pork, full stop.

The cheap fix nobody takes is asking for the leaner slab. Belly from closer to the ribs has more meat and less fat, and a 150g piece can be 450 calories instead of 600. At a stall the fatty pieces are the ones that look striped white. A liempo meal with rice at a carinderia runs 100 to 150 pesos and about 860 calories, which is more than a Chickenjoy meal.
lighter: Pick the slab with more pink than white. A leaner belly piece is about 450 calories instead of 600.
Order pork chop or pork kasim (shoulder) grilled the same way. Same marinade, about 300 calories per 150g.
Trim the top fat cap off before eating. That cap alone is about 100 to 150 calories on a standard slab.
Keep rice to 1 cup and load up on the ensaladang kamatis or atchara on the side.

variants.name: Liempo with rice and chicken oil
variants.note: Inasal-style chicken oil on the rice

faq.q: How many calories in liempo with rice?
faq.a: About 860 calories for a 150g grilled slab and 1 cup of rice. Add a second cup of rice and it is around 1,120.

faq.q: Is grilled liempo healthier than lechon kawali?
faq.a: A little. Grilling lets some fat drip off, so 150g of inihaw na liempo is about 600 calories versus about 520 for a smaller 120g serving of lechon kawali. Gram for gram they are close, since both are belly.

faq.q: How many calories in one slice of liempo?
faq.a: About 100 calories per slice if the slab is cut into 6 pieces of roughly 25g each. Three slices is a 300 calorie ulam.

faq.q: What is the leanest inihaw at the stall?
faq.a: Chicken inasal pecho without skin at about 250 calories, then grilled pork kasim at about 300 per 150g, then liempo at 600.

foods.source: estimate from components (USDA pork belly, cooked, with grill fat loss); Kawaling Pinoy recipe card 830 kcal per serving noted as the high end

foods.name: Bicol Express
aka: Pork in Coconut Milk with Chili
foods.metaDescription: A carinderia scoop of Bicol Express is about 520 calories. Pork belly plus coconut cream is the reason, and here is how much each part adds.
foods.summary: Pork belly simmered in coconut milk and coconut cream with shrimp paste and a lot of green and red chili. From Bicol, sold everywhere, always eaten with too much rice.
foods.answer: One carinderia serving of Bicol Express is about 520 calories for a 180g ladle of pork and sauce. The pork belly is about 330 of that and the coconut milk sauce about 180. It is one of the highest calorie ulam per scoop because both main ingredients are mostly fat.
realTalk: Two fatty ingredients in one pot. Pork belly is about 50 percent fat and coconut cream is about 35 percent fat, so there is nothing lean to dilute anything. A 180g carinderia ladle usually holds about 70g of cooked belly (around 330 calories) and 100g of coconut sauce (around 180 calories). The chilies, garlic and bagoong add maybe 10. Home recipes are far worse: Kawaling Pinoy's version works out to 1,100 calories per serving because it uses 2 pounds of belly and both coconut milk and cream for 6 people.

The sauce is the sneaky part. People eat the pork, then spoon the sauce over rice, then ask for more sauce. Each extra ladle of coconut sauce is about 90 calories, and it soaks straight into the rice so it does not feel like eating anything. A 60 to 80 peso serving with 1 cup of rice is about 780 calories, and with the extra sauce habit it is closer to 900.

The chili does not burn any of it off. Capsaicin raises your metabolism by a rounding error, maybe 10 calories over the day. What the chili actually does is make you eat more rice to cool down, which is the opposite of helping. If you want Bicol Express to fit, the lever is the cut of pork, not the heat.
lighter: Order the version made with kasim (shoulder) or chicken if the carinderia has it. Chicken Bicol Express is about 300 per serving.
Take the pork, leave most of the sauce in the tray. That is about 350 calories instead of 520.
Ask for it with the gata (coconut milk) only, no kakang gata (cream). About 80 calories less per scoop.
One cup of rice. The sauce makes rice disappear, so decide the amount before you start.

variants.name: Chicken Bicol Express
variants.note: Breast or thigh instead of belly

variants.name: Home style, coconut milk plus cream
variants.note: Kawaling Pinoy recipe card, 1 of 6 servings

faq.q: Is Bicol Express fattening?
faq.a: It is one of the highest calorie Filipino ulam by weight, about 290 calories per 100g. A single carinderia scoop is 520 calories, roughly the same as a Jollibee Chickenjoy with rice.

faq.q: How many calories in Bicol Express with rice?
faq.a: About 780 calories for a standard scoop with 1 cup of rice. With 2 cups of rice it is around 1,040.

faq.q: Is Bicol Express keto?
faq.a: Technically it is low carb at about 6g per serving, but it is 520 calories of mostly saturated fat. Low carb does not mean low calorie.

faq.q: What is the difference between Bicol Express and laing?
faq.a: Same coconut milk base, but laing is built on taro leaves with a little pork, so a serving is about 350 calories versus 520 for Bicol Express, which is built on pork belly.

foods.source: estimate from components; Kawaling Pinoy (1102 kcal) and Panlasang Pinoy (1224 kcal) recipe cards used as home-portion reference

foods.name: Pork BBQ
foods.metaDescription: One stick of Filipino pork BBQ is about 130 calories. The sweet glaze and the fat in the pork are the two things that decide the number.
foods.summary: Thin slices of pork marinated in soy, banana ketchup, calamansi, brown sugar and 7-Up, threaded on a stick and grilled over charcoal. Sold from street carts for 20 to 40 pesos.
foods.answer: One standard street stick of pork BBQ is about 130 calories for roughly 45g of grilled pork with its sweet glaze. About 100 calories is the pork and 30 is the sugar in the marinade and basting sauce. Three sticks with 1 cup of rice is about 650 calories.
realTalk: Pork BBQ is fairly reasonable per stick. Most vendors use kasim (shoulder) with a bit of fat, which grills to about 220 calories per 100g, so a 40 to 45g stick is around 100 calories of meat. The marinade is where the sugar lives: brown sugar, banana ketchup and 7-Up, then a basting sauce with more of the same. About 8g of sugar sticks to each skewer, which is 30 calories. Kawaling Pinoy's recipe card shows 175 per stick, but that counts a full 3 cups of brown sugar across 50 skewers as if all of it ended up on the meat.

The stick size is the real variable. A 20 peso street stick is thin, maybe 35g, and lands near 100 calories. The fat 40 peso sticks outside a restaurant can be 80g of pork with visible fat chunks between the slices, and those are 230 to 250 calories each. Ask yourself whether it is 3 bites or 6 bites and you have your answer.

Nobody eats one. The normal order is 3 to 5 sticks with rice, and vendors sell them in a pile for a reason. Five standard sticks is 650 calories before rice. With 1 cup of rice that is 910 calories, and the sweet glaze makes rice go down fast. Compared to a 150g slab of liempo at 600 calories, BBQ is actually the leaner ihaw choice if you stop at 3 sticks.
lighter: Three sticks, 1 cup rice, about 650 calories. That is a real meal and easy to remember.
Pick the sticks with less white fat between the slices. A lean stick is closer to 100 calories.
Skip the extra basting. Ask for it without the last brush of sauce and save about 15 calories per stick.
Chicken BBQ sticks are about 90 calories each if the vendor has them.

components.name: Grilled pork shoulder with some fat
Brown sugar and banana ketchup glaze

variants.name: Stick with extra basting and fat cubes

faq.q: How many calories in 5 sticks of pork BBQ?
faq.a: About 650 calories for 5 standard street sticks, or around 1,200 for 5 jumbo sticks. With rice add 260 per cup.

faq.q: Is pork BBQ healthy?
faq.a: Per stick it is fine: about 9g of protein for 130 calories. The problems are the sugar glaze (about 8g per stick) and the habit of eating 5 with 2 cups of rice.

faq.q: How much sugar is in pork BBQ?
faq.a: About 8g per stick from the brown sugar, banana ketchup and 7-Up in the marinade and basting sauce. Five sticks is 40g of sugar, roughly a can of soft drink.

faq.q: Pork BBQ or liempo, which is lower in calories?
faq.a: Pork BBQ. Three sticks is about 390 calories, while a standard 150g liempo slab is about 600, because BBQ uses shoulder and liempo uses belly.

foods.source: estimate from components (USDA pork shoulder, grilled); Kawaling Pinoy recipe card 175 kcal per skewer noted

foods.name: Kwek-Kwek
foods.metaDescription: Four pieces of kwek-kwek with sweet sauce are about 280 calories, roughly 65 per egg. The orange batter and the frying oil matter more than the quail egg.
foods.summary: Hard boiled quail eggs dipped in an orange annatto flour batter and deep fried, served with a sweet chili vinegar sauce. The 5 peso street snack outside every school.
foods.answer: Four pieces of kwek-kwek are about 280 calories including a spoon of the sweet sauce, or roughly 65 calories per piece. The quail egg itself is only 14 calories. The rest is about 35 calories of flour batter and 15 to 20 calories of oil absorbed in the fryer.
realTalk: The egg is the smallest part. A quail egg is about 9g and 14 calories, which is nothing. Then it gets a thick coat of flour and cornstarch batter, about 10g dry per egg, and goes into oil that has been reused since morning. The batter soaks up 3 to 4g of oil per piece. That turns a 14 calorie egg into a 65 calorie ball. Kawaling Pinoy's recipe card comes out at 275 for 3 pieces, but it counts the whole pot of frying oil across the batch, which overstates it.

The sauce is sugar. The sweet kwek-kwek sauce is vinegar, brown sugar, cornstarch and chili, and a good ladle over 4 pieces is about 30 calories. The spicy vinegar version (sukang maanghang) is closer to 5. Most vendors let you choose, and the spicy vinegar is the one to pick if you are counting.

At 5 pesos a piece it is easy to eat 8 or 10 while waiting for a jeep. Ten pieces is 650 calories, which is a full meal from something that felt like a snack. The tokneneng version made with a chicken egg is bigger, about 150 calories each, because the batter shell is thicker and there is more egg.
lighter: Four pieces is a snack at 280 calories. Ten pieces is lunch at 650. Decide before you order.
Choose the spicy vinegar dip instead of the sweet orange sauce. About 25 calories saved per serving.
Pick the pieces with the thinner batter shell. A thin coat is about 50 calories per piece instead of 65.
If you want eggs for protein, plain boiled quail eggs are 14 each. Ten of them is 140 calories, the same as 2 kwek-kwek.

variants.name: Tokneneng, 1 piece
variants.note: Chicken egg in the same batter

faq.q: How many calories in one kwek-kwek?
faq.a: About 65 calories per piece with a standard batter coat, plus about 7 calories per piece for the sweet sauce.

faq.q: Is kwek-kwek healthy?
faq.a: The quail egg is, at 14 calories and 1g of protein. The batter and reused frying oil are not. Four pieces is a 280 calorie snack with 18g of fat, most of it from the fryer.

faq.q: Kwek-kwek or tokneneng, which has more calories?
faq.a: Tokneneng, at about 150 per piece, because it is a whole chicken egg in a thicker batter. One tokneneng is roughly 2.5 kwek-kwek.

faq.q: How many calories in the kwek-kwek sauce?
faq.a: The sweet orange sauce is about 30 calories per ladle from sugar and cornstarch. The spicy vinegar is about 5.

foods.source: estimate from components (quail egg USDA 14 kcal, batter and oil uptake); Kawaling Pinoy recipe card 275 kcal per 3 pieces noted

foods.name: Leche Flan
foods.metaDescription: A slice of leche flan is about 240 calories. Egg yolks and condensed milk are the whole recipe, so here is how a llanera splits up.
foods.summary: A dense custard of egg yolks, condensed milk and evaporated milk steamed over a layer of caramelised sugar. Richer than any Western flan because there are no egg whites in it.
foods.answer: One slice of leche flan is about 240 calories for a 90g piece, which is one llanera cut into 4 or 5. Condensed milk supplies most of the sugar and the egg yolks most of the fat. A whole standard llanera is around 1,000 calories.
realTalk: Leche flan is condensed milk you can cut with a spoon. A standard recipe is 10 to 12 egg yolks, a 14 oz can of condensed milk and a 12 oz can of evaporated milk, plus about half a cup of sugar for the caramel. That is about 2,900 calories in the mixing bowl, poured into 2 or 3 llaneras. Kawaling Pinoy's card puts a 1 of 12 portion at 239 calories, and Goldilocks lists their baked flan at 190 per slice, which is a thinner cut.

The yolks are why it hits harder than it looks. Each yolk is about 55 calories and 4.5g of fat, and there are no whites to lighten the mix. Per 100g leche flan is about 265 calories, which is denser than ice cream (about 200 per 100g) and about the same as a slice of cake. A 90g slice does not look like much on the plate, which is how a second slice happens.

At fiestas and buffets it is not really a slice. It is a spoonful on top of halo-halo (about 60 calories for the flan alone), then a real slice later, then a bit more when the tray comes around. Two slices of leche flan is 480 calories, more than the ulam you had for dinner. A slice at a carinderia or bakery is 40 to 60 pesos.
lighter: Cut the llanera into 6 instead of 4. A 60g slice is about 160 calories and still feels like dessert.
Have it as the dessert, not as a topping and a dessert. The flan on your halo-halo already counted.
At home, swap half the condensed milk for evaporated milk and use 8 yolks instead of 12. That drops a slice to about 170.
Eat it after a protein heavy meal, not with merienda coffee, so it does not become a 500 calorie snack.

variants.name: Leche flan, 1 of 6 from a full recipe

faq.q: How many calories in a whole leche flan?
faq.a: About 1,000 calories for one standard llanera (about 380g). A big oval llanera can reach 1,400.

faq.q: Is leche flan high in sugar?
faq.a: Yes. A 90g slice has about 30g of sugar, most of it from the condensed milk and the caramel layer. That is close to a can of soft drink.

faq.q: Leche flan or halo-halo, which is worse?
faq.a: Halo-halo, at about 450 calories per tall glass, versus 240 for a slice of flan. But halo-halo usually has a spoon of flan in it too.

faq.q: Can leche flan be made lower in calories?
faq.a: Somewhat. Using fewer yolks and swapping some condensed milk for evaporated milk gets a slice down to about 170 calories, but it will be softer and less rich.

foods.source: Kawaling Pinoy recipe card (239 kcal per 1/12); Goldilocks baked flan 190 kcal per slice via FatSecret

foods.name: Taho
foods.metaDescription: A regular cup of taho is about 220 calories, and 150 of that is the arnibal syrup. Numbers for small, large and the strawberry version.
foods.summary: Warm silken tofu ladled into a cup with brown sugar syrup (arnibal) and sago pearls, sold from two metal buckets by the magtataho walking past your house at 7 in the morning.
foods.answer: A regular cup of taho is about 220 calories for a 250g serving. The soft tofu is only about 80 calories, the sago pearls about 30, and the arnibal syrup about 110. The syrup is the whole difference between a healthy breakfast and a sugary one.
realTalk: The tofu part is genuinely good for you. Silken tofu is about 55 calories per 100g with 5g of protein, so the 150g in a regular cup is 80 calories and 7g of protein. Kawaling Pinoy's recipe card comes out at 213 calories per serving, which matches a vendor cup. The rest is arnibal: brown sugar boiled into a syrup. A vendor ladles in about 40g of it, which is 110 calories of straight sugar.

Ask for 'konting arnibal' (less syrup) and the cup drops to about 150 calories. Most magtataho will do it without blinking. The sago is minor at about 30 calories for a spoonful, though it is also just starch. A large cup at 30 to 35 pesos is about 350 calories, because the vendor scales the syrup with the tofu.

The strawberry taho from Baguio is a different animal. The strawberry syrup is sugar with fruit flavour and they tend to pour more of it, so a regular cup is closer to 260 calories. Same for the ube and pandan versions at mall stalls, which also add condensed milk. Taho is a 20 peso breakfast that is fine at 220 calories. It is not fine as a 350 calorie large on top of pandesal and coffee.
lighter: Say 'konting arnibal' and save about 60 calories. Half the syrup, same tofu.
Regular cup, not large. The large is 350 calories, and the extra is mostly syrup.
Skip the sago if you do not care about it. About 30 calories saved and nothing lost.
Make it your protein for the morning instead of an extra: taho plus 1 pandesal is about 330 calories.

variants.name: Ube or pandan taho with condensed milk

faq.q: Is taho healthy?
faq.a: The tofu is, with about 7g of protein per cup. The arnibal is 110 calories of sugar. Ask for less syrup and it becomes a decent 150 calorie breakfast.

faq.q: How many calories in taho without syrup?
faq.a: About 110 calories for the tofu and sago alone. Plain silken tofu is 55 calories per 100g.

faq.q: How much sugar is in a cup of taho?
faq.a: About 28 to 30g in a regular cup, nearly all from the arnibal. A large cup is closer to 45g.

faq.q: Is taho good for weight loss?
faq.a: It works as a breakfast if it replaces something, not if it is added on top. A regular cup with less syrup is 150 calories and keeps you full for a couple of hours.

foods.source: Kawaling Pinoy recipe card (213 kcal per serving); silken tofu from USDA

foods.name: Arroz Caldo
foods.metaDescription: A carinderia bowl of arroz caldo is about 400 calories with the chicken and half an egg. Where the toasted garlic and chicken oil push it, and how to cut it.
foods.summary: Rice porridge cooked with ginger, garlic, chicken pieces and safflower, topped with toasted garlic, spring onion, a boiled egg and calamansi. What you eat when it rains or when you are sick.
foods.answer: One carinderia bowl of arroz caldo is about 400 calories for a 350g serving with a piece of chicken and half a boiled egg. The porridge itself is around 200 calories, the chicken 120, the egg 35 and the toasted garlic in oil about 45. A plain lugaw bowl without chicken is closer to 220.
realTalk: Porridge stretches a little rice a long way. A 350g bowl of arroz caldo has only about 60g of dry rice in it, cooked in 5 times its weight of broth, so the rice contributes about 200 calories. That is less than a cup of plain rice. The chicken piece, usually a thigh or a chunk of breast with skin, adds 100 to 150. Kawaling Pinoy's recipe card lands at 572 per serving because it splits a whole chicken 6 ways, which is a much bigger piece than a carinderia gives you.

The toppings are where the oil hides. Toasted garlic is fried in oil and spooned on with some of that oil, about 45 calories. Some places also drizzle chicken fat or use the annatto oil from inasal, which adds 60 more. A whole boiled egg instead of half is another 35. A fully loaded bowl with a big thigh, whole egg and extra oil is about 550 calories, still a reasonable meal.

The calamansi and patis are free, so use them. A bowl costs 50 to 70 pesos at a carinderia and 90 to 130 at a Goto King or a mall stall, and the mall versions come with more chicken and often a side of tokwa't baboy, which is another 250. As comfort food goes, arroz caldo is one of the better deals: warm, filling, about 20g of protein and under 400 calories if you keep it simple.
lighter: Ask for breast instead of thigh and pull the skin off. About 60 calories less per bowl.
Go light on the toasted garlic oil, or ask for the garlic without the oil. Saves about 30 to 40.
Skip the chicharon topping that some stalls add. A small handful is 100 calories of fried pork skin.
Add more ginger, calamansi and patis for flavour. All of them are close to zero.

components.name: Toasted garlic in oil, spring onion

portions.label: Standard bowl with chicken and half egg
Large bowl with big thigh and whole egg

variants.name: Goto (with beef tripe)
variants.note: Tripe is lean, about the same

variants.name: Arroz caldo with tokwa't baboy on the side

faq.q: Is arroz caldo good for weight loss?
faq.a: Yes, it is one of the better carinderia bowls. About 400 calories with 20g of protein and a lot of water, so it fills you up. Keep the garlic oil and chicharon topping in check.

faq.q: What is the difference between arroz caldo, lugaw and goto?
faq.a: Same porridge base. Lugaw is plain (about 220 calories), arroz caldo has chicken (about 400), goto has beef tripe (about 380).

faq.q: How many calories in a bowl of arroz caldo without egg?
faq.a: About 365 calories. The half egg is only 35, so it is not the thing to skip. The garlic oil and chicken skin are bigger.

faq.q: Is arroz caldo high in carbs?
faq.a: About 45g per bowl, which is less than a single cup of rice (55g) because the rice is diluted with broth.

foods.source: estimate from components; Kawaling Pinoy recipe card (572 kcal per 1/6 of a whole chicken) used as the high end

foods.name: Laing
foods.metaDescription: A carinderia serving of laing is about 350 calories. The taro leaves are nearly free, so the number is all coconut milk and pork. Here is the split.
foods.summary: Dried taro leaves cooked down slowly in coconut milk with chili, ginger, shrimp paste and bits of pork or dried fish. Bicol's vegetable dish, and the reason 'gulay' is not always low calorie.
foods.answer: One carinderia serving of laing is about 350 calories for a 150g scoop. The dried taro leaves are about 30 calories, the coconut milk around 200 and the pork belly bits about 110. It is a vegetable dish by name, but by calories it is a coconut dish.
realTalk: Laing is a lesson in what 'vegetable' means at a carinderia. Dried gabi leaves are light and absorb liquid, so 10g of dried leaves swells to a big serving in the pot. Those leaves are about 30 calories. The coconut milk they soak up is the problem: about 100ml per serving at 200 calories, and some cooks finish with coconut cream on top. Kawaling Pinoy's home recipe card comes to 927 per serving, but that uses a full pound of belly and 5 cups of coconut for 6 people.

The pork is the second lever. Carinderia laing usually has small belly pieces or a few flakes of tinapa or dried dilis for flavour. About 30g of belly is 110 calories. The dried fish version is about 40 calories for the same weight, so laing na may daing is closer to 280 per serving. Ask which one it is, because they look the same under the coconut.

The saving grace is that laing is eaten in small amounts. A 40 to 60 peso scoop with 1 cup of rice is about 610 calories, which is a normal lunch. The trouble is when laing is the side to another coconut dish like Bicol Express, and you end up with 870 calories of ulam before the rice. One gata dish per plate is the rule.
lighter: Ask for the version with dried fish instead of pork belly. About 70 calories less per serving.
Take it as your only coconut dish. Laing plus Bicol Express plus rice is about 1,130 calories on one plate.
At home, use light coconut milk or half milk half water. The leaves still cook down fine at about 200 per serving.
Pair it with a grilled protein like inasal or bangus rather than another rich ulam.

variants.name: Laing with dried fish, light coconut milk
Laing with dried fish (daing or tinapa)

faq.q: Is laing healthy?
faq.a: The taro leaves are, with fibre, iron and vitamin A. But a serving is 350 calories and 31g of fat from the coconut milk, so treat it like a rich ulam, not a salad.

faq.q: How many calories in laing with rice?
faq.a: About 610 calories for a standard scoop with 1 cup of rice. With 2 cups it is about 870.

faq.q: Is laing keto?
faq.a: It is low carb at about 10g per serving and high in fat, so it fits keto macros. It is still 350 calories, so it is not a free food.

faq.q: Why does laing make your throat itch?
faq.a: Undercooked taro leaves contain calcium oxalate crystals. Cooking them a long time in coconut milk without stirring breaks it down, which is why laing simmers for an hour. Nothing to do with calories, but everyone asks.

foods.source: estimate from components; Kawaling Pinoy (927 kcal) and Panlasang Pinoy (618 kcal) recipe cards used as home-portion reference

foods.name: Pinakbet
foods.metaDescription: A carinderia serving of pinakbet is about 230 calories. The vegetables are 60 of that; the pork belly and bagoong oil are the rest. Ilocano vs Tagalog.
foods.summary: Squash, ampalaya, eggplant, okra and sitaw stewed with shrimp paste and pieces of pork belly or bagnet. The Ilocano vegetable dish that every region has its own version of.
foods.answer: One carinderia serving of pinakbet is about 230 calories for a 180g scoop. The mixed vegetables are only about 60 calories, the pork belly pieces about 130 and the bagoong and cooking oil about 40. FatSecret lists a leaner cup at 152 calories.
realTalk: Pinakbet is one of the better ulam choices, but the pork decides it. Squash, ampalaya, eggplant, okra and sitaw together are about 40 calories per 100g, so the 130g of vegetables in a scoop is 60 calories. Then the cook adds pork belly for flavour, about 30g per serving at 130 calories, and a tablespoon of oil to fry the bagoong. Kawaling Pinoy's Tagalog version comes to 434 per serving with half a pound of belly for 4 people, which is a very pork heavy home portion.

The Ilocano version with bagnet on top is a different number. Bagnet is deep fried pork belly, about 500 calories per 100g, and a proper Ilocano pinakbet has a handful of it crumbled over the top. That pushes a serving to 350 or more. The Tagalog version with kalabasa and a little belly is the 230 calorie one, and the carinderia version with mostly vegetables and a few pork scraps can be as low as 170.

At 40 to 50 pesos a scoop it is the cheapest way to fill half your plate. Pinakbet with 1 cup of rice is about 490 calories, and the fibre from the ampalaya and okra makes it more filling than the number suggests. The bagoong is salty rather than caloric, about 15 calories per tablespoon, so the taste does not cost much.
lighter: Ask for it without the bagnet or with the pork on the side. Vegetables and bagoong alone are about 110 calories per scoop.
Scoop from the vegetable side of the tray, not where the pork settled at the bottom.
Use pinakbet as your vegetable next to a lean protein like inasal or grilled bangus. Together with rice that is about 800 for a full plate.
At home, use shrimp instead of pork belly. Same bagoong flavour at about 150 per serving.

components.name: Mixed vegetables (squash, ampalaya, eggplant, okra, sitaw)

variants.name: Home style, 1 of 4 servings
variants.note: Kawaling Pinoy card, half a pound of belly

faq.q: Is pinakbet good for weight loss?
faq.a: Yes, as far as carinderia ulam goes. About 230 calories for a scoop with pork, and about 110 without. High fibre, decent protein, and it makes rice go slower.

faq.q: How many calories in pinakbet with bagnet?
faq.a: About 360 per serving. Bagnet is deep fried belly at about 500 calories per 100g, and a serving gets 25 to 30g of it.

faq.q: Is pinakbet high in sodium?
faq.a: Yes, from the bagoong. A serving can carry 800 to 1,000mg of sodium. Calories are low but it is a salty dish.

faq.q: Pinakbet or laing, which is lower in calories?
faq.a: Pinakbet, at about 230 versus 350 for laing. Pinakbet has no coconut milk, which is what makes laing heavy.

foods.source: estimate from components; FatSecret generic pinakbet 152 kcal per cup; Kawaling Pinoy recipe card 434 kcal per serving

foods.name: Dinuguan
foods.metaDescription: A carinderia serving of dinuguan is about 330 calories, and the pork cut is what moves it. Numbers for belly, kasim and offal versions, with and without puto.
foods.summary: Pork (meat, offal or both) stewed in pig's blood with vinegar, garlic, onion and a long green chili. Dark, sour, savoury, and usually eaten with puto or rice.
foods.answer: One carinderia serving of dinuguan is about 330 calories for a 180g ladle. The pork pieces are about 250 of that and the blood gravy about 80. Red Ribbon's version is listed on FatSecret at 255 per cup, and versions made with pork belly go over 450.
realTalk: Pig's blood is not the problem. Cooked blood is about 80 calories per 100g and mostly protein and iron, which surprises people. What decides dinuguan is the pork that goes in. Carinderias use a mix of kasim (shoulder), a bit of belly and offal like intestine and liver, which averages about 300 calories per 100g cooked. An 80g share of that is 250 calories. Kawaling Pinoy's belly-only recipe card lands at 857 per serving, and that is the home version with 2 pounds of belly for 6 people.

Red Ribbon and Goldilocks sell it as a takeout tub, and Red Ribbon's is listed at 255 calories per cup with 34g of protein. That is leaner than most carinderias because they use more lean meat and less fat. The Ilocano dinardaraan is the opposite: drier, fattier, often with bagnet and chicharon crumbled in, and a serving is 450 to 500.

The puto is the part everyone forgets. Dinuguan at merienda comes with 2 or 3 puto, and each small puto is about 40 calories. Three puto is 120, so dinuguan with puto is about 450. With 1 cup of rice instead it is about 590. At 50 to 70 pesos a serving it is a high protein ulam at about 22g, so the calorie return is decent if the cook did not use belly.
lighter: Ask if it is kasim or liempo. Kasim dinuguan is about 280 per serving, liempo dinuguan about 450.
Take the meat and half the gravy. The gravy is about 80 calories per serving and you do not need all of it.
Two puto instead of three, or half a cup of rice. That is 80 to 130 calories saved.
Skip the chicharon topping that some stalls add. A small handful is 100 calories.

faq.q: Is dinuguan healthy?
faq.a: It is high in protein (about 22g per serving) and iron from the blood. Calories depend on the pork cut: 280 with shoulder, 450 with belly. Sodium is also high from the vinegar and patis.

faq.q: How many calories in dinuguan with puto?
faq.a: About 450 calories for a standard serving with 3 small puto. Each puto adds about 40.

faq.q: How many calories in pig's blood?
faq.a: About 80 calories per 100g cooked, almost all protein. It is the pork fat, not the blood, that makes dinuguan heavy.

faq.q: Is dinuguan high in cholesterol?
faq.a: Yes. Blood and offal push a serving to around 150 to 200mg of cholesterol, more if there is liver. If that matters for you, keep it to once a week.

foods.source: estimate from components; FatSecret Red Ribbon dinuguan 255 kcal per cup; Kawaling Pinoy belly recipe card 857 kcal noted as the high end

foods.name: Caldereta
foods.metaDescription: A carinderia serving of beef caldereta is about 390 calories. The liver spread and cheese in the sauce add more than the potatoes do. Beef, goat and pork.
foods.summary: Beef (or goat) braised in tomato sauce with liver spread, bell peppers, potatoes, carrots, olives and often cheese. The fiesta stew that shows up at every handaan and most carinderias.
foods.answer: One carinderia serving of beef caldereta is about 390 calories for a 200g ladle with meat, vegetables and sauce. The beef is about 230 calories, the sauce with liver spread and cheese about 120, and the potato and carrot pieces about 40. Kawaling Pinoy's home version is 448 per serving.
realTalk: Caldereta looks like a tomato stew but the sauce is richer than tomato. The base is tomato sauce plus a can of liver spread (about 60 calories per tablespoon) plus, in most Tagalog versions, a handful of grated cheese and sometimes peanut butter. About 80g of sauce per serving is 120 calories. The beef is usually brisket or shank with some fat, about 90g cooked per scoop at 230 calories. Kawaling Pinoy's card with bottom round lands at 448 per serving; Panlasang Pinoy's with short ribs hits 610.

The cut of beef swings it by 150 calories. Shank or round is about 200 calories per 100g cooked, short ribs or brisket with fat closer to 350. Carinderias tend to use whatever is cheap, which is usually fattier. Goat caldereta (kalderetang kambing) is a bit leaner at about 340 per serving, and the pork version made with belly is the heaviest at about 480.

A serving costs 70 to 100 pesos, more than most ulam, so people do not double up on it. With 1 cup of rice it is about 650 calories, which is a normal lunch. The potato and carrot in the sauce count for something: a serving gets about 40g of them at 40 calories. The olives and bell pepper are close to zero, so they are the parts you can eat freely.
lighter: Ask for more sauce vegetables and less meat if the cut is fatty. Potato, carrot and bell pepper are about 1 calorie per gram.
Skim the orange oil that pools on top. That layer is rendered beef fat and about 50 to 80 calories per serving.
Goat caldereta is leaner than beef if the carinderia has it, about 340 per serving.
One cup of rice. The sauce is thick enough that half a cup goes a long way.

components.name: Tomato sauce with liver spread and cheese

faq.q: How many calories in caldereta with rice?
faq.a: About 650 calories for a standard 200g serving with 1 cup of rice. With 2 cups it is around 910.

faq.q: Is caldereta healthy?
faq.a: It has about 28g of protein per serving and some vegetables, but the liver spread and cheese make the sauce about 120 calories per ladle. Moderate, not light.

faq.q: What makes caldereta different from mechado and afritada?
faq.a: The liver spread and cheese. Afritada is plain tomato sauce, about 300 per serving. Mechado adds soy and a fat strip through the beef, about 350. Caldereta is the richest at about 390.

faq.q: Beef or goat caldereta, which is lower in calories?
