faq.a: Goat, at about 340 per serving versus 390 for beef. Goat meat is about 140 calories per 100g cooked, beef with fat closer to 250.

foods.source: estimate from components; Kawaling Pinoy recipe card 448 kcal per serving; Panlasang Pinoy 610 kcal (short ribs) as high end

foods.name: Jollibee Chickenjoy
foods.metaDescription: A 1-pc Chickenjoy with rice and gravy is about 600 calories. Thigh is 380, drumstick 220, so the piece you get matters. Solo and 2-pc numbers too.
foods.summary: Jollibee's fried chicken, brined and pressure fried, served with a cup of steamed rice and a small tub of gravy. The most ordered meal in the Philippines.
foods.answer: A 1-pc Chickenjoy with rice and gravy is about 600 calories. The chicken piece averages 300 calories (a thigh is listed at 380, a drumstick at 220, a breast at 320), the cup of rice is 260 and the gravy about 40. A 2-pc meal is close to 900.
realTalk: Jollibee does not put a full nutrition table on its Philippine site, but per-piece figures from their US listings are on FatSecret: thigh 380, breast 320, drumstick 220, spicy drumstick 200. The piece you get is random, so 300 is a fair average. The skin and coating are about half of that. A skinless piece of the same chicken would be around 170, but nobody buys Chickenjoy to peel it.

The rice is a full cup at about 260 calories, and the gravy tub is around 40, mostly flour and chicken fat. So the meal is 600 give or take 80 depending on the piece. The 2-pc Chickenjoy with rice, which is what most adults order, is about 900. Add a regular Coke (about 140) and the peach mango pie (270 on FatSecret) and lunch is 1,300 calories for about 250 pesos.

For a fast food meal it is not the worst. A 1-pc meal gives you about 30g of protein for 600 calories, better than a Jolly Spaghetti at 560 with 15g. The gravy habit is what adds up: people ask for 2 or 3 extra tubs and pour them all over the rice, which is another 80 to 120 calories that does not register as food.
lighter: Hope for a drumstick, or ask. A drumstick meal is about 520 versus 680 for a thigh meal.
One gravy tub, not three. Each extra tub is about 40 calories of flour and fat.
Skip the drink or get water. A regular Coke adds 140 and the pineapple juice about 120.
Peel the skin off half the piece. That alone saves about 80 calories and the meat is still juicy.

components.name: Chickenjoy piece (average of thigh, breast, drumstick)

variants.name: 1-pc meal with regular Coke and peach mango pie

faq.q: How many calories in 2-pc Chickenjoy with rice?
faq.a: About 900 calories: two pieces averaging 300 each, 1 cup of rice at 260 and a gravy tub at 40. With a Coke it is about 1,040.

faq.q: How many calories in Chickenjoy without rice?
faq.a: About 300 per piece on average. A thigh is 380, a breast 320, a drumstick 220 according to the FatSecret Jollibee entries.

faq.q: Is Chickenjoy healthier than KFC?
faq.a: About the same. A KFC Original Recipe thigh is about 280 and a Chickenjoy thigh 380, but Chickenjoy pieces are larger. Per gram they are close.

faq.q: How many calories in Jollibee gravy?
faq.a: About 40 calories per small tub, from flour, oil and chicken drippings. Three tubs over rice is 120.

foods.source: FatSecret Jollibee entries (thigh 380, breast 320, drumstick 220 kcal); rice and gravy from components

foods.name: Jollibee Spaghetti
foods.metaDescription: A regular Jolly Spaghetti is about 560 calories, most of it from the sweet sauce and the noodles. Numbers for the solo, family pan and Chickenjoy combo.
foods.summary: Spaghetti in a sweet tomato and banana ketchup sauce with ground meat, sliced hotdog and grated cheese. The birthday party dish of every Filipino kid, still on the menu for adults.
foods.answer: A regular solo Jolly Spaghetti is about 560 calories for a 280g serving, per the FatSecret Jollibee listing (72g carbs, 25g fat, 10g protein). The noodles are about 280 of that, the sweet sauce with meat and hotdog about 230, and the cheese about 50.
realTalk: Sweet spaghetti is heavier than it tastes because the sauce is half sugar. Banana ketchup, tomato sauce and added sugar make the sauce about 130 calories per 100g before the meat goes in. A solo serving gets around 120g of sauce with ground pork and hotdog slices, which is 230 calories. The 200g of cooked noodles is 280. FatSecret lists it at 560 per container, and a second listing for the Jolly Spaghetti at 610, so 560 to 610 is the range.

The protein is low for the calorie cost. About 15g in a solo serving, most of it from the hotdog and the sprinkle of cheese. Compare that to a 1-pc Chickenjoy with rice at 600 calories and 30g of protein. If you are choosing between the two for the same calories, the chicken meal keeps you full longer.

The combos are where it goes over 1,000. Chickenjoy with Jolly Spaghetti, which is the classic birthday plate, is about 860 calories. The family pan (about 1.2kg) is around 2,400, meant for 4 to 5 people but easily eaten by 3. At about 65 pesos for a solo it is cheap, and the sweetness means adults eat it fast and go back for the second serving at parties.
lighter: Order it solo, not as the Chickenjoy combo. That is 560 versus 860.
Skip the extra cheese sachet. About 50 calories for a sprinkle that is mostly salt.
At a party, take half a plate of spaghetti and a piece of chicken. About 580 total and you get both.
Do not pair it with the Coke float. A regular float is about 250 calories on top.

components.name: Sweet meat sauce with hotdog slices

faq.q: How many calories in Jollibee spaghetti with chicken?
faq.a: About 860 calories for the Chickenjoy with Jolly Spaghetti combo: 560 for the spaghetti and about 300 for the chicken piece.

faq.q: Why is Filipino spaghetti sweet?
faq.a: Banana ketchup and added sugar in the sauce. That sugar is also why a serving carries about 75g of carbs, more than 1.3 cups of rice.

faq.q: Is Jollibee spaghetti or Chickenjoy with rice lower in calories?
faq.a: They are close: about 560 for the spaghetti and 600 for a 1-pc Chickenjoy with rice. The Chickenjoy meal has double the protein, so it is the better pick for the same calories.

faq.q: How many calories in a Jollibee spaghetti family pan?
faq.a: About 2,400 for the whole pan. Split 4 ways that is 600 each, split 3 ways about 800.

foods.source: FatSecret Jollibee Spaghetti listing (560 kcal per container; 610 kcal in a second listing)

foods.name: Turon
foods.metaDescription: One turon is about 220 calories: the saba banana is 70, the sugar coat and frying oil are the rest. Numbers with jackfruit and with ice cream.
foods.summary: Saba banana (often with a strip of jackfruit) rolled in a lumpia wrapper, rolled in brown sugar and deep fried until the sugar turns to a glassy shell. The 15 peso merienda from every street cart.
foods.answer: One street turon is about 220 calories for an 80g piece. The saba banana inside is about 70 calories, the wrapper 35, the caramelised brown sugar shell about 50 and the oil absorbed during frying about 65. Two pieces, which is the usual order, is 440.
realTalk: The banana is the healthy part and it is a third of the calories. A saba banana is about 120 calories per 100g, so the 60g piece inside a turon is about 70. Then it gets a lumpia wrapper (35 calories), a roll in brown sugar that melts into a shell (about 12g, 50 calories) and a trip through hot oil, where the wrapper soaks up about 7g of oil (65 calories). Panlasang Pinoy's recipe card comes out at 292 per piece, but that counts a cup and a half of sugar across 12 pieces as all sticking.

The vendor's sugar habit is the variable. Some carts roll lightly and the shell is thin, about 200 calories per piece. Others dredge heavily and then drizzle more syrup on the finished turon, which pushes it to 280. The jackfruit strip adds about 15 calories and a lot of flavour, so it is not the thing to worry about.

Turon is sold in pairs for 25 to 30 pesos and eaten as merienda, usually with a soft drink. Two turon and a Coke is about 580 calories at 4pm, which is bigger than a lot of people's dinner. The turon with ice cream at restaurants (turon a la mode) is about 370 for one piece with a scoop.
lighter: One piece, not two. 220 versus 440, and one is enough with coffee.
Pick the cart with the thinner sugar shell. Light coat is about 200, heavy coat about 280.
Boiled saba (nilagang saging) is about 100 calories for the same banana without wrapper, sugar or oil.
Skip the soft drink with it. Turon is already 36g of carbs, most of it sugar.

portions.label: 2 pieces with a regular soft drink

variants.name: Turon, heavy sugar with syrup drizzle
Turon a la mode (with ice cream)

faq.q: How many calories in 2 pieces of turon?
faq.a: About 440 calories. Turon is usually sold in pairs, so that is the real serving for most people.

faq.q: Is turon healthy?
faq.a: The banana is. The rest is a fried wrapper and a sugar shell, so a piece is about 220 calories with 36g of carbs and 8g of fat. It is a dessert, not a fruit serving.

faq.q: Turon or banana cue, which has fewer calories?
faq.a: About the same. Banana cue is a whole saba coated in caramelised sugar and fried, around 200 to 230 per stick. Turon has the wrapper but slightly less banana.

faq.q: How many calories in turon with jackfruit?
faq.a: About 235. The strip of langka adds only 15 calories to a standard piece.

foods.source: estimate from components (saba banana, wrapper, sugar, oil uptake); Panlasang Pinoy recipe card 292 kcal per piece noted

foods.name: Pandesal
foods.metaDescription: One bakery pandesal is about 110 calories plain. The number only gets interesting when you count how many you eat and what goes inside them.
foods.summary: A slightly sweet, breadcrumb-dusted bread roll sold warm from neighbourhood bakeries every morning at 3 to 5 pesos each. Eaten plain, dipped in coffee, or stuffed with anything.
foods.answer: One standard bakery pandesal is about 110 calories for a 35g roll, or about 310 calories per 100g. FatSecret lists a larger 45g pandesal at 138. Plain, it is a small amount of bread. The usual breakfast of 3 pandesal with butter and coffee is closer to 500.
realTalk: A pandesal on its own is modest. Bread is bread: about 310 calories per 100g, and a corner bakery roll is 30 to 40g, so 100 to 125 calories. FatSecret's entry is 138 for a 45g roll, which is the bigger supermarket size. Kawaling Pinoy's recipe card agrees at 138 per roll from a 24-roll batch. The problem has never been one pandesal.

It is the count and the palaman (filling). Nobody eats one. Three pandesal is 330 calories, and that is before anything goes inside. A teaspoon of butter or margarine per roll is 35, a tablespoon of peanut butter is 95, a slice of cheese 70, coconut jam about 60. Three pandesal with butter is about 440. Three with peanut butter is about 615. A pandesal with a fried egg and a slice of Spam is about 300 by itself.

Then the coffee. 3-in-1 sachets are about 100 calories each, so a normal Filipino breakfast of 3 buttered pandesal and one 3-in-1 is around 540 calories, mostly refined flour and sugar, with about 12g of protein. It is not a terrible breakfast, but it is a bigger one than it looks, and it does not hold you until lunch.
lighter: Two pandesal instead of three saves 110 calories and you will not notice by 10am.
Fill it with egg, tuna or kesong puti instead of butter or peanut butter. Same calories, 3 to 4 times the protein.
Black coffee or kapeng barako instead of 3-in-1. About 100 calories saved per cup.
Whole wheat or malunggay pandesal is the same calories but keeps you full longer.

faq.q: How many calories in 2 pandesal?
faq.a: About 220 calories for 2 standard 35g rolls, plain. With a teaspoon of butter on each it is about 290.

faq.q: Is pandesal good for weight loss?
faq.a: It can fit. Two pandesal with egg or tuna is about 300 calories with 20g of protein. Three with peanut butter and 3-in-1 coffee is over 700, which is the version to avoid.

faq.q: Is pandesal healthier than white bread?
faq.a: About the same. Pandesal is white flour with a bit of sugar and fat, roughly 310 calories per 100g, the same as a sliced loaf. Whole wheat pandesal has more fibre at the same calories.

faq.q: How many calories in ube pandesal with cheese?
faq.a: About 250 to 300 per piece. Those are bigger rolls (70 to 80g) with ube jam and a cheese centre, so more than double a plain one.

foods.source: FatSecret generic pandesal (138 kcal per 45g roll, 307 kcal/100g), scaled to a 35g bakery roll; Kawaling Pinoy recipe card 138 kcal

foods.name: Puto
foods.metaDescription: Three small puto are about 120 calories, roughly 40 each. Cheese and butter versions cost more. Numbers for putong puti, puto cheese and puto bumbong.
foods.summary: Small steamed cakes of rice flour, sugar and a little coconut milk, sold in packs of 10 to 12 or handed out next to a bowl of dinuguan. Plain white, or topped with a cube of cheese.
foods.answer: Three small puto are about 120 calories for 75g, or about 40 calories per piece. Plain putong puti is rice flour, sugar and a splash of coconut milk with almost no fat. A puto cheese is about 55 each. Kawaling Pinoy's batch of 36 works out to 39 calories per piece.
realTalk: Puto is one of the lightest kakanin because it is steamed and mostly air. A small 25g piece is about 40 calories: 30 from rice flour, 8 from sugar, 2 from coconut milk. Kawaling Pinoy's recipe card lists 1,421 calories for a batch of 3 dozen, which is 39 each. White King's boxed mix is listed at 100 per serving on FatSecret, which is about 2 to 3 pieces.

The toppings change it. A cube of cheddar on top adds about 15, so puto cheese is 55. Puto with a slice of salted egg is about 60. Puto pao, the big one stuffed with asado and a quail egg, is a different food entirely at about 180 each. Puto bumbong, the purple Christmas version with butter, sugar and grated coconut, is around 150 to 200 per stick depending on how much butter the vendor brushes on.

The count is the thing. Puto comes in packs of 10 to 12 for 30 to 50 pesos and a pack disappears during one episode of anything. Ten small puto is 400 calories, about the same as a rice meal but with no protein. With dinuguan, 3 puto is the usual side and adds 120 to a 330 calorie serving.
lighter: Three pieces is a snack at 120 calories. Ten pieces is a meal at 400. Count them out before you open the pack.
Plain putong puti over puto cheese saves about 15 per piece, or 150 over a pack.
Puto bumbong: ask for less butter. The butter and sugar brush is about half the calories.
Pair puto with something that has protein, like dinuguan or a boiled egg, so it is not just carbs.

variants.name: Puto pao, 1 piece
variants.note: Stuffed with asado and quail egg

faq.q: How many calories in one puto?
faq.a: About 40 calories for a small plain putong puti (25g), and about 55 for a puto cheese. A large puto from a Bulacan bakery (50g) is about 80.

faq.q: Is puto healthy?
faq.a: It is low fat and low calorie per piece, but it is refined rice flour and sugar with almost no protein or fibre. Fine as a small snack, not as a meal.

faq.q: How many calories in puto bumbong?
faq.a: About 150 to 200 per stick. The glutinous purple rice is about 80, and the butter, muscovado sugar and coconut on top add the rest.

faq.q: Puto or kutsinta, which has fewer calories?
faq.a: About the same, 40 to 50 each. Kutsinta is denser and chewier but similar in size. Both are rice flour and sugar.

foods.source: Kawaling Pinoy recipe card (1421 kcal per 36 pieces, 39 each); White King puto 100 kcal per serving via FatSecret

foods.name: Isaw
foods.metaDescription: One stick of chicken isaw is about 45 calories, and even 5 sticks is under 250. Pork isaw is roughly double. The sweet basting sauce moves the number.
foods.summary: Chicken (or pork) intestines cleaned, boiled, threaded onto a skewer in a zigzag, then grilled and brushed with a sweet soy and ketchup sauce. Dipped in spiced vinegar, sold at 10 to 15 pesos a stick outside every campus.
foods.answer: One stick of chicken isaw is about 45 calories for a 30g skewer with its basting sauce. The intestine itself is about 30 calories and the sweet glaze about 15. Pork isaw is fattier and bigger, around 90 per stick. Five chicken sticks with vinegar is about 225 calories.
realTalk: Isaw is the cheapest high protein snack on the street and the numbers back it up. Chicken intestine is about 110 calories per 100g cooked with 15g of protein, and after cleaning and boiling a stick carries about 25g of it, so around 30 calories. Then the vendor brushes on the sauce: soy, banana ketchup, sugar and a bit of oil. About 5g clings per stick, 15 calories. Five sticks is 225 calories with 20g of protein, which beats most merienda.

Pork isaw (isaw baboy) is the heavy one. Pork intestine is about 200 calories per 100g cooked because of the fat lining, and the sticks are thicker at about 40g, so 90 calories each. Five pork sticks is 450. Same cart, same sauce, double the number. The vinegar dip (sukang maanghang) is about 5 calories per dunk, so it is free for practical purposes.

The real concern with isaw is not calories but cleaning. A well cleaned intestine is boiled for an hour before grilling. A badly cleaned one gives you a bad night. Pick the cart with a queue. The other thing to watch is the sweet sauce: some vendors dredge the stick through it twice, which doubles the glaze to about 30 calories per stick. Not a big deal on 3 sticks, more noticeable on 10.
lighter: Chicken isaw over pork isaw. 45 versus 90 per stick, and the chicken has more protein per calorie.
Dip in vinegar, not the sweet sauce cup. The vinegar is about 5 calories, the sweet sauce about 30 per spoon.
Five sticks is a snack at 225. Ten sticks is a small meal at 450. Both are fine, just know which one you are having.
Skip the rice. Isaw is one of the few street foods that does not need it.

faq.q: Is isaw healthy?
faq.a: For a street snack, yes. Chicken isaw is about 45 calories a stick with 4g of protein and very little fat. The risks are cleaning and hygiene, not calories.

faq.q: How many calories in 10 sticks of isaw?
faq.a: About 450 calories for chicken isaw, about 900 for pork isaw. The sweet sauce adds about 15 per stick either way.

faq.q: Is isaw high in cholesterol?
faq.a: Moderately. Intestines carry about 200mg of cholesterol per 100g, so 5 chicken sticks is about 250mg. If you are watching cholesterol, keep it to a few sticks.

faq.q: Chicken or pork isaw, which is lower in calories?
faq.a: Chicken, at about 45 per stick versus 90 for pork. Pork intestine has more fat in the lining and the sticks are bigger.

foods.source: estimate from components (chicken intestine, cooked; pork intestine, cooked; basting sauce)

foods.name: Balut
foods.metaDescription: One balut is about 190 calories with 14g of protein. More than a chicken egg because it is a bigger duck egg. Penoy and how the salt and vinegar figure in.
foods.summary: A fertilised duck egg incubated for 14 to 18 days, boiled and eaten warm from the shell with rock salt or spiced vinegar. Sold by the balut vendor shouting past your gate at night for 20 to 25 pesos.
foods.answer: One balut is about 190 calories with about 14g of protein and 14g of fat, per the figures cited for both chicken and duck balut. That is roughly 2.5 chicken eggs' worth of nutrition in one shell. The salt and vinegar add nothing, and the broth you sip first is about 5 calories.
realTalk: Balut is an egg, so it counts like an egg, just a big one. A duck egg is about 70g of edible content versus 50g for a chicken egg, and duck yolks are richer. The figure that circulates from Philippine sources is 188 calories and 14g of crude protein per balut, and that lines up with USDA duck egg data at about 185 calories per 70g. The embryo adds some protein and calcium (about 100mg) but does not change the calories much.

As a snack it is one of the best protein deals on the street. 190 calories with 14g of protein for 20 to 25 pesos beats almost everything else the same vendor sells. Chicharon, which balut vendors often carry as well, is 150 calories for a small bag with 8g of protein and a lot more salt. The yolk carries the fat, about 14g, half of it saturated, and about 600mg of cholesterol, which is the thing to be aware of if you eat 2 or 3 a night.

Penoy is the unfertilised version and is basically a boiled duck egg at about 180 calories. Balut sa puti, the younger 14 to 16 day egg with a white membrane and less embryo, is about the same. The only way balut gets expensive is the habit of eating it with 2 sticks of pork BBQ and a beer, which turns a 190 calorie snack into 600.
lighter: One balut is a good 190 calorie snack. Two is still fine at 380. Three a night is where the cholesterol gets silly.
Use the spiced vinegar instead of salt if you are watching sodium. Both are calorie free.
Eat it instead of a late dinner, not on top of one. It is filling for its size.
If you want the protein without the yolk fat, eat the white and the embryo and leave half the yolk. About 120 calories that way.

portions.label: Balut, white and embryo only (half the yolk)

variants.name: Balut with 2 pork BBQ sticks and a beer

faq.q: Is balut high in protein?
faq.a: Yes, about 14g per egg, which is more than 2 chicken eggs. It is one of the highest protein snacks per peso on the street.

faq.q: Is balut high in cholesterol?
faq.a: Yes, about 600mg per egg, mostly in the yolk. That is 3 chicken eggs' worth. One a day is fine for most people; several a night is not.

faq.q: How many calories in penoy?
faq.a: About 180, close to balut. Penoy is an unfertilised duck egg, so it is a plain hard boiled duck egg with no embryo.

faq.q: Is balut good for weight loss?
faq.a: As a snack, yes. 190 calories, 14g of protein, very filling, and it takes a few minutes to eat. Just do not add the pork BBQ and the beer every time.

foods.source: 188 kcal and 14g protein per egg as cited on Wikipedia (Balut) from Philippine sources; cross-checked with USDA duck egg

foods.name: Buko Juice
foods.serving: 1 cup (350ml, with buko strips and sugar)
foods.metaDescription: A cup of buko juice from a stand is about 160 calories with the sugar and buko strips. Straight from the coconut it is about 100. Where the gap comes from.
foods.summary: Young coconut water served with strips of soft buko meat, usually with sugar syrup and a lot of ice. From a 25 peso cup at a stand to a whole coconut with a straw at the beach.
foods.answer: A regular 350ml cup of buko juice from a stand is about 160 calories: about 60 from the coconut water, 40 from the buko strips and 60 from the sugar syrup the vendor adds. A whole young coconut with its meat and no added sugar is about 100 calories.
realTalk: Coconut water alone is light. About 19 calories per 100ml, so the 300ml in a cup is 57 calories. The soft young buko meat is about 80 calories per 100g, and a cup gets 50g of strips for 40 calories. That is the honest coconut, about 100 calories. Then the stand adds simple syrup, usually 15 to 20g of sugar, because plain buko water tastes flat to people used to soft drinks. That is another 60 to 80 calories.

The 'buko juice' in a plastic cup at a mall or a Buko Nation type stall is often not straight from a coconut. It is diluted coconut water with sugar, sometimes condensed milk, and more buko strips, and a large cup can hit 250 calories. The bottled versions at the supermarket run 60 to 90 calories per 330ml, which is less than soft drinks but still 15 to 20g of sugar.

Buko juice is a good replacement for Coke (140 calories) and an even better one if you ask for 'walang asukal' (no sugar), which vendors will do. It is not a free drink though. Two cups of the sweetened kind in an afternoon is 320 calories, which people do not count because it is 'just coconut'. The potassium claim is real, about 250mg per 100ml, useful after a hot day.
lighter: Ask for walang asukal (no sugar). The cup drops from 160 to about 100.
Buy the whole coconut. A vendor with a bolo gives you about 100 calories with no way to add syrup.
Skip the condensed milk versions at mall stalls. Those are 220 to 250 per cup.
Have the buko strips. They are the part with fibre and they make the drink more filling for about 40 calories.

variants.name: Whole young coconut, water and meat
Buko juice, regular cup with sugar
Buko juice with condensed milk, regular

faq.q: Is buko juice good for weight loss?
faq.a: Compared to soft drinks, yes. Without sugar it is about 100 calories per cup with potassium and some fibre from the strips. With the vendor's syrup it is 160, which is close to a Coke.

faq.q: How much sugar is in buko juice?
faq.a: About 8g naturally from the coconut water and meat, plus 15 to 20g of added syrup at a stand. Ask for no sugar and it is under 10g.

faq.q: Is buko juice the same as coconut water?
faq.a: Buko juice is coconut water plus strips of young coconut meat, and usually sugar. Plain coconut water is 19 calories per 100ml; the meat and syrup add the rest.

faq.q: How many calories in a whole buko?
faq.a: About 100 calories for a typical young coconut: 300ml of water at 57 calories and about 50g of soft meat at 40. A very meaty older buko can reach 150.

foods.source: estimate from components (USDA coconut water 19 kcal/100ml, young coconut meat, added sugar)

foods.name: Sago't Gulaman
foods.metaDescription: A large cup of sago't gulaman is about 200 calories, and 150 of that is the arnibal syrup. The sago and gulaman are minor. Small, large and mall numbers.
foods.summary: Brown sugar syrup (arnibal) flavoured with banana essence or pandan, poured over ice with tapioca pearls and cubes of gulaman jelly. The 15 to 25 peso drink from the samalamig cart on every corner.
foods.answer: A large 400ml cup of sago't gulaman is about 200 calories. The arnibal syrup is about 150 of that, the sago pearls about 35 and the gulaman cubes about 10. The ice and water are free. Kawaling Pinoy's recipe card lands at 248 per serving with a heavier syrup pour.
realTalk: Sago't gulaman is brown sugar water with chewy things in it, and the calories follow the sugar. A vendor ladles about 40g of arnibal (brown sugar boiled with water and a drop of banana extract) into a large cup, which is 150 calories. The sago pearls are cooked tapioca starch, about 30g at 35 calories. The gulaman is agar jelly set with a little sugar, about 40g at 10 calories. Then ice and water to the top. Kawaling Pinoy and Panlasang Pinoy both land around 250 per serving, with a cup of sugar for 6 servings.

The cart drinks are all the same sugar in different colours. Melon juice, buko pandan, black gulaman, the sago't gulaman with a squeeze of calamansi: 150 to 250 per large cup, and the difference is mostly how heavy the vendor's hand is. A large cup is about the same as a can of Coke (140) plus a bit, and people drink 2 in an afternoon because it is 20 pesos and it is hot.

The mall versions with cream or condensed milk are a step up. A large buko pandan with cream is about 280, and the 'special' sago't gulaman with extra sago and a milk float is around 300. Sago't gulaman is a fine drink to have instead of a soft drink, but it is not water with jelly in it. It is 49g of carbs, all of it sugar and starch.
lighter: Ask for konting arnibal (less syrup). A vendor will halve it and the cup drops to about 120.
Small cup instead of large. About 120 versus 200, and it is the same drink.
Skip the extra sago. Each spoon of pearls is about 20 calories of starch.
If you want the cold sweet hit, a calamansi juice with less sugar is about 80 for a large cup.

portions.label: Large cup with extra sago and syrup

variants.name: Buko pandan drink with cream, large
Special sago't gulaman with milk float

faq.q: Is sago't gulaman healthy?
faq.a: No, it is sugar water with tapioca and jelly. About 200 calories and 45g of sugar in a large cup. The gulaman itself is nearly free; the arnibal is the problem.

faq.q: How many calories in the sago alone?
faq.a: About 35 calories for the 30g of cooked pearls in a large cup. Sago is pure starch, about 120 calories per 100g cooked.

faq.q: Is sago't gulaman lower in calories than Coke?
faq.a: Not really. A large cup is about 200 calories versus 140 for a 330ml can of Coke. With less syrup it drops to 120, which is when it becomes the better choice.

faq.q: How many calories in gulaman?
faq.a: Almost none. Gulaman is agar, about 5 to 10 calories per 40g cube portion once the sugar in the jelly is counted. It is the syrup and sago around it that add up.

foods.source: estimate from components; Kawaling Pinoy (248 kcal) and Panlasang Pinoy (255 kcal) recipe cards used as reference

foods.name: Beef Brisket Noodles (Ngau Lam Min)
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of Hong Kong beef brisket noodles is about 550 calories with 50g of protein, per Centre for Food Safety data. Ho fun takes it to 670.
foods.summary: Ngau lam min is thin egg noodles in clear beef broth with chunks of brisket that have been simmered for 3 or 4 hours until they fall apart. Noodle shops from Central to Kowloon City charge HK$45 to HK$70 a bowl.
foods.answer: One bowl of beef brisket noodles with thin egg noodles is about 550 calories, based on Centre for Food Safety analysis of a 640g bowl. The same brisket on thick noodles is 520, on rice vermicelli 610, and on ho fun 670. Protein is high at around 50g, which is more than most Hong Kong noodle dishes.
realTalk: Brisket noodles are one of the better deals on a Hong Kong noodle menu if you care about protein. CFS measured 50g of protein in a 640g bowl, which is close to two chicken breasts, for 550 calories. The brisket is the reason: about 120g of slow cooked beef per bowl. The trade off is fat, at 17g with 6g of it saturated, because brisket is a fatty cut and the broth is skimmed less than you would like.

The noodle choice moves the number more than people expect. Thin egg noodles land at 550 and thick at 520, but a bowl of ho fun with the same brisket is 670 because flat rice noodles are heavier and soak up more soup. Rice vermicelli sits at 610. If you always order 牛腩河 out of habit, switching to 牛腩麵 saves about 120 calories a bowl with the same amount of beef on top.

The soup is the sodium problem, not the calorie problem. CFS found 3,100mg of sodium in a bowl of brisket with thin noodles, which is one and a half days of the 2,000mg WHO limit in a single lunch. Most of it is in the broth, so the trick is simple: eat the noodles and the meat, leave at least half the soup. The famous brisket shops also serve a curry version (咖喱牛腩) and that adds around 100 calories from the coconut and oil in the sauce.
lighter: Order thin egg noodles rather than ho fun. Same brisket, about 120 fewer calories.
Ask for lean brisket (瘦腩) or tendon (牛筋). The tendon version is 480 calories with only 9g of fat.
Leave half the soup. That alone cuts sodium by well over 1,000mg.
Add a plate of blanched choy sum without oyster sauce (走油). About 30 calories and it stretches the meal.

components.name: Rendered fat and oil in the soup

portions.label: Ho fun bowl with extra brisket

faq.q: How many calories in a bowl of beef brisket noodles?
faq.a: About 550 calories for a 640g bowl with thin egg noodles, according to Centre for Food Safety data. The ho fun version is about 670.

faq.q: Is beef brisket noodle soup healthy?
faq.a: It has 50g of protein per bowl, which is excellent, but also around 3,100mg of sodium, mostly in the broth. Eat the noodles and beef, skip most of the soup.

faq.q: Which noodle is lowest in calories with brisket?
faq.a: Thick egg noodles at about 520 calories, then thin egg noodles at 550. Rice vermicelli is 610 and ho fun is 670 for the same amount of brisket.

foods.source: Centre for Food Safety Hong Kong, Nutrient Values of Indigenous Congee, Rice and Noodle Dishes (550 kcal per 640g bowl, thin noodles; 670 kcal ho fun)

foods.name: Wonton Noodle Soup (Wan Tan Min)
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of Hong Kong wonton noodle soup is about 450 calories according to the Centre for Food Safety. The small noodle shop bowl is closer to 300.
foods.summary: Wonton noodle soup is springy thin egg noodles in a clear shrimp and pork bone broth with 4 to 6 shrimp wontons underneath. The old school shops in Central, Wan Chai and Jordan charge HK$40 to HK$60 for a small bowl.
foods.answer: A standard bowl of wonton noodles with thin egg noodles is around 450 calories, based on Centre for Food Safety analysis of a 630g bowl. A small noodle shop bowl (細蓉) with fewer noodles is closer to 300. Protein is decent at about 33g because the wontons are mostly shrimp and pork.
realTalk: This is different from the Malaysian dry wantan mee. The Hong Kong version is a soup, the noodles are thin and alkaline, and the wontons are shrimp heavy. At 450 calories for a full cha chaan teng bowl it is one of the lighter noodle dishes in the city, well under beef brisket noodles (550) and nowhere near a plate of fried beef ho fun (970). Fat is only 14g and most of that is the pork in the wontons.

The classic wonton shop bowl is small on purpose. A 細蓉 at the famous places in Central is maybe 250g of food with 4 wontons and a tight nest of noodles, and that lands near 300 calories. The 630g bowl CFS tested is what you get at a cha chaan teng or a noodle chain, with nearly double the noodles. So the same dish can be 300 or 450 depending on where you sit down, and the price gap is about HK$10.

The sodium is the catch, as with every Hong Kong soup noodle. CFS found 2,900mg in the full bowl, which is well over the 2,000mg daily limit. The broth is made with dried flounder and shrimp shells and it is heavily salted, so it tastes better than it is for you. The noodles themselves are around 190 calories per bowl; the wontons about 35 to 40 each; the soup adds almost nothing except salt.
lighter: Order the small bowl (細蓉). It is about 300 calories and the same 4 wontons.
Try 淨雲吞 (wontons in soup, no noodles). Six wontons in broth is about 250 calories with 20g of protein.
Leave most of the soup. The broth carries nearly all of the 2,900mg of sodium.
Skip the side of pig skin or fish skin (炸魚皮). A small plate is another 150 to 200 calories.

variants.name: Wontons in soup, no noodles (淨雲吞, 6 pieces)

faq.q: How many calories in Hong Kong wonton noodles?
faq.a: About 450 calories for a 630g cha chaan teng bowl with thin noodles, per Centre for Food Safety data. A small wonton shop bowl is closer to 300.

faq.q: How many calories in one wonton?
faq.a: A shrimp and pork wonton is roughly 35 to 40 calories. Four in a bowl come to about 150, with around 12g of protein.

faq.q: Is wonton noodle soup good for weight loss?
faq.a: It is one of the lighter Hong Kong noodle dishes at 300 to 450 calories with 33g of protein. The problem is sodium at about 2,900mg per bowl, so leave the soup.

foods.source: Centre for Food Safety Hong Kong, Nutrient Values of Indigenous Congee, Rice and Noodle Dishes (450 kcal per 630g bowl, thin noodles)

foods.name: Luncheon Meat and Egg Instant Noodles (Chaan Daan Min)
foods.serving: 1 bowl (instant noodles, 2 slices luncheon meat, 1 fried egg)
foods.metaDescription: A cha chaan teng bowl of instant noodles with luncheon meat and fried egg is 680 to 785 calories, the heaviest breakfast on the menu. Here is why.
foods.summary: Chaan daan min is a packet of instant noodles in broth topped with two slices of fried luncheon meat and a fried egg. It is the most ordered cha chaan teng breakfast in Hong Kong, HK$32 to HK$42 as a set with a drink.
foods.answer: One bowl of instant noodles with luncheon meat and egg is about 680 calories, based on Centre for Food Safety analysis of a 450g bowl. A Hong Kong dietitian ranking of cha chaan teng breakfasts puts it higher at 785 when the noodles are Demae Iccho and the luncheon meat is fried in extra oil. Either way it is the heaviest breakfast on the board, with 38g of fat.
realTalk: This bowl beats every other cha chaan teng breakfast by a wide margin. Ham macaroni is 320. Buttered toast with a fried egg is 427. Satay beef noodles are 667. Chaan daan min sits at 680 to 785, and unlike those, over half the calories come from fat. CFS found 12g of saturated fat and 190mg of cholesterol in one bowl, which is most of a day's worth before 9am.

All three parts are fried. The instant noodle cake is deep fried at the factory, so a 90g packet is already about 390 calories and 15g of fat before anything touches it. Two slices of luncheon meat (60g) fried in the pan are around 190 calories and 17g of fat. The fried egg is 100. There is no ingredient in this bowl that is not oily, which is why the number is so far above ham macaroni that uses the same broth.

The set makes it worse. A breakfast set adds a buttered bun or toast (250) and a hot milk tea (110), so the full tray is over 1,000 calories. That is half of a 2,000 calorie day sitting in front of you at 8am, with only 22g of protein. If you eat this every workday, that is around 3,500 calories a week over what a macaroni breakfast would cost you, which is roughly half a kilo of body fat a month with nothing else changed.
lighter: Swap the luncheon meat for ham (火腿). The bowl drops by about 140 calories and most of the saturated fat.
Swap instant noodles for macaroni or rice vermicelli (米粉). Boiled noodles save around 150 calories versus the fried cake.
Ask for a boiled egg instead of fried. Saves 30 calories and a few grams of oil.
Skip the buttered toast in the set. That is 250 calories you will not miss with a bowl this heavy.

portions.label: One slice luncheon meat, boiled egg
Full set with buttered toast and milk tea

variants.name: Luncheon meat and egg rice vermicelli
Luncheon meat and egg instant noodles
Five spice pork instant noodles (五香肉丁公仔麵)

faq.q: How many calories in 餐蛋麵?
faq.a: About 680 calories per bowl according to Centre for Food Safety data, or up to 785 in a Hong Kong dietitian ranking. It is the heaviest breakfast on a cha chaan teng menu.

faq.q: How many calories in two slices of luncheon meat?
faq.a: Around 190 calories for 60g once fried, with about 17g of fat. Two slices of ham are about 50 calories.

faq.q: Is instant noodle soup unhealthy because of the noodles or the toppings?
faq.a: Both. The fried noodle cake alone is about 390 calories and 15g fat. The luncheon meat and fried egg add another 290 calories and 25g of fat.

foods.source: Centre for Food Safety Hong Kong, Nutrient Values of Indigenous Congee, Rice and Noodle Dishes (680 kcal per 450g); HK01 registered dietitian Charlene Wong ranking (785 kcal)

foods.name: Beef Chow Fun (Gon Chau Ngau Ho)
foods.metaDescription: A plate of Hong Kong dry fried beef ho fun is about 970 calories according to the Centre for Food Safety, roughly three and a half bowls of rice.
foods.summary: Gon chau ngau ho is wide rice noodles tossed over a screaming hot wok with sliced beef, bean sprouts, spring onion and dark soy until the edges char. Every cha chaan teng and dai pai dong does it, HK$55 to HK$80 a plate.
foods.answer: One plate of dry fried beef ho fun is around 970 calories, based on Centre for Food Safety testing of a 650g restaurant portion. Carbs make up 140g of that, from roughly 400g of rice noodles, and fat is 33g from the oil the noodles need to fry without sticking.
realTalk: The number surprises people because there is nothing creamy or deep fried on the plate. But the wok needs a lot of oil to keep 400g of flat rice noodles from tearing, around 30g per plate, and rice noodles themselves are dense. CFS measured 140g of carbohydrate in one plate, which is the same as three and a half bowls of white rice. The beef is only about 100g, so protein is a modest 26g for nearly 1,000 calories.

Among Hong Kong fried noodle dishes this is actually mid table. Singapore fried vermicelli is 1,100. Fried noodles with black bean spare ribs is 1,500. Fried instant noodles with pork chop is 1,200. Beef ho fun at 970 is the one everyone names as the villain because it is the most ordered, and a dietitian in the HKET ranking pointed out it does not even make the top three. That is not a reason to order it twice a week, just context.

Portion size at a dai pai dong is the real issue. The 650g CFS plate is a standard single order, but the plates in Sham Shui Po and Mong Kok that come with a mound of noodles hanging off the edge are closer to 900g and 1,300 calories. Sodium is 2,300mg a plate from the soy sauce alone. If you split a plate between two people and add a plate of greens, each person gets a 500 calorie meal, which is reasonable.
lighter: Share one plate between two. Half a plate is about 485 calories.
Ask for less oil (少油). Some places will, and it can save 100 to 150 calories.
Order the wet version (濕炒牛河) if you must have ho fun. The gravy style uses less oil, roughly 750 calories a plate.
Pair it with blanched vegetables, not another fried dish. The noodles are already the whole carb budget for the day.

variants.name: Wet fried beef ho fun (濕炒牛河)
Dry fried beef ho fun (乾炒牛河)
Beef ho fun with vegetables (菜遠牛河)

faq.q: How many calories in a plate of beef chow fun?
faq.a: About 970 calories for a 650g plate, according to Centre for Food Safety data. Dai pai dong portions can pass 1,300.

faq.q: Why is dry fried beef ho fun so high in calories?
faq.a: Around 400g of rice noodles (440 calories) plus about 30g of oil (265 calories) needed to fry them without sticking. The beef is only about 200 of the total.

faq.q: Is wet or dry fried ho fun healthier?
faq.a: Wet (濕炒) is lower, roughly 750 calories, because the noodles are blanched rather than fried in oil and the gravy is mostly stock and starch.

foods.source: Centre for Food Safety Hong Kong, Nutrient Values of Indigenous Congee, Rice and Noodle Dishes (970 kcal per 650g plate)

foods.name: Tomato Beef Macaroni (Ke Ngau Tung)
aka: Cha Chaan Teng Tomato Beef Soup Noodles
foods.metaDescription: A cha chaan teng bowl of tomato beef macaroni is about 370 calories, one of the lightest hot meals on the menu. The rice plate version is 665.
foods.summary: Ke ngau tung is macaroni in a tangy tomato soup with sliced beef, sometimes with an egg dropped in. It is the cha chaan teng lunch that dietitians keep recommending, HK$35 to HK$48 with a drink.
foods.answer: One bowl of tomato beef macaroni is around 370 calories, based on a Hong Kong registered dietitian's tally of cha chaan teng dishes (368 kcal). About 200 is the macaroni, 80 is the beef and the tomato broth is around 90. It carries about 20g of protein and only 10g of fat.
realTalk: Of the 12 cha chaan teng dishes in the HK01 dietitian ranking, tomato beef macaroni came in at 368 calories, sixth from the top and less than half of the luncheon meat instant noodles (785) that most people at the next table are eating. The macaroni is boiled, the beef is sliced lean flank, and the soup is tomato, ketchup and stock. There is nothing fried in the bowl unless you add a fried egg, which is another 100.

The same ingredients on a rice plate are a different story. 鮮茄牛肉飯 with a reduced portion of rice is 665 calories in a Weekend Weekly dietitian list, and a full rice portion pushes it over 750. Rice is denser than macaroni in soup, and the plate version uses more oil to stir fry the beef and tomato. So if you want the tomato beef flavour, the noodle soup gets you there for about 300 fewer calories.

Where it goes wrong is the sugar and salt in the soup. Cha chaan teng tomato broth leans on ketchup, and a bowl can hold 15 to 20g of sugar plus 1,500mg or more of sodium. Drinking every drop is what tips this from a light lunch into a sweet, salty one. Eat the macaroni and beef, take a few spoons of the soup, and the number stays near 320.
lighter: Order it with sliced beef, not minced beef patty. Minced beef in Hong Kong is fatty and adds about 80 calories.
Skip the fried egg on top. That is 100 calories; a poached egg dropped in the soup is 70.
Leave most of the soup. It holds nearly all the sugar and sodium.
Choose macaroni or rice vermicelli over instant noodles. The fried noodle cake alone adds about 150 calories.

portions.label: Set with fried egg, buttered toast and milk tea

variants.name: Tomato beef macaroni with fried egg
Tomato beef instant noodles
variants.note: Fried noodle cake instead of macaroni

faq.q: How many calories in a bowl of tomato beef macaroni?
faq.a: About 370 calories per cha chaan teng bowl, according to a Hong Kong registered dietitian ranking (368 kcal). That is less than half of a luncheon meat and egg instant noodle bowl.

faq.q: Is tomato beef macaroni healthy?
faq.a: It is one of the better cha chaan teng choices: 20g of protein, 10g of fat, nothing fried. The soup is high in sugar and sodium, so do not drink all of it.

faq.q: Tomato beef noodles or tomato beef rice, which is lower?
faq.a: The noodle soup at about 370 calories. The rice plate is about 665 even with less rice, because of the rice portion and the oil used to stir fry.

foods.source: HK01 registered dietitian Charlene Wong ranking of 12 cha chaan teng items (tomato beef macaroni 368 kcal); Weekend Weekly dietitian list for the 665 kcal rice plate

foods.name: Siu Mei Rice (Roast Pork Rice)
foods.metaDescription: A plate of Hong Kong roast pork rice is about 930 calories according to the Centre for Food Safety. Char siu rice is 1,000, soy sauce chicken rice 770.
foods.summary: Siu mei rice is a plate of steamed rice with roast meat chopped over it from the window of a siu mei shop: crispy roast pork (siu yuk), char siu, roast goose, roast duck or soy sauce chicken. Around HK$42 to HK$58 for a single meat, more for a double combo.
foods.answer: One plate of roast pork (siu yuk) rice is about 930 calories, based on Centre for Food Safety analysis of a 470g plate. Char siu rice from the same study is 1,000 calories, roast goose rice 970, plain poached chicken rice 940 and soy sauce chicken rice 770. The meat is 40g of fat on its own; the rice is around 110g of carbs.
realTalk: Siu yuk is pork belly with the skin blistered. A 130g portion on rice is about 500 calories before you count the rice, because belly is roughly a third fat by weight. CFS measured 12g of saturated fat in a plate of roast pork rice, more than the 10g the WHO considers a reasonable daily ceiling. Char siu is leaner meat but it is glazed in maltose and the fatty 半肥瘦 cut is what most shops chop by default, which is why it comes out slightly higher at 1,000.

The rice is the quiet half of the plate. Most siu mei shops put 280 to 300g of cooked rice under the meat, which is about 360 calories and more than the meat's carb-free 500. Then the shop spoons roast juices and sweet sauce over it, another 30 to 50. Ask for less rice (少飯) and the plate drops by around 120 calories with the same amount of meat, which is the cheapest calorie cut in Hong Kong.

Soy sauce chicken is the one to know about. The CFS figure for 油雞飯 is 770 calories versus 930 for roast pork, a 160 calorie gap for the same plate size. Peel the skin and it is closer to 650. The double combo (雙拼) plates that stack char siu and roast pork are 1,100 or more, and the roast goose leg on rice with skin can pass 1,000 on its own. Pick one meat, pick it lean, and this is a decent 30g plus protein lunch.
lighter: Ask for lean char siu (瘦叉燒) or soy sauce chicken without skin. Either saves 200 to 300 calories versus roast pork belly.
Order less rice (少飯). About 120 calories off with no change to the meat.
Skip the sweet sauce and the extra ladle of roast juices. That is 30 to 50 calories and a lot of sodium.
Add a plate of blanched choy sum for HK$12. Around 30 calories and it makes the plate a real meal.

portions.label: Double combo (雙拼) roast pork and char siu

variants.name: Soy sauce chicken rice (油雞飯)
variants.note: CFS figure, lowest of the siu mei plates

faq.q: How many calories in a plate of siu mei rice?
faq.a: Between 770 and 1,000 depending on the meat, per Centre for Food Safety data. Roast pork rice is about 930, char siu rice 1,000, roast goose rice 970 and soy sauce chicken rice 770.

faq.q: Which siu mei is the lowest calorie?
faq.a: Soy sauce chicken at about 770 calories on rice, or closer to 650 with the skin removed. Roast pork belly is the highest in fat at about 40g per plate.

faq.q: Is siu yuk or char siu higher in calories?
faq.a: On a rice plate they are close: roast pork 930 and char siu 1,000 in the CFS study. Char siu is glazed with maltose and usually chopped from the fatty cut, which is why it edges ahead.

foods.source: Centre for Food Safety Hong Kong, Nutrient Values of Indigenous Congee, Rice and Noodle Dishes (roast pork rice 930 kcal per 470g; char siu rice 1,000; soy sauce chicken rice 770; roast goose rice 970)

foods.name: Sweet and Sour Pork Rice (Gu Lou Yuk Fan)
aka: Sweet and Sour Pork with Rice
foods.serving: 1 plate (rice with sweet and sour pork)
foods.metaDescription: A plate of sweet and sour pork rice is about 800 calories. The Centre for Food Safety measured 240 kcal and 10g of sugar per 100g of the pork alone.
foods.summary: Gu lou yuk is cubes of fatty pork battered, deep fried and tossed in a glossy sweet and sour sauce with pineapple and peppers. On a cha chaan teng rice plate it is HK$50 to HK$65, or HK$80 to HK$120 as a shared dish at a dai pai dong.
foods.answer: A cha chaan teng plate of sweet and sour pork on rice is roughly 800 calories: about 480 from 200g of the pork and sauce, and 330 from the rice. The Centre for Food Safety measured the pork at 240 calories, 15g of fat and 10g of sugar per 100g in its survey of Hong Kong style dishes, the highest sugar of the 10 dishes tested.
realTalk: Sweet and sour pork is a three layer problem. The pork is shoulder or belly with visible fat. It is coated in batter and deep fried, which soaks up oil. Then it is tossed in a sauce that is mostly sugar, vinegar and ketchup. CFS found that a single portion sample carried 35g of sugar, which is 70 percent of the WHO daily limit of 50g, before you count the rice under it. That sauce is why it topped the sugar column in the survey.

The per 100g numbers tell you how fast it adds up. At 240 calories per 100g, a normal 200g rice plate portion is 480 calories from the pork alone, and dai pai dong portions of 350g served on a shared plate are 840 before anyone has touched the rice. Compare that to steamed chicken with mushroom at around 90 calories per 100g. Same amount of food on the plate, less than half the energy.

The rice plate version is at least portion controlled. A full cha chaan teng plate at about 800 calories is lower than a plate of baked pork chop rice (1,300) and in the same range as a roast pork rice (930). What tips it over is the second helping of sauce most shops ladle across the rice, which is another 60 to 80 calories of pure sugar, and the fact that fried batter holds oil long after it leaves the wok.
lighter: Ask for the sauce on the side or less sauce (少汁). That is where most of the 35g of sugar lives.
Order less rice (少飯). Around 110 calories off the plate.
Share a dai pai dong portion between three people with a plate of greens. Each share is about 280 calories of pork.
If the menu has lemon chicken or steamed chicken with mushroom, those are 260 and 400 calories a portion by dietitian estimates, and both are a lot lighter.

components.name: Battered fried pork in sweet and sour sauce

portions.label: Dai pai dong dish (350g pork) with a bowl of rice

variants.name: Sweet and sour pork, 200g portion, no rice
Sweet and sour pork rice plate
Sweet and sour pork, dai pai dong dish (350g)

faq.q: How many calories in sweet and sour pork rice?
faq.a: About 800 calories for a cha chaan teng rice plate. The pork itself is 240 calories per 100g according to the Centre for Food Safety, so a 200g portion is 480 before the rice.

faq.q: How much sugar is in sweet and sour pork?
faq.a: About 10g per 100g in the CFS survey, the highest of the 10 Hong Kong dishes tested. One single portion sample had 35g of sugar, about 70 percent of the WHO daily limit.

faq.q: Is sweet and sour pork worse than roast pork rice?
faq.a: Slightly better on calories (800 versus 930) but much worse on sugar. Roast pork has almost none; sweet and sour pork has about 20g per rice plate portion.

foods.source: Estimate from components: Centre for Food Safety Hong Kong, Nutrient Content of Hong Kong Style Savoury Dishes 2017 (sweet and sour pork 240 kcal, 15g fat, 10g sugar per 100g) plus 250g steamed rice

foods.name: Claypot Rice (Bo Zai Fan)
foods.metaDescription: A cured meat claypot rice from a Hong Kong street stall is about 1,300 calories per pot, the same as three fast food burgers. Here is why.
foods.summary: Bo zai fan is rice cooked in a small clay pot over charcoal until the bottom crisps, topped with lap cheong, cured pork belly or liver sausage and finished with sweet soy. The Temple Street stalls charge HK$60 to HK$95 a pot in winter.
foods.answer: One pot of cured meat claypot rice (臘味煲仔飯) is about 1,300 calories, based on Hong Kong dietitian figures of 1,315 kcal. Chicken and mushroom is around 1,030, minced beef with egg 1,170, and the lightest common choice, frog with mushroom, is about 860. The cured meats, the oil in the pot and the sweet soy account for more than half of the total.
realTalk: The pot is oiled before the rice goes in so the crust releases, and that is 15 to 20g of oil sitting under the rice before any topping. Then the cured meats render. One lap cheong (40g) carries about 20g of fat by dietitian estimates, and a pot gets two sausages plus a slice of cured belly or liver sausage. All that fat drips straight into 400g of rice. You are eating rice that has been fried from underneath and from above, which is why a bowl-sized portion tops 1,300.

The ranking from the dietitians is useful. Cured meat 1,315. Chicken feet and spare rib 1,300. Minced beef with egg 1,167. Pork patty 1,108. Taro with preserved duck leg 1,074. Chicken and mushroom 1,026. White eel 912. Frog and mushroom 860. The gap between the top and bottom is 450 calories, which is a whole extra meal, from the same pot of rice. The cured stuff is worst because it is preserved in fat and sugar; frog and chicken are lean meat steamed on top.

The sweet soy is the part nobody counts. It is thick, sugary and salty, and the stall pours it on from a squeeze bottle. One tablespoon holds around 825mg of sodium by dietitian estimate, and most people use two or three. A pot can easily pass 2,500mg of sodium and 20g of added sugar. The crust at the bottom (飯焦) that everyone fights over is the most oil soaked rice in the pot, roughly 4 calories per gram versus 1.3 for plain steamed rice.
lighter: Pick chicken and mushroom (北菇滑雞) or frog (田雞) over cured meat. That is 300 to 450 calories less per pot.
Share one pot between two and order a plate of blanched vegetables (走油). Half a pot is 650 calories.
Use one squeeze of sweet soy, not three. Saves about 60 calories and over 1,500mg of sodium.
Leave the oiliest crust. The bottom 50g of rice is close to 200 calories on its own.

components.name: Cured pork belly or liver sausage
Pot oil and sweet soy sauce

portions.label: Large pot with extra lap cheong and full sweet soy

variants.name: Minced beef with egg (窩蛋牛肉)
Chicken feet and spare rib (鳳爪排骨)

faq.q: How many calories in a claypot rice?
faq.a: About 1,300 calories for a cured meat pot, according to Hong Kong dietitians. Chicken and mushroom is around 1,030 and frog with mushroom about 860.

faq.q: Why is claypot rice so high in calories?
faq.a: The pot is oiled, the cured meats render 30g or more of fat into the rice, and the sweet soy adds sugar. One lap cheong alone has about 20g of fat.

faq.q: Which claypot rice is the healthiest?
faq.a: Frog and mushroom at about 860 calories, then white eel at 912. Both are lean meat steamed on top of the rice rather than cured meat rendering into it.

foods.source: Hong Kong dietitians via Cigna HK and HK01 (cured meat claypot rice 1,315 kcal; chicken and mushroom 1,026; frog and mushroom 860)

foods.name: Hong Kong Borscht (Lo Sung Tong)
foods.metaDescription: A cha chaan teng bowl of Hong Kong borscht is about 90 calories, the lightest of the set meal soups. The cream soup next to it is 325.
foods.summary: Hong Kong borscht is a tomato based vegetable soup with cabbage, potato, carrot, onion and a few bits of beef, nothing like the beetroot original. It comes free with most cha chaan teng set meals or HK$12 to HK$18 on its own.
foods.answer: A 250ml bowl of cha chaan teng borscht is about 90 calories, based on figures from a Hong Kong nutrition service (87.5 kcal per 250g bowl, 2.5g fat). It is by far the lightest of the two set soup options; the cream soup alternative is around 170 for mushroom and 325 for the version with croutons and cream.
realTalk: When the waiter asks 紅湯定白湯 (red soup or white soup), red is the right answer every time. Borscht is about 90 calories a bowl and cream of mushroom is 170. The cream soups are made with roux and evaporated milk, so a bowl carries 11g or more of fat. Borscht is tomato, cabbage and stock with almost no fat, about 2.5g. Choosing red over white every workday saves around 400 calories a week without changing anything else you eat.

The soup is mostly vegetables and water, which is why the number is low. A bowl has maybe 15g of beef, 60g of cabbage, potato and carrot, and 170ml of tomato stock. The tomato paste and a bit of sugar give it around 12g of carbs. This is the closest thing to a volume food on a cha chaan teng menu: 250ml of hot food for 90 calories that takes the edge off before the main plate arrives.

The catch is salt. The same nutrition service put the sodium at around 1,000mg per bowl, and a dietitian estimate elsewhere puts some cha chaan teng versions near 1,950mg, which is a full day's worth. Restaurants boost the flavour with tomato paste, stock cubes and salt because the vegetables are cheap and bland. So the calories are fine; the sodium is not, and a person watching blood pressure should treat it as a few spoonfuls rather than a bowl to finish.
lighter: Pick borscht over cream soup. That single choice is about 80 to 235 calories saved per set.
Do not add the bread roll and butter that comes with the soup. That is about 180 calories on top of a 90 calorie soup.
If sodium matters to you, eat the vegetables and beef with a spoon and leave the liquid.
Make it at home with no stock cube. A homemade bowl with fresh tomatoes and lean beef is about 70 calories and under 400mg of sodium.

portions.label: Large bowl with bread roll and butter

variants.name: Carrot and pork bone soup (例湯)

faq.q: How many calories in Hong Kong borscht?
faq.a: About 90 calories per 250ml bowl, with around 2.5g of fat, based on Hong Kong nutrition service figures. The cream soup alternative is 170 to 325.

faq.q: Is Hong Kong borscht healthy?
faq.a: Low in calories and fat, and mostly vegetables. The problem is sodium, around 1,000mg or more per bowl, so it is not a soup to finish every day.

faq.q: Why does Hong Kong borscht have no beetroot?
faq.a: It came via Shanghai in the 1930s, where beetroot was hard to get, so cooks used tomato and cabbage instead. The tomato version is about 90 calories a bowl and stuck.

foods.source: Fit Fit Food HK nutrition service, cha chaan teng soup comparison (borscht 87.5 kcal, 2.5g fat, 1,000mg sodium per 250g bowl)

foods.name: Swiss Wings (Sui Si Gai Yik)
foods.metaDescription: Three Hong Kong Swiss wings are about 310 calories. The sweet soy braising sauce adds 12g of sugar; the wings themselves are the fat. Full breakdown here.
foods.summary: Swiss wings are whole chicken wings braised in a sweet soy sauce made with dark soy, rock sugar, Shaoxing wine and spices. They have nothing to do with Switzerland; the name is a mishearing of Sweet. Tai Ping Koon charges HK$190 for 8, a cha chaan teng about HK$40 for 3.
foods.answer: Three Swiss wings are around 310 calories, built from the wings themselves (about 240 calories of meat and skin) and the sweet soy sauce they soak up (about 55). Protein is roughly 24g for three wings, fat about 19g, and the sauce adds around 12g of sugar.
realTalk: A chicken wing is the fattiest part of the bird because of the skin to meat ratio. Hong Kong dietitians put three plain wings (about 100g of edible meat and skin) at around 220 calories, and suggest three per meal as a sensible cap. Swiss wings are braised, not fried, so no oil is added in the cooking. The extra over plain wings is the sauce, which is dark soy and rock sugar reduced until it clings, and that is where the 12g of sugar and about 55 calories come from.

Compared with the other things on the same menu this is not bad. Three Swiss wings at 310 calories beat a baked pork chop rice (1,300) by a mile and come in under a plate of sweet and sour pork (800 with rice). The problem is what they come with. The Tai Ping Koon afternoon tea set is two wings with rice or noodles for HK$74, and the rice or fried noodles under them is another 300 to 450. Eaten as a side dish with a shared plate of greens they are a decent protein option.

The sauce is reused all day at a lot of places, which means it gets saltier and sweeter each hour as it reduces. Three wings can carry 900mg or more of sodium. Eating the skin is the difference between 310 and about 230 for three, since the skin holds most of the 19g of fat. Whether that is worth it is your call; the skin is the reason people order the dish.
lighter: Order them as the meat, not the snack. Three wings plus a plate of blanched vegetables and a small bowl of rice is a 600 calorie meal with 30g of protein.
Take the skin off two of the three wings. That saves around 50 calories and most of the saturated fat.
Do not spoon the sauce over your rice. Each tablespoon is about 30 calories of sugar and soy.
Pick Swiss wings over fried chicken wings. Three fried wings are about 420 calories versus 310 braised.

components.name: Chicken wings, meat and skin (3 wings)
Swiss sauce absorbed (soy, rock sugar, wine)
Rendered fat and sauce on plate

portions.label: 8 wings (Tai Ping Koon full order, shared)

variants.name: 3 Swiss wings, skin removed
variants.note: Most of the fat is in the skin

variants.name: Swiss wings tea set with fried noodles (2 wings)
variants.note: Noodles are two thirds of it

faq.q: How many calories in Swiss chicken wings?
faq.a: About 310 calories for three wings, or roughly 100 per wing. The braising sauce adds about 55 calories and 12g of sugar; the rest is the meat and skin.

faq.q: Are Swiss wings from Switzerland?
faq.a: No. The name comes from a foreign customer at Tai Ping Koon in the early 1900s calling the soy sauce wings Sweet, which the waiter heard as Swiss. It is a Hong Kong Cantonese dish.

faq.q: Are Swiss wings healthier than fried wings?
faq.a: Yes, by about 110 calories per three wings, because they are braised rather than deep fried. They are higher in sugar and sodium though, from the soy sauce reduction.

foods.source: Estimate from components: Ming Pao dietitian figure for chicken wings (3 wings, about 100g edible, 220 kcal) plus sweet soy braising sauce

foods.name: Cocktail Bun (Gai Mei Bao)
foods.metaDescription: A cocktail bun from a Hong Kong bakery is about 350 calories, more than a pineapple bun, thanks to the sugar, butter and coconut filling.
foods.summary: The cocktail bun is a soft oval bun filled with a paste of shredded coconut, sugar, butter and milk powder, topped with sesame seeds. It was invented in the 1950s to use up day old bread. Every Hong Kong bakery has it, HK$6 to HK$12.
foods.answer: One cocktail bun is about 350 calories, according to a Hong Kong dietitian ranking of bakery items that put it at the top of the list, above the pineapple bun (310). The filling is the reason: about 25g of coconut, sugar and butter paste adds around 130 calories and gives the bun 14g of fat, nearly half again more than a pineapple bun.
realTalk: This bun beats the pineapple bun and most people assume it is the other way round. A cocktail bun is 350 calories to a pineapple bun's 310, and the fat is where the gap opens: 14g versus 10g. The pineapple bun's crust is a thin layer on top. The cocktail bun's filling runs through the whole thing and it is made from butter, sugar and desiccated coconut, three of the densest ingredients in a bakery. A dietitian in am730 called it the one to be most careful with if you are watching weight or blood sugar.

Sugar is the second problem. Between the sweet dough and the filling, one bun carries around 18 to 20g of sugar, which is 4 to 5 teaspoons. Hong Kong bakery bread rankings put it near the top for sugar as well as calories, which is why dietitians flag it for anyone with diabetes. It hits fast: 48g of carbs, very little fibre, 7g of protein, so an hour later you are hungry again.

Size varies by shop. A small neighbourhood bakery bun is around 75g and closer to 290 calories. The big glossy ones at the chain bakeries near MTR stations push 110g and can hit 420. The tell is how much filling shows when you break it: if the coconut paste runs edge to edge, it is the high end. Two of these with a milk tea on the way to work is a 810 calorie breakfast with almost no protein.
lighter: Have one, not two. The second bun is a full 350 calories you will not notice eating.
If you want a bakery bun, the sausage bun (豬仔包) is about 290 and the raisin bun 274, both lower than the cocktail bun.
Pair it with a boiled egg or a cup of milk. That gives the 350 calories some protein and keeps you full longer.
Skip the butter some cha chaan tengs slide inside. That adds another 75 calories.

faq.q: How many calories in a cocktail bun?
faq.a: About 350 calories for a standard 90g bun, per a Hong Kong dietitian ranking of bakery items. That is 40 more than a pineapple bun and about 14g of fat.

faq.q: Why is it called a cocktail bun?
faq.a: Bakers in the 1950s mashed unsold bread with sugar and coconut into a filling, a mix or cocktail of leftovers, and baked it into a new bun. The name stuck.

faq.q: Is a cocktail bun or pineapple bun healthier?
faq.a: The pineapple bun, slightly: 310 calories and 10g fat versus 350 and 14g. Neither has much protein, so both are a snack rather than a meal.

foods.source: am730 Hong Kong dietitian bakery ranking (cocktail bun 350 kcal, pineapple bun 310, sausage bun 290, raisin bun 274)

foods.name: Put Chai Ko (Red Bean Pudding Cake)
aka: Hong Kong Red Bean Rice Cake
foods.metaDescription: One put chai ko (Hong Kong red bean pudding cake) is about 130 calories with almost no fat, per Centre for Food Safety data. Sugar is about 13g per piece.
foods.summary: Put chai ko is a small steamed pudding of rice flour, wheat starch and brown or white sugar set in a porcelain bowl, studded with red beans, then popped out and speared on two bamboo sticks. Street stalls in Sham Shui Po and Yuen Long sell them for HK$5 to HK$10.
foods.answer: One put chai ko of about 100g is around 130 calories, based on the Centre for Food Safety figure of 130 kcal per 100g. It is nearly all carbohydrate: about 29g, of which 13g is sugar, with 2g of protein and 1g of fat. The Macau Sports Bureau food guide gives a similar 140 calories per piece.
realTalk: This is one of the few Hong Kong street snacks that is not fried, and it shows. At 130 calories a piece, a put chai ko is a third of a sheet of egg waffle (390) and less than half a fish siu mai skewer (294). There is no oil in the recipe at all; the 1g of fat comes from the red beans. What you are eating is rice starch and sugar set with steam, which is why it is chewy and translucent.

The sugar is the whole story. CFS puts it at 13g per 100g, so one piece is about 3 teaspoons, and the brown sugar version (黃糖) has slightly more than the white. That is a fast hit of carbs with no protein or fibre to slow it down, which is why dietitians in Hong Kong flag it for people managing blood sugar. Two pieces is 26g of sugar, over half the WHO daily suggestion of 50g, for a snack that takes 3 minutes to eat.

Size is the variable. The old style bowl cakes from the Sham Shui Po stalls are about 100g and land at the 130 figure. The mini versions sold in packs of 6 at Taipo and Yuen Long markets are 40 to 50g each, so around 60 calories a piece, which is the number the Centre for Health Protection used in its snack post. Check which one you are holding before you assume it is a light snack.
lighter: One piece is a fair 130 calorie snack. Two is a sugar bomb.
Choose the red bean version over the plain. The beans add about 1g of fibre and a little protein for the same calories.
Skip the sweet sauce some stalls brush on. It adds another 20 calories of pure sugar.
Eat it after a meal with protein rather than on an empty stomach. The 13g of sugar lands softer.

variants.name: Brown sugar red bean put chai ko
Sesame or green tea put chai ko

faq.q: How many calories in a put chai ko?
faq.a: About 130 calories for a standard 100g piece, according to Centre for Food Safety data. The mini versions are around 60.

faq.q: Is put chai ko healthy?
faq.a: It is low in fat and calories for a street snack, but about 13g of sugar per piece with no protein. Fine as an occasional snack, not a daily one if you are watching blood sugar.

faq.q: Is put chai ko gluten free?
faq.a: Mostly rice flour, but many recipes add wheat starch for the chewy texture, so not reliably. Ask the stall if it matters to you.

foods.source: Centre for Food Safety Hong Kong Nutrient Information Inquiry System via Bowtie (130 kcal, 13g sugar per 100g); Macau Sports Bureau nutrition guide (140 kcal per piece)

foods.name: Stinky Tofu (Chau Dau Fu)
foods.metaDescription: A street portion of Hong Kong fried stinky tofu is about 174 calories per the Centre for Health Protection, with 10g of protein. Sauces add more.
foods.summary: Stinky tofu is fermented bean curd deep fried until the outside crackles, served on a stick or in a paper bag with sweet sauce and chili. You smell the stall from 50 metres away in Mong Kok or Sham Shui Po. About HK$15 to HK$22 a portion.
foods.answer: One street portion of fried stinky tofu is about 174 calories, the figure the Centre for Health Protection used in its street snack ranking. The Centre for Food Safety database puts it at around 150 calories per 100g, so a single large cube of 70g is roughly 105. Protein is about 10g a portion, which is better than most things on the same cart.
realTalk: For a deep fried snack this is on the lighter end. A portion at 174 calories sits below fish siu mai (294 for six) and egg waffle (390), though above curry fish balls (65 to 120 a skewer). Tofu is about 8 percent protein and does not soak up oil the way batter does, so the 12g of fat is mostly from the surface crust and the oil that clings to it. The fermentation itself adds no calories; it just adds the smell.

The sauce is what pushes it up. Stalls brush on sweet sauce, hoisin and chili, often all three, and each squeeze is 15 to 20 calories of sugar. A portion that came out of the fryer at 174 can be 230 by the time it reaches your hand. Some stalls also serve it with pickled cabbage, which is nearly free on calories but adds sodium to a snack that already carries around 500mg from the brine.

Where people go wrong is the count. A portion is 3 to 4 pieces at most stalls, but the big Taiwanese style cubes are 70g each and a bag of 5 is 350g and over 500 calories. The Hong Kong street version is smaller and thinner, which is why the CHP figure is what it is. If you are handed a full bag rather than a stick, treat it as a meal's worth, not a snack.
lighter: Ask for one sauce, not three. That saves 30 to 40 calories of sugar.
Order a stick (3 pieces) rather than a bag. A bag of 5 large cubes is 350 calories or more.
Let the pieces drain on the paper before eating. The oil that soaks in during the walk is real.
If the stall has the steamed or braised version (滷水臭豆腐), it is around 100 calories a portion with the same protein.

portions.label: Bag of 5 large cubes with sauce

variants.name: Fried stinky tofu with three sauces

faq.q: How many calories in stinky tofu?
faq.a: About 174 calories per street portion of 3 pieces, per the Centre for Health Protection. The Centre for Food Safety database puts it at roughly 150 calories per 100g.

faq.q: Is stinky tofu healthy?
faq.a: It has about 10g of protein per portion and fewer calories than most fried street snacks. The fermentation brine and sauces make it high in sodium, around 500mg or more.

faq.q: Why does stinky tofu smell but not taste bad?
faq.a: The tofu is soaked in a fermented brine for a day or two, which produces sulphur compounds you smell. Frying at high heat drives most of them off, leaving a mild, salty flavour.

foods.source: Centre for Health Protection Hong Kong street snack ranking via Medical Inspire (174 kcal per portion); Centre for Food Safety database via Bowtie (150 kcal per 100g)

foods.name: Zha Leung (Rice Roll with Fried Dough Stick)
foods.metaDescription: A plate of zha leung, a fried dough stick wrapped in rice roll, is about 450 calories. The Centre for Food Safety puts it at 230 kcal per 100g.
foods.summary: Zha leung is a you tiao (fried dough stick) rolled inside a thin sheet of steamed rice noodle, cut in two, and dressed with sweet soy, sesame and sometimes hoisin. Congee shops sell it as the side to a bowl of congee for HK$16 to HK$24.
foods.answer: One plate of zha leung, about 200g, is around 450 calories, based on the Centre for Food Safety figure of 230 kcal per 100g. Roughly 230 of that is the fried dough stick, 140 is the rice roll, and the sauces and sesame oil add the rest. Fat is around 23g, nearly all from the you tiao.
realTalk: Zha leung looks like a light dim sum plate and is not. The rice roll on the outside is steamed and about 130 calories per 100g, but the dough stick inside is deep fried and roughly 380 per 100g. Wrapping one in the other does not dilute anything. CFS lists the finished dish at 230 calories per 100g with 12g of fat, which is about the same density as a slice of pizza, and a plate is a third of a day's fat.

Where it hurts is the pairing. Almost nobody eats zha leung alone; it is the side to congee. A bowl of century egg and lean pork congee is 260 calories. Add a plate of zha leung and breakfast is 710. Add a hot milk tea and it is 820. The congee was the smart part of that order. A plain steamed rice roll with soy (齋腸) instead of zha leung is about 130 calories and gets you most of the texture.

The sauces are not free either. Congee shops finish zha leung with sweet soy, sesame oil, sesame seeds and often a squeeze of hoisin and peanut sauce. That dressing is 60 to 80 calories on top of the fried dough. Sodium is around 480mg per 100g in the CFS figure, so a plate is close to 1,000mg before the soy in your congee counts. It is a once a week breakfast, not a daily one.
lighter: Order plain rice roll (齋腸) with your congee instead. About 130 calories versus 450.
Share the plate. One piece of zha leung is 225 calories, still a snack rather than a meal.
Ask for less sauce (少醬). The dressing is 60 to 80 calories and a lot of sodium.
If you want the crunch, half a plain you tiao dipped in congee is about 135 calories, less than a full zha leung piece.

components.name: Sweet soy, sesame oil, sesame seeds, hoisin

portions.label: Plate with congee and milk tea

variants.name: Plain rice roll with soy (齋腸)
Zha leung with extra peanut and hoisin sauce

faq.q: How many calories in zha leung?
faq.a: About 450 calories for a standard two piece plate, based on the Centre for Food Safety figure of 230 kcal per 100g. One piece is around 225.

faq.q: Is zha leung or plain cheung fun healthier?
faq.a: Plain rice roll by a wide margin: about 130 calories a plate versus 450 for zha leung. The fried dough stick inside is what adds the 300 difference.

faq.q: What is zha leung made of?
faq.a: A deep fried dough stick (you tiao, about 230 calories) wrapped in a sheet of steamed rice noodle (about 140), dressed with sweet soy and sesame.

foods.source: Centre for Food Safety Hong Kong Nutrient Information Inquiry System via Bowtie (230 kcal, 12g fat, 480mg sodium per 100g); plate weight estimated at 200g

foods.name: Mango Pomelo Sago (Yeung Zi Gam Lou)
foods.metaDescription: A bowl of mango pomelo sago is about 250 calories and holds around 36g of sugar, the most sugar of any Hong Kong tong sui tested by the Consumer Council.
foods.summary: Yeung zi gam lou is a chilled dessert of mango puree and chunks, pomelo pulp and pearl sago in coconut and evaporated milk. It was invented at Lei Garden in 1984 and every dessert shop in Hong Kong now sells it, HK$32 to HK$48 a bowl.
foods.answer: One bowl of mango pomelo sago is around 250 calories, based on a nutritionist figure of 254 kcal for a 350ml serving. The bigger number is sugar: the Consumer Council and Centre for Food Safety measured an average of 11g per 100g, the highest of the 10 tong sui they tested, so a 330g bowl carries about 36g and a 600g dessert shop bowl about 66g.
realTalk: The calories are not the shocking part; the sugar is. Mango is already sweet, then the shop adds syrup, then coconut milk and evaporated milk on top of that. The Consumer Council test found one 330g bowl with 40g of sugar and one 600g bowl with 66g, which is 32 percent over the WHO daily limit of 50g in a single dessert. For comparison, tofu pudding (豆腐花) in the same test ranged from 0 to 5.4g per 100g.

As a tong sui it is middle of the pack on calories. A 350ml bowl at 254 is about the same as a bowl of taro coconut sago (262) and well under walnut paste or black sesame paste, which the same tests put at 130 calories per 100g, so over 400 a bowl. Grass jelly with all the toppings tops the list at around 430. The fat is modest at about 8g, mostly from the coconut milk, so this is a sugar and starch dessert rather than a fatty one.

The dessert shop bowl is the trap. Hui Lau Shan and the chain shops serve it in a 500 to 600ml bowl, sometimes with extra mango, ice cream or a second scoop of sago, and that is 400 to 500 calories and over 60g of sugar. The 250 calorie figure is a normal restaurant tong sui portion after dinner. If you are ordering it as a standalone afternoon snack in a big cup, count it as a meal.
lighter: Order the small bowl or share the large one. Half a dessert shop bowl is about 220 calories.
Ask for less syrup (少糖). The mango is sweet enough on its own and this saves 40 to 60 calories.
Skip the extra scoop of ice cream or the mango sorbet on top. That is another 100 to 150.
If you want a cold dessert with less sugar, tofu pudding is about 150 calories and one fifth the sugar.

variants.name: Tofu pudding (豆腐花)
variants.note: For comparison, one fifth the sugar

variants.name: Mango pomelo sago with ice cream

faq.q: How many calories in mango pomelo sago?
faq.a: About 250 calories for a standard 330g bowl, or 254 for 350ml by a nutritionist estimate. A large dessert shop bowl of 600g is closer to 450.

faq.q: How much sugar is in mango pomelo sago?
faq.a: About 11g per 100g according to Consumer Council and Centre for Food Safety testing, the highest of 10 Hong Kong tong sui. A 330g bowl has around 36g, a 600g bowl about 66g.

faq.q: Is mango pomelo sago healthier than sesame paste?
faq.a: Lower in calories (250 versus around 420 a bowl) and fat, but higher in sugar. Sesame paste has more fat and a bit more protein; mango sago is mostly fruit sugar and syrup.
